title: F1 2027 grid: Who will be racing and where? The full line-up
summary: Next year's grid has fallen into place - but who's driving where?
content: Motorsport photo The 2027 Formula 1 grid is now complete following the announcement from Haas that it has retained star youngster Oliver Bearman . But the American squad is also the only team that is altering its driver pairing for next season, as many potentially enthralling storylines failed to materialise. So, here’s a look at the situation. Mercedes : Kimi Antonelli, George Russell George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes The 2026 season has witnessed a significant shift in the dynamic down at Mercedes between Kimi Antonelli and George Russell, as the latter headed into the year as the heavy title favourite - only to fall flat early on. It came after Russell finished 169 points ahead of Antonelli last season in what was a very up-and-down rookie campaign for the Italian, while the Briton arguably delivered his best yet. So, with Mercedes expected to master the regulation switch, which it did, Russell was the natural favourite yet Antonelli learned his lessons impressively fast to vastly improve upon 2025. This eventually led to the 20-year-old becoming F1’s youngest ever world champion by securing his maiden title at the Mexico Grand Prix, with four rounds still to play at the time. Although this came as a surprise to many, Mercedes would have argued that his performances had been as forecast when it plucked him from karting and into its junior programme. Read Also: What was Kimi Antonelli’s best moment of his F1 title-winning campaign? Our writers have their say As for Russell, his season has been a “complete disaster” - per Max Verstappen - and with two grands prix left in 2026, he sits fourth in the standings and could easily drop to fifth as he is level on points with 2025 world champion Lando Norris . Nevertheless, he will remain with Mercedes for 2027 with his and Antonelli’s fate known for quite some time. Ferrari : Charles Leclerc , Lewis Hamilton Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Ferrari and Charles Leclerc agreed upon a new deal earlier in 2026 - announced in June - meaning the 29-year-old is continuing his length association with the Italian outfit. Leclerc joined its junior programme in 2016, made his F1 debut with customer squad Alfa Romeo Sauber in 2018 before moving to the works’ outfit in 2019. The Monegasque has won nine grands prix in that time, which can be seen as a disappointment considering the promise displayed early on. But with Ferrari’s improved performance in 2026, jumping from fourth to second in the championship, Leclerc’s hope is that the team can press on and finally deliver a championship-winning car having signed a multi-year contract. But he will have Lewis Hamilton to worry about in the neighbouring garage, as the seven-time world champion is understood to be under contract until the end of 2027 after joining in 2025. Last year was a disappointment for the Briton, finishing 86 points behind Leclerc, but he’s strengthened in 2026 with a 17-point advantage over his team-mate. Tensions have also been high recently, with the two colliding on various occasions, most notably Monza, Mexico and Las Vegas, so that is a dynamic Ferrari must manage heading into 2027. Read Also: Why Ferrari believes written rules won't help manage Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton McLaren : Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Lando Norris, McLaren Oscar Piastri, McLaren, Lando Norris, McLaren It was known that at one stage Verstappen held some level of talks with McLaren when his Red Bull future was up in the air. Though this simply may have been a tactic to secure a more lucrative deal with the Austrian outfit, which is something he eventually earned, so McLaren is remaining with Norris and Oscar Piastri. The Briton seems content with being a one-team man for the time being, staying with McLaren since his debut in 2019, and why not? Norris has secured that world title he so strived for and has been impressive in 2026 with three victories, even if the car hasn’t been quite there on several occasions. As for Piastri, what happens with him is an on-and-off talking point given the Australian would have likely been the man to move had Verstappen joined. This year has been a disappointment for him, continuing on from his late title collapse in 2025, as he is seventh in the standings and 97 points behind Norris. His most recent victory was Zandvoort in August last year. But he is on a “multi-year contract”, signed in 2025, and looks set to stay for now. Red Bull: Max Verstappen, Isack Hadjar Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing The 2026 season has been quite similar to 2025 for Red Bull, having started quite slowly before a late rejuvenation with Verstappen enjoying four wins and nine podiums since this year’s summer break. That has vaulted him into second in the drivers’ standings and should he carry such momentum into 2027, then a fifth world title could easily be on the way for the Dutchman. That would put him one short of Hamilton’s record for the most championships with one team - he achieved six at Mercedes - as Verstappen signed a bumper deal until at least 2030 this year. It will see him start a second season alongside Isack Hadjar, who has had a solid first campaign at Red Bull and gave the team no reason to replace him. Perhaps the team now has its ideal number two driver to assist Verstappen in his title charge next year. Racing Bulls : Liam Lawson , Arvid Lindblad Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls Arvid Lindblad, Racing Bulls, Liam Lawson, Racing Bulls The situation down at Red Bull’s sister outfit was one of the biggest sources of uncertainty, given it was only in November that Racing Bulls confirmed its pairing for 2027. It will be an unchanged duo, however, as Arvid Lindblad will return for his second season in F1 alongside Liam Lawson, whose seat was in doubt despite his best year yet. Lawson is on course for a career-best ninth in the standings with 89 points, securing a top 10 finish at all but six grands prix, which in itself is enough for the Faenza outfit to secure its highest-ever constructors’ championship finish of fifth. But Red Bull junior Nikola Tsolov has impressed as an F2 rookie this year, sitting second to Rafael Camara , and historically Racing Bulls doesn’t keep drivers for long if a promotion to the main squad isn’t on the cards. Read Also: Retaining Liam Lawson isn't enough – Red Bull must stop treating him like a failure With 2027 going to be Lawson’s third proper season at Racing Bulls, historically the team may have dropped him in favour of its next protege. Tsolov, however, will have to settle for a reserve driver role in 2027 while Lindblad continues to perform, taking 38 points from his rookie year so far and 11th in the standings. Alpine : Pierre Gasly , Franco Colapinto Pierre Gasly, Alpine Pierre Gasly, Alpine Pierre Gasly signed a contract extension with Alpine last year, demonstrating his commitment to the cause despite the team being adrift at the back of the constructors' order across 2025. The arrival of Flavio Briatore, Steve Nielsen, and Mercedes has put the team back into the midfield battle, and the Frenchman is hoping that the Enstone squad can deliver a car worthy of his immense - and oft-underrated - talent. Gasly is 10th in the 2026 standings with 52 points, helping Alpine sit sixth in the constructors’ championship and although he’s the French outfit’s clear number one driver, Franco Colapinto has still made a considerable step. The Argentine has taken 35 points in 2026, compared to zero last year, and that earned him a new deal in August for 2027. Haas: Oliver Bearman , Rafael Camara Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team, Rafael Camara, Haas F1 Team Oliver Bearman, Haas F1 Team, Rafael Camara, Haas F1 Team Haas is another squad to have endured serious question marks surrounding its driver pairing for next year. The first concerned Esteban Ocon, who just couldn’t make things click ever since he joined the American outfit from Alpine for 2025. At the time he was seen as a real coup, the first grand prix winner to drive for Haas, but instead he was consistently outperformed by his much more inexperienced team-mate - Bearman - across both last year and 2026. In the end things turned quite ugly and after it being confirmed that the 198-time grand prix starter wouldn’t continue into 2027, he was dismissed by Haas with five rounds still to play in the season. His replacement is F2 championship leader Camara, who has signed a “multi-year” deal and given up his title ambitions in the feeder series to finish the season in F1 before his first, full campaign in 2027 . That will come alongside Bearman, who has mightily impressed in his time at Haas so far. Although the Briton was all but certain to continue with Haas into 2027, his announcement came rather late as Bearman's camp was looking for long-term assurances ahead of his third season at Haas on loan from Ferrari. Read Also: Salary dispute holding up Ollie Bearman’s new Haas F1 deal Audi : Gabriel Bortoleto , Nico Hulkenberg Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi F1 Team, Nico Hulkenberg, Audi F1 Team Gabriel Bortoleto, Audi F1 Team, Nico Hulkenberg, Audi F1 Team Audi F1 boss Mattia Binotto confirmed in September that it will retain Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto for the 2027 season. At the time it didn’t really cause any particular conversations because the announcement came as little surprise, considering how well both drivers have done - thus giving Audi no reason to change its line-up. The German marque, which made his F1 debut in 2026 after taking over from Sauber, has the perfect blend of youth and experience, plus a harmonious relationship between the pair. Bortoleto is set for his third season in the championship, compared to Hulkenberg’s 16th, and both drivers have scored 14 points this year to give Audi eighth in the standings. Williams : Alex Albon , Carlos Sainz Alexander Albon, Williams, Carlos Sainz, Williams Alexander Albon, Williams, Carlos Sainz, Williams Williams' decision to lock in Alex Albon and Carlos Sainz for at least another year demonstrates the buy-in for its long-term ambitions from both drivers, even if this season has presented a step back in fortunes. Some might uncharitably suggest that there was nowhere else for either driver to go, which is probably also true, but the retention of both drivers is a significant boost for the team. Had Sainz decided to do something else, Williams is said to have hedged its bets and had spoken to the management of Sergio Perez and Colapinto for 2027, while Luke Browning has also impressed in his FP1 outings with the team. Aston Martin: Fernando Alonso , Lance Stroll Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing Fernando Alonso, Aston Martin Racing, Lance Stroll, Aston Martin Racing The situation at Aston Martin was another which promised potential drama for 2027 but failed to materialise as such. That is because for months the questions surrounding Fernando Alonso’s future were strife, considering he is 45 years old, driving for a backmarker and heavily dislikes the current regulations with his previous contract expiring at the end of 2026. But all speculation stopped in September when the two-time champion announced his extension with Aston Martin into 2027. It is believed that him not publicly committing to F1 through the summer months was partly an effort to put pressure on the series to make changes. As for team-mate Lance Stroll, his extension into 2027 arrived on the same day as Alonso, but was far from the same talking point considering father Lawrence owns the team. So, the 28-year-old Canadian, who next season will have had a decade in F1, effectively has a contract for as long as he likes. Cadillac: Sergio Perez, Valtteri Bottas Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac, Sergio Perez, Cadillac Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac, Sergio Perez, Cadillac F1 newcomer Cadillac was the final squad to hold intrigue surrounding its driver pairing for 2027. Said intrigue didn’t really concern Sergio Perez, who in October signed a multi-year extension, but more Valtteri Bottas. The 10-time grand prix winner has been outperformed by Perez this year, with a losing 16-10 head-to-head record in qualifying (including sprints), causing his seat to be thrown in doubt. Team management refused to publicly commit to him for some time as it weighed up the possibility of promoting reserve driver Colton Herta, given its desire to have an American driver racing for an American team. Read Also: Why Cadillac F1 boss provoked fresh intrigue by dodging driver question One sticking point for Herta was his lack of an FIA Superlicence - required to compete in F1 - despite winning nine races in IndyCar. But he eventually obtained one via six FP1 appearances this year, yet that still wasn’t enough to grab an F1 seat with his highly disappointing F2 season, sitting 19th in the standings, in mind. So, in November Cadillac announced its decision to stick with Bottas for 2027. title: Bears vs. Lions: Best odds, bets, and parlays
summary: Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions Week 12 best player prop bets and parlays
content: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - NOVEMBER 22: Amon-Ra St. Brown #14 of the Detroit Lions warms up prior to the NFL football game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field on November 22, 2026 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thanksgiving, people are surrounded by loved ones, enjoying food, and most importantly, watching Detroit Lions football. It’s a classic tradition across Michigan, but it doesn’t always end well, as the franchise has a losing record on the holiday. This time, though, they aim to make it a happy Thanksgiving with a win over the Chicago Bears, and what better way to do it than with some extra cash coming to you too! It was another dominant week for me on the bets last week : I went 3-0 on all my straight bets, and if the refs hadn’t called some horrible defensive pass interference penalties on the final Lions defensive possession, it would’ve been a perfect day on the bets. We also hit our first bold bet parlay, so I can’t complain too much. Stay with me here as I try to keep the hot streak going, so make room on that plate for these bets. Here are three wagers to watch in this matchup. The odds are with FanDuel Sportsbook . 1. Over 55.5 Points (-112) Hope you saved room for some offense because this game should have it. In their first battle last year, the Lions dominated the Bears 52-21 in Bears head coach Ben Johnson’s first game back in Detroit. Detroit won the season finale, but it wasn’t as explosive, 19-16. This year, I expect it to be more of a fight, and both offenses will be humming along. Detroit enters at 28.8 points per game, while Chicago averages 26.2. Now the Lions defense has been playing better lately, holding their last four opponents to an average of 12.7 points per game, while the Bears defense started strong but has allowed an average of 22 points per game in their last four games. I expect Johnson will want revenge from 2025, and doing so on Thanksgiving will make it that much sweeter. This is the same coach who wants to lead the NFL in all-time scoring offense . I think this game could be a high-scoring, close contest, with each team putting up at least 30 points. Each team has plenty of weapons, and as a divisional game, the stakes are higher. The winner takes control of the NFC North and, given how contested the division is, could determine how the standings fall come January. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.93 2. Jared Goff alt passing yards 300+ (+132) Since I could see this game being high-scoring, I think Lions quarterback Jared Goff will have a dominant performance against the Bears. The reason isn’t the Bears defense itself; it’s also how Goff has performed against them recently. Last season, Goff threw for over 300 yards in both games: 334 yards and five touchdowns in their dominant Week 2 victory, and 331 yards in the low-scoring season finale. Despite the Bears’ defensive line upgrades, Detroit’s offensive line is a big improvement from 2025. If Goff can throw for over 300 with that line, how can he not do it again this year? What also helps Goff this year is the Bears’ inconsistent pass defense. They’re either shutting down passing attacks, holding six teams to under 200 yards, or they’re letting them air it out, with three games where they’ve allowed over 300 yards. Goff has thrown for over 300 yards in four games so far this season, and if teams keep paying attention to running back Jahmyr Gibbs, Goff will gladly slice and dice them upfield. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $23.20 3. Amon-Ra St. Brown Over 82.5 yards (-113) It wasn’t just Goff who went off on the Bears last season; wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown had some strong performances. In the first game, St. Brown had six catches for 115 yards and three touchdowns, then snagged 11 balls for 139 yards in the last game. St. Brown made it a point to go off against his former coordinator in Johnson, and as long as he’s the head coach of the Bears, I think St. Brown will try his best to play well. He’s averaging 84 yards a game this season, so I think hitting the over on this game is a must. Detroit lost its Thanksgiving game last year too, and I don’t think St. Brown wants Johnson to rain on the Detroit parade. He will do whatever it takes for Detroit to win this game, and with the offense humming, I wouldn’t put it past St. Brown to have another great performance this week. Bet potential winnings: $10 -> $18.85 If you want to turn these three single bets into a same-game parlay, the odds are +312 and $10 -> $41.22 Record: 17-13 Brandon’s Bold Bet If you want to go bold and build a big parlay that could pay well, put these three bets together in a parlay: St. Brown anytime touchdown (-150) Jared Goff alt passing touchdowns 3+ TD (+178) Jameson Williams anytime touchdown (+200) Speaking of St. Brown, you best believe he will want to find the end zone on Thanksgiving. If he doesn’t get as many yards as he wants, but scores at least once and comes away with the win, I think he would be content with his performance. While this game isn’t as big as the Germany game, St. Brown wants to play well when matched up against Johnson. With my expectations of this game being high-scoring, I see the passing offense taking the stage against the Bears. If Goff is throwing for over 300 yards, I think he throws three touchdowns as well. He’s done it three times this season, but he hasn’t done it at home in Ford Field. That changes when Goff put up a big performance on Thanksgiving afternoon. So far, I’ve hyped up Goff and St. Brown, but I don’t think I’ll overlook Jameson Williams for a good performance too. While his play has been up and down this season, I think he’ll find the end zone and gobble up some turkey on Thursday afternoon. Goff could throw three touchdowns to St. Brown as they did against the Bears last year, but I think he spreads the wealth and gives Williams one, perhaps on a unique trick play that catches Johnson’s defense by surprise. Odds +559 and bet $10 -> $ 65.95 Record: 1-9 Do-it-all parlay If you want to combine all six plays into a parlay and go big, here are the odds: Over 55.5 points Jared Goff alt passing yards 300+ Amon-Ra St. Brown Over 82.5 yards St. Brown anytime touchdown Jared Goff alt passing touchdowns 3+ TD Jameson Williams touchdown Odds +1254 and bet $10 -> $135.41 Record: 0-10 Use this information however you like. You can ignore it and watch the game, or, if you want to risk some money, follow these recommendations or test your own luck. Whatever you decide, please gamble responsibly and bet only money you can afford to lose.

title: Full Fury vs Joshua undercard confirmed with unusual running order
summary: Welsh star Joe Cordina and Tyson Fury’s brother Roman will both feature
content: The full undercard for Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua has been confirmed, with an unusual running order in place . The standout addition on Wednesday was Welsh star and former world champion Joe Cordina , who faces Mauricio Lara in an intriguing lightweight bout. However, the fight will headline the preliminary card at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium, rather than taking place on the main card. That move alone has led to further criticism of the main card, which was already seen as underwhelming by many fans . Joe Cordina (left) during a win in July 2025 (Getty) Also on the prelims will be Fury’s brother Roman, taking on Adam Kolarik at heavyweight, while British super-welterweight prospect Odel Kamara steps out for just the second time, fighting Patrik Matejcek. Two of the other bouts feature Japanese brothers Hayato Tsutsumi and Reito Tsutsumi, who respectively face Vic Pasillas at featherweight and Muheeb Fazeldin at super-featherweight. Mikie Tallon will feature in an all-British super-flyweight tilt with Sean Bruce, Saudi prospect Mohammed Alakel boxes Rogger Rivera at super-featherweight, and Constantino Nanga fights Lerrone Richards at light-heavyweight. These contests support the main card, which will be headlined by the heavyweight clash between Fury and Joshua – arguably the biggest British fight in history. In fact, the main card consists solely of heavyweight fights, with the chief-support bout pitting Deontay Wilder against Martin Bakole. The latter was originally paired with Solomon Adebayo, who was pulled from the event as Bakole stepped up to replace the injured Jai Opetaia against Wilder. Deontay Wilder (left) is a three-time opponent of Tyson Fury, losing to the Briton twice and drawing once (Getty) Rounding out the main card, Moses Jolly boxes Igor Adiel Macedo and Da’Mazion Vanhouter fights Michael Essomba. The event will take place on Friday 11 December, streaming live exclusively on Netflix. Wednesday brought the news that main-event ring walks will begin at 1am GMT on Saturday 12 December, with travel plans and police presence also confirmed .

title: Tosin Adarabioyo: ‘No one can chat s*** about Cole Palmer’
summary: Interview: Adarabioyo, speaking at the launch of his trading card shop, issued a passionate defence of his former Chelsea team-mate Palmer amid criticism of his attitude
content: Tosin Adarabioyo has leapt to the defence of former Chelsea team-mate Cole Palmer amid criticism of the Englishman’s attitude . Palmer came under fire for a viral interaction with Joao Pedro after Chelsea’s bruising 4-1 thrashing by Leeds last weekend, brushing off the Brazilian after opting not to acknowledge the home fans who booed the team at full-time. The 24-year-old is going through a difficult patch at the moment, having been left out of Thomas Tuchel ’s England squad again for the November internationals after the German manager claimed “he misses too opportunities to impress” . This led to questions over Palmer’s commitment to the England cause, something club team-mate Morgan Rogers emphatically refuted as “nonsense” and “a lie” . And Tosin, who moved to from Chelsea to rivals Tottenham in the summer, has now become the latest to publicly back Palmer, with whom he shared two seasons at Stamford Bridge. Tosin Adarabioyo (right) has leapt to the defence of his former Chelsea team-mate Cole Palmer amid criticism of his attitude (Getty) “No one can chat s*** about Cole,” Tosin said. “For me, he's one of the best players I've ever seen. You can say what you want. Honestly, you guys can say what you want. He's a top level player. He will continue to get better.” Asked whether he was surprised about Palmer’s omission from the England squad, he replied: “Yeah, for sure. Of course, I'm surprised. For me, he's the best No 10 in the Premier League .” Tosin also echoed Rogers’ sentiment in regards to doubts over Palmer’s hunger to play for the Three Lions, with the Chelsea forward struggling to get back in favour with Tuchel after missing out on the World Cup, before his return to the international fold in September was swiftly curtailed by injury. “False, false, false,” Tosin added. “I know Cole's dreams, his aspirations. So, yeah, it's completely false.” While Tosin will passionately defend Palmer against his critics, this doesn’t spare the Chelsea man of a friendly jibe, especially in the wake of Tottenham’s first win at Stamford Bridge in eight years last month. Palmer was sent off in the 2-0 defeat to their fierce rivals and Tosin, who missed the match through injury, was sure to savour the triumph at his mate’s expense. Asked if the pair shared some post-match banter, Tosin laughed: “Cole's my guy, man - yeah, of course. But I'll keep that secret.” Palmer was sent off in Tottenham's landmark 2-0 win at Chelsea last month (Getty) Palmer was among a number of Tosin’s team-mates, past and present, supporting him at the launch of his trading card shop, Card Cop, in London. The retail space in Borough Yards will open to the public on Thursday 26 November. The Spurs defender, who is an avid collector, is joined by the likes of former Blues team-mates Reece James and Levi Colwill , as well as West Ham defender Kyle Walker-Peters , in investing in the business. Along with the investors, Chelsea’s contingent at the launch party included Rogers, Emmanuel Emegha and Jamie Gittens, while the likes of Dominic Solanke , Micky van de Ven , Archie Gray and Ben Davies came down to support their relatively new Spurs colleague. “It’s a testament to what we're like as a team,” Tosin said. “We're all very close and very supportive of each other. The boys didn't have to turn up today, but they did. It's amazing. I'm very thankful to them.” A number of Tottenham players came down to support Tosin at the launch of his trading card shop (Getty) After a dire start to the season, feeling the hangover of their near-miss with relegation last term, Spurs have finally found their groove under Roberto De Zerbi and are now just one point off Chelsea after four wins in five. Tosin puts the uptick in form down to the team’s Marbella training camp during the first international break of the season, which was crucial in forming a bond within the team. “It's our trip to Marbella,” he said. “We had a great time. We bonded together. We learned a lot about each other, and we're all striving to put this club where we think it belongs.”

title: Adepoju Adebawore reveals what it will take to beat Missouri
summary: Adepoju Adebawore says Oklahoma must match Missouri's physicality and win battles up front and in the back seven.
content: The Oklahoma Sooners are heading into their final game of the 2026 regular season. The season has been disappointing overall, as the Sooners entered ranked No. 10 and had national championship aspirations after going to the College Football Playoff last season. Still, Oklahoma has a chance to end the season on a high note, as the Sooners have won three straight games and a win over the Missouri Tigers would be four straight, with three of those wins being against ranked opponents. That would be the most ranked wins in college football. Oklahoma EDGE Adepoju Adebawore revealed what it will take to knock off the Tigers in Columbia. "They're big up front, strong up front," Adebawore said via SoonerScoop. "They're really good at the skill positions. So, we just have to come with a mindset ready to go because they're going to fire off that ball, so we've got to do the same. Got to be able to knock them back. Got to be strong up front and in the back seven." Adebawore's comments highlight the importance of winning the physical battle against Missouri. The Tigers have enough talent at the skill positions to create problems for Oklahoma, but the Sooners will have to start by controllilng the line of scrimmage. Getting pressure on quarterback Austin Simmons, limiting the running game and making tackles in the open field will all be critical to slowing down the Missouri offense. For Oklahoma, Saturday offers a chance to turn a frustrating season into one with a strong finish. The Sooners have responded well over the past three games, and another win would give them four straight wins while adding another ranked opponent to their list. They'll need the same physicality and discipline Adebawore described to accomplish that goal and carry some momentum into the offseason. title: Alabama reportedly lands elite 2027 JUCO linebacker
summary: Alabama has reportedly landed a commitment from Dylan Gill, the top JUCO linebacker in the 2027 class.
content: Alabama appears to have gotten good news on Thanksgiving morning as they have reportedly landed top JUCO linebacker Dylan Gill, per Rivals' Hayes Fawcett . Gill is a 6'3, 240 pound linebacker out of Hutchinson Community College in Hutchinson, Kansas. Gill was named the KJCCC Defensive Player of the Year for his play this season. On the year he has 69 tackles, 11.5 tackles-for-loss, 3.5 sacks, and three interceptions. Gill is the consensus top JUCO linebacker in the 2027 class according to 247, On3, and ESPN. ESPN ranks him as the No. 2 overall JUCO prospect, 247 ranks him as the No. 10 overall JUCO prospect, and On3 ranks him as the 18th best JUCO player in the 2027 class. Again, all three rank him as the top linebacker. Hutchinson CC is one of the premier JUCO programs in the country and are playing in the NJCAA D1 national championship on December 6 following an 11-0 regular season and a blowout win in the national semifinals. Gill is originally from Columbus High School in Miami, Florida. Gill spent his Freshman season in 2025 at FCS West Georgia. Gill is set to join a talented Alabama linebacker room for next season that is currently set to return off-ball linebackers Luke Metz, QB Reese, Xavier Griffin, and Abduall Sanders Jr. Caleb Woodson could also return as he has a decision to make on whether to use his final season of eligibility. Gill is Alabama's first JUCO commitment of the 2027 class, although they are in the mix for others. Alabama's 2027 class now sits 25th nationally with 19 commits per 247Sports and is on an upward trajectory heading towards the Early Signing Period. Gill is Alabama's first off-ball linebacker commit in the class, but it does also feature Edge rushers Tyler Younger and Jeremiah Beverly. title: The Athletic names Florida football a team to watch in QB market
summary: Florida football named a team watch in the 2027 quarterback transfer portal market, with both Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr. in question to return.
content: Florida football could face a major decision at quarterback this offseason, with uncertainty about the program’s future at the position despite having two experienced options on its roster. With the 2026 regular season nearing its conclusion, The Athletic recently identified the Gators as a program to monitor in the upcoming quarterback transfer portal market, suggesting changes could be on the horizon in Gainesville. They highlighted the inconsistent performances of Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones Jr., raising questions about whether either quarterback has done enough to establish himself as Florida’s unquestioned starter entering the 2027 season. Philo, who offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner handpicked, entered the season with high expectations but has had his share of ups and downs. Meanwhile, Jones, a former three-star, has also received opportunities under center, including his first start during Florida’s 27-24 upset victory over Texas in Week 7. Although Jones helped guide the Gators to one of their biggest victories of the season, neither quarterback has consistently separated himself enough to eliminate questions about the position’s long-term outlook. However, Philo’s recent performances have provided reasons for optimism as Florida approaches the end of its regular-season schedule. The third-year has emerged as a more dynamic rushing threat in recent weeks, combining for 175 rushing yards and three touchdowns in consecutive victories over Kentucky and Vanderbilt. Against the Commodores, Philo completed 20 of 26 passes for 241 yards while rushing for 73 yards and two scores, helping Florida secure a 34-27 victory. His performance followed a 102-yard rushing outing against Kentucky, showing another dimension to his game that could factor into the coaching staff’s offseason evaluation. Still, two encouraging performances do not necessarily settle Florida’s quarterback situation heading into 2027. The Gators will have to weigh the development of their current signal-callers against the possibility of bringing in an experienced transfer who could elevate the offense immediately. That decision could become particularly complicated given the uncertainty surrounding this year’s quarterback transfer market. With the transfer portal scheduled to open Jan. 4, Florida’s quarterback situation figures to be among the program’s most important offseason storylines. title: Big 12 football bowl projections, CFP picture after Week 12 results
summary: Updated Big 12 bowl projections have Utah, Texas Tech and BYU in the College Football Playoff conversation, while Colorado eliminated from contention.
content: After Week 12's results, three Big 12 teams can no longer become bowl-eligible this season: Colorado, Kansas and Kansas State . However, three other teams are entering the final week of the season with five wins and have a chance to secure eligibility this week: TCU, West Virginia and Iowa State. The playoff picture for the Big 12 has also changed significantly from last week following the chaos in the Big Ten, especially Indiana's loss. In the most recent projections from ESPN , CBS Sports and USA TODAY Sports , three Big 12 teams now have a realistic chance of making the College Football Playoff. Utah is the top seed in the conference, while Texas Tech and BYU are commonly projected to make it into the playoffs. BYU was not previously projected to make the playoffs, and their near-disaster against Kansas over the weekend did not affect their CFP ranking. Here are the updated bowl projections. Colorado Buffaloes USA TODAY Sports: No projection CBS Sports: No projection Bonagura projection: No projection Schlabach projection: No projection Colorado can no longer become bowl-eligible after their loss to Cincinnati. Therefore, once their game against UCF is over, instead of focusing on a bowl game, they will have larger questions about their program as a whole, including whether Deion Sanders should remain their head coach and whether it is time to move on from the Go-Go offense since it did not go anywhere in most of their games this season. Texas Tech Red Raiders USA TODAY Sports: No. 10 seed in the CFP vs. Tennessee CBS Sports: No. 11 seed in the CFP vs. Miami Bonagura projection: Alamo Bowl vs. Oregon Schlabach projection: No. 11 seed in the CFP vs. Tennessee After weeks of being projected by most outlets to make the playoffs, Texas Tech is finally ranked high enough to be in the playoff picture. Unless the Red Raiders lose to TCU or get blown out in the Big 12 Championship, I highly doubt they will be in the playoffs. However, they are almost guaranteed to be on the road. UCF Knights USA TODAY Sports: Independence Bowl vs. Jacksonville State CBS Sports: Cactus Bowl vs. Nebraska Bonagura projection: Cactus Bowl vs. Nebraska Schlabach projection: Liberty Bowl vs. Auburn UCF secured bowl eligibility last weekend, and it seems like there could be a few options for the Knights. But what is more likely is that the Knights will face Nebraska in the Cactus Bowl. Both teams have upset wins over ranked teams, with UCF beating BYU and Nebraska beating Ohio State, making this an interesting matchup. Baylor Bears USA TODAY Sports: Texas Bowl vs. Auburn CBS Sports: Liberty Bowl vs. LSU Bonagura projection: Texas Bowl vs. Missouri Schlabach projection: Liberty Bowl vs. Tulane Baylor is another Big 12 team that has secured bowl eligibility. Seeing the Bears get a rematch against Auburn remains my favorite projection for Baylor given how that game ended. A revenge game is a perfect way for the Bears to end their season, although Auburn also has a unique opportunity to get two wins against a non-conference team in the same season. Arizona State Sun Devils USA TODAY Sports: Poinsettia Bowl vs. San Diego State CBS Sports: Poinsettia Bowl vs. Oregon State Bonagura projection: Poinsettia Bowl vs. San Diego State Schlabach projection: Poinsettia Bowl vs. San Diego State The projection of Arizona State playing in the Poinsettia Bowl has been consistent for weeks. Since the winner of the Pac-12 is presumably Boise State and they are projected to go to the playoffs, the Sun Devils should get the chance to face another talented team from their old conference, including San Diego State, which beat Boise State last week. Houston Cougars USA TODAY Sports: Alamo Bowl vs. UCLA CBS Sports: Pop-Tarts Bowl vs. Louisville Bonagura projection: Pop-Tarts Bowl vs. Louisville Schlabach projection: Alamo Bowl vs. USC Houston had a promising season, but their loss to Colorado was the final nail in the coffin that kept them out of the playoffs. The Cougars have been projected to play in the Pop-Tarts Bowl for multiple weeks and it seems like that is most likely how their season will end. BYU Cougars USA TODAY Sports: No. 9 seed in the CFP vs. Oregon CBS Sports: Alamo Bowl vs. UCLA Bonagura projection: No. 9 seed in the CFP vs. Tennessee Schlabach projection: No. 9 seed in the CFP vs. Wake Forest The chaos in the Big Ten may have gotten BYU into the playoffs. They will not be playing in the Big 12 Championship game unless Texas Tech loses to TCU, and since that is unlikely, the playoff committee will have to go off their regular-season tape. Indiana has dropped out of the playoffs in the most recent rankings, while the Cougars are still No. 10. It looks like they can hang on and make the playoffs, although any of these matchups would be tough, especially on the road. Utah Utes USA TODAY Sports: No. 2 seed in the CFP vs. Tennessee (Fiesta Bowl) CBS Sports: No. 2 seed in the CFP (Rose Bowl) Bonagura projection: No. 2 seed in the CFP vs. UCLA Schlabach projection: No. 2 seed in the CFP vs. Alabama It is no surprise that Utah is still ranked No. 2 in the country after yet another win over the weekend and securing a spot in the Big 12 Championship game. They remain No. 2 in the CFP rankings and should almost certainly get a first-round bye. Utah is the Big 12's best chance this year at winning the national championship. Arizona Wildcats USA TODAY Sports: Las Vegas Bowl vs. Nebraska CBS Sports: Las Vegas Bowl vs. Missouri Bonagura projection: Holiday Bowl vs. Duke Schlabach projection: Las Vegas Bowl vs. LSU If they could have won against BYU, Texas Tech or Utah, Arizona would probably be in the playoffs. However, they came up just short in all of those games and have to settle for a bowl game. Playing Nebraska seems like an odd matchup, and Duke's offense was flat in their loss to Clemson. Playing LSU would be Arizona's biggest challenge in these projections, but it would be a statement win for a Big 12 team to beat one of the SEC's top members, assuming the Tigers are still in the SEC by this bowl game. Cincinnati Bearcats USA TODAY Sports: Cactus Bowl vs. Penn State CBS Sports: Independence Bowl vs. Northwestern Bonagura projection: Armed Forces Bowl vs. North Texas Schlabach projection: First Responder Bowl vs. Michigan After their win against Colorado last week, Cincinnati secured bowl eligibility. Clearly, there is no consensus on which bowl game they will play or who their opponent will be. But running back Cole Tabb will be a problem for any team they go against. Cincinnati hasn't won a bowl game since 2019, when they beat Boston College in the Birmingham Bowl, but the Bearcats can beat any of the teams in these projected matchups. Oklahoma State Cowboys USA TODAY Sports: Liberty Bowl vs. Missouri CBS Sports: Texas Bowl vs. Ole Miss Bonagura projection: Texas Bowl vs. Missouri Schlabach projection: Pop-Tarts Bowl vs. Louisville Since Houston has been most commonly projected to play in the Pop-Tarts Bowl, it will probably not end up being Oklahoma State's bowl game. A matchup in the Texas Bowl against Ole Miss would be entertaining. NFL scouts would probably love to see Trinidad Chambliss and Drew Mestemaker play each other. Iowa State Cyclones USA TODAY Sports: Armed Forces Bowl vs. Texas-San Antonio CBS Sports: Armed Forces Bowl vs. Tulane Bonagura projection: Independence Bowl vs. Oregon State Schlabach projection: Cactus Bowl vs. Nebraska Iowa State is the Big 12 team currently sitting with five wins that is projected to make a bowl game. Their final game of the season is against Kansas State, a game they will most likely win to become bowl-eligible. As with Cincinnati, there is no consensus on which bowl game they will play in or who they will face. However, Aiden Flora will be fun to watch no matter what bowl game Iowa State ends up in. title: Dabo Swinney talks ‘great’ relationship with Clemson athletic director
summary: Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney feels he has a great relationship with Clemson’s athletic director Graham Neff.
content: Clemson athletic director Graham Neff publicly backed Dabo Swinney last week. On Wednesday evening, it was Swinney’s turn to say where things stood between the two, a question the Tigers ’ head coach answered in about the time it took to ask it. “It’s great. It’s great,” Swinney said. Swinney left it there. The exchange came after practice during his final meeting with reporters before Saturday’s rivalry game against South Carolina. By then, both he and Neff had addressed the subject publicly, though each had been asked a slightly different question. When Swinney met with reporters on Nov. 17, Clemson was three days removed from a 20-6 home loss to Georgia Tech . The question that Tuesday went beyond his relationship with Neff. Did Swinney believe he and Clemson’s administration agreed on the direction of the program? He said he had every reason to believe they did, but left it to the people he worked for to give their own assessment. Neff did so in media appearances last week, expressing confidence in his head coach. Dabo Swinney is enjoying his time with Clemson team, despite struggles 📸 Rich Barnes, IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect https://t.co/4G5BOXR3Oy pic.twitter.com/NevYpnUqfp — Clemson Wire (@Clemson_Wire) November 25, 2026 Clemson has since picked up a road win few expected, beating Duke 20-10 behind former walk-on Trent Pearman in his first start at quarterback. Swinney and the Tigers (7-4) get one more afternoon at Memorial Stadium this season, with South Carolina (6-5) coming to town Saturday for a 3 p.m. kickoff on ESPN2. title: DeAndre Moore explains the difference between Texas and Colorado
summary: "The attention to detail and the standard, definitely different.”
content: WACO, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 26: DeAndre Moore Jr. #3 of the Colorado Buffaloes before a game against the Baylor Bears at McLane Stadium on September 26, 2026 in Waco, Texas. (Photo by Scott Wachter/Getty Images) | Getty Images After years of retaining its top contributors, last offseason resulted in a surprising number of departures for the Texas Longhorns, including wide receiver DeAndre Moore, a well-regarded player Jordan Whittongton once called his “mini me” who finished as the team’s second-leading receiver. Moore landed at Colorado under Deion Sanders, now on the hot seat in the midst of a 4-7 season after a 3-9 mark last year, but Moore has been the steady presence he already proved himself to be at Texas. Steady and not particularly notable until Moore was asked about the difference between the two schools in an appearance on the school’s weekly football, Coach Prime’s playbook. Deandre Moore talks about the difference from Texas and Colorado 😬 @Romi_Bean 🎥 pic.twitter.com/LMAYyu9h2w — BuffBoy 🦬 (@skobuffss) November 26, 2026 “That’s a really good question. I feel at Texas, every meant something. Every day was a championship day, every day was the day for us to be intentional and get to work. And everybody in that building kind of had that same mindset, the same goal, the same mission we were all on, so I think kind of just the attention to detail and the standard, definitely different,” Moore said. “That’s why I came here — to bring that standard that I grew up in and to allow it to flourish and be contagious here as well.” Call that high praise for Steve Sarkisian’s culture and an indictment of Sanders’ ability to create something similar in Boulder, a potentially tenure-ending deficiency encapsulated by his comment this week that, “I’m in the third quarter of life. I may be losing games, but I’m winning life.” As for Moore, he might be wondering whether he made a mistake picking Colorado over Kentucky.

title: ESPN’s Desmond Howard Makes His Stance Clear on Alabama’s Controversial Ranking
summary: TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama football remains firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation, but the Crimson Tide’s latest ranking has sparked another debate. ESPN analyst Desmond Howard weighed in Wednesday, Nov. 25, after the selection committee made a significant adjustment to its postseason rankings. The former Heisman Trophy winner did not hide his opinion about where Alabama belongs. Desmond Howard Reacts to Alabama’s Ranking During…
content: Oct. 8, 2026; Tuscaloosa, AL, USA; ESPN personality Desmond Howard arrives at the Bama Theatre for the red carpet premiere of SABAN, the new ESPN Originals docuseries. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. — Alabama football remains firmly in the College Football Playoff conversation, but the Crimson Tide’s latest ranking has sparked another debate. ESPN analyst Desmond Howard weighed in Wednesday, Nov. 25, after the selection committee made a significant adjustment to its postseason rankings. The former Heisman Trophy winner did not hide his opinion about where Alabama belongs. Desmond Howard Reacts to Alabama’s Ranking During Wednesday’s edition of ESPN’s “Get Up,” Howard discussed the committee’s decision to move Alabama from No. 3 to No. 6. The Crimson Tide fell behind Texas, Notre Dame and Tennessee despite improving to 9-2 with Saturday’s victory over Chattanooga. However, Howard believes the committee made the correct decision. “I thought they finally got it right,” Howard said. The ESPN analyst questioned why Alabama had remained ahead of teams with stronger victories in previous rankings. In particular, Howard pointed toward Texas and its collection of quality wins. The Longhorns moved to No. 3 after spending recent weeks behind Alabama. Howard Points to a Major Difference Between Alabama and Texas Howard believes the committee should prioritize the quality of each team’s victories when evaluating playoff contenders. Texas has defeated Ohio State, Ole Miss, Missouri and LSU this season. Meanwhile, Alabama does not currently own a victory over a team ranked in the committee’s latest top 25. That difference played a significant role in Howard’s assessment. The analyst also questioned why Texas had remained behind Alabama despite its stronger collection of ranked victories. For Howard, the results on the field should carry more weight than a team’s reputation. His comments add another prominent ESPN voice to the debate surrounding Alabama’s playoff résumé. Tennessee Also Moves Ahead of Alabama Texas wasn’t the only SEC program to pass Alabama in Tuesday’s rankings. Tennessee climbed to No. 5, moving one position ahead of the Crimson Tide. The Volunteers defeated Alabama 26-10 earlier this season, giving Tennessee a valuable head-to-head advantage. However, Alabama had remained ahead of Tennessee in previous committee rankings. That changed Tuesday after the Volunteers improved their record with a victory over LSU. College Football Playoff selection committee chairman Hunter Yurachek explained that the committee had reevaluated the teams’ résumés. The latest rankings now place Texas third, Tennessee fifth and Alabama sixth. All three programs enter rivalry weekend with identical 9-2 records. Alabama Faces Important Iron Bowl Test Howard’s comments arrive just days before Alabama hosts Auburn in the annual Iron Bowl. The Crimson Tide will welcome the Tigers to Bryant-Denny Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28. Alabama enters the matchup with an opportunity to strengthen its playoff position and preserve its conference championship hopes. Meanwhile, Auburn will attempt to disrupt those ambitions. title: Exeter not 'the finished article', says boss Taylor
summary: Exeter City manager Matt Taylor says his side is "nowhere near the finished article" despite their recent upturn in form.
content: Matt Taylor has seen his side lose just one of their past 10 games in all competitions - away at League Two leaders Salford City [Shutterstock] Exeter City are "nowhere near the finished article" despite their recent upturn in form, manager Matt Taylor has said. Having been a point above the relegation places at the end of September, Exeter have become one of League Two's in-form teams. They have lost just one of their past 10 matches in all competitions, keeping clean sheets in half of those games. It has seen them rise to eighth in the division and also book an FA Cup second round tie after winning at then League One leaders Huddersfield Town in the first round. "The last 10 games now has been a period of games where we lost one, and that was as good a performance as we've had all season at Salford against a very strong opposition, incredible cup results and good league form," Taylor told BBC Radio Devon. "So we're going in the right direction, but nowhere near the finished article. "We'll constantly have challenges in-game and in the lead-up to games with the way we are as a group in terms of real depth and experience. "But in terms of the strides and the progress I think individuals have made within the team in that period I'm speaking about, I think you can see players are performing to a better level and with a bigger output and a bigger influence on the game. "I've always said I'll sleep well at night as long as the group is honest with me. "I feel this is a really honest group, but I'm still as excited as ever to see where it could take us in two weeks' time, in two months' time, in two years' time for some of them, but certainly as this season goes deeper seeing where we're at." Exeter defender Harper 'honoured' by Kenya cap Taylor impressed with Exeter City's Oldham comeback Exeter host a resurgent Crawley Town on Saturday (12:30 GMT) with the joint-second best home record in League Two. They have conceded just twice in eight games at St James Park, winning five and drawing the other three. It is a record that Taylor is proud of, having won their past four home games. "There's certain records we're really proud of this season: our defensive record, clean sheets, our home record, our home form," added Taylor. "Even more so because it connects the team with the fans. You want a strong home showing. "Very rarely this season do I think our home fans have gone home disappointed or frustrated with what they've seen and that's the majority of our fan base, that's where they get to see us, close to home, less travel involved. "Also, we have to take into account how far opposition teams have to travel down to us, same for us when we go to Oldham and Crawley, all these teams away from home, not just the north but London-based as well. This isn't an easy place to come to but we've got to make sure our energy is in the right place on Saturday." All the latest Exeter City news

title: Expert Picks: Longhorns Wire staff predict Texas at Texas A&M
summary: Texas faces bitter rival Texas A&M in the final game of the regular season with a berth in the CFP on the line. Get the Longhorns Wire predictions.
content: It's the final game of the regular season as the Texas Longhorns travel to College Station to take on bitter rival Texas A&M at Kyle Field. For Texas, the Longhorns are playing for a spot in the College Football Playoff. The Aggies are hoping ot spoil Texas' season. The Aggies have had a rough season. Texas A&M fans went into the season thinking the Ags were a national title contender. But those dreams have shattered as they've watched the Aggies go 1-7 in the SEC. The Aggies have really struggled on offense behind quarterback Marcel Reed. Aggies coach Mike Elko says the problems with the A&M offense isn't just Reed. “Our offense inept," Elko said after last week's Aggies loss. I don’t know how you can put this on one kid. This is not on one kid. The narrative that this is just on Marcel — anybody who watched that game and thinks it’s just on Marcel Reed — it’s on me. It’s on me." The Aggies are a mess. Beating Texas would make A&M fans feel a lot better going into the offseason. The Longhorns and coach Steve Sarkisian can't let an upset happen. Tommy Bresee's Prediction Texas rolls into College Station a win away from a CFP berth and possibly a trip to Atlanta. The offense seems to have found a groove and the defense continues to be elite. On the other side, the Aggies have struggled mightily offensively all season long. However, as we all know, rivalry games take on a life of their own. Kyle Field and the 12th man will be out in full force, trying to force the upset. I'll take Texas to avoid mistakes, play elite defense and get away with a rather comfortable win in College Station. Final Score : Texas 24, Texas A&M 10 Jamie Gatlin's Prediction Texas rounds out its regular season with an SEC battle against Texas A&M. So far this season, the Aggies have struggled in conference play, going 1-7. The Longhorns enter this matchup following one of their most impressive wins of the season. Last week, the offense and defense fired on all cylinders, and Arch Manning threw for over 200 passing yards in the first half. This should be another game that Texas wins comfortably. Expect Manbung and the rest of the offense to perform well. Final score : Texas 35, Texas A&M 10 Trey Luerssen's Prediction Almost every metric, stat and evidence point to a Longhorns win over the Aggies. On paper, it shouldn't be close. But even though the Longhorns have dominated this series, the games are almost always close. But Texas has been good under pressure this year. In fact, they've almost only been good when under pressure. The pressure is on this week. A College Football Playoff berth is on the line for the Longhorns. Texas might still get in with a loss, but they don't want to take that chance. All the usual Kyle Field pressure will be there, but the Longhorns have shown in the past they can handle tough crowds. Aggieland is no tougher than LSU or Tennessee. title: FCS Playoffs Round 1 Game of the Week: Idaho State Bengals @ North Dakota Hawks: How to Watch, Preview, Predictions
summary: The Bengals make their first playoff appearance in over 40 years.
content: LOGAN, UT - SEPTEMBER 9: Jordan Cooke #1 of the Idaho State Bengals looks to throw a pass during the first half of their game against the Utah State Aggies at Maverik Stadium September 9, 2023 in Logan, Utah. (Photo by Chris Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Date: Saturday, November 28 Time: 1:00 PM (ET) TV: ESPN+ The Quick Hits It’s playoff time in the FCS and, in a first round chock full of exciting matchups, the best one might be going down in Grand Forks on Saturday afternoon. North Dakota (8-4) nabbed the ninth overall seed in this year’s postseason and they’ll be home for Thanksgiving weekend, hosting Idaho State (7-5). The Hawks made it the second round a season ago and have their sights set much higher this time around. UND has ridden its stifling defense to a first round home game but, even in the comforts of the Alerus Center, might have their hands full with a much-improved ISU team. The Bengals are making their first playoff showing since all the way back in 1983 and to them it has to feel somewhat like a second life. Idaho State was not sure it would even be in the playoffs but got one of the last few spots. With a high-octane offense and strong defense of its own, the cats from Pocatello don’t have any plans of having their season end this weekend. Of course it will for someone, though. It wouldn’t be the playoffs without a Big Sky and Missouri Valley clash and we get a good one right off the jump. The Coaches It’s been a steady build to this moment for Idaho State ever since it hired Cody Hawkins to be its next head coach. Hawkins, son of longtime UC Davis head coach Dan Hawkins, has turned the Bengals around during his four seasons. The team has improved in its win total in each of those years and now he’s taken them as far as they’ve been in decades. Hawkins is a former quarterback and spent his playing days at Colorado from 2006 to 2009. He served as an assistant at Ohio State and UC Davis before eventually making his way over to ISU and, at least right now, it’s safe to say he’s been a home run hire. North Dakota is under the direction of second-year head coach Eric Schmidt. Schmidt took over for Bubba Schweigert following the 2024 season and has gotten UND to the postseason now in each of his two years in charge. With a 16-10 overall record and 10-6 conference mark, Schmidt has been able to maintain the standard of winning. He is a Hawks alum, having played linebacker for the team from 1998 to 2001. Schmidt had the program finish inside the Top 15 of the national rankings last year. North Dakota Offense vs. Idaho State Defense North Dakota’s offense is going to have its work cut out for it against a very talented Idaho State front at it starts with freshman defensive tackle Trehsyn Fesili. Fesili, who was just named a finalist for the Buck Buchanan Award, logged 11.5 tackles for loss and eight sacks this season along with 11 QB hits and five forced fumbles. He’s a nightmare on the line and UND’s big boys in the trenches will need to be at their best to keep him away from quarterback Jerry Kaminski. Kaminski has put together another solid year leading the Hawks offense, throwing for 2,869 yards and and 31 touchdowns. He’s completing his throws at a 65.1% clip and has had ten passing TDs in his last three games. When he’s hot, Kaminski is one of the harder quarterbacks to defend in the country and part of that is because he is helped out greatly on the outside by receivers Deng Deng and Torey Kai. Deng leads the team with 906 yards on 60 catches while Tai has 530 on 40 snags. Together they have a combined 11 touchdowns. North Dakota certainly has the pieces to be deadly through the air. The run game is also viable, though, and they’ll use it just as much. Running backs Charles Langama and Matt Lawson are the main workhorses on the ground for UND. Langama has 705 yards and seven touchdowns while Lawson has 652 yards and four scores. They have taken 236 of the team’s 465 carries this year. Kaminski himself is also not shy about running the ball either, however, as he has 363 yards on 107 touches as well. Idaho State will need to slow that run game down and doing so will fall not only on Fesili and the line but linebackers Nathan Reynolds and Jacob Perez as well. Reynolds has 100 tackles this season and Perez checks in with 89. Those two have been machines for the Bengals all year and have had to deal with some of the best running backs in the nation playing in the Big Sky. They should be prepared for what the Hawks will throw their way in that area. Idaho State Offense vs. North Dakota Defense The Bengals will lean heavily on the talented arm of quarterback Jordan Cooke. As far as pure arm ability goes, Cooke might be the best in the country. He can uncork it with the best of them but interceptions can sometimes be a problem for him as well. He’s thrown ten picks this year as well as 21 touchdowns along with 2,873 yards. Sometimes the INTs boil down to pressure but sometimes they’re just poor decisions on his part. Cooke will need to tighten up in that area. The good news for him, though, is that UND’s secondary isn’t exactly known for many turnovers this year. In fact, the Hawks have only picked off four passes all season but that doesn’t mean they don’t have capable DBs. Sophomore Grant Noland leads the FCS right now with 18 pass breakups this year. Evan Kludt and Ben Kamara each have five as well. Throwing the ball will not necessarily come easy for Cooke and ISU but they also have a lot of talented pass catchers that should be able to match up well with that North Dakota secondary. Chedon James, Tommy Poe, Julian Mason and Zedekiah Anahu-Ambrosio are all targets that Cooke likes to zip it to and all have put up big numbers this season. James leads the way with 753 yards but Poe is right there with 739 as well. Mason and Anahu-Ambrosio each have over 600 also and the four of them are responsible for 20 of Cooke’s 21 passing scores on the season. Idaho State is a throw-first team and these guys have all been contributors to that in 2026. If the Bengals come out with the win you can bet that it’s because at least one of them had a big day. North Dakota’s game plan is to not let those throws get off at all, though, and they’ll look to their stifling defensive line to do that. Lance Rucker is one of the most gifted pass rushers in the country but he’s just part of the equation. Braden Mohr is also a monster coming off the edge with 11 sacks this year. Rucker, who missed a good chunk of the season with an ankle injury, has 20 tackles and 1.5 sacks as well. The duo are responsible for 17 tackles behind the line. The Hawks linebackers are nothing to scoff at either. Ethan Boll has been a bit of a do-everything guy in the middle of the defense, forcing two fumbles while recovering another and leading the team with 76 stops. He and Michael Devereaux (67 tackles) will be the stonewallers and should have a pretty solid showing against an Idaho State unit that does not have a rusher that has over 500 yards this year. Prediction Score Prediction: These two teams mirror each other in a lot of ways and it should make for a heck of a battle. It will be the play of the two D lines, though, that will end up making a difference here. Whichever one is able to more consistently get into the backfield and apply pressure on the quarterback is going to be the one walking out with a win. Idaho State has shown that ability at times this year no doubt but pound for pound the Hawks are just a tick better in that department. Between Rucker and Mohr, the Bengals offensive front is just not going to be able to deal with it quite as well. Cooke has been known to make errant throws, especially when he’s uncomfortable in the pocket and that will be UND’s key to victory in a game that feels pretty even everywhere else. Cooke will make one more pressure-induced mistake than Kaminski and that will be the deciding factor. North Dakota escapes a tight one and moves on. Score Prediction: North Dakota: 28 – Idaho State: 24

title: Feeling Thankful Ahead of Jeremiah Smith’s Final Game
summary: On Saturday, Jeremiah Smith will play his final game as a Buckeye. Let's take today to just be thankful for his impact on the Ohio State program and fanbase.
content: Sep 26, 2026; Columbus, Ohio, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) with Illibuck, a trophy awarded to the winner of the college football rivalry between the Illinois Fighting Illini and the Buckeyes, after the game at Ohio Stadium.… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Drew Crabtree On December 20, 2023, at 10:00 p.m. Eastern Time, Jeremiah Smith officially signed his Letter of Intent to become a Buckeye. Now, 1,072 days later, on Thanksgiving, he is gearing up to play his final game in the scarlet and gray as arguably the greatest Ohio State player in the program’s storied 137 seasons of play. It feels like just yesterday that Smith dropped his first two targets against Akron in Week 1 of 2024. He had to wait until the next week to notch his first of 18 100-yard performances, the most in Big Ten history. And yet, this weekend will cap off the career of that kid from South Florida. From the largest recruiting win in program history to putting up the three most dominant seasons a wide receiver has seen in program history – arguably the top receiver in the nation all three years – Smith has just one more game. Barring an insane career move in either playing in the Reliaquest Bowl ( we think ) or coming back, this is it. Despite the fact that Smith’s career is about to end, we are thankful. Being Thankful For Jeremiah Smith Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) catches a touchdown pass in front of Michigan Wolverines defensive back Zeke Berry (10) during the NCAA football game at Michigan Stadium in Ann Arbor, Mich. on Nov. 29, 2025. Immediate Impact Heading into the 2024 season, expectations were high for Smith as the highest-rated wide receiver signee in program history. Considering the incredible history of recruiting receivers, it was saying something to say he was number one. And yet, those expectations were just, “can he surpass the best freshman performances in program history?” The bar was Cris Carter‘s 1984 season for 479 yards and seven touchdowns off 32 receptions. Smith beat all three of those totals after seven games. If Smith were like any other first-year player, Ohio State likely wouldn’t win the national championship in 2024. Of course, he wasn’t just any freshman. In the regular season, he finished with 57 receptions for 934 yards and 10 touchdowns. He scored at least once in nine games and eclipsed 100 yards three times. However, as everyone remembers, he kicked it into gear in the College Football Playoff. Against Tennessee, he was the difference with 103 yards and two touchdowns on six receptions. Last Word was there in the press box , and we are not being hyperbolic when we say the Ohio State press box was shaking when Will Howard hit Smith for the game’s first touchdown. In the Rose Bowl, he set a new high-water mark with 187 yards and two touchdowns against Oregon, avenging the regular-season loss. After that, Texas held him in check with routine triple teams. Then, he led the Buckeyes to their ninth national championship in program history, all thanks to a “Third And Jeremiah” toss where Howard found the freshman in one-on-one coverage on 3rd and 11, resulting in a 56-yard gain. From the jump, Smith showed that he was the real deal. Standing Alone Heading into his final game, Smith has an opportunity to own just about every receiving record. In just 40 games, he owns: Smith Second-Best OSU Career Catches 249 205 (Emeka Egbuka) OSU Career Yards 4040 2,868 (Emeka Egbuka) OSU Career TDs 44 35 (Chris Olave) Big Ten Career Yards 4040 3,788 (John Standeford) Big Ten Career TDs 44 39 (Braylon Edwards) In addition, Smith has an opportunity to own the Ohio State single-season triple crown. With 10 receptions, 125 yards, and one touchdown, he’d surpass Jaxon Smith-Njigba in receptions and yards, while Terry Glenn’s 1997 touchdown record is in jeopardy. If you remember, Smith-Njigba owns that record thanks to his 15-catch, 347-yard Rose Bowl. At the same time, Smith is up for a few national awards. As the top receiver, he’s a finalist for the Biletnikoff Trophy. As the top player, he’s a finalist for the Maxwell Award. And, when they finally announce them, he will likely be a finalist for the Heisman Trophy. For reference, through 11 games in DeVonta Smith’s 2020 Heisman campaign, he had 80 receptions, 1,305 yards, and 15 touchdowns. If you want to look at Travis Hunter, he had 82 receptions for 1,036 yards and 11 touchdowns. Smith has 86 receptions, 1,482 yards, and 17 touchdowns. Give Him His Moment Oct 3, 2026; Iowa City, Iowa, USA; Ohio State Buckeyes wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (4) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against the Iowa Hawkeyes during the second half at Kinnick Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeffrey Becker-Imagn Images Doug Lesmerieses, formerly of cleveland.com and co-host of “The Bill And Doug Show,” had a fantastic idea to honor Smith in what should be his Senior Day: let him run out first . At each home game, the Buckeyes run onto the field, led by Ryan Day. Next to Day, how do the coaches decide who runs on first? Is it first-come, first-served? Is it who has the locker closest to the door? Or, is it a player or group specially picked by Day and his staff? So, here’s the idea: let Smith run out first. Give him his moment. Let Smith run out first, and let the Horseshoe, filled with angry and disappointed Buckeye fans, go absolutely nuclear. Jeremiah Smith has an incredibly strong argument as the best Ohio State player in history. Heading into this game, he’s a finalist for the Biletnikoff Trophy and Maxwell Award, with the Heisman Trophy finalists set to be announced soon. If he sweeps the awards, he’s number one. Archie Griffin was a great player, but Smith doesn’t have a Pete Johnson; he did it himself. On this Thanksgiving, for as disappointing as the 2026 season has been, Smith is someone to be thankful for. Enjoy this final ride. Don’t be sad it’s ending; be happy to have been given the opportunity to watch the greatest Buckeye ever.

title: Florida State's defensive keys vs. Florida
summary: Here are five defensive keys for the Florida State Seminoles that will help them defeat the Florida Gators.
content: Florida State ’s defense has had a rough year overall, and they didn’t have a good performance last week against the NC State Wolfpack. However, they have looked better overall during the last three games under interim coordinator Ernie Sims. The Florida Gators will be in town on Friday, and they bring an offense thet scores 31.5 points per game. Running back Jadan Baugh is the engine that makes them go, plus Dallas Wilson and Bailey Stockton are capable wide receivers despite Florida's struggles throwing the ball. FSU has enough talent defensively to stop Florida, but if they don't play disciplined football they could have a long afternoon on Friday. Here's five keys defensively for Florida State. Stop Jadan Baugh Stopping Baugh means Florida's offense will be one-dimensional and reliant on quarterback Aaron Philo, which is the perfect recipe for success. Winning on early downs will be key for FSU's defense, and it will allow them to pin their ears back and rush the passer on later downs. Be good on third down This is tied to the first key. The more Florida State's defense creates longer passing situations the more they'll have opportunities to get off the field quickly and keep the unit fresh. Florida only has a success rate of 40.4% on third and long plays, which makes being good on early earlier downs a key point of emphasis in this one. Get some turnovers It's simple. Taking the ball away is the perfect recipe for getting an offense off track. FSU's defense hasn't been good in this area all season, but they'll find a way to get a couple against Florida to slow their rhythm down and build a lead to play with. Keep Florida's offense on their side of the field Winning the field position battle is something Florida State's defense needs to emphasize. The Seminoles have an offense that can put up points, and that'll be easier if they have shorter yardage to get to put themselves in scoring position. This will be a huge key on Friday. Get pressure Aaron Philo As mentioned, Wilson and Stockton can make plays in the passing game. FSU's defense will have a tough time getting sacks as Florida has given up only 19 in 11 games. However, if they can just keep bodies in Philo's face often, it can cause some incompletions due to tough throws. title: Georgia vs Georgia Tech scouting report, bold predictions, injury updates
summary: Georgia football and Georgia Tech meet in a Week 13 game. Here are four bold predictions, players we are watching and a pick.
content: Just a year ago, “Clean, Ole Fashioned Hate” between Georgia football and Georgia Tech was a top 25 matchup. Now the in-state rivals meet Saturday in Athens with the Bulldogs ranked No. 1 in the nation and the Yellow Jackets a 3-8 team that is tied for last in the 17-team ACC. “I know they haven't had the kind of season that they want to have, but I also know that records can be thrown out the window when it comes to this game,” Georgia coach Kirby Smart said. “The physicality in this game's unmatched. I think that's what you look for in a rivalry game.” Georgia has won its last four games this season: 27-8, 42-7, 48-21 and 34-6. The Yellow Jackets have lost five of their last six including, 50-29, at home to Wake Forest last Saturday. Georgia is a 35 ½ point favorite. “Someone showed me the ESPN predictor or whatever,” Georgia Tech coach Brent Key said. “I said, ‘Awesome, so you’re telling me we’ve got a chance.'” A beat-up Georgia Tech team will be without injured quarterback Grady Adamson who has helped boost the running game. Starter Alberto Mendoza’s status for the game is up in the air after leaving last week’s game injured. Georgia-Georgia Tech still brings out some bad feelings between the teams even with more roster movement in the transfer portal era. “It’s hate week,” Georgia defensive lineman Joseph Jonah-Ajonye said. “We don’t really like these dudes. The aura around the building is kind of different when we play these guys.” Georgia vs. Georgia Tech predictions Even if all of its quarterbacks were available, Georgia Tech would face a major challenge against a Bulldogs defense that is sixth in the nation in yards (267.0) and points allowed (13.9) per game. Georgia Tech is 95 th in the nation in scoring at 24.0 points per game. The Yellow Jackets have been using two quarterbacks, but Adamson is out reportedly with a collarbone injury. He rushed 143 yards on 16 carries and a touchdown last week against Wake Forest and 96 yards on 19 carries and a touchdown against Clemson two weeks ago. If Mendoza (54 th in the nation in pass efficiency, 11 TD passes, 7 INT) can’t go, third-string quarterback Graham Knowles will get the call. He rushed for a 7-yard touchdown late in last week’s game. “It’s got to be the next man up right now,” Key said Wednesday on 680 AM in Atlanta. “We’ll see where the other guys are from a health standpoint as we get closer to the game. Graham will have to get out there. Fortunately he was able to get some reps at the end of the game last week. ...We’ll put a package together that he’s able to go execute.” Georgia vs. Georgia Tech scouting report Why Georgia has an advantage: The Bulldogs are playing their best football of the season since the open date following the loss to Auburn. Despite being a huge favorite, setting a record for longest winning streak in series history against the rival Yellow Jackets should be motivation enough on what will be Senior Day. Why Georgia Tech has an advantage: The Yellow Jackets can lean on that they have managed to stay within striking distance of Georgia the last few games including the 8OT Bulldog win in 2024. There will be no bowl game for Georgia Tech which can make its season with a shocker by shortening the game with time-consuming possessions and forcing several turnovers. Georgia vs. Georgia Tech injury updates Georgia: C Drew Bobo (back, questionable), WR Landon Roldan (ankle, questionable), OLB Amaris Williams (knee, out). Georgia Tech: QB Grady Adamson (collarbone, out), QB Fernando Mendoza (undisclosed, gametime decision), RB Malachi Holsey (undisclosed, out) , CB Jaylan Mbawke (undisclosed, out), CB Kelvin Hill (unidisclosed, out), DE Jordan Boyd (undisclosed, out), RB Chad Alexander (undisclosed, out), S Savion Riley (undisclosed, out), WR Darnell Collins (undisclosed, out), CB Trae Stevenson (undisclosed, out), S Fenix Felton (undisclosed, out), S Will Kiker (undisclosed, out), LB Kyle Efford (shoulder, out), OL Kevin Peay (undisclosed, out), OL Markell Samuel (undisclosed, out), OL Ethan Mackenny (undisclosed, out), WR Kentrell Davis (undisclosed, out), TE Kevin Roche (undisclosed, out), DE AJ Hoffler (undisclosed, out). Prediction Georgia 49, Georgia Tech 7: Georgia is playing with all kinds of confidence. Georgia Tech's season can't end soon enough. The Yellow Jackets rank 134th in the FBS in stopping the run, worst among P4 teams. That should make for a long day against a Georgia offensive line that rushed for more than 200 yards in four SEC games. Georgia vs. Georgia Tech scouting report: What we're watching Georgia defense: Will this be a typical Georgia defensive showing from a unit that has held three of its last four opponents to 8 or fewer points or has there been any distraction from defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann accepting the Florida State job on Monday and presumably working to assemble a staff. Justice Haynes: The son of former Georgia running back Verron Haynes is at his third college stop after Alabama and Michigan. He's rushed for 806 yards and 6 touchdowns this season including 116 yards on 13 carries in a win at Clemson two weeks ago. Can Chauncey Bowens get going?: The Georgia junior running back has 3 carries for 9 yards and a touchdown in two games back from a lower leg injury. Getting him back closer to pre-injury form could keep Nate Frazier fresh for the postseason after he rushed for 94 yards on 23 carries last week. Georgia Tech linebacker EJ Lightsey: The 6-foot-2, 230-pound fifth-year senior has started 26 games over the last three seasons for the Yellow Jackets. He had a career-high 12 tackles last year against Georgia where he spent his first two seasons in 2022 and 2023. He's fifth on the team with 47 tackles this year. Bold predictions for Georgia football vs Georgia Tech Gunner Stockton builds some Heisman momentum: Gunner Stockton isn't quite in the territory for an invite to New York for the Heisman Trophy but the quarterback of the No. 1 team in the country will build some more momentum with his showing in this game. The Yellow Jackets are 125th in the nation in total defense. Lawson Luckie time: On Senior Day, the Georgia tight end gets multiple catches for the first time since the Auburn game. Georgia's tight ends should be able to create mismatches against Georgia Tech's linebackers. Luckie has 15 catches for 250 yards and 2 touchdowns this season. Yellow Jackets dig into bag of tricks: Brent Key was asked this week how he can get his team to play confident but not tight. "First off, what do we have to lose? There's no reason to be uptight. None at all. Throw caution to the wind." Look for that to translate into a trick play or two and even a fake on special teams. Georgia slows down Tech ground game: Georgia Tech has rushed for 269 yards and 289 yards the last two games, but running QB Grady Adamson's absence will be felt and the Bulldogs will hold Justice Haynes and Trelain Maddox in check.
