title: Why Florida State will beat Florida
summary: These are five reasons why the Florida State Seminoles will get a win over the Florida Gators to become bowl eligible.
content: Friday afternoon inside Doak Campbell Stadium is the scene for the Florida State Seminoles to battle the Florida Gators . If FSU wants to play in a bowl for the first time in three years, this is a must-win as they come into the contest with a 5-6 record. It's been a roller-coaster year for the Seminoles, from alternating wins and losses to firing the head coach. However, getting a victory against Florida would be a great way to end the regular season, and it would also serve as great motivation heading into a bowl game. This isn't about competing for the national title like so many times before, but anytime Florida State and Florida get together, it's a big deal. Here's five reasons why the Seminoles will pull out a win against the Gators. FSU's wide receivers will have a big day Florida's defense is 92nd in the nation against the pass. This sets the stage for Micahi Danzy, Jayvan Boggs, and Jasen Lopez to feast for four quarters. As long as Florida State's offensive line holds up in pass protection, these three should make plays and help the Seminoles put up points. Florida State's defense will neutralize running back Jadan Baugh This is the key for the Seminoles defensively. The Gators are not a great passing team, so the more they keep Baugh in check the more they'll put Florida in difficult passing situations on later downs. This will lead to short drives and an advantage in field position for FSU, which will set them up for easier scoring opportunities. Rick Stockstill will coach his best game Stockstill got brought back down to earth against the NC State Wolfpack last week after winning his first two games as interim head coach. He'll shake that off and put together a great game plan to pull out a tough win versus Florida State’s biggest rival. Anything can happen in a rivalry game Florida may look like the slightly better team on paper, but records and talent can be thrown out of the window when they step on the same field with FSU. The sight of each uniform brings out something in eachother, but on Friday, Florida State will be the team that rises to the occasion. Making a bowl will fuel FSU As mentioned earlier, Florida State hasn't played in a bowl since 2023. They have an opportunity to make that happen on Friday, and with Florida being the opponent, and them being at home, this will be a huge boost of motivation to end their streak of not making bowl games. It will likely be close, but FSU will get it done. Follow us @FSUWire on X and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Florida State news, notes, and opinions . You can also follow Matthew on X @StarConscience. This article originally appeared on FSU Wire: Why Florida State will beat Florida

title: Barcelona teenage starlet making major strides at La Masia after slow adaptation
summary: As reported by SPORT, Ajay Tavares is beginning to slowly show his true potential at La Masia following his arrival at Barcelona during the winter transfer window earlier this year.Signed from Norwich...
content: Barcelona teenage starlet making major strides at La Masia after slow adaptation As reported by SPORT , Ajay Tavares is beginning to slowly show his true potential at La Masia following his arrival at Barcelona during the winter transfer window earlier this year. Signed from Norwich City in England, the 16-year-old starlet had a quiet start, due to injuries and adaptation difficulties, but is now starting to show by Barça moved to rope him in. A bet for the future Tavares was one of the more unusual bets made by Barcelona’s scouting department during the previous winter. The recruitment drive was led by Joao Amaral and directly overseen by sporting director Deco, with the club also bringing in other promising youngsters such as Juwensley Onstein and Patricio Pacifico. It is a part of the wider strategy by the Catalans to sign talented young prospects before their market value shoots up and develop them at La Masia . Ajay Tavares joined Barcelona from Norwich. (Picture credit: Instagram/@ajay_tavares) Tavares arrived after having turned 16 years old, with his Portuguese passport playing an important factor in making the move possible. However, he endured a rather slow start to life in Catalonia. After all, moving to Barcelona meant adapting to a completely different environment, both personally and football-wise. It was his first experience of living away from home, while La Masia’s approach to the game presented a new challenge for the teenager. An unfortunate wrist injury in April then brought his season to a premature end , hampering his development. Turning things around Tavares was already close to recovering towards the end of the season, and he then used the summer to prepare himself for a fresh start. The teenager worked individually with personal trainers, and the effort appears to have paid off. The winger, known for his explosive change of pace, has become more influential and looks increasingly comfortable with Barcelona’s style of play. His understanding of the team’s movements and his confidence in possession have both improved. Playing for the Juvenil A side, he has impressed heavily in the league, while he also has a goal and two assists in two UEFA Youth League appearances this season. Those within the club describe Tavares as calm, humble and a good teammate, with a strong willingness to learn. There is also a feeling that he is now much more relaxed than he was when he first arrived in Barcelona. The academy staff are pleased with his progress, although they are aware that there is still plenty of development ahead.

title: Everton Under 21s fall short as another cruel deflection goes against them
summary: A narrow victory for Tranmere but Matos shows mettle
content: Melvin Matos and a few others shone against League Two opponents | Getty Images On a cold but dry November Tuesday night, Dave Hughes’ young Everton Under 21 side made the 6 mile trip under the River Mersey and through Birkenhead to take on League Two opponents and their second-nearest neighbours, Tranmere Rovers. The contest was part of the appetisingly-named Jersey Mike’s Subs trophy, otherwise known as the Football League Trophy. Everton sat bottom of the 4 team group going into the game so pride was the main prize. The side named by Hughes featured 16 year old Jonathan Nsangou up as the lone striker, ably supported by the attacking midfield trio of Omari Benjamin, Malik Olayiwola and Braiden Graham. That came as a bit of a surprise to all concerned as the easy assumption was that the more experienced 20 year old Benjamin would lead the line. We didn’t get the chance to see any of David Moyes’ fringe players getting a chance or former Blue and non-contract player Tom Davies either. Shame as the extra experience would have made a difference on the night, not to mention giving a few players some actual competitive minutes!!!! The side was as below: View Link In an entertaining and well-contested match, the young Blues certainly held their own in the opening exchanges with the defence looking more solid than I have seen them this season. The midfield duo of Harvey Foster and Melvin Matos ahead of them also had a good blend of control under pressure and a bit of bite. First real chance fell the Blues’ way after 19 minutes. 18 year old John Dodds, looking the part alongside the powerful captain Will Tamen, intercepted near the half way line and played the ball forward to Olayiwola who saw Graham point where he wanted it. He delivered it perfectly and the young Northern Irishman did what he does best, score in a one v one with the ‘keeper. 1-0 and looking good! Six minutes later and those two players combined again as a neat flick by Olayiwola at the edge of the penalty area allowed Graham to cut inside and he saw his goal-bound drive deflected for a corner. The next chance came as Olayiwola was crowded out near the centre circle by two Rovers players and a smart pass through to Kamara. He got behind Tamen and beat ‘keeper Fraser Barnsley and the despairing tackle from young Dodds. To be honest, at first sight I thought the player was definitely offside but there were few Toffes protests and, of course, no VAR, 1-1. See their goal below. 🔥 A well-taken first Rovers goal from David Kamara. Match highlights: https://t.co/5slsk6nLnB #TRFC #SWA pic.twitter.com/BnuQzAfZIU — Tranmere Rovers FC (@TranmereRovers) November 25, 2026 Immediately before half-time , Matos, hemmed in near the left touchline, swivelled and got himself free and lashed a left-footed volley across goal from an acute angle, glancing the crossbar and causing panic for the home goalkeeper. This (below) is a still of the action immediately before the audacious shot. View Link Shortly after the second half started, Dodds went down for the 2nd time in the match and had to give way, hopefully as a precaution, with Luis Gardner replacing him alongside Tamen. Almost immediately, the irrepressible Matos tumbled in the penalty area under a challenge and it looked a fair shout but wasn’t given. As Toffees’ current luck would have it, just 3 minutes after we could have been ahead again, we were behind and, you guessed it, a 16-yard shot by Veevers was deflected over Barnsley by Tamen who had thrown his body in the way of the shot, 1-2. As the game flowed end to end, Barnsley made a smart near post save then Olayiwola set up Matos on the edge of the area and his shot left the crossbar shaking for several seconds afterwards. After 77 minutes, familiar face, former Blue and lifelong Evertonian Lewis Warrington came on against his old team-mates to try to shore things up. Everton pressed with Shea Pita feeding fellow sub George Finney for a goal-bound shot and yet again, Matos who volleyed straight at the goalkeeper in the 90+1 minute. So it ended in a 1-2 defeat but the Blues gave a really good account of themselves, so who stood out? It won’t surprise you to hear me say Melvin Matos who was excellent on the night, a cross between N’Golo Kante and Gana Gueye. There’s a fearlessness about him, he has strength, tackles anything and everything, has pace, a bit of trickery and an eye for a shot. His energy alone should have him fast-tracked for senior development in my humble opinion. Besides Matos, Malik Olayiwola was really good with his energy and trickery, Harvey Foster with his elegant movement and passing range, Dodds and Tamen were solid and left-back Josh Van Schoor was back to his very best. Nsangou had a quiet game, did nothing wrong but there were only glimpses of his undoubted talent. Maybe centre-forward for him is too tough an ask at this stage, he needed to be on the ball more, not competing in the air with six-foot defenders. Graham took his goal well and a few other good pieces but again one of his quieter games. Next up for the Under 21s is a home Premier League 2 game with Leeds United on Monday November 30th. Meanwhile the U18s face arch-enemies Liverpool on Saturday November 28th, 24 hours before the first team derby on Sunday.

title: Rangers Legend Tips Big-Name Manager for Celtic Job
summary: The Rangers legend has tipped the big-name manager to be interested in the Celtic job.
content: It does feel like the managerial situation has settled down a bit at Celtic over the past few weeks, even though there are still serious question marks over the long-term future of Martin O'Neill. Ideally, one would like to see O'Neill at least finish the season at Celtic. But beyond that, it is hard to see him continuing as manager of the club. Of course, that means that sooner or later, Celtic will need to find themselves a new manager, and hopefully, a long-term one. Quite a few names have been bouncing around in the media as potential solutions to the club's current needs. Could a former Celtic player be the solution? Ally McCoist tips Premier League manager for Celtic job Celtic do have a habit of hiring those with a past with the club. Neil Lennon, Brendan Rodgers and O'Neill all fall under that category. David Moyes is someone whose past with the club dates farther back than any of those three though. It was in 1980 that he broke through the ranks at Celtic as a player. Now, could a return be on the cards as a manager? Rangers legend, Ally McCoist, seems to believe that such a move could be a possibility. As reported by Glasgow World , he said on talkSPORT: “I think the Celtic job would be of interest to him (than Scotland), having played there. I genuinely don’t know what is going on in David’s head, but I would think that job might appeal to him more than the Scotland job. "You could argue that the Scotland job would be the one that everyone wants, being a Scotsman, but he could look around and look at the squad at this time and I’m not sure it would be a massive encouragement to him. He is definitely more hands on, he would struggle to fill his day, David.” Celtic Make Final Decision on January Transfer Move Celtic have already made a final decision amid rumours of a January transfer move. Would David Moyes be the right manager for Celtic? Moyes is one of the managers who has been linked heavily with the Celtic job in recent times. And someone of his experience and calibre would be a welcome addition. Moyes is someone who has a habit of overdelivering with what is presented to him. Right now, he has Everton sitting 9th in the Premier League. Before his arrival, the club had spent several years barely avoiding relegation, often taking it down to the wire. Before that, Moyes had delivered Conference League success at West Ham United and gotten them European football more than once. Since the Scotsman's departure, the Hammers have been relegated to the Championship. Moyes was fantastic during his first stint at Everton as well, a run that lasted over a decade and earned him the chance to be the successor to Sir Alex Ferguson at Manchester United. Obviously, that did not work out. But having seen a long list of high-profile managers fail after him at Manchester United, it is quite clear that the problems were much deeper than what Moyes was capable of. At the end of the day, if Celtic were able to bring in Moyes, it would have the potential to be an excellent appointment, given he is backed by the board.

title: A Thanksgiving thank you from your local sportswriter | Richards
summary: The stories are great. The people behind them are better. A Thanksgiving thank you to the Lenawee County sports community.
content: It always seems like a great idea. “Alright, everybody, let’s go around the dinner table and each share what we’re thankful for.” On the surface, it’s a lighthearted icebreaker that brings family and friends together to commemorate the start of the holiday season. In practice, it’s a ruthless mind game that feeds on the social anxieties lying beneath our cheerful exteriors. “Family,” the first person says, a layup. The next in line follows suit with another gimme, “Friends.” By this point, the wholesome answers have come to an end, and the jokes start rolling in. “This big ol’ turkey,” the third person chimes in, prompting a chuckle from the other participants in the annual ritual. When it reaches the fourth person, a nervous response follows: “All of this yummy food,” they say. At this point, family, friends and food are off the table. The big three have already been swooped up and we’re only through four people. Obviously, there’s no repeating. It’s the unspoken rule that everyone knows. I’m next. Of course there’s plenty to be thankful for, but at a moment like this nothing comes to mind. All I can hear is a single question racing through my head like static on a dead television channel — “What am I thankful for?” Fortunately, this year, I already know my answer. Three months ago, I started my job as the sports editor for The Daily Telegram in Adrian. It's been a whirlwind of a fall, and while I've spent plenty of time writing stories, compiling stats and emailing coaches, I haven't been able to properly acknowledge the people who have made the last three months possible. So, this Thanksgiving, I'd like to take a moment to do so on behalf of all local sportswriters. To athletic directors: Thank you for putting up with our copious amounts of emails. Keeping tabs on one sport is difficult enough, but overseeing numerous programs and hundreds of student-athletes makes you invaluable resources for writers and equally important figures in your respective schools. To coaches: Thank you for carving time out of your busy schedules to talk to us. For many of you, coaching comes on top of a full-time job as a teacher. Despite the demands on your time, you remain committed role models to your athletes, teaching lessons that extend well beyond the playing field. To student-athletes: Thank you for sharing your stories. Whether it's a quick postgame interview or a longer conversation about your journey, you give us stories worth telling. Your willingness to let us share a small piece of your lives with the community is something writers don't take for granted. And lastly, to our readers: Thank you for supporting local sports coverage. In a world increasingly dominated by algorithms, artificial intelligence and fleeting social media posts, you still make time for stories on those in your community. Whether through the mail slot or on your screens, you welcome our work into your homes. And in doing so, you remind us that there's still value in telling human stories. Best, Your local sportswriter Contact sports editor Quinn Richards at QRichards@usatodayco.com. Follow him on X, formerly known as Twitter, at @Quinn_Richa. title: 102 matches, over five-thousand runs: Former India U19 World Cup winner quits first-class cricket at 32
summary: Aparajith announced his retirement through an Instagram post on Wednesday, revealing that his last first-class match was played on January 24, 2026.
content: Former India Under-19 World Cup-winning all-rounder Baba Aparajith has retired from first-class cricket at the age of 32, ending a career in which he represented Tamil Nadu, Kerala and India A, besides being part of Chennai Super Kings and Rising Pune Supergiant in the IPL. Aparajith announced his retirement through an Instagram post on Wednesday, revealing that his last first-class match was played on January 24, 2026. "I played my last first-class cricket match on January 24, 2026, officially bringing my first-class cricketing career to a close. Looking back, it has been an incredible journey filled with experiences, challenges, lessons, friendships and memories that I will cherish for a lifetime. It has been an absolute privilege to represent Tamil Nadu, India Under-19, India A, Kerala, Chennai Super Kings, Rising Pune Supergiant, TNPL franchises and my club teams, and to be part of the many teams and dressing rooms that have shaped my journey. Each experience has played a significant role in shaping me, both as a cricketer and as a person," he wrote on Instagram. Aparajith was part of India's Under-19 World Cup-winning team in 2012. He scored 171 runs and took five wickets during the tournament, finishing as India's fourth-highest run-scorer. He also won the Man-of-the-Match award in the quarter-final against Pakistan Under-19s and the semi-final against New Zealand Under-19s. The batting all-rounder made his Ranji Trophy debut for Tamil Nadu at the age of 17 before representing India Under-19s at the World Cup in Australia in 2012. He later broke into the India A setup in 2015 but could not establish himself consistently at that level. Aparajith was part of Chennai Super Kings for three consecutive seasons between 2013 and 2015 but never made his IPL debut for the franchise. He was also part of Rising Pune Supergiant in the league. However, he was largely viewed as an accumulator, with his overall strike rate of 108 across 63 T20 matches reflecting his batting approach. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Aparajith (@aparajithbaba) He played 102 first-class matches, most of them for Tamil Nadu, scoring 12 centuries and 27 half-centuries. He also contributed with his off-spin and had the opportunity to captain Tamil Nadu. Aparajith was part of three title-winning Tamil Nadu squads, winning the Vijay Hazare Trophy in 2017-18 and the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy in 2020-21 and 2021-22. He also represented Kerala during the final phase of his domestic career. Aparajith, whose twin brother Baba Indrajith is also a cricketer, thanked the cricketing bodies, his family, coaches, teammates and support staff for their backing throughout his career. "My sincere gratitude to the BCCI, TNCA and KCA for the opportunities and support throughout my career. A special mention to my wife, my parents, my brother, my extended family, and all my friends and well-wishers for their unconditional support, sacrifices and belief in me throughout this journey. I’m grateful to my coaches, support staff and teammates who have been an integral part of this journey. My connection with the game will remain as strong as ever. I look forward to carrying forward the knowledge, experiences and lessons gathered over the years, continuing to learn, contribute and hopefully make a meaningful impact on the game in the years ahead," he added.

title: 'Baz pulled me aside': Tom Banton recalls emotional moment he was named England captain
summary: In an unexpected twist, Tom Banton has been appointed captain for England's fifth T20I against Australia in Canberra. Upon hearing the news from head coach Brendon McCullum, Banton showed heartfelt emotion. With Harry Brook away for Test preparations against South Africa and Will Jacks sidelined due to injury, Banton seizes this pivotal moment in his evolving international career.
content: Tom Banton is set to achieve a major milestone in his international career after being named England captain for the fifth and final T20I against Australia. The 27-year-old described the moment as emotional, admitting that he initially struggled to react when head coach Brendon McCullum informed him about the decision. Banton will lead England in the series finale in Canberra on December 2 'I was pretty emotional' Speaking about the moment, Banton revealed that McCullum, popularly known as 'Baz', pulled him aside at the airport and shared the news. "I was pretty emotional, a little bit, when I got told. It's a great honour and a great privilege, and something I'm really looking forward to," Banton said. He further explained how McCullum personally informed him about the responsibility. "Baz did it actually in the airport. He just pulled me aside and told me. I didn't really know how to react, to be honest. But yeah, to be told you'll be captaining your country in any format is a real privilege," he added. Why will Tom Banton captain England against Australia? England's captaincy change comes after two major developments during their ongoing Australia tour. Regular skipper Harry Brook is set to leave Australia after the fourth T20I to prepare for England's upcoming Test commitments against South Africa. Will Jacks was expected to take over the captaincy for the final match but suffered a broken hand during the opening T20I against Australia, ruling him out of the remainder of the white-ball tour. With both players unavailable, Banton has been handed the responsibility of leading England in the series finale. Tom Banton's journey to England captaincy Banton made his international debut for England in 2019 and has since featured across formats. The Somerset batter has experienced ups and downs in his international career but has continued to work his way back into the national setup. The captaincy opportunity marks a significant moment for the 27-year-old, who will now get the chance to lead his country on the international stage.

title: Gloucs CEO 'confident' Bristol rebrand will work
summary: Gloucestershire are "really confident" their rebrand to Bristol Lions for the T20 Blast will work, says outgoing CEO Neil Priscott.
content: Gloucestershire are "really confident" their rebrand to Bristol Lions for the T20 Blast will work, says outgoing chief executive Neil Priscott. The club will change their name from 2027 for the competition, incorporating the city where their home stadium is based. Priscott, who will be stepping down in December after seven-and a-half-years at the county, said the change was made to help make them more sustainable for the future. "I'm really confident that this will work and that the population of Bristol and our region will get behind this," Priscott told BBC Radio Gloucestershire. "This is entirely about ensuring that Gloucestershire County Cricket Club is relevant and can compete with the best in the 18 professional county system. It starts and stops with that." Gloucestershire were formed in 1870 and have played at the County Ground, now named the Seat Unique Stadium, in the Ashley Down area of Bristol for more than a century. They have won the T20 title once, in 2024, but have never won a County Championship title. Since 2022 they have played in Division Two of the Championship and finished bottom in two of the past four seasons, including this summer. The club will continue to play under the Gloucestershire name for both the County Championship and One-Day Cup. Gloucestershire renamed Bristol Lions for T20 Blast Northants begin T20 Blast defence at Hampshire Priscott said T20 Blast ticket sales accounted for 60% of the club's domestic ticket revenue, despite the competition only equating to six games being played at home during a season. He added that research had shown them fans of Gloucestershire in the north of county did not engage with the club in Bristol enough to help drive their ticket sales, while people in Bristol did not relate to the Gloucestershire name. "This year we tried loads of different initiatives to try to migrate that audience in the north of the county to Bristol and we had very little success in doing that," Priscott said. "Most of what we are doing is the product of research and data led decisions and we are just simply not able to bring our supporters from the north of the county to Bristol in the numbers that will help us drive revenues." He added: "There's just a lack of cut-through in Bristol when you say you're Gloucestershire. "Generally speaking, youngsters, young families don't make the connection between Gloucestershire and elite cricket in Bristol." There has been a significant amount of criticism to the rebrand on social media, with one fan stating he would be cancelling his membership at Gloucestershire in light of it. Priscott accepted that there would be some who would not be happy with the change but that the club had also spoken to those in favour and that fans on both sides of the argument ultimately wanted "what's best for the club". "We understood that there would be some that would either take some time in getting used to the idea and some that would be opponents to the idea," he said. "It's our belief that the only way we can truly have a seat at the top eight at the table of English cricket is by doing something bold and different in T20."

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi made 204 from 53 deliveries with seven fours and 28 sixes, and the seven-wicket win lifted India A's net run rate to 3.523, comfortably the highest in the tournament. title: Pant joins New Zealand club match under false name
summary: India wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant unexpectedly joins a club game in Christchurch before the second Test against New Zealand and scores 54 off 21 balls.
content: Rishabh Pant scored 128 in the first Test at Wellington [Getty Images] India wicketkeeper Rishabh Pant made a surprise appearance for a club team in Christchurch under the false name 'Stan Stan'. Pant, 29, played for the Open House Swingers against The Chosen Ones and smashed 54 from 21 balls in a 16-run win. His appearance came a day before India's second Test against New Zealand, which begins at the Hagley Oval at 22:00 GMT on Thursday. Open House player Mohammad Safi told the New Zealand Herald that he had seen Pant on an electric bike in the city and approached him, saying that his team were a player short. Safi also said that Pant was not immediately recognised by many on either side, and he turned up in a purple tracksuit and had to borrow kit. New Zealand captain Tom Latham said Pant's appearance was "brilliant" and showed his "real character", while India bowling coach and former South Africa quick Morne Morkel said he "nearly fell off my chair" when he saw the footage that circulated on social media. The first Test in Wellington ended in a high-scoring draw, where Pant scored 128 in India's only innings of 720-9. Pant is regarded as one of the world's most entertaining cricketers, and has scored 3,853 runs in his 53 Tests at an average just shy of 45. Of those to have scored more than 2,000 Test runs for India, only Virender Sehwag and Kapil Dev have a better strike-rate than Pant's 74.43. title: 'Sooryavanshi will score 500 in a Test': Kevin Pietersen's jaw-dropping prediction for India's 15-year-old sensation
summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, at just 15, has already made waves in List A cricket with a historic double century, scoring an impressive 204 runs against the UAE. Although he faced challenges with only 40 runs against Sri Lanka A, former England captain Kevin Pietersen has high hopes for Sooryavanshi's Test future, as he continues to impress with his skills across various international tournaments this year.
content: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's extraordinary rise continues to attract attention from some of cricket's biggest names, with former England captain Kevin Pietersen making a staggering prediction about the 15-year-old batting sensation after his record-shattering double century in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026. Pietersen took to social media on Thursday to make a bold forecast about the teenager's future in the longest format, suggesting that Sooryavanshi could produce a monumental individual score in Test cricket in the coming years. "Here’s a shout — Vaibhav will score a 500 in a Test Match within the next 5yrs!," Pietersen wrote on X. The prediction comes after Sooryavanshi delivered one of the most extraordinary innings in List A cricket, smashing 204 off just 53 balls against the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in India A's final group-stage match. Although the teenager could not replicate that astonishing performance in Thursday's semifinal against Sri Lanka A, his reputation continues to grow following a year in which he has rewritten several records. — KP24 (@KP24) From 52-ball double century to Pietersen's 500-run prediction Sooryavanshi's innings against the UAE was a record-breaking assault, featuring 28 sixes and seven fours. He reached his century in just 28 deliveries, brought up 150 in 40 balls and completed his double century in only 52 deliveries. The International Cricket Council confirmed that the 15-year-old had registered the fastest century and double century in men's List A cricket. His 200 came almost twice as quickly as the previous record of 103 balls. India A eventually chased down the UAE's 250-run target in just 14.2 overs, finishing at 254/3, with Sooryavanshi contributing more than 80 per cent of the team's total. After the innings, the teenager explained how he adjusted his approach after assessing the conditions. “In the last two matches, I got set but couldn’t convert those starts. So the plan was to go out there and take my time initially. But after facing a ball or two, I felt the bowlers weren’t getting much help from the surface, so I backed my strengths,” he said. “There wasn’t anything specific on my mind. The only thought was that if the wicket was helping the bowlers, I would take my time and play a longer innings. But thankfully, that wasn’t the case. The wicket was good, the ball was coming nicely onto the bat, so I tried to back my game,” he added. Sooryavanshi falls for 40 in semifinal The teenager's remarkable run continued to be a talking point even though he managed only 40 off 27 balls against Sri Lanka A in the semifinal. His innings included four fours and three sixes, and he shared an explosive 80-run opening partnership with Abhishek Sharma in eight overs. Sooryavanshi was eventually dismissed in the eighth over, caught by Lasith Croospulle off Janith Liyanage while attempting to pull a short delivery. The latest exploits add to an extraordinary year for the youngster, who smashed 175 in India's Under-19 World Cup final triumph in February, made a significant impact in the IPL and became the youngest player to represent India in a full international match. With Pietersen now predicting a 500-run Test innings within five years, the spotlight on the teenage prodigy is only getting bigger.

title: Bearman to continue with Haas in 2027
summary: Britain's Oliver Bearman will continue to race for the Haas team in Formula 1 in 2027.
content: In 2025, Oliver Bearman outscored his team-mate Estaban Ocon by three points. This season, he scored three times the points of Ocon before the Frenchman was dropped during the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend [Getty Images] Britain's Oliver Bearman will continue to race for the Haas team in Formula 1 in 2027. The US-based team announced the 21-year-old's new deal on Thursday, at the start of the Qatar Grand Prix weekend. It marks Bearman's third full season with Haas, for whom he first raced for two one-off events in 2024 before becoming a full-time driver in 2025. The announcement ends a protracted negotiation period in which Bearman's management were seeking reassurances about his future from Ferrari. Bearman is a member of the Italian team's driver academy and has ambitions to race for Ferrari in the future. It was not immediately clear what reassurances Bearman had been given about his future by Ferrari. Is Hamilton and Leclerc's Ferrari partnership sustainable? F1 Q&A Camara to continue with Haas for final two races Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said: "Continuing with Ollie into 2027 was a natural decision for us. "We've seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track. "He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward." Bearman added: "It's no secret that I'm delighted to be continuing with Haas into 2027. "This team has played an integral role in my development, and I've felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here. "We've got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I'm excited to lead that work, building on what we've achieved, and striving for even more together – we have unfinished business." Bearman will be partnered at Haas next season with Brazilian Rafael Camara, who is also a member of the Ferrari driver academy. Camara has started racing for Haas at the end of this season, following the team's sacking of Frenchman Esteban Ocon midway through the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend. Bearman's concerns about his future had been rooted in the fact that there might not be a seat available at Ferrari for some considerable time. Charles Leclerc is on a long-term contract there, and while Lewis Hamilton's deal is believed to end after 2027, the seven-time champion is keen to continue in F1 for a number more years. Bearman, who said at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix, that he was "quite disappointed" his new contract had not yet been sorted so late in the season, is believed to have been exploring his options. His management is said to have been asking Ferrari for reassurances about his future, either about the possibility of racing for the main team, or if that is not an option, being allowed to pursue a career at a more competitive team than Haas. title: Charles Leclerc refuses to reveal Ferrari's "rules of engagement" after Lewis Hamilton crash
summary: Charles Leclerc agrees Ferrari contact is "unacceptable" and confirms private talks with Lewis Hamilton before Qatar GP
content: Motorsport photo Charles Leclerc walked into Thursday’s FIA press conference at the Losail International Circuit knowing the spotlight would stay locked on Ferrari ’s garage. Five days after spinning team-mate Lewis Hamilton at the Las Vegas Grand Prix - and absorbing a blunt post-race dressing-down from team principal Fred Vasseur - the Monegasque driver did not attempt to dodge the fallout, even as he shut the door on detailing how Maranello plans to stop it from happening again. "I knew what Fred’s position was, and as a driver I have to accept it," Leclerc said. "We are strong drivers who want to finish ahead of each other. Unfortunately, too many incidents have happened recently." Leclerc’s contrition follows a turbulent final stretch of the 2026 campaign that has repeatedly tested Ferrari’s two-No. 1 philosophy. After earlier friction at Monza and an opening-lap Turn 4 clash in Mexico City - where Leclerc cut the grass while challenging polesitter Hamilton and picked up a five-second penalty as Max Verstappen slipped through to win by 0.799 seconds - Vasseur sat both drivers down in São Paulo to clear the air. That truce lasted barely one race. In Las Vegas, where Leclerc started 10th directly ahead of Hamilton in 11th, a late-race lunge into Turn 7 spun the seven-time champion and landed Leclerc a 10-second penalty, leaving the pair seventh and 10th for a meagre seven-point haul. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Vasseur’s fury was audible before the cars even reached parc fermé; he summoned Leclerc over cooldown-lap radio to see him "before anything else". Speaking to reporters afterwards, the Ferrari boss made clear the exchange was strictly one-way: "No, it was not a discussion – I spoke!" Calling the collision "unacceptable" and "a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors," Vasseur went even further with Sky Italia, warning that the situation between his drivers was "becoming unmanageable" due to "a human misunderstanding between them, not between them and the team". Why Leclerc won’t discuss Ferrari’s “rules of engagement” In Qatar, Leclerc aligned himself squarely with his boss while drawing a clear line between off-track harmony and wheel-to-wheel tension. "The solution? I can't go into detail and talk about the rules of engagement," Leclerc said. "However, I believe there is a very high level of external attention, but the most important thing is to find a solution to avoid problems as much as possible. We are doing it, but I can't talk about it. I took responsibility for Las Vegas, but I agree with Vasseur that contact between two Ferraris is unacceptable. "Lewis and I have already spoken to find a solution, and I believe our relationship off the track is very strong. Then the issue came up again on the track, and that’s where we need to find a solution, but as I said, I don’t want to talk about it or go back over the incident." Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Leclerc’s reluctance to discuss formal guidelines mirrors Vasseur’s own scepticism in Nevada. Asked whether Ferrari finally needed written racing rules on paper, Vasseur pushed back, insisting: "Honestly, it's not a matter of rules... You can't put it on the paper... They just have to act in a professional way." Ahead of Friday practice at Losail, Vasseur struck a calmer, target-driven tone in Ferrari’s official weekend preview. "We head to Qatar determined to respond as a team and deliver the kind of weekend we expect from ourselves," he said, emphasising that the Scuderia’s goal is to "bring home a solid result with both cars". A 10-point target to calm the noise On the scoreboard, Ferrari actually stands on the brink of wrapping up its main remaining team objective. With Mercedes already crowned Constructors’ champions on 666 points, Ferrari holds second on 517—a 77-point cushion over third-placed Red Bull (440) and 86 ahead of McLaren (431) with 86 points left across Qatar and next week’s Abu Dhabi finale. Scoring just 10 points on Sunday - whether through a single top-five finish or a routine double-points haul - seals P2 for Maranello regardless of what its rivals do. Individually, however, pride remains sharply on the line: Hamilton enters Losail third in the Drivers’ standings on 267 points—just three ahead of George Russell and Lando Norris - while Leclerc sits 17 points back on 250 with two races left to close the gap. With Qatar’s mandatory 27-lap tyre cap turning Sunday into a flat-out strategic sprint, clean execution between Ferrari’s two stars will tell far more than anything said in Thursday’s press room. title: Charles Leclerc urges to find "solution" after several clashes with Lewis Hamilton
summary: The Ferrari duo have tangled several times since the 2026 F1 summer break
content: Motorsport photo Charles Leclerc was left furious by those ‘questioning his integrity and love for Ferrari ’ after yet another clash with Formula 1 team-mate Lewis Hamilton - having urged to find a “solution”. The Ferrari pair have been at loggerheads several times during the second half of the 2026 F1 campaign, clashing at Monza, Zandvoort and Mexico before their latest spat in Las Vegas. Last weekend Leclerc attempted to overtake Hamilton for sixth down the inside of Turn 7, but copped a 10-second penalty for causing a spin - leaving team boss Fred Vasseur furious. The Frenchman said on team radio during the cooldown lap: “Charles, I want to see you at the end of the race, before anything else.” Read Also: Why Ferrari believes written rules won't help manage Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton Now a week later in Qatar, Leclerc has accepted responsibility for the “unacceptable” clash but refuted any theory that he is attempting to establish dominance as Ferrari’s number one driver. “I absolutely have zero clause that says that in my contract,” said Leclerc, who signed a “multi-year” renewal in June. “It's never something that I was interested in and never something that I personally wanted. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari “So no, I don't. I think the only thing that I don't like seeing is people questioning my integrity to the team, my love for the team. I've been in Ferrari since 2019. “I think there's nothing clearer than the love I have for the team and I'll do absolutely everything in order to bring Ferrari back to the top. “Then, of course, mistakes happen along the way and always will. We just have to minimise them and particularly between team-mates. “But yeah, I think it's more the question mark of that that I have seen going around that hurts me more than anything else. “The rest is a lot of noise and it's not the most enjoyable time, but it's part of the game and I have to accept that.” Leclerc then insisted that the relationship between him and the seven-time world champion is still “very good”, claiming much of the talk has been heightened due to the nature of driving for Ferrari. Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari So the team is striving to find a solution with several internal discussions, which started in the aftermath of the Mexico incident amid Hamilton criticising Leclerc’s “do or die” attitude to racing. “At least one more year together, we've got to do the best for the team,” said Leclerc, with Hamilton’s current contract expiring at the end of 2027. “So, I think I've been very much thinking about trying to find a solution together with the team in order to make sure that we maximise the team points and that episodes like last week don't happen again. “That is my main priority. We're just really very much focused on trying to find a solution that works and particularly because I really believe we are in a good momentum. “If next year we are to be in a position of fighting for the championship, it's even more important to find the right solution for both of us to bring Ferrari back to the top.” Leclerc eventually finished 10th in Vegas with Hamilton three spots higher, leaving Ferrari still second in the championship ahead of the final two rounds: Qatar and Abu Dhabi. title: David Croft: Max Verstappen has Fernando Alonso's race intelligence but is faster
summary: David Croft believes Max Verstappen combines the strategic brain of Fernando Alonso with a clear speed advantage
content: Motorsport photo Sky Sports Formula 1 lead commentator David Croft sees Fernando Alonso's smart racing in Max Verstappen , but adds that the four-time champion has more speed. Speaking on Sky Sports' F1 Show podcast after Verstappen's Las Vegas Grand Prix win, Croft was asked to sum up what he had seen from the Red Bull driver. He started by comparing him with the two-time champion who is still racing at 45. Croft said Verstappen already has the quality that has defined Alonso's career, and then some. "Max has got what Fernando Alonso has got, but more pace to go with it," Croft explained. "And that's an ability to strategise and think your way through a race and know exactly what you're doing at all times. But he's actually faster than Fernando Alonso." That ability was on show in the closing laps in Las Vegas, where Croft said Verstappen was happy to run second into the final lap rather than lead it. He felt Mercedes' George Russell had a different plan. "That's why he went for the move on Kimi, because he wanted to then make the move on Max and be out in front. Max wanted to be second. It was almost like a cycling velodrome sprint race," he added. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Croft was in no doubt where that leaves Verstappen, even if he does not always approve of what the Dutchman says or does. "He is just the all-round complete driver at the moment," he said. "And whatever you think about what he says, whatever you think about what he does sometimes on track, there is no doubting he is the current greatest driver on the track. And you're going to have to go some to beat him in equal machinery, which makes next year so fascinating." Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli claimed the drivers' championship title at the Mexican Grand Prix, but Verstappen is fighting for second. The 29-year-old currently sits second with 304 points, with Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in third with 267 points. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

title: Ferrari facing 'very challenging times' - Hamilton
summary: Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari are facing "very, very challenging times" as a result of the series of on-track incidents between himself and team-mate Charles Leclerc.
content: Lewis Hamilton is third in the drivers' championship [Getty Images] Lewis Hamilton says Ferrari are facing "very, very challenging times" as a result of the series of on-track incidents between himself and team-mate Charles Leclerc. The two drivers had talks on Thursday after arriving at the Qatar Grand Prix to discuss the fall-out from their collision in the race in Las Vegas last weekend, which team boss Frederic Vasseur said was "completely unacceptable" . Both said the conclusion of those discussions would "stay internal" but admitted a solution needed to be found. Hamilton said: "I like to think that we're stronger from these difficult... "If everything was just great all the time, I don't think you learn anything when you're winning all the time. You learn really through the hardest times. "These are definitely very, very challenging times for Fred (Vasseur, the team principal) and Charles and I." Is Hamilton and Leclerc's Ferrari partnership sustainable? F1 Q&A Hamilton-Leclerc collision 'completely unacceptable' Leclerc admitted that there was "tension around that we need to dissipate". The incident in Las Vegas was the second in three races between Hamilton and Leclerc . In Mexico City last month, their battle on the first lap led to them handing victory to Red Bull's Max Verstappen in a race that Ferrari should have finished one-two. After that event. Hamilton said Ferrari "had to have some serious talks behind closed doors" and that the team had "big, big problems". They had those talks in the next race in Brazil, brokered by Vasseur, only for there to be two flashpoints in Las Vegas. Hamilton was first penalised 10 seconds for gaining an advantage by cutting the track while racing with McLaren's Lando Norris, in an incident to which Leclerc was also in close proximity. And then Leclerc received a 10-second penalty for pitching Hamilton into a spin. Leclerc said: "We have a very good relationship outside the car with Lewis. "I wouldn't say the atmosphere was good because we are disappointed by the situation we are in. "But we are all grown up and responsible and we have to find a solution and there is also a big willingness to find a solution." Leclerc said the incidents kept happening because "we are two very strong drivers who want to finish one ahead of the other". He added: "I do believe some level of tension is always there in top teams when you have two drivers. "If you look this year there have been more than 10 times we have started side by side. We are always together. So a certain amount of tension is obviously always there, but it doesn't necessarily have to escalate and that is why we need to find a solution and fix that." Hamilton added: "I have no doubts that next year we'll come back working hard together and in a better place. I think we'll quickly get better processes in place so that we can really get a right team." Russell says Verstappen's criticism 'quite amusing' How to follow Qatar Grand Prix on the BBC

title: George Russell says he found Max Verstappen's comments 'amusing'
summary: George Russell said he will refuse to engage in a “war of words” with Max Verstappen and claimed he was left “amused” by the Dutch driver’s personal attack on him after the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Verstappen delivered a brilliant win and then took aim at Russell by describing his British rivals as “below his level”.
content: FILE PHOTO - British Formula One driver George Russell of team Mercedes reacts following qualifying for the Las Vegas Grand Prix at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit. (is associated with: «George Russell says he found Max Verstappen's comments 'amusing'») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa George Russell said he will refuse to engage in a “war of words” with Max Verstappen and claimed he was left “amused” by the Dutch driver’s personal attack on him after the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Verstappen delivered a brilliant win and then took aim at Russell by describing his British rivals as “below his level”. He also said “karma is a bitch” after Russell fell from second to ninth following a collision with the wall in the closing laps. Verstappen’s extraordinary outburst arrived after Russell criticized the four-time world champion for his conduct in practice. Russell’s remarks reignited a long-standing feud between the two drivers. But speaking ahead of this week’s penultimate round in Qatar, Russell said: “I found some of his comments after the race to be quite amusing. “At the end of the day, he drove an incredible race and won it and he can afford to say what he wants. “I stand by what I said after practice, but he was the one that went out and won the race and I didn’t, and I am sure he had a laugh about that. “I want to win, and it is as simple as that. It is not a war of words off track. I don’t think it is important to have a good relationship, or no relationship with anyone. We are all competitors and there is no right or wrong way about the mentality that we all have. “We are different, and you don’t need to agree with one another. I am not looking to be best mates with anybody on the grid. But it is all avoidable and unnecessary and not something I am looking to continue. I don’t want to have poor relationships with people. That is not the type of person I am.” Russell, who started the season as the world championship favourite before his title challenge unravelled, also suggested he is being “hindered” for having an “open” relationship with the media. Will Buxton, a talking head in Netflix’s hit "Drive to Survive" series, claimed this week that Russell asked him off-camera to ask a question about Verstappen at the season-ending race in Abu Dhabi in 2024. Sky Sports’ pit-lane reporter Ted Kravitz recounted a similar story in a book he released last year. Russell called Verstappen a “bully” and said he “lashes out with unnecessary anger and borderline violence” during a round of interviews ahead of the race in Abu Dhabi. On Thursday, Russell continued: “There are lessons to be taken away from these situations, and maybe I am too honest and open with the media, and that has probably hindered me a little bit. Sometimes you forget you are not speaking to just one person but millions of people. “I remember in Abu Dhabi when I was having an open conversation with Ted Kravitz and Will Burton [Buxton] about the whole situation, and I said, ‘Ask me the question on camera, rather than having the conversation off-camera’. “So, they asked me the question on camera, and then went away and spun the truth into something slightly different, so you think, ‘that is a bit cheeky’. “The competition is on track, and that is where I want to battle and fight. I respect Max immensely for his driving talents and everything he has achieved on track.”

title: Haas retains Oliver Bearman for 2027 F1 season after contract standoff
summary: LUSAIL, Qatar (AP) — Oliver Bearman is staying with Haas for the 2027 Formula 1 season, the team said Thursday, after a lengthy delay in confirming his contract left him frustrated. Haas confirmed ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix that Bearman will partner new arrival Rafael Câmara at Haas for next year after consistently outperforming him and former teammate Esteban Ocon this year.
content: LUSAIL, Qatar (AP) — Oliver Bearman is staying with Haas for the 2027 Formula 1 season, the team said Thursday, after a lengthy delay in confirming his contract left him frustrated. Haas confirmed ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix that Bearman will partner new arrival Rafael Câmara at Haas for next year after consistently outperforming him and former teammate Esteban Ocon this year. The announcement fills the last remaining empty seat on the 2027 grid. The wait for a confirmation of the British driver's status dragged on through the season as Haas dealt with the fallout from its relationship with Ocon breaking down . Bearman went public with his frustration at the delays at the Las Vegas Grand Prix last week. “This team has played an integral role in my development, and I’ve felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here," Bearman said in a statement Thursday. "We’ve got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I’m excited to lead that work, building on what we’ve achieved, and striving for even more together — we have unfinished business.” Bearman's situation was complicated because he is also under contract with Ferrari, which brought him into F1 as part of its young driver program. That could eventually lead to a full-time role with Ferrari in the future if Lewis Hamilton or Charles Leclerc leaves. Ferrari is Haas' engine supplier and the two teams have a technical partnership. Câmara is also a Ferrari junior. Bearman, who was 18 at the time, became the third-youngest driver in F1 when he made his debut for Ferrari as a late stand-in at the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in 2024. Then in Formula 2, he also stepped in for Haas later that year before joining the American team on a permanent basis for 2025. Bearman's fourth place at the Mexico City Grand Prix in 2025 matched Haas' best-ever F1 result. ___ See AP’s full auto racing coverage here

title: Haas Sees a Leader in Bearman to Extend His Contract for 2027 F1 Season
summary: Haas has confirmed a deal with Oliver Bearman ahead of the F1 Qatar GP after the Brit shared his disappointment. In Las Vegas, Bearman shared his disappointment due to the delay in signing his contract with Haas. He didn’t name…
content: Haas has confirmed a deal with Oliver Bearman ahead of the F1 Qatar GP after the Brit shared his disappointment. In Las Vegas, Bearman shared his disappointment due to the delay in signing his contract with Haas . He didn’t name anyone for the delay, but felt the situation was inexcusable, considering it is known that he would race for the American F1 team in 2027. The reason for the delay remains unclear, with reports linking it to salary demands and the Ferrari connection. Team boss Ayao Komatsu maintained his stance that Bearman is certain alongside newly signed Rafael Camara. The Brazilian was announced to join Haas for the 2027 F1 season, but the untimely episode involving Esteban Ocon allowed the American team to hand an early debut to Camara. He sacrificed his F2 title chance to race in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. On the eve of the F1 Qatar GP, Haas officially confirmed Bearman to race for the American team in the 2027 season. It will be his third season after joining the team in 2025. After finishing 13th in the drivers’ standings last year, he is currently 13th with two races to go. Oliver Bearman prepares to drive during practice for the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Nov. 19, 2026. Image Credit: Lars Baron/LAT Images Bearman Excited for the Future With Haas “It’s no secret that I’m delighted to be continuing with TGR Haas F1 Team into 2027,” said Bearman in Haas’ announcement on Nov. 26. “This team has played an integral role in my development, and I’ve felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here. “We’ve got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I’m excited to lead that work, building on what we’ve achieved, and striving for even more together – we have unfinished business.” Haas Sees a Leader in Bearman The call has been made Ollie’s extended for 2027 #HaasF1 #F1 | @OllieBearman https://t.co/bs556BAwmQ — TGR Haas F1 Team (@HaasF1Team) November 26, 2026 For Haas, it is a natural decision, as they embark on a journey with two relatively young drivers in the 2027 F1 season, with an average age of 21 years. The team sees Bearman as the leader going forward. “Continuing with Ollie into 2027 was a natural decision for us,” said Komatsu in the same announcement. Haas did not disclose the length of the deal. “We’ve seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track. He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward. TGR Haas F1 Team has one of the most exciting driver pairings on the grid, and I look forward to seeing Ollie flourish further with this incredible team.”

title: Jorge Martin: "My relationship with Aprilia has been difficult, but it's made me a better person and rider"
summary: Martin reflects on his two years at Aprilia as he looks to deliver the constructors title in Valencia
content: Motorsport photo Jorge Martin says he would like to finish the world championship as runner-up in Valencia this weekend, but admits that the most important thing now is to enjoy his final outing with Aprilia and secure the constructors' title for the Noale manufacturer. Martin and Aprilia have had a short but intense two years together - a rollercoaster that comes to an end this weekend at the Valencia Grand Prix. There, the Spaniard will be fighting for second place in the world championship with his team-mate Marco Bezzecchi - while the manufacturer is looking to secure the constructors' title. At the pre-event press conference this Thursday, Martin was seated alongside Pedro Acosta and Fabio Quartararo , the rider he will replace at Yamaha. They were spotted chatting ahead of the press conference, and Martin was asked in his subsequent Spanish interview if they had been discussing what lay in wait at the Japanese marque. "No, no, not at all," said Martin. "I'll see that on Tuesday. Right now, we're focused on this weekend, which we have to finish well. "The goal is to enjoy this final weekend of the year. I think that, right now, the result is the least important thing. I'm as competitive as anyone and I'm going to give it everything to try to win. Obviously, it's better to finish second in the world championship than third, but it won't change anything for me. Above all, the goal is to secure the constructors' title for Aprilia." Aprilia leads Ducati by nine points in the constructors' championship, with only the score of the highest-placed rider from each manufacturer counting towards the total (satellite riders can also score points). And it will go all the way to the wire. Even if an Aprilia grabs all 12 points for winning the Saturday sprint, without any Ducati scoring, thus extending the lead to 21, the title would still be technically be up for grabs on Sunday. "We're going to go for it," continued Martin. "I want to say goodbye to Aprilia in the best possible way, because I think I deserve it after everything I've fought for to get here, and it could be a great moment." Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team Jorge Martin, Aprilia Racing Team It should not be forgotten that Martin has been racing with a fracture to the radius in his right hand since his sprint crash at the Australian GP. "I think I'm arriving in better shape than in Portimao [the last race]. I felt the effects of the effort for a few days after last weekend, and I was generally feeling unwell until yesterday. The effort there was tough. But I feel good and I think this track is not as physically demanding, so I'll be able to cope better." Following a first year plagued by injuries and a contractual dispute, and then a successful second season in 2026, Martin's time with Aprilia has been complicated. "It has been a rollercoaster in general, not just on track. It has been a complicated relationship, but we've managed to turn things around. During the year, I've said many times that we don't need to be friends, we just need to work together to win. In the end, the relationship has turned out to be good and I'm happy. "They've given me all the tools I needed, and they're grateful because they know I've given everything on track, which is ultimately the only thing they can ask of me. "I leave Aprilia a much better person than when I arrived. Stronger and with more confidence in myself, knowing that I'm capable of much more than I could ever have imagined in my life. I think this is a sweet moment and I want to bring it to an end in the best possible way. "I'm not someone who looks in the mirror or talks to himself, but I'm very proud. I'm a very strong, very tough person. A year ago, I didn't believe in myself, I had a lot of doubts, and being able to turn everything into energy to fight for the title again has shown me that I can do it a thousand more times. I'm going to be stronger from now on, I'm going to believe in myself more because I think I'm a better person and a better rider than I was a year ago." title: Leclerc reveals true state of Ferrari atmosphere amid Hamilton tensions
summary: Charles Leclerc has admitted that the atmosphere within Ferrari is not particularly good amid the team's ongoing struggles, although the Monegasque insists his relationship with Lewis Hamilton remains unaffected by their recent on-track clashes. Tensions between the two Ferrari drivers reached new heights at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where contact between the pair resulted in Hamilton spinning and Leclerc receiving a 10-second time penalty.
content: Charles Leclerc has admitted that the atmosphere within Ferrari is not particularly good amid the team's ongoing struggles, although the Monegasque insists his relationship with Lewis Hamilton remains unaffected by their recent on-track clashes. Tensions between the two Ferrari drivers reached new heights at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, where contact between the pair resulted in Hamilton spinning and Leclerc receiving a 10-second time penalty. The incident capped off another disappointing weekend for the Scuderia, with team principal Frederic Vasseur also expressing his frustration over the situation involving his two drivers. Speaking during the FIA press conference ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix, Leclerc offered an insight into the current atmosphere within Ferrari, also addressing his relationship with Hamilton away from the track. “We have a very good relationship outside the car with Lewis,” the Monegasque explained. “I wouldn't say the atmosphere is good because obviously we are all disappointed of the situation we find ourselves in.” With two rounds remaining in what has been a frustrating campaign for Ferrari, Leclerc stressed that both drivers are aware of their responsibilities and remain committed to working together to address the team's shortcomings. “At the same time, we are all grown up and we are the ones that needs to find the solutions in order to make that better. So, there's also a big willingness in trying to find a solution.” Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Leclerc sets the record straight over Ferrari contract rumours Amid growing scrutiny over the relationship between the two Ferrari drivers, Leclerc was also asked about speculation that his contract includes a clause granting him number one driver status over Hamilton. Although the Monegasque is usually reluctant to discuss the details of his contractual arrangements with the Italian outfit, he made an exception to categorically dismiss the suggestion. “I normally never disclose what I have in my contract, but I think this one is an important one to kind of speak about, and I absolutely have zero clause that says that in my contract. It's never something that I was interested in and never something that I personally wanted.” Rather than the speculation surrounding his status within the team, Leclerc admitted that what frustrated him most was the suggestion that his personal interests could come at the expense of Ferrari's. “I think the only thing that I don't like seeing is people questioning my integrity to the team, my love for the team,” he said. “I'll do absolutely everything in order to bring Ferrari back to the top.”

title: Lewis Hamilton on latest Charles Leclerc flashpoint: "We're going to figure it out"
summary: Lewis Hamilton struck a conciliatory tone as he and Ferrari Charles Leclerc try to co-exist as joint-number one drivers after their latest on-track clash in Las Vegas
content: Motorsport photo Ferrari driver Lewis Hamilton says he is confident he and team-mate Charles Leclerc will "figure it out" following their latest on-track skirmish at last week's Las Vegas GP. Two weeks on from a costly on-track incident fighting for the lead in Mexico, which drew the ire of team boss Fred Vasseur, history repeated itself when Leclerc was found responsible for contact with Hamilton on the streets of Las Vegas, robbing both drivers of a solid result. The clash prompted more anger from Vasseur and fresh talks over how he will get his two number one drivers in line. "It's unacceptable," Vasseur fumed after the race. "It's a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors, the same speech as after Mexico. I think we had a clear discussion in Sao Paulo. Today it wasn't professional." Speaking in Doha on Thursday, Leclerc said he was "very much thinking about trying to find a solution together with the team in order to make sure that we maximise the team points and that episodes like last week don't happen again", stopping short of offering any suggestions. Hamilton also struck a conciliatory tone and said he was still convinced he and Leclerc could co-exist in harmony at the team as joint number one drivers. "I do, I do. We're going to figure it out," Hamilton said. "We're team-mates at the end of the day, and I think we always learn from these experiences, whilst maybe it doesn't necessarily look like it. But there will be learnings that we take from this difficult period. "I still believe in everything we're building and working towards in the background. We came here with the goal of taking Ferrari back to the top." He added: "You learn really through the hardest times. And these are definitely very, very challenging times for Fred and Chares and I. But think these are the moments that you really learn and grow closer together through conversation and communicating and having those sit-downs." Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Hamilton revealed he and Leclerc have gone through every corner and every incident between the pair this year, which also included a clash at Monza. But the seven-time world champion also acknowledged every incident is different and dynamic, so it's not as simple as imposing strict racing rules. Instead, he suggested that he and Leclerc have to use their instinct while keeping the team's interests in the back of their minds. "You can never cover everything, because every scenario is different," Hamilton explained. "But you can definitely go through every single race, corner by corner, and discuss things, which Charles and I have. "But there's always going to be something new that you maybe haven't foreseen. You also have to use your instinct, and at the core you always have to have the team. Speaking for myself, when I'm driving, when I'm attacking, whoever it is on track, I'm always thinking: 'OK, how is this going to impact everybody behind me, team-wise?' So, I really do try to be as responsible as I can, and make the best decision when I am attacking, I think." title: Max Verstappen and George Russell rivalry "really cool for the sport", says F1 pundit
summary: Sky Sports pundit Jamie Chadwick believes George Russell provokes Max Verstappen more than any other driver
content: Motorsport photo The Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend reignited the long-running tension between Red Bull and Mercedes drivers, Max Verstappen and George Russell , and it was the talking point of Sky's F1 Show podcast this week. Three-time W Series champion and Sky Sports pundit Jamie Chadwick discussed the reignited rivalry on the podcast, claiming that no other driver gets under Verstappen's skin as much as Russell. The row began in final practice and continued after the race, which Verstappen won while Russell hit the wall trying to pass his Mercedes team-mate. Russell had told Sky Italia that "someone's got to stand up to that guy". Verstappen's response was that Russell was "so far below my level" that it did not bother him. Chadwick said she knows Russell very well and Verstappen less so, and gave her view of what is driving it. "It is just an extreme clash of personalities in a way. I don't think any other driver gets beneath Max's skin as much as George does. We've seen that across multiple races and multiple situations and scenarios between them. Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes "On one side it's really cool for the sport to have this kind of rivalry because it gets everyone talking. It's a little bit of times of old, in a way, of drivers of the past. But equally, there's a bit of frustration." She added: "Max is the best driver of our generation at the moment, proved that in the race. Unbelievable talent. "Does he need to say comments like that? Does he need to let it get under his skin and let himself go to that level? Clearly it relieves something for him, but for me as a sports person seeing it, it's always frustrating, because everything he achieves on track, I just don't feel like he needs to drag himself down to that off track." The pair meet again at this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, which arrives one week before the season finale in Abu Dhabi. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

title: Oliver Bearman locks in Haas F1 seat as 2027 grid officially set
summary: The 2027 Formula 1 grid is set as Haas confirms it has reached an agreement with Oliver Bearman for a third season

title: Ollie Bearman to continue with Haas in 2027
summary: British driver Ollie Bearman’s Formula One future has been confirmed for another season after Haas announced he will be retained for 2027. Bearman’s time with the American team had been placed in some doubt after the 21-year-old said at the previous round in Las Vegas that he was “quite disappointed” an extension had not been agreed.
content: FILE PHOTO - British Formula One driver Oliver Bearman of team Haas speaks to the media at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez, ahead of the Mexican Formula One Grand Prix on Sunday. (is associated with: «Ollie Bearman to continue with Haas in 2027») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa British driver Ollie Bearman’s Formula One future has been confirmed for another season after Haas announced he will be retained for 2027. Bearman’s time with the American team had been placed in some doubt after the 21-year-old said at the previous round in Las Vegas that he was “quite disappointed” an extension had not been agreed. But ahead of the penultimate round of the campaign in Qatar this weekend, Haas announced a one-year deal for Bearman, extending his stay with them into a third season. “It’s no secret that I’m delighted to be continuing with Haas into 2027,” said Bearman. “This team has played an integral role in my development, and I’ve felt a huge amount of belief and support from everyone here. “We’ve got big ambitions to keep pushing forward, and I’m excited to lead that work, building on what we’ve achieved, and striving for even more together – we have unfinished business.” Bearman, who is a member of the Ferrari driver academy and has ambitions to drive for the Italian giants in the future, has scored 23 of Haas’ 31 points so far this season. He will drive alongside Brazilian Rafael Camara next year. “Continuing with Ollie into 2027 was a natural decision for us,” said Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu. “We’ve seen his growth, his commitment, and the quality he brings to the team, both on and off the track. “He has a tremendous work ethic and a strong desire to develop both himself and the team, and there is no better person, in my opinion, to lead this team forward. “Haas has one of the most exciting driver pairings on the grid, and I look forward to seeing Ollie flourish further with this incredible team.”

title: Russell says Verstappen's criticism 'quite amusing'
summary: George Russell says Max Verstappen can "say what he wants" and that he found the Red Bull driver's criticisms of him after the Las Vegas Grand Prix "quite amusing".
content: Russell and Verstappen have had several rows during the past few years [Getty Images] George Russell has said Max Verstappen can "say what he wants" and explained he found the Red Bull driver's criticisms of him after the Las Vegas Grand Prix "quite amusing". Verstappen said Russell was "so far below my level" after winning the race on Saturday. His remarks were a response to Mercedes driver Russell saying "somebody has to stand up to this guy" after an on-track confrontation in practice. Russell said before this weekend's penultimate grand prix of the season in Qatar: "I stand by what I said after practice, but he was the one who went out and won the race and I didn't, and I'm sure he had a bit of a laugh about that and it was reasonably amusing. "He drove an incredible race and won it and he can afford to say what he wants." Russell v Verstappen: F1’s New Rivalry Explodes in Vegas Is Hamilton and Leclerc's Ferrari partnership sustainable? F1 Q&A Asked whether he wanted to pursue reconciliation with Dutchman Verstappen, Russell said: "We're all competitors out there. There's no right or wrong way about the mentality everybody has. "We are all different in many regards and you don't need to agree with one another. I'm not looking to be best mates with anybody on the grid. I am just working and looking and fighting to win. Simple as that." British driver Russell said he had learned lessons from the incident in Vegas, which is the latest in a series of flashpoints between himself and four-time champion Verstappen dating back several years, and he might change how open he is with the media in future. "It's all avoidable at the end of the day," Russell said. "It's all a bit unnecessary. It's not something I am looking to continue. I am not looking to have a poor relationship with people. That's not really the kind of person I am. "There are lessons to be taken from these situations. Maybe I am just too open and honest with the media. I need to remember I'm talking to a camera that is broadcasting to millions of people. That's the biggest takeaway. "It is not a war of words off track. I maybe have been guilty of being too open and honest when I speak with you guys. "I feel like I have a good relationship with the media and I sometimes forget I am not talking to one person - I am talking to millions of people on the television. "That good relationship has probably hindered me a bit and that is life lessons. I respect Max immensely for his driving talent and what he has achieved on track."
