title: Russell Sticks With His Stance But Found Verstappen’s Comments Amusing
summary: George Russell found the comments from Max Verstappen amusing, but he stands by what he said after the FP3 incident. The run-in between Mercedes’ Russell and Red Bull’s Verstappen in the F1 Las Vegas GP started another spat between the…
content: George Russell found the comments from Max Verstappen amusing, but he stands by what he said after the FP3 incident. The run-in between Mercedes ’ Russell and Red Bull’s Verstappen in the F1 Las Vegas GP started another spat between the two drivers. The Brit said somebody needed to stand up to the four-time champion’s antics after qualifying on Friday. After winning the Las Vegas GP on Saturday evening, Verstappen hit back with the “below the level” jibe along with karma. The Dutchman found it fantastic, especially since Russell made a mistake and dropped off from fighting for the F1 race win. In his first response since the statement, Russell said he found the comments amusing while standing on his own from Friday. He credited Verstappen for doing the better job. Russell Found Verstappen’s Comments Amusing Max Verstappen, Kimi Antonelli and George Russell after qualifying for the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Image Credit: Rudy Carezzevoli/Getty Images “I don’t really have much to say, to be honest,” said Russell in the press conference at the Qatar GP. “It was quite amusing, some of the comments after the race. At the end of the day, he drove an incredible race and won it, so he can afford to say whatever he wants, really. “And my side, [it is] moving on.” Asked if he wanted to respond, he said: “No, not really. At the end of the day, I guess I stand by what I said after practice. But he is the one that went out and won the race, and I didn’t, so I am sure he had a bit of a laugh about it; that was reasonably amusing. “From my side, [it is] a new race weekend; just try to focus on the driving and move on.” Russell doesn’t feel there needs to be a relationship among drivers to show respect; it is already there among the majority of the drivers. The Brit felt the back and forth is something that he is not interested in. Back and Forth Avoidable “It’s all avoidable at the end of the day and it’s all a bit unnecessary,” said Russell. “It’s not something I’m looking to continue. I’m not looking to have poor relationships with people. That’s just not really the type of person I am. It’s not a war of words off track. I respect Max immensely for his driving talents and everything he’s achieved on track.” Russell admitted a bit of guilt that he talks a bit too much. “I think I maybe have been guilty of being just too open and honest when I speak with you guys,” he said. “You sometimes forget that you’re not talking to one person. We’re having a conversation now, and you forget actually, I’m not really talking to you, I’m talking to millions of people on the television.” Russell Explains Aggressive Move That Cost Him in Las Vegas Kimi Antonelli and George Russell side by side in the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Nov. 21, 2026. Image Credit: Jiri Krenek/Mercedes-AMG F1 Russell wouldn’t have hustled for the move on teammate Andrea Kimi Antonelli if it was early in the season. At this juncture, he is looking for a highlight a bit more in the risk-taking zone. “I don’t think it is important to have a relationship or no relationship in that regard, to be honest,” he continued. “We are all fighting for race wins. My mistake in Vegas came when I was trying to overtake my teammate. I think the truth is my risk dial was a bit too great at the moment because I am just kind of going in for these big results and get some highlights on the board towards the end of the season. “If it was Race 1 of the season, no way I would have gone for that move two laps remaining, but with two races to go in the season, I kind of wanted to go for it. But I think the majority of us respect one another out there, and we are part of good battles out there, and even the race with Max until then was good and fair. “It was very strategic; it is difficult. I don’t really want to overtake in the last corner and lose the Overtake Mode, but we were so fast down the straight and slow everywhere else; it was challenging to know what the right approach was to try and win that race.”

title: The unexpected riding shift that took Marc Marquez to a 10th world title
summary: Clockwise circuits used to be Marquez's weak point. But things flipped as he closed in on his latest title...
content: Motorsport photo Upon bursting into MotoGP in 2013, Marc Marquez showed a unique ability in left-hand corners. This made him practically untouchable at anti-clockwise venues such as Austin, where he took his first victory in only his second grand prix as a premier-class rider. That day, he also became the youngest winner in history, at 20 years and 63 days. The win in his debut year was only the first of the six consecutive victories he strung together in Texas, where he has seven in total. That's a tally surpassed only by his eight at Aragon or the nine he has accumulated at the Sachsenring, his favourite track of all. What these tracks have in common is that they are all anti-clockwise. In the decade he competed in Honda HRC colours , Marquez took 29 victories on anti-clockwise circuits, a success rate of 69%. The percentage drops to less than half on tracks that run clockwise (29.3%). The arm injury he suffered in 2020, which put his career in jeopardy, further accentuated the influence of that left side on his riding. This was demonstrated in the 2021 German and United States grands prix, where he won despite the severe physical limitation he was carrying. In 2024, after leaving Honda to ride the Gresini Racing Ducati , his first victory came at Aragon, one of his anti-clockwise strongholds. In 2025, racing with the official Ducati team, Marquez crushed his rivals and was crowned for a seventh time in the premier class. In that season, he won on all types of tracks - until he crashed in Indonesia, where he once again injured his right shoulder. Changes to the routine After an initial operation just days after the crash at Mandalika, Marquez began the 2026 season without the energy or strength that had carried him to his ninth world title. That forced him to go under the knife again, this time following the French GP in May. But surgery wasn't enough. The shoulder injury and the process of becoming competitive again led him to reinvent himself. The man from Cervera has made changes to his recovery and energy-management routines during race weekends. Marc Márquez, Ducati Team Marc Márquez, Ducati Team Before every race, he now drops to the ground to do five push-ups next to his bike. He says this activates the area most affected by all the injuries he has accumulated. Also, for some time now, he has limited off-track events as much as he can and conserved his energy in sprint race celebrations. On the bike, this Marquez is also a different animal. "This year, Marc has been a little less aggressive because he doesn't have the strength he used to have to do all the laps he did in practice," explains Marco Rigamonti, Marc's engineer, in a conversation with Motorsport.com. "He has also tried to set up the bike for a less physical riding style, which allows him to compete at this level without suffering an energy crisis," the Italian adds. Adapting the riding style Tempering his intensity has resulted in a rider who is more precise when the time comes to attack the corners. That has allowed him, data in hand, to match rivals who, in the past, took right-handers faster than him. "It has been more an adaptation than a rehabilitation. I ride in a different way, but I am still able to go fast," the Ducati rider explained at the recent Malaysian GP. "It's curious, but the data shows that, when I compare myself with the others, I am worse in left-hand corners than in right-handers," he continued. The remarks carried particular weight at Sepang, given he had scored 34 of the 37 points on offer at a venue where he had not won since 2018. And a track with half as many left-hand corners (five) as right-handers (10). "The data confirms it: I don't know the reason, but in left-hand corners I don't have the same control I had before, while in the right-handers, I am now better," he confirmed, referring to recent rounds. When asked to pinpoint the trigger for that metamorphosis in his riding, the multiple champion fully agrees with Rigamonti: "I can't be as explosive as before. If I wanted to fight for this world championship, I had to be calmer and more calculating, less impulsive. In the second half of the season I managed to control my instincts, something that was always my weak point," admits the world champion. title: Blake Corum is the Perfect Fantasy Football Sell-High Candidate Following Week 12 Career Night
summary: Rams running back Blake Corum had a career game in Week 12, rushing for 184 yards on 32 attempts, making him a prime sell-high candidate.
content: Nov 25, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; MJ Acosta-Ruiz interviews Los Angeles Rams running back Blake Corum (24) after the game between the Rams and the Green Bay Packers at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A variety of fantasy football leagues are entering the final week, when they can make a trade. The deadline is upon us, and it's a tool for title-winning aspirations. The savviest minds can spot an overvalue, flip it for an undervalue, and profit. After analyzing a bunch of data points, I identified Blake Corum as the prime sell-high candidate. Why? Let's dive in. The Sell-High Case of Blake Corum Blake Corum celebrated his 26th birthday with the best game of his NFL career against Green Bay. 32 CAR, 184 RUSH YDS, 1 TD, 2 REC, 21 REC YDS. With a rushing attack like this, the Rams have everything they need to make a Super Bowl run. https://t.co/ihXa9lX4LH pic.twitter.com/LF8VibPU0E - Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) November 26, 2026 Corum is mostly being valued as a mid-tier RB2 in fantasy football. However, we can capitalize on knee-jerk reactions to his Wednesday night stunner. The night before Thanksgiving, Corum went lethal on the Packers. The Michigan Wolverine product left Kyren Williams in the dust as he ran the ball 32 times for 184 yards and 1 touchdown. He had 103 yards after contact with four rushing attempts of at least 10 yards. Corum has now had more rushing attempts than Williams in back-to-back games. I do see a world where Corum stays the RB1, and Williams becomes the third-down back. But we are in a window where hype can turn into a profit. Many fantasy managers will see that Corum is on a premier NFL offense, is running rampant as their starter, and ranks top-10 at his position. A neutral, predictive process will not agree with that ranking. Hence FantasyPros' Rest of Season Ranking of RB20 for Corum. I personally ranked Corum RB25 this week, albeit with high upside, but this one game will not warrant a 10+ spot jump. It's not that simple. Not to mention, the Rams face a brick wall in the coming games. In the next two games, Corum will have to face the Chiefs and the 49ers. They rank 4th and 3rd in EPA per Rush Allowed, respectively. To compare, Corum has recently faced the following teams, paired with their current EPA per Rush Allowed ranking (1st = Most Difficult): Packers: 17th Cardinals: 15th Commanders: 28th Chargers: 18th Raiders: 30th A normalization is in store. The way I see it, Corum is still nothing more than a mid-tier RB2. Thus, he can be sold high. The best buy-low running backs of mine feature the following names: Omarion Hampton: Averaging nearly 20 touches per game recently. Upcoming easy games against the Patriots, Raiders, and Dolphins. Chase Brown: Riskier, but averaging over five receptions per game on one of the NFL's best offenses. Shallow depth chart; low threat to his role. title: Brandon Aiyuk Bolsters Fantasy Football Stock, Signs With Commanders
summary: Former San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk signed with the Washington Commanders, elevating his fantasy football outlook for 2026.
content: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk warms up before the game against the Arizona Cardinals | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Brandon Aiyuk's fantasy football value has been rejuvenated, finding a new home in the NFL after being released by the San Francisco 49ers . He's set to take the field for the first time since the 2024 season, after suffering a catastrophic ACL and MCL tear that left him sidelined through the entire 2025 campaign. During his two-year absence, Aiyuk took to social media with critical comments about the 49ers and the team's front office. He shared his praise for Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and the team as a whole, ultimately landing with the NFC East contenders following his release from San Francisco earlier this week. Free-agent WR Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders practice squad, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus. Aiyuk once again becomes teammates with his Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. pic.twitter.com/jt8diY95o3 - Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 25, 2026 He finished his breakout 2023 campaign ranked as WR14 in PPR, hauling in 75 of his 105 targets for 1,342 receiving yards and seven touchdowns, carving out 15.6 fantasy points per week. Aiyuk won't capture this success from the jump in Washington, landing on the practice squad to start his tenure with the team, but will provide valuable depth to an injury-riddled receiving corps. Commanders' Injuries Will Thrust Brandon Aiyuk Back Into Action Washington Commanders wide receiver Terry McLaurin looks on before the game against the San Francisco 49ers | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Commanders' passing game has been hampered by nagging injuries throughout the season. Daniels has missed time with an elbow injury. Star wideout Terry McLaurin hit Injured Reserve with a torn patellar tendon in his left knee in October, sidelining him for the remainder of the season, joining second-year receiver Jaylin Lane who suffered a season-ending ankle injury early last month. Rookie Antonio Williams has come on strong with a breakout performance against the Cincinnati Bengals and veteran Stefon Diggs has provided reliable consistency, but the team has a void at WR3. Aiyuk will need a few weeks to ramp up efforts before making his Commanders debut, but could fill this void as the third option in the passing game down the stretch of the season. The Commanders are yet to present a timetable for Aiyuk's debut, but the depth is everything for Washington as they look to enter the playoff picture over the next several weeks. Brandon Aiyuk Returns to Fantasy Spotlight, Set for Valuable Role San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk against the Arizona Cardinals | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect Though he may not get the start from game No. 1 in a Commanders uniform, Aiyuk has a clear path to work his way into the starting unit for Washington during the regular season. The offense's current WR3 Treylon Burks has cooled off during Williams' recent surge, and without cemented volume, Burks could be unseated over the next month of action. With a starting role, Aiyuk could make a strong FLEX case among fantasy lineups in a passing attack that has posted 538 passing yards and three touchdowns over the last two games, ranked eighth in passing production among 18 qualifying units with two games during that stretch. title: Sutton's predictions v Kings of Leon drummer Nathan Followill
summary: BBC Sport football expert Chris Sutton takes on Kings of Leon drummer Nathan Followill with his predictions for this weekend's Premier League games.
content: [BBC] Arsenal co-chairman Josh Kroenke should probably turn his phone off if the Gunners fall behind against Manchester City on Sunday. Chris Sutton's predictions guest this week, Kings of Leon drummer and City fan Nathan Followill, is good friends with Kroenke - and says he will be in touch if the game is going City's way. "I'm super excited for this weekend and I've got my smack talk ready for Josh already," Followill told BBC Sport. "I've heard about the City fans with their inflatable bananas and I need to get myself one. My wife is going to be like 'er, an inflatable banana just arrived in the mail - do you know anything about that?' "We are going to win 4-2 so I will be texting Josh throughout the game... and, after Erling Haaland's second goal, I will send him a picture of me kissing the banana!" AI has also made its predictions, and you can pick your own below. The most popular scoreline selected for each game is used in the scoreboards and tables at the bottom of this page. A correct result (picking a win, draw or defeat) is worth 10 points. The exact score earns 40 points. Want to make more predictions? You can play BBC Sport's new Match of the Day predictor game every week, featuring six fixtures from domestic and European competition. Followill has supported City for more than 20 years and his children have followed in his footsteps by becoming Blues, despite the best efforts of his next-door neighbour in Nashville, as well as Kroenke. "When my kids were born, they both received a full Arsenal kit - head to toe - in the mail from Josh," he explained. "Both times, they were returned to sender - instantly. "My son and daughter are both City fans now, but my neighbour, Jeremy Connor, is Tottenham, and I mean flying the flag full on. "When they lose, you can hear him screaming - and when they win, you can hear him screaming too. "His son is trying to convert my son to Spurs and I am like 'that is never going to happen in this house!'" Chris Sutton and Nathan Followill were speaking to BBC Sport's Chris Bevan. The AI predictions were generated using Microsoft Copilot Chat - we simply asked the tool to 'predict this weekend's Premier League scores'. Premier League predictions Friday, 27 November City Ground, 20:00 GMT Chelsea have scored and conceded 20 goals so far this season, which kind of sums up where they are at. Xabi Alonso's side have also lost as many league games - five - as Manchester United, and United are in crisis. Alonso is not under pressure, or anything like that, but if they lose this game too, you can imagine the mood of the club - and it won't be good. Apparently their fans were singing 'you don't know what you're doing' at him after their defeat by Leeds - which is what they sang at me when I was there. Alonso needs to decide on a shape and a way of playing, and stick with it. Anything could happen here, because Nottingham Forest's form is hardly convincing either. They tore Manchester City apart in their previous home game, before the international break, but can they really dig out another result like that here? I think they will go about it in a similar way, and be aggressive and have a real go at Chelsea... and I don't see Chelsea's defence keeping them out. Sutton's prediction: 2-1 Nathan's prediction: No-one thought Forest would beat us, and while Chelsea need a big result, I can see Forest getting a point here. 1-1 AI's prediction: 1-2 Saturday, 28 November Elland Road, 15:00 We talked about Leeds on the Monday Night Club and how they have upgraded their team with the players Daniel Farke bought over the summer. Farke strengthened in the areas he needed to improve, but is still trusting some of the players who did well for him last season - the likes of Jayden Bogle and James Justin, who have been outstanding. They are a really well-balanced team and they have good depth to their squad too. The only criticism would be that they are not usually free-scoring - they hit four against Chelsea but before then they had only managed 10 goals in their first 10 league games. Leeds do not give much away at the back either, though, and I think that will be key in this game. When I watch Coventry they are dynamic with their counter-attacks and I always fancy them to nick a goal like that. Not this time, however. Leeds might take a while to break them down, but I think they will come out on top. Sutton's prediction: 2-0 Nathan's prediction: Coventry play in sky blue too? Part of the reason I became a Manchester City fan was the kit, and I have always gravitated towards teams in light blue, so I am going to go with Coventry here. 0-1 AI's prediction: 2-1 Old Trafford, 15:00 I am at this game for 5 Live and I am not expecting much to change for Manchester United. No-one thought it was going to be easy for Mauricio Pochettino to go in at United and turn things around. He has taken over a complete rabble. United's draw in Lisbon on Wednesday was chaotic, but you also have to consider how Sporting have not got going in the Portuguese league or the Champions League this season. That was not a great Sporting side. They are pretty average and Brentford will be a much bigger test. The Bees are supremely well-organised and will be full of confidence, too, after putting four goals past Everton on Monday. They were against 10 men for the entire second half, but were 2-0 up by then anyway. Pochettino needs something to cling to, but for him picking that backline must be like pinning the tail on the donkey. Whoever he picks, they are not very good. I really want to be more positive about United, because I heard from quite a few of their fans last weekend, but this prediction is about as positive as I can be about them at the moment. Sutton's prediction: 1-2 Nathan's prediction: It is tough for me to talk about United because in America we have a saying 'don't kick a man when he's down' and it's pretty rough for them right now... but I'm not going to lie, it is nice to see United this low in the table. I don't think it is the manager that is the problem for United right now, so I don't think Pochettino coming in is going to be an instant fix. They've got some growing pains to get through, and I won't be disappointed to watch that. When I watch the Premier League at home, Brentford always cracks me up because I am huge fan of The Office and I just imagine a bunch of David Brents out there, just running around the pitch, which is a very funny thing for me. I know I just said don't kick a man when he's down, but I don't think United would be nice to us if we were down there... so, I think the David Brents are going to win. 1-2 AI's prediction: 1-2 Portman Road, 17:30 I actually think Villa will win this game 2-1 but I want to make it clear the scoreline I have gone for is from my commentary colleague, Alistair Bruce-Ball, who is an Ipswich fan - a fake one, but still a fan. I asked him about this game when we were in Belgium for Liverpool's Champions League game on Wednesday. He will be at Portman Road on Saturday for 5 Live and he is backing the Tractor Boys to get something, so I am doing the same out of respect for him. Ipswich really need a result too. They have gone five league games without a win and, with Hull and Coventry both winning last week, they are the lowest placed of the promoted sides. That is never a good thing, and it feels like Gary O'Neil's side are in a precarious position at the moment, where they are getting sucked towards the bottom three. I've been surprised to see Villa hit a bit of a sticky patch too, with three successive league draws and no wins in six in all competitions, so it will be interesting to see if they are any better here. Sutton's prediction: 2-2 Nathan's prediction: Villa have had some surprising results recently but I do think they will win this. 1-3 AI's prediction: 1-2 Sunday, 29 November Hill Dickinson Stadium, 12:00 I was in Bruges to watch Liverpool in midweek and it was interesting to see two of their players who came in for some heavy flak last season, Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz, both shine. Isak is looking like the player who Liverpool thought they signed in 2025. He is finding his rhythm, and Wirtz also seems to be in a really good place confidence-wise. When I watch them now, it feels like something is going to happen. There are other positives for Reds boss Andoni Iraola too. I know there will be a debate about Bradley Barcola's end-product but I love watching him in full flow when he is running past defenders - there is no better sight in football than moments like that. Rio Ngumoha is exciting as well, and he has such a good football brain which makes him even more dangerous. Everything points to a Liverpool win, but I am hesitant to just go with that because Everton are coming off the back of a drubbing by Brentford. You can imagine David Moyes giving his side a miserable old week and getting stuck into his players. I didn't think James Tarkowski should have been sent off in that game, but he will be suspended here. It is his absence that swings it for me because he is a real leader for Everton. Sutton's prediction: 1-2 Nathan's prediction: Everton are usually the underdogs in this game but both teams are pretty level at the moment. One of our record producers is a huge Liverpool fan so he won't be happy with me... but I am going to say Everton will take it. 2-1 AI's prediction: 1-2 Amex Stadium, 14:05 I was at Newcastle's draw with Arsenal last week and, in fairness to Magpies boss Matthias Jaissle, he changed things around at half-time and got his reward. Jaissle needed that half of football, because I don't think the Newcastle fans have been too convinced by his approach, but this is another very tough game for him. Brighton probably still can't believe they lost to Hull last week - but lightning is not going to strike twice. Sutton's prediction: 3-1 Nathan's prediction: I have to give a shout out to my statistician Lucy here, because there were a couple of teams I didn't know a lot about and she gave me some good insight. So, Brighton have scored a lot of goals this season and I think they will get more here. 3-1 AI's prediction: 2-2 Selhurst Park, 14:05 Thomas Frank has got a huge task at Crystal Palace. They are conceding so many goals. Losing Maxence Lacroix and Marc Guehi from their defence was like Robbie Williams and Jason Orange leaving Take That, because they were never going to be the same without them. I still think Frank has got some decent attacking players, however. The Hull keeper, Konstantinos Tzolakis, looks like a great signing. I don't know how he made some of his saves against Brighton and he probably doesn't know himself either. Brighton should have buried them and I think Palace will get plenty of chances too. Fair play to Hull for their spirit and the way they scrap for each other, but I still think they are going to go down. Hull fans are probably wondering if I am ever going to predict they will win a game... the answer is no, at least not this week anyway. Sutton's prediction: 2-1 Nathan's prediction: Palace have given up 27 goals in 11 games which is a lot. Hull have surprised a few people this season and I am backing them here. 0-2 AI's prediction: 1-1 Craven Cottage, 14:05 Bournemouth are on a long winning run in the league but I've been impressed by Fulham whenever I've watched them. Alvaro Arbeloa's side have not been great at home, with only one win at Craven Cottage so far, so I am going with them to get another draw - which would be their fourth in a row. Sutton's prediction: 1-1 Nathan's prediction: Both these teams have picked up a lot, so this is a tough one to call. 2-2 AI's prediction: 1-2 Stadium of Light, 14:05 Tottenham boss Roberto de Zerbi must think a lot of 18-year-old midfielder Luca Williams-Barnett after picking him for their win over Ipswich. I love to see managers trust young players like that, especially because Spurs have had such a tricky season so far. It will be interesting to see whether De Zerbi picks him again here, but I feel like the outcome of this game is more dependent on which Sunderland we see. They picked up a good point at Villa last time out, but they never seem to be quite the same after they have played in Europe, like they are doing this week. The Black Cats will be without injured duo Brian Brobbey and Granit Xhaka for this game too, so I don't think they will have enough to win it. Sutton's prediction: 0-0 Nathan's prediction: Dave Stewart from Eurythmics lives in Nashville too and is a good buddy of mine - and he is Sunderland until death! He is such a die-hard fan that every time we have dinner, we will sit there and talk about 'Haway the Lads' and just shoot the breeze about Sunderland. So I am going to back them in this one, because of Dave and also because of my neighbour Jeremy, who I mentioned earlier. Jeremy was especially cocky when they had Harry Kane and he would just talk so much smack - I always knew if they were doing good because I'd get a text from him. So, because Jeremy is such a cocky little Spurs fan, I am saying Sunderland will win. 2-1 AI's prediction: 1-3 Emirates Stadium, 16:30 I always enjoy this game because of Gabriel's battle with Erling Haaland, but it is in midfield where I think it will be decided. Manchester City have spent a lot of money on players in that part of the pitch but Enzo Maresca has not found the right combination yet. Somehow Maresca has got to find a way of nullifying Declan Rice, but that will be very difficult because Rice is just an absolute machine. You can never rule City out because of Haaland's ability to score goals but the only result I see here is an Arsenal win, and I am going for a classic Gunners scoreline. Sutton's prediction: 1-0 Nathan's prediction: This is the big one! It's huge. I feel really good about it, too. Arsenal are riding so high at the moment, I feel like we might catch them snoozing. I predict Haaland will get two goals, Phil Foden will get one too and we will end up with four. 2-4 AI's prediction: 2-1 How did Sutton do last time? After drawing a blank since week two, Chris finally picked up another win in week 11 - and it was his spot-on prediction for Liverpool to thump Manchester United 4-0 that sealed the deal. That meant he got three correct results, including two exact scores - at Anfield, and Tottenham's 2-0 win over Ipswich - giving him a total of 90 points. In a tricky week for predictions, where Liverpool were the only team to start the weekend in the Premier League's top six who won, it was those exact scores that made all the difference. Chris' guest, undisputed world champion boxer Lauren Price, the BBC readers and AI also all got three correct results. But the BBC readers were the only ones to also get an exact score - in the Spurs game - giving them 60 points. Lauren and AI both ended up on 30 points - AI did call Newcastle's draw with Arsenal correctly, but it was wrong about Bournemouth's win over Nottingham Forest, which everyone else got right. Not many of you got that Liverpool-United scoreline correct, either. From around 27,000 predictions, the most popular scoreline picked was a 2-1 home win and only 570 of you went for 4-0. "When has AI ever gone for a 4-0?" said Sutton. "That's what the crowd wants. The crowd don't want AI - who wants mathematics? "The crowd want gut-feeling and instinct. I think I should get 1,000 points for that prediction, because I was brave enough to go for it." For the first time this season, there were SIX games where no-one made a correct prediction - who thought it was easy? The biggest shock of the week was Leeds' 4-1 victory at Stamford Bridge. Again from around 27,000 predictions, more than 3,600 (14%) of you did back Daniel Farke's side to win... but just 11 of you saw that scoreline coming. title: 14,453 runners set for 90th Manchester Road Race on Thanksgiving morning
summary: Nearly 15,000 participants registered for the race's 90th running.
content: The 90th Manchester Road Race, shown here in 2025, kicks off at 10 a.m. Thursday, November 26, 2025, in downtown Manchester. (Jim Michaud/Hearst Connecticut Media) MANCHESTER - The 90th Manchester Road Race is on . Tens of thousands, including top-level athletes, are headed to Main Street to spectate and participate in the 4.737-mile run , set to begin at 10 a.m. on Thanksgiving morning. The race, presented by Hartford HealthCare and organized by more than 400 volunteers, will take participants on a loop through Manchester starting and finishing in front of St. James Church on Main Street. Organizers have designated affordable housing as the philanthropic target for this year's event, with proceeds from the race going to Rebuilding Together of Manchester and Habitat for Humanity of North Central Connecticut . As of closing Tuesday night, 14,453 participants had registered to run or walk the course Thursday morning. Elite runners expected in the men's division include 2025 winner Edwin Kurgat and runner-up Dave Mullarkey, as well as World Champion Dawit Seare, 2023 Manchester Road Race winner Morgan Beadlescomb, and Mexican Olympian Eduardo Hererra. The women's division features Olympic silver medalist and two-time champion Sally Kipyego and two-time runner-up Annie Rodenfels, alongside other elite long-distance runners including Sarah Hall, Molly Huddle, Hannah Nuttall, Florencia Borelli, Diane Van Es, and twin sisters Eilish and Roisin Flanagan. To facilitate the race, Main Street will close at 5:30 a.m. and all roads intersecting with the course, as well as the nearby Interstate 384 exit ramps, will close starting at 9 a.m. For those arriving after closures, a free shuttle will run from the parking lot at the nearby Connecticut State Community College Manchester campus, departing continuously from 7:15 to 9:15 a.m. and resuming operations after 11 a.m. until 12:30 p.m. This story will be updated with results once runners start to cross the finish line. title: "About to be 42 years old in a month. S---, it takes a …
summary: "About to be 42 years old in a month. S---, it takes a …
content: 76ers coach Nick Nurse said James' long-range shooting was the most impressive part of Wednesday's performance. "I kind of know when my hand is feeling pretty good," James said, "especially from the outside." James' play has fluctuated this season. For as good as he's been in the past two games, there are performances such as his eight-point outing against the Cleveland Cavaliers earlier this month, when shot 3-for-12 and had six turnovers. Or days later against the Celtics when he was 4-for-12 with 11 points and a minus-17 rating. "About to be 42 years old in a month. S---, it takes a little bit longer for the ramp up," he said. "But I'll never be second guessing myself or whatever the case may be because I know the work I put in." James' performance was welcomed from guard Tyrese Maxey, who led Philadelphia with 30 points. title: Ashes to ashes: FC Barcelona reveals plans to let Camp Nou be fans' final resting place
summary: Extra-time may soon have a different meaning for fans of FC Barcelona. Supporters are now being offered the chance to keep their ashes at the Spanish football club, under recently announced plans to build a memorial within the walls of the famous Camp Nou stadium.View on euronews
content: Liverpool's legendary manager Bill Shankly once famously said "Some people believe football is a matter of life and death. I am very disappointed with that attitude. I can assure you it is much, much more important than that." Sentiments shared, it seems, by FC Barcelona as the Spanish Liga champions have recently unveiled plans for their fans to remain part of the club well into the afterlife. Barça want to open up the Camp Nou columbarium complex at the end of 2027, a 1,500-square-metre space where supporters will be able to leave their ashes. The project, called Memorial FC Barcelona, will have 26,000 columbarium niches and 9,000 commemorative plaques. Presenting the plans, architect Quique Montoya said the design was inspired by the shape of a "trainer" and that the 26,000 niches represent as many supporters who will accompany the team in spirit. A computer rendered Image of FC Barcelona's columbarium - Courtesy: Memorial FC Barcelona The Memorial will have its own entrance from the street, open on a permanent basis. On match days and on special dates it will also be accessible from inside the stadium, via gate 35. There is already a first name on the team sheet. Former club captain, Josep Vicenç 'Tente' Sánchez , has said that he wants to be laid to rest there. There's a price to pay of course for such a coveted spot at a legendary club. Leases run for 10, 25 or 50 years for a niche of your own at the blaugrana stadium with costs starting from €2,490 euros for a decade, €4,990 for 25 years and €5,990 for half a century. To reserve one, you have to pay €500 up front, which is deducted from the total, and after that there is a yearly maintenance fee of €70. The club is also offering a cheaper option by way of a commemorative plaques, which costs between €490 and €990 depending on how long you want your name on the hallowed walls. But even within these options there are surcharges, for example if you want a specific spot or to be seen close to the legends of the club . Atlético de Madrid, the original Barcelona are not however, the first Spanish side to offer fans a eternal place in a stadium. Similar ventures are also available to supporters of Espanyol, at Cornellà-El Prat, and Betis, which opened their own at the Benito Villamarín in 2011 with around 4,000 urns. The Spanish pioneer in this 'field of dreams' was Atlético de Madrid which opened their Espacio Memorial at their former Vicente Calderón stadium back in 2008. It had space for 4,200 ceramic urns at a cost of €3,600 each, according to a study in the journal Disparidades. The club itself boasted at the time that it was the first football stadium in the world with a space of this kind. As a result of its stadium's demolition, however, the remains of Atléti's deceased fans have sinced been moved to a final resting place at their new Metropolitano stadium, a process carried out "with the permission of the families".

title: Botham back as Morgan-Williams to make first start
summary: Wales flanker James Botham is recalled by head coach Steve Tandy as one of five changes for the Nations Championship finale against Japan.
content: James Botham and Reuben Morgan-Williams were part of the Wales squad that beat New Zealand [Getty Images/Huw Evans Picture Agency] Wales flanker James Botham has been recalled by head coach Steve Tandy as one of five changes for the Nations Championship finale against Japan at Allianz Stadium on Saturday. In the only backline alteration for the game in Twickenham, Ospreys scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams will make his first Wales start, with Tomos Williams named among the replacements. Exeter lock Dafydd Jenkins will captain the side for the first time in more than two years with regular skipper Dewi Lake and flanker Jac Morgan also dropping to the bench. Prop Rhys Carre and hooker Ryan Elias make their first starts of the November campaign, while lock Adam Beard returns at the expense of Ben Carter. Wales have named an experienced bench that includes 294 caps. Botham back after missing Australia Botham produced a player-of-the-match display in the 35-28 victory against New Zealand after making 30 tackles but was left out of the 29-26 defeat by Australia in favour of Cardiff colleague Alex Mann. It was a decision which Botham’s father Liam, himself a former Cardiff wing, said Tandy had got wrong. “I know there's a lot been spoken about it,” said Tandy. “Everyone has got their opinions and people generally tell you who should be in the team and they never tell you who shouldn't. “We're a tight group and as a coach I make sure I speak to all the players before if they are not selected. There'll be reasons why, whether it be bigger picture or whether it is form. “I'll always speak to those, that's a special thing and the connection we feel in our environment.” Botham, who became a father earlier this week, will play at open-side flanker against Japan after starring at blind-side against the All Blacks, with Mann and number eight Aaron Wainwright completing the back row. “James was outstanding against the All Blacks, but we've got a back row depth there that we can move things around and freshen things up," said Tandy. “James has had his little one, he's coming back in full of energy. We were so pleased for him things have gone well there." Wales need strong finish to campaign - Morgan A world-class winger - Louis Rees-Zammit 2.0 Chance for Morgan-Williams to shine at nine Ospreys number nine Morgan-Williams is preparing for his first start in a position that has been dominated by Saracens scrum-half Williams during the Tandy era. Williams has started 14 out of the 15 internationals, including the previous 11, with opportunities in short supply for others. But Williams came off early in the second half against Australia with a groin problem. Carre, named Welsh rugby writers player of the 2025-26 season, is given his first start this autumn, with Nicky Smith dropping out of the squad. Saracens loose-head Carre missed the first month of the season because of a hamstring injury and his only appearance of the autumn Tests so far was off the bench against Japan. Elias, a replacement in the three previous November internationals, is handed his first Test start since the 2024 Six Nations match against France. Montpellier lock Beard returns after missing the loss to Australia after suffering a shoulder injury against New Zealand. Scarlets wing Ellis Mee is given his first involvement in the campaign after being named as a replacement. Tandy has settled on his backline with full-back Blair Murray, wing Louis Rees-Zammit, centres Eddie James and Max Llewellyn and fly-half Sam Costelow starting all four matches in the November campaign as well as prop Archie Griffin and Jenkins. Uncapped quartet Che Hope, Macs Page, Rhys Barratt and Aneurin Owen are among the players who will not be given game time. Wales have won three and lost three of their six Nations Championship matches to finish fifth in the northern hemisphere group, a position matched by Japan in the southern hemisphere section. Wales will face Eddie Jones’ Japan side for a fifth time inside two years with Wales winning three out of the four games. It is the first match of a Saturday double-header, with England and New Zealand to follow. “We were frustrated and disappointed with losing last weekend,” said Tandy. “We probably weren't as accurate as we could have been but there were a lot of positives in the performance to take also. “We want to go out there, be ruthless and show improvement on our previous performance against Japan." How they line up Wales: Murray: Rees-Zammit, E James, Llewellyn, Adams: Costelow, Morgan-Williams; Carre, Elias, Griffin, D Jenkins (capt), Beard, Mann, Botham, Wainwright. Replacements: Lake, G Thomas, Lewis, Plumtree, J Morgan, Tomos Williams, Hawkins, Mee. title: 'He can't be the lead bowler': Cheteshwar Pujara warns Punjab Kings against relying on Hardik Pandya
summary: As the IPL auction approaches, Punjab Kings are focused on bolstering their bowling attack in a bid to secure their maiden title. Former cricketer Cheteshwar Pujara highlights the necessity of finding a reliable replacement for Arshdeep Singh, who has departed. He suggests that acquiring Hardik Pandya could solidify the batting order, especially following early setbacks.
content: Punjab Kings (PBKS) will need to make the right bowling acquisitions at the upcoming IPL auction if they are to end their long wait for a maiden title in 2027, according to former India batter Cheteshwar Pujara. While the arrival of Hardik Pandya has strengthened their all-round options and added depth to the batting order, the departure of Arshdeep Singh to Mumbai Indians has left a significant void in their pace attack. Pujara believes the identity and quality of Arshdeep's replacement could prove decisive in determining Punjab's title prospects, with the franchise needing to build a bowling attack capable of delivering consistently throughout the tournament. Speaking to JioStar, Pujara highlighted the contrasting impact of Hardik's arrival and Arshdeep's departure, stressing that Punjab must prioritise their bowling requirements at the auction. Arshdeep Singh's replacement could hold the key For PBKS "The arrival of Hardik Pandya has been one huge positive for Punjab, though alongside it there is a slight negative as well, that Arshdeep Singh isn't there. Even though his performance last season wasn't as special as expected, given the way he is bowling right now, he is back in form. "So that could be a big blow for Punjab, and who's going to be his replacement will be the deciding factor. Of course, with Hardik Pandya coming in, their batting strength will increase. How his bowling is coming along, we don't know yet, because he has been recovering from an injury. "While his bowling will also be important, he can't be the lead bowler, he can be a supporting bowler. The bowlers they pick at the auction and how they shape up will determine whether they can go on to win the trophy," Pujara said. 136190202 Hardik Pandya can solve PBKS' no. 6 and no. 7 concerns Pujara also believes Hardik's presence could address one of Punjab's long-standing batting concerns, particularly their inability to find stability in the lower middle order when early wickets fall. "With Hardik in the team, the slight issue they used to face of needing someone to stabilise the innings after early wickets fall is a role he can fulfil very well, solving Punjab's No. 6 and No. 7 problems," Pujara added.

title: Former England rugby player and BBC commentator Nigel Starmer-Smith dies aged 81
summary: Starmer-Smith, who was diagnosed with dementia in 2015, made seven international appearances
content: Nigel Starmer-Smith, a former England international who became one of the sport’s most prominent commentators, has died at the age of 81. A scrum half, Starmer-Smith was capped seven times for his country between 1969 and 1971, and represented Harlequins and the Barbarians . Having retired from playing in 1976, he was a stalwart voice of the BBC ’s rugby union coverage, commentating on highlights programme Rugby Special for 15 years. He also played a prominent part in ITV’s coverage of the 2003 Rugby World Cup in Australia. Starmer-Smith was diagnosed with dementia in 2015. "Dad passed away peacefully this morning after a long battle with dementia," his son Charlie posted on social media on Thursday. "He was (as they say in rugby circles) one of life's great tourists. A rugby player, commentator, editor, writer, raconteur, charity fundraiser, volunteer, speaker, prankster, family man, life and soul of the party, but, above all, the greatest father anyone could wish to have. "He did everything for us and, despite having to bury two of his children at cruelly young ages, both he and my Mum refused to let the cavernous holes that Charlotte and Julian left behind define them. "Just as I choose not to let the cruel condition that robbed him of his ability to communicate (and ultimately of his dignity), define my memories of him. Nigel Starmer-Smith won seven caps for England (Getty) "He was a modest man and he'd hate for people to make a fuss. He loved to laugh but not as much as he loved to see others laughing. So for those that knew him think of a happy memory and smile. For that's how I'll remember him."

title: 'Gautam Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting': World Cup-winner sends strong message on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hammered 204 off just 53 balls for India A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars, bringing the debate over his promotion to the senior Indian team back into focus.
content: NEW DELHI: At just 15, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has already delivered several remarkable batting performances. But his stunning innings against the UAE in the Asia Cup Rising Stars could well be the most special of them all. The youngster went after the bowlers from the start and completely dominated the opposition attack. Sooryavanshi hammered 204 off just 53 balls for India A in the Asia Cup Rising Stars, bringing the debate over his promotion to the senior Indian team back into focus. Many former cricketers and experts have backed the youngster for a regular place in India's T20I team. However, his latest knock also underlined his ability to make an impact in the 50-over format. Former India captain and 1983 World Cup winner Krishnamachari Srikkanth feels the team management must take bold decisions to give Sooryavanshi a bigger role in Indian cricket. Srikkanth questions Gambhir's approach Sooryavanshi has featured in 10 T20Is for India but is yet to cement his place in the playing XI. With the full-strength team available, Abhishek Sharma and Sanju Samson have been preferred as openers. Srikkanth feels the youngster is not getting enough opportunities despite his impressive performances. He also had a strong message for India head coach Gautam Gambhir. "We need to make some strong moves. Vaibhav was made Bihar captain right away. He was the vice-captain in the Duleep Trophy; him and Ishan (Kishan) won the title. He has been promoted to that level. Gautam is just keeping deaf ears," Srikkanth said, speaking on his YouTube channel. "The team management is playing one game, saying he has to be groomed, and not giving him chances. This guy, on the other hand, is playing his own game. You say it is not in your hands and all of that. Gautam Gambhir, just look at how he is hitting. No one can hit like this. Just look at this," he added. 'This is another level' Srikkanth was left stunned by the variety of shots Sooryavanshi played during his remarkable innings. He also praised the youngster's power and timing, saying he had rarely seen anything like it. "What is this? Have you seen anyone hitting the ball like this? Look at the shots he has played. He has his shots everywhere in all ranges. This is another level. This does not happen in book cricket either. I have never seen these kinds of shots. Who is this guy? Which generation is he from? Where does he get so much power and sense of timing?" he further said. Srikkanth also compared the 15-year-old's batting to that of some of the biggest hitters in the game, including AB de Villiers and Chris Gayle. "I have not seen anyone playing like this in a team. Even (AB) De Villiers and (Chris) Gayle did not play like this," Srikkanth concluded. 136184442

title: Jordie Barrett to captain All Blacks for first time in England rematch
summary: The youngest Barrett brother will follow in the footsteps of siblings Scott and Beauden
content: Jordie Barrett will follow in the footsteps of elder brothers Scott and Beauden as he captains New Zealand for the first time in their rematch with England . Hooker Codie Taylor, who had been deputising for regular skipper Ardie Savea, has been ruled out of the encounter with a tight calf, with the youngest Barrett brother installed as Dave Rennie seeks a response following a record defeat last week. The All Blacks were beaten 37-12 by England, and are bidding to avoid becoming the first New Zealand side to be beaten by their opposition in three successive contests. Richie Mo’unga takes over at fly half from Damian McKenzie, who shifts to full-back with Beauden Barrett displaced from the starting side. Leicester Fainga’anuku partners the captain in midfield with Anton Lienert-Brown another injury absentee, while Anton Segner is the replacement for Tupou Vaa’i on the blindside flank. Cam Roigard also drops to the bench with Cortez Ratima preferred as Mo’unga’s half-back partner. “That was a pretty simple choice for us,” head coach Rennie said of the appointment of captain. “I think anyone who has worked with Jordie would know he is very impressive, has a great game understanding on both sides of the ball. He’s prepared to challenge. “He’s been great in our leadership group and he’s taken over the captaincy role when Codie has left the field. It was a pretty straightforward decision for us.” New Zealand XV: 1 Ethan de Groot, 2 Asafo Aumua, 3 Fletcher Newell; 4 Scott Barrett , 5 Fabian Holland; 6 Anton Segner, 7 Peter Lakai, 8 Wallace Sititi; 9 Cortez Ratima, 10 Richie Mo’unga; 11 Josh Moorby, 12 Jordie Barrett (capt.), 13 Leicester Fainga’anuku, 14 Rieko Ioane; 15 Damian McKenzie. Replacements: 16 George Bell, 17 Xavier Numia, 18 Pasilio Tosi, 19 Josh Lord, 20 Ethan Blackadder; 21 Cam Roigard, 22 Timoci Tavatavanawai, 23 Beauden Barrett.

title: Regulator could force Manchester City’s Abu Dhabi ownership out of English football
summary: David Kogan, the chair of the Independent Football Regulator, says the body has ‘the stomach’ to take strong action against City
content: The Independent Football Regulator could force Manchester City ’s Abu Dhabi ownership out of English football if the guilty verdicts over breaches of Premier League financial rules are upheld. City were found guilty of nearly every charge brought against them by the league when the commission’s verdict was published in September. A three-person adjudication panel found that the club had systematically inflated revenues and disguised losses by a combined £900m through “sham” deals between 2009 and 2018, aiding their rapid ascent to the summit of the game. The club have always strongly denied wrongdoing and have appealed against the commission’s verdict . If City’s appeal fails, a sanction hearing will follow and is expected to recommend seismic sporting and financial punishments. Separately, the regulator (IFR), which was established last year following the fallout from the European Super League scandal, has legal powers to investigate and sanction both the club and any individuals involved in breaching rules. The IFR grants operating licenses to football clubs and has the power to withdraw them. It also carries powers to order officials who it deems unsuitable to “take all reasonable steps to cease to be an owner of the club” within a given time frame. The regulator faces a major test of its ability to referee the English game, given both the enormity of the City case and Abu Dhabi’s political and economic relationship with the UK. Some senior figures within English football were concerned by comments from prime minister Andy Burnham appearing to downplay the significance of the verdict when it first emerged, although Downing Street later clarified that Burnham’s view is that no-one is “above the rules”. But David Kogan, the IFR chair, has told parliament’s Digital, Culture, Media and Sport select committee that the regulator is prepared to take strong action against City, if necessary. David Kogan says the regulator has the ‘stomach’ to take on Manchester City (PA) “Forget the name of the club, forget the size of the club, forget the scale of the issue,” Kogan said. “We cannot simply ignore our statutory duties in relation to a club because it happens to be of a certain size. “We absolutely will have to take the appropriate action as laid out in the legislation, depending on the circumstances as they come to us, which are the evidence that’s been presented and collated by the independent commission of the Premier League and by any judgement that takes place on that evidence through an appeal. “But in one sense, the evidence has already been judged by those cases having been found guilty, so we will absolutely have the stomach to do so.” City are owned by City Football Group , a parent company controlled by Emirati royal Sheikh Mansour via his Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG) investment vehicle. The commission found that ADUG money was used to artificially inflate City’s revenues, something the club continues to dispute. Kogan added: “Would I, with an organisation that has a relatively new, fairly young staff, that’s been going for less than a year, would I have chosen to have this particular issue in our laps this early? Well, probably not. But the truth is, if we don’t act – assuming those circumstances are triggered – if we don’t act, what is the purpose of having a football regulator? “So I think we have to absolutely, clearly be seen to be doing the job that you as legislators have asked us to do, and we absolutely will do that, whatever that means.” City’s appeal against the commission’s verdict has no set timetable but is expected to be concluded early in the new year, with the sanctions hearing then set to follow if any or all of the verdicts are upheld. City’s most recent statement, on 2 October, read: “Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7pm on Thursday 1st October 2026 the Club lodged its comprehensive Appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter. “The Club’s firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe. The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. “We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete.”

title: Two-point drop-goals & other Super League changes announced
summary: A number of rule changes will come in for the 2027 Super League season, including two-point drop-goals.
content: Super League will return in February [Swpix.com] A number of rule changes will come in for the 2027 Super League season, including two-point drop-goals. With the proposed partnership between Super League and Australia's National Rugby League (NRL) being ironed out in its final stages, the Rugby Football League has approved a series of amendments which will bring it closer to the Australian game. From next season, drop-goals from outside the opposition's 40-metre line will be worth two points rather than one. A try will also count if the ball rotates from hand to wrist or forearm and there has also been a change in the law on ball stealing, as defenders can now steal the ball if a player is in the act of scoring, no matter how many players are in the tackle. To counter-act stoppages in play, delaying a restart can now result in a sin-bin. Gameday squads will also increase from 17 to 19 players, with each side now being able to name six replacements but only four of those will be able to come on. The full list of rule changes Catalans out of 2027 Challenge Cup Wigan Warriors beat Hull KR in the 2026 Challenge Cup final to lift the trophy for the 22nd time [SWPIX.COM] Meanwhile, the Rugby Football League has confirmed the format for the 2027 Challenge Cup, with both French sides Catalans Dragons and Toulouse not involved. Les Dracs won the Cup in 2018, while Toulouse have opted against entering since 2017. The first round of the competition will be played on the weekend of 16-17 January, with both the men's and women's finals to be held at Wembley on Saturday, 5 June. The bottom four teams from last season's Super League, Bradford Bulls, Castleford Tigers, Huddersfield Giants and Hull FC plus London Broncos, who were announced as the top tier's 15th side for 2027 on Wednesday, will enter at the fourth round stage. The remaining Super League teams, other than Catalans and Toulouse, will then join in the fifth round.

title: Wales make five changes for Japan finale as Rhys Carre earns recall
summary: Wales will look to improve on their narrow win in their first meeting with Japan in the Nations Championship
content: Head coach Steve Tandy has made five alterations to his Wales team for the Nations Championship finale against Japan , recalling loosehead prop Rhys Carre. The Saracens forward was named Wales player of the year in September after an outstanding 2026 Six Nations campaign, but is yet to make a Test start this autumn. Exeter lock Dafydd Jenkins assumes the captaincy with Dewi Lake named on the bench, while Ryan Elias comes in to start at hooker. Adam Beard partners Jenkins in the second row as James Botham makes his return as openside flanker. Botham was player of the match during Wales’ landmark victory against New Zealand – their first since 1953 – but was left out for last weekend’s defeat to Australia . Scrum-half Reuben Morgan-Williams makes his full Test debut, with Tomos Williams among the replacements despite having started 14 of Tandy's 15 matches, including the last 11 consecutively. Wales have been much improved in this Nations Championship (Reuters) Wales ended up fifth in the northern hemisphere table of the inaugural Nations Championship after being edged out 29-26 by Australia in Cardiff. They now face southern hemisphere fifth-placed side Japan at Allianz Stadium, Twickenham , on Saturday to determine ninth and 10th position in the competition. Tandy said: "We were frustrated and disappointed with losing last weekend. We probably weren’t as accurate as we could have been. "But there were a lot of positives in the performance to take as well. "We have one more match in this competition on Saturday, away from home. "We want to go out there, be ruthless and show improvement on our previous performance against Japan." Wales starting XV : Blair Murray (Scarlets), Louis Rees-Zammit (Bristol), Eddie James (Scarlets), Max Llewellyn (Gloucester), Josh Adams (Cardiff), Sam Costelow (Scarlets), Reuben Morgan-Williams (Ospreys); Rhys Carre (Saracens), Ryan Elias (Scarlets), Archie Griffin (Bath), Dafydd Jenkins (Exeter, capt), Adam Beard (Montpellier), Alex Mann, James Botham (both Cardiff), Aaron Wainwright (Leicester). Replacements : Dewi Lake (Gloucester), Gareth Thomas (Ospreys), Dillon Lewis (Dragons), Taine Plumtree (Scarlets), Jac Morgan (Gloucester), Tomos Williams (Saracens), Joe Hawkins, Ellis Mee (both Scarlets).

title: 300 elk take over Colorado golf course, and golfers just keep playing
summary: Golfers continued to play like usual after a herd of elk took over Mariana Butte Golf Course in Loveland, Colorado.
content: "Birdie" and "eagle" are common golf terms. But the animal that took over a golf course in Loveland, Colorado, this week was elk. Meagan Schrecengost captured a video of a large herd of elk lounging around at Mariana Butte Golf Course and posted it to her Facebook on Sunday, Nov. 22. Not only were there a large number of the animals filling in portions of the course, but people were continuing to drive their carts and take their shots around the elk. She estimated that there were about 300 elk on the course, which was designed by architect Dick Phelps and opened in 1992. "Apparently you just play around them!" she said in the caption. "Only in Colorado!" The video went viral as sports enthusiasts were fascinated by the scene. ABC News' reel of the video has 250,000 views on Instagram at the time of publication. Local radio station KYGO reports that the golf course put up fencing a month earlier to keep wildlife out. The elk seemingly weren't deterred. The golf course is located along the Big Thompson River at the foot of the Rocky Mountains. It is about 55 miles, an hour drive, north of Denver. title: Anthony Kim Set to Make History With Joe Rogan Podcast Appearance
summary: Anthony Kim is reportedly set to become the first professional golfer to appear on The Joe Rogan Experience. The former LIV Golf player is expected to join Joe Rogan for an interview that could introduce his remarkable comeback story to a much wider audience. The news was reported by Flushing It Golf, which said sources …
content: | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Ajayi Segun Anthony Kim is reportedly set to become the first professional golfer to appear on The Joe Rogan Experience . The former LIV Golf player is expected to join Joe Rogan for an interview that could introduce his remarkable comeback story to a much wider audience. The news was reported by Flushing It Golf , which said sources had indicated that Kim would become the first professional golfer to feature on the popular podcast. Flushing It later reported that Kim had recorded the interview with Rogan, with the episode expected to be released around Thanksgiving. Kim’s reported appearance comes after an impressive return to professional golf. The 41-year-old has attracted attention beyond the sport since winning LIV Golf Adelaide in February, when he produced a final-round 63 to finish ahead of Jon Rahm and Bryson DeChambeau. ALSO READ: Nick Faldo Calls on Former LIV Golf Stars to Help Pay Unpaid Suppliers Anthony Kim’s Comeback Story Reaches Wider Audience Kim’s victory in Adelaide was one of the biggest moments of his comeback. He had spent more than a decade away from professional golf before returning to competition in 2024 with LIV Golf. The American had previously won three times on the PGA Tour and represented the United States at the 2008 Ryder Cup and 2009 Presidents Cup. However, injuries and personal struggles interrupted his career , leaving fans uncertain about whether he would ever return to the sport. His Adelaide victory changed the conversation around his career. Kim went from trying to rebuild his game to beating two of LIV Golf’s biggest names in a tournament that attracted attention outside the regular golf audience. He also appeared as a special speaker at the Milken Institute Global Investors’ Symposium in Mexico City. The event has previously featured major sporting figures, including Tom Brady and Shaquille O’Neal. A Joe Rogan interview could take that wider attention to another level. The podcast is known for its long conversations with personalities from sports, entertainment and other industries. Kim could have the opportunity to discuss his years away from golf, his return and the experiences behind his comeback. Anthony Kim Also Working on New Documentary The podcast appearance is not the only major media project involving Kim. It was announced in September that he is working on a documentary with Ben Silverman and Propagate Content. The project will explore his rise as a golf prodigy, his disappearance from professional competition and his eventual return to the sport. The production company described the documentary as a personal story of recovery and redemption. In its announcement, Propagate Content said Kim would tell his story for the first time on his own terms. The documentary is expected to give viewers a closer look at the experiences behind his long absence from golf. Kim has built a strong following since returning to competition, with his Adelaide victory bringing renewed attention to his career. His story has also attracted interest from people who may not regularly follow professional golf. With the reported Joe Rogan appearance and documentary in the works, Kim is continuing to attract attention away from the course. His next chapter could reach an even bigger audience as fans wait to hear more about his journey and future in golf. Main Photo Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect

title: Faldo urges LIV stars to 'chip in' for unpaid firms
summary: The six-time major winner calls on those who benefited financially from LIV Golf to help small businesses still owed money by the tour.
content: Sir Nick Faldo's comments follow a BBC Sport investigation [Getty Images] Sir Nick Faldo has suggested those who financially benefited from LIV Golf should "chip in and take care of" businesses owed money by the Saudi-backed tour. His comments have been welcomed by UK companies still waiting to be paid. A BBC Sport investigation found that LIV paid millions to players and executives in the weeks before filing for bankruptcy, while bills from suppliers were already overdue. Faldo - arguably Britain's greatest golfer - said the controversial breakaway tour risked "ruining the small businesses that help make their events possible". "British suppliers who cleaned venues and kept events running are still owed hundreds of thousands of pounds," added the six-time major winner. "Maybe if those on and off the golf course feel they were overcompensated for their worth, they should chip in and take care of this matter." Since the investigation was published, more firms have contacted us about money they are owed by LIV. They include sports communications company Soapbox, which works with the likes of Anthony Joshua and Luke Littler and is owed tens of thousands of pounds. "I'm incredibly grateful to Sir Nick Faldo for speaking out," said Krissi Foskett, whose cleaning company BD365 Clean is £75,225 out of pocket. "For the last couple of months I've felt powerless. Having someone of his standing recognise the injustice of what's happening to businesses like ours genuinely means a lot. "Sir Nick's suggestion that those who have benefited financially could contribute towards paying the outstanding suppliers is something I wholeheartedly welcome." LIV Golf has not responded to requests for comment on the original investigation or Faldo's remarks. In August, chief executive Scott O'Neil said he hoped the tour would be able to pay its suppliers. "What I would say to them is we're doing everything we can to make sure we can do right by them and the work they committed. "I come from a family of entrepreneurs, a family of small business entrepreneurs and know the challenge." Scott O'Neil (right) took over from Greg Norman (left) as LIV chief executive in January 2025 [Getty Images] Faldo's one-time on-course rival, Greg Norman, was chief executive of LIV Golf until last year. Court filings show the Australian received $9.4m (£7.2m) in settlement and bonus payments in September 2025. His successor, O'Neil, received a retention bonus of $6.4m (£4.9m) in June this year. In September, Norman told The Real Deal with Bob Philion podcast that he was proud of bringing private equity into the sport. "In a period of basically 2021 to now, close to $8bn (£6.1bn) has been brought into the game of golf," he said. Responding to those comments, Faldo told BBC Sport: "Eight billion dollars is 8,000 million dollars. If that is a full six years, that is approximately $3.6m (£2.8m) a day. "Before LIV filed for bankruptcy, seven executives received $15.6m (£11.9m) in retention payments, with further bonuses also paid. "Now they risk ruining the small businesses that help make their events possible." BBC Sport has contacted Norman for a response. 'I'm not the one who should feel ashamed' Companies still owed money include Global Infusion Group, which provided catering at July's LIV Golf UK event and is awaiting £321,671 - which was due on 7 August. Public records also list more than £3,000 owed to Goodysphere, a family-run Yorkshire firm that provides a sensory bus designed to help autistic children who may find busy events overwhelming. Just $2m (£1.5m) has been proposed so far by LIV's Saudi owners to pay unsecured creditors, leaving many smaller companies unsure whether they will receive anything at all. "I've spent months questioning myself, feeling ashamed that our financial difficulties might be perceived as poor management," said Foskett. "When I look at the billions poured into LIV Golf and the millions reportedly paid to executives, whilst I was personally climbing in and out of skips to meet their zero-waste policy, I've come to realise that I'm not the one who should feel ashamed. "We didn't invest in LIV Golf. We didn't gamble on its success. We simply went to work. "Scott O'Neil talks about understanding small businesses. Sir Nick Faldo is standing up for them. Right now, I know whose words mean more to me."
