title: Navajo Stirling responds to Josh Hokit's offer to 'save' 205-pound division
summary: Navajo Stirling wants Josh Hokit to stand behind his words after ripping the "bum" UFC light heavyweight division.
content: If Josh Hokit wants to move down to the UFC light heavyweight division, he won't have to look far for a taker. Hokit was among the wave of backlash to the press conference hosted by City Kickboxing coach Eugene Bareman where, with UFC light heavyweight champ Carlos Ulberg and high-ranked contender Navajo Stirling standing behind him, said the teammates would absolutely not be fighting each other next. There's been a push from fans and media to see Stirling (12-0 MMA, 7-0 UFC) challenge for gold after his second-round knockout of Jiri Prochazka at UFC Fight Night 294 this past Saturday, but the messaging from Bareman was clear. That didn't sit well with recent heavyweight title challenger Hokit (10-1 MMA, 4-1 UFC), who offered to bring his name into the contender mix at 205 pounds if Ulberg (13-1 MMA, 10-1 UFC) and Stirling won't fight (via X ): I need to save this bum division as well.. If you need a guy, you know who to call @ufc https://t.co/nKsBe3EZfn — The Incredible Hok (@Josh_HokitUFC) November 26, 2026 Stirling wasted no time putting his hand up to welcome the outspoken and polarizing Hokit to the weight class, responding on social media while urging UFC CEO Dana White and the company brass to book the matchup (via X ): Book it then 🙋‍♂️ @ufc @danawhite — N A V A J O (@navajostirling) November 26, 2026 Hokit has been pushing for an immediate rematch with heavyweight champ Ciryl Gane after his unanimous decision loss at UFC 334 earlier this month. title: Alex Bowman Says He Retires Because He Cares Too Much
summary: Alex Bowman reveals he is walking away from NASCAR because he cannot separate his self-worth from race results, a struggle he detailed in a recent interview.
content: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Alex Bowman is retiring from full-time Cup Series racing after the 2027 season because the pressure of losing affects him more than anyone else. The Hendrick Motorsports driver told Danielle Trotta that his inability to detach his personal identity from the performance of his car is the main reason he is leaving the sport. This admission comes after fans and critics questioned his commitment to the team during recent races. Bowman has faced rumors that he no longer wants to race or work hard, but he says those claims are completely false. “I’ve seen comments and stuff that say that I don’t want to be there and I’m not working hard, and I don’t care about results. That is as far from the truth as it could possibly be,” Bowman said, according to MotorBiscuit . He argues that he cares about results far too much, a trait he believes Jeff Gordon would confirm if asked directly. This intense drive helped him become an eight-time Cup Series winner, but it also made the job emotionally exhausting over time. The Weight of Every Bad Race For years, Bowman has struggled to leave a bad day at the track behind him when he goes home. He admits that poor results hit him harder than they hit most other drivers. “When we have bad results, I don’t think there’s anybody that affects more than me. I think that’s part of the reason that I’m retiring,” Bowman said. He stated that separating his personal identity from the race car’s outcome was genuinely difficult for him. This internal battle has been a constant part of his career, especially after moving from smaller teams with limited resources to the top tier of NASCAR. His final season offers a fresh start with a new crew chief and a team built to win. Bowman will keep his No. 48 Chevrolet but will take over William Byron’s former group, which includes veteran crew chief Rudy Fugle. Working with a team that is used to winning races gives him a real chance to make his last year one of his best. Despite the pressure, he has not slowed down his preparation for the upcoming year. Still Working While Others Rest He has worked out every day and completed several long runs to keep his body ready for the grind. With simulator work scheduled before Christmas, it is evident he retains the motivation to compete at a high level. While Bowman prepares for his final run, other drivers are facing similar crossroads. Denny Hamlin plans to retire after 2027, but team owner Joe Gibbs is trying to change that mind. Gibbs has been visiting Hamlin’s home late at night to discuss his future, hoping to keep the veteran driver on the track. Hamlin said he needs to talk to retired drivers like Kevin Harvick before making a final call on his career. For now, both drivers remain focused on the 2027 season as their expected final year in the Cup Series.

title: JJ Redick on importance of Lakers' upcoming three-game road trip
summary: The Lakers face a big test in the form of their upcoming three-game road trip.
content: Every Los Angeles Lakers fan is focused on the team's game this Friday against the San Antonio Spurs . It is sure to be a showdown, as the Lakers have the best record in the NBA at 15-3 and the Spurs are right behind them at 15-4. This will also be the final NBA Cup group play contest for both teams, and it could single-handedly determine which team finishes first in West Group C. But it will also be the first game of a three-game road trip for Los Angeles. It will face the Memphis Grizzlies on Sunday and the Houston Rockets on Monday, and it should be quite a barometer for a team that has performed better than quite possibly anyone could've expected to this point. Coach JJ Redick feels this trip would result in some sort of narrative about the Lakers that will fall at or near either extreme, via ESPN. "We're either going to be contenders or we're going to be a fake team," Redick said of the commentary that would follow the Lakers, no matter what happens on the road trip. "If we win that [San Antonio] game and then we lose to Memphis and Houston, we're back to being a fake team. So ... the overreactions game-to-game are what they are, and we've got to, as a group, manage that and manage the noise and that's just part of being in the NBA." While the Lakers have defeated a few quality teams so far this season, there are those, such as Ramona Shelburne of ESPN , who feel they only have a strong record because they have beaten up on inferior teams. L.A.'s offense has fallen off during its last four games. It averaged 122.8 points a game in its first 14 games, but it has put up just 107.5 points per game since then. Austin Reaves has missed the team's last five games, and it has definitely missed his ability to be a volume scorer while also facilitating and putting pressure on the rim. Reaves fully practiced on Wednesday, and the hope is that he'll be able to play in all three games of this upcoming trip. title: JJ Redick Reveals When He Was Convinced Lakers Had To Sign Ziaire Williams
summary: Ziaire Williams quickly won over JJ Redick when they met.
content: Mandatory Credit: Jon Endow-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers brought in many new faces this past offseason, and Ziaire Williams has proven to be one of their better acquisitions. There wasn’t much hype about Williams’ arrival, but Lakers head coach JJ Redick revealed at Wednesday’s practice that all it took was one meeting to convince him they had to sign the forward. “I’ve been collecting intel on players for 20 years now,” Redick said, via Infanity TV. “I did it as a player, I did it in media, I do it now as a coach, so yeah you certainly want to bring the right people in here… Ziaire was supposed to make six and a half million, I think, from Brooklyn this year, and then he was a non-guaranteed deal, so they waive him. “He becomes a free agent, and he was willing to go to a gym in Vegas and work out for our coaching staff and for Rob [Pelinka],” Redick continued. “We put him through that; he looked great. I met with him the next day at the hotel for about 45 minutes, and towards the middle of that conversation, I just kept thinking to myself, holy s***, we got to get this guy in our locker room. We need this guy to be a Laker.” Williams hit free agency after the Brooklyn Nets didn’t pick up his $6.25 million team option for 2026-27. The Lakers were immediately linked to the 25-year-old , as he had fans inside their facility. Redick then joined that group of fans after meeting Williams for the first time. The 42-year-old felt the Lakers had to get him in, and it doesn’t look like they faced much competition. Why? Well, the Lakers signed Williams to just a one-year, $3 million deal . That’s looking like quite a bargain now. Williams is averaging 9.1 points, 2.3 rebounds, 1.7 assists, 1.2 steals, and 0.1 blocks per game in 2026-27 while shooting 53.8% from the field and 42.1% from beyond the arc. He has been the kind of athletic 3-and-D wing the Lakers have been crying out for in recent years. Williams also said in the offseason that Lakers fans can expect a lot of energy and hard work from him on the court . He has been true to his word and is becoming a fan favorite. With role players like Williams impressing and superstar guard Luka Doncic on a tear, the Lakers have gotten off to an excellent 15-3 start to the season. Not many expected them to have the best record in the NBA, but it has now been claimed that this is down to an easy schedule. Well, the Lakers will get a chance to make a statement as they take on the 15-4 San Antonio Spurs next at Frost Bank Center on Friday at 9:30 p.m. ET.

title: Knicks Get Double Dose of Great News After Crushing Cavaliers by 19 Points
summary: Injuries seemingly coming out of nowhere? No problem for the suddenly surging New York Knicks.The Knicks improved to 12-6 on the season after a dominant 19-point victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday, giving them a 2-1 season series lead over their East rival.New York has now rattled off 12 wins in the last 15 […] The post Knicks Get Double Dose of Great News After Crushing Cavaliers by 19 Points appeared first on HEAVY.
content: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - NOVEMBER 19: Jalen Brunson #11 of the New York Knicks looks on after the game against the Minnesota Timberwolves at Target Center on November 19, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) Getty Injuries seemingly coming out of nowhere? No problem for the suddenly surging New York Knicks. The Knicks improved to 12-6 on the season after a dominant 19-point victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers on Wednesday, giving them a 2-1 season series lead over their East rival. New York has now rattled off 12 wins in the last 15 games after dropping to 0-3 after a disappointing Oct. 25 home loss to the Orlando Magic. The Knicks have won six games in a row, tying them with the Boston Celtics for the second seed in the Eastern Conference. And best of all, the Knicks got a double dose of welcome news after handling the Cavs last night. Knicks Can Make NBA Cup History Getty New York Knicks’ head coach Mike Brown shouts instruciton to his team during the NBA basketball game between the New York Knicks and the Philadelphia 76ers at the Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi on October 2, 2025. (Photo by Giuseppe CACACE / AFP via Getty Images) After that 0-3 start, even winning the in-season tournament felt like it was thrown out the window. Suddenly, the Knicks find themselves still possessing a path to the NBA Cup’s knockout round . “After beating the Cavaliers 121-102 (more on this later) in group play on Wednesday night, New York moved to 1-2 and has a chance to become the first team since the NBA Cup started to advance to the knockout round with two losses,” wrote The Athletic’s James L. Edwards. “In order to do so, the Knicks would have to beat the Miami Heat on Friday by seven or more points while also needing the Philadelphia 76ers to lose to the Indiana Pacers. In the event those two things happen, the Knicks, 76ers, Pacers and Heat would all be 2-2 with wins over each other. Point differential would decide the winner. The Heat are currently plus-25 in group play. The Knicks are right behind them at plus-12, which is why a seven-point victory would allow New York to overtake Miami in East Group B.” Edwards noted that for the Knicks also have a path to advance as a wild card in the the NBA Cup, consisting of games that head coach Mike Brown says “adds a level of stress or whatever on your mind and body,” they would need “the Detroit Pistons to lose to the Milwaukee Bucks; the Toronto Raptors to lose to the Brooklyn Nets; the Atlanta Hawks to lose to the Boston Celtics; and New York would have to beat Miami by seven.” Mikal Bridges Coming Alive at the Right Time Getty NEW YORK, NEW YORK – NOVEMBER 21: Mikal Bridges #25 of the New York Knicks reacts after making the game winning three point shot during the fourth quarter against the Portland Trail Blazers at Madison Square Garden on November 21, 2026 in New York City. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) It’s nice for the Knicks knowing that they can do something no team ever has. But it is even cooler to think about the recent turnaround star forward Mikal Bridges has had. After a brutal start to the season, Bridges is starting to find his rhythm, and that is extremely welcome news for the Knicks, who need Bridges to step up while OG Anunoby is sidelined and stars Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart get back to full strength. Bridges answered the call last night, recording 19 points (17 in the first half) and playing a big role in his team’s blowout win over the Cavs. “As OG Anunoby missed his third straight game with a left calf strain, the Knicks are showing signs of missing him,” wrote Sports Illustrated’s Matthew Miranda. “They missed him as a tertiary scorer, though Mikal Bridges continued his renaissance doing yeoman’s work in that role, particularly pouring in 15 in the second quarter.” If Bridges keeps up his strong play, the Knicks, with a healthy roster, can continue climbing the standings as they remind the world why they are the defending champions. title: Knicks’ Mike Brown Called Out 1st-Round Pick Before Win
summary: The New York Knicks are leaning on young players lately. That includes Pacome Dadiet, though he got a talking-to from Mike Brown. The post Knicks’ Mike Brown Called Out 1st-Round Pick Before Win appeared first on HEAVY.
content: Pacome Dadiet #4 of the New York Knicks Getty Credit to Knicks coach Mike Brown for at least attempting to keep his team sparked and motivated through the doldrums of a post-championship NBA season, one in which players are simultaneously battling the difficulty of a title hangover while also keeping an eye on the big-picture problem of being paid long-term extensions by an owner who is intent on pinching nickels. He has deployed the end of the bench frequently in the early part of the year, hoping the energy there would jolt his veterans and, frequently, it has worked. He’s been doing it recently with 2024 NBA first-round pick Pacome Dadiet, who has mostly been a bust in the league, but who got 28 total minutes in the two games running up to Wednesday’s game against the Cavaliers, a 121-102 win. But Brown did not like what he was seeing from Dadiet in those two games. Here he was being given a chance to show his wares (he had played 18 total minutes the entire season before the last three games), and Brown felt his effort was lacking. Knicks Coach Gives Pacome Dadiet a Lesson Brown did not simply bench Dadiet. He warned him about his effort, pointed out that plenty of other Knicks can get those minutes, and gave him a chance to redeem himself on Thursday. He did–in 14 minutes, he was 3-for-7 shooting with two assists. More than that, Brown saw the effort he did not see earlier in the week. Said Brown: “I called him into my office and showed him some film this morning after shootaround and I told him, I said, ‘As a young guy, if you don’t play hard, I can’t play you. Believe me, I got a lot of guys I can go to and you know I am not afraid to go to someone else. The least you can do is play hard.’ I showed him how he wasn’t, and I thought tonight he did play hard.” Dadiet, speaking to Knicks reporters in the locker room after the game, said the lesson stuck. Said Dadiet: “You just got to take accountability, at the end of the day. He showed me some clips, it was clear, obvious. You just got to nod your head and keep going.” Pacôme Dadiet was asked about Mike Brown saying Dadiet isn’t playing as hard as he needs to be/showing him clips of it:"You just got to take accountability. He showed me some clips, it was clear, obvious. You just got to nod your head and keep going" pic.twitter.com/FiBbzp3CBk — Ian Begley (@IanBegley) November 26, 2026 The Knicks are off on Thanksgiving but return to play the Heat on Friday. title: Lakers coach JJ Redick wants to give rookie Cameron Carr more minutes
summary: Lakers rookie guard Cameron Carr likely deserves more playing time, but the challenge is how to find opportunities for him.
content: For the first time in several years, the Los Angeles Lakers have a fair amount of depth, especially at the gurd and wing spots. But having that type of depth also has a downside of sorts. Rookie guard Cameron Carr, the No. 24 pick in June's NBA draft, clearly has potential, and many fans have wanted him to get enough playing time to develop. That playing time has been hard to come by for him, but in the Lakers' last two games, he has gotten on the court for some decent slivers of time. On Friday against the Sacramento Kings, he played 12 minutes and shot 2-of-5 from the field to score five points. In Monday's win over the Utah Jazz, he got 10 minutes of playing time and scored nine points on 3-of-6 shooting. he has now made a 3-pointer in each of his last three games. Carr has apparently impressed coach JJ Redick enough to earn some real minutes, and Redick admitted that he has to find playing time for Carr, via Silver Screen and Roll . “Well, we have to look for opportunities to give Cam rotation minutes. With Austin out, I thought the last two games were opportunities for that,” Redick told reporters following the victory over Utah. “We’ve got to also get him, simultaneously, opportunities to get minutes and, with that, minutes where he can play through the mistakes.” The absence of Austin Reaves, who has been sidelined for the last five games with a heel bruise, has made it easier for Redick to find a way to fit Carr into his rotation a bit. But Reaves fully practiced on Wednesday and could be on track to return for the Lakers' showdown against the San Antonio Spurs on Friday, and that could make it difficult for Carr to get on the court. All in all, this is a good problem for the team to have. In past seasons, it would've had to throw Carr into the water and see if he would sink or swim. Now, they have the luxury of letting him get acclimated to the shallow end first. title: LaMelo Ball’s Injury Overshadows a Major Timberwolves Win
summary: The Minnesota Timberwolves left Oklahoma City with one of their biggest wins of the season. They also left with an […]
content: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Minnesota Timberwolves left Oklahoma City with one of their biggest wins of the season. They also left with an unsettling question about LaMelo Ball . The point guard injured his left ankle late in Wednesday’s 113-106 victory over the Thunder, giving a team already missing Anthony Edwards, Donte DiVincenzo and Jaylen Clark another reason to worry about its backcourt. Ball was hurt with 2:29 remaining in the fourth quarter, when he landed on Isaiah Hartenstein’s foot while defending near the basket. He went down in pain and needed help getting off the court before being evaluated near the Timberwolves’ bench. He eventually made his way to the locker room and did not return. After the game, coach Chris Finch had little information to share about the severity. “It looked pretty bad, but I’m not sure,” Finch told reporters . The Timberwolves had not announced a diagnosis or return timetable after the game. Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic reported that the team expected to examine Ball further after returning to Minneapolis. An encouraging sight, but no answers yet Nov 2, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves center Rudy Gobert (27) and guard LaMelo Ball (1) enjoy a moment after a break from action with the Milwaukee Bucks in the fourth quarter at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images The scene on the court was concerning, particularly for a player who has dealt with injuries to both ankles during his career. Ball initially struggled to put weight on his left foot, and his teammates had to continue a close game without their starting point guard. There was a more encouraging sight in the locker room afterward. Krawczynski noted that Ball was smiling, laughing and joking with teammates while icing his ankles. Ball did not speak to reporters. His mood was welcome news for a team hoping to avoid another extended absence, but it doesn’t establish the severity of the injury. Until the Timberwolves provide an update, it remains unclear whether Ball will miss time or be available for Friday’s NBA Cup game against Memphis. Ayo Dosunmu said his thoughts were with his teammate as soon as he saw Ball go down. “Just praying for him, hoping nothing’s too serious,” Dosunmu said . “I know he wants to be out there and compete.” Rudy Gobert expressed a similar hope, telling The Athletic that Ball means a lot to the team and that he hoped the guard would be back soon. Ball finished with 19 points, seven rebounds and eight assists in just under 29 minutes. He made five of his nine 3-point attempts and helped Minnesota recover after Oklahoma City built an 11-point lead. Minnesota closes without its point guard Nov 25, 2026; Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard Ayo Dosunmu (13) reacts after scoring against the Oklahoma City Thunder during the second half of a NBA Cup game at Paycom Center. Mandatory Credit: Alonzo Adams-Imagn Images The injury came at a difficult moment. Minnesota was protecting a one-point lead, on the road against a Thunder team that had already shown it could erase a deficit. Dosunmu took on more ball-handling responsibility after Ball’s exit. He scored on a driving layup and later knocked down a corner three after having a layup attempt blocked by Alex Caruso, helping the Wolves hold off Oklahoma City. Dosunmu finished with 16 points and four assists. Afterward, he said being prepared to adapt to different situations is part of his mindset. “For sure,” he said when asked whether he was ready to become the primary ballhandler. “Always being ready for anything.” Jaden McDaniels led Minnesota with 32 points, 10 rebounds and five assists, following his career-high 34-point performance against Brooklyn. He did it while spending much of the night defending Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, who also scored 32. The victory moved the Timberwolves to 14-5 overall and 3-0 in NBA Cup group play. With Memphis also winning Wednesday, Friday’s meeting between the Wolves and Grizzlies will decide West Group B and send the winner into the knockout stage. Another test for the backcourt Nov 23, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball (1) looks on against the Brooklyn Nets in the second half at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images Minnesota has already shown it can win while missing important players. Edwards has been sidelined since undergoing knee surgery, DiVincenzo is working his way back from an Achilles tear, and Clark is out with a hamstring strain. Ball has been central to the Wolves’ response. He started each of their first 19 games, giving Finch a primary creator who can push the pace, create shots for teammates and generate offense when possessions become difficult. If Ball needs time off, Dosunmu and Bones Hyland would be among the guards Minnesota could lean on more heavily. The Wolves would also need to determine how to fill Ball’s starting spot and distribute his playmaking responsibilities across the lineup. Finch acknowledged those questions after the win, including the possibility of activating two-way players, but said it was too early to provide answers. For now, the Wolves can take pride in finishing a demanding road win without their point guard. Their attention will quickly turn to what the examination reveals and whether Ball can join them for the next one. title: LeBron James Delivers Unforgettable Quote After Sixers Masterclass
summary: LeBron James no longer believes it is his job to dominate every night. Against the Miami Heat, the Philadelphia 76ers […]
content: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LeBron James no longer believes it is his job to dominate every night. Against the Miami Heat, the Philadelphia 76ers got a reminder of his career-long majesty. James scored 14 consecutive points in the second quarter, finished with 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds, and helped Philadelphia beat Miami 111-104 in Wednesday’s NBA Cup matchup. It was his first triple-double in a Sixers uniform and his best all-around performance since arriving in Philadelphia. The circumstances made it especially valuable. Joel Embiid missed a second straight game because of illness, while Jaylen Brown exited at the end of the first half with left hamstring tightness. Tyrese Maxey supplied a team-high 30 points, but James provided the stretch that gave Philadelphia control. Nov 25, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) controls the ball against the Miami Heat during the fourth quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Afterward, the 41-year-old explained how he views his place on a team that also features a former league MVP in Embiid, a Finals MVP in Brown and a star guard in Maxey. “I don’t think my job is to dominate the game every night for this ball club,” James said . “We have a Finals MVP, we have a regular-season MVP. We got an up-and-coming superstar point guard, a young fella in VJ who’s up and coming as well. “My dues is paid. … If they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, I can still accomplish that. But that’s not my job. I don’t think that’s my job, but if they need it, I can do it at any given moment.” Maxey had a response when he heard the cape line. “Dust it off then,” he shouted . Nov 25, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) talks with guard Vj Edgecombe (77) during the fourth quarter against the Miami Heat at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images James had already rekindled his unprecedented summer-of-2018 flair. His second-quarter run began with a three-point play and continued with three consecutive 3-pointers. After the third, a deep shot that sent the Philadelphia crowd into a frenzy, James headed back up the floor nodding his head as Miami called timeout. He then drove for a layup to complete the 14-point burst. The Sixers led for the rest of the game. James also found VJ Edgecombe for a long-distance alley-oop in the fourth quarter, another demonstration that his passing remains one of the most dangerous parts of his game. absolutely sensational. 🤯 pic.twitter.com/8wEUF9Yu4K — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) November 26, 2026 For much of his career, James was expected to produce nights like this as a matter of routine. That expectation helped define his greatness: He could carry an offense as a scorer, organize it as a passer and still have enough control over a game to find the play his team needed. The version in Philadelphia is different. James turns 42 on Dec. 30, and the physical decline that comes with age has been visible. He has not consistently beaten defenders off the dribble the way he once did, and his scoring and shooting have fluctuated. There have been nights when creating separation and finishing possessions looked harder than they did during his prime. James acknowledged that his body needs more time to get going than it once did. “The difference between the start of the season and now is that my legs are feeling better, my ramp-up is feeling better,” he said . “About to be 42 years old in a month. It takes a little bit longer for the ramp-up, but feeling pretty good as of late.” Nov 23, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) reacts after a play against the Portland Trail Blazers during the third quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images His recent shooting offers a glimpse of what that improvement has looked like. James went 4-for-6 from 3 against Miami after making four of five against Portland. He is 8-for-11 from deep over those two games, following a 10-for-46 start over his first 13 appearances. Two games do not establish a season-long turnaround, but they show how quickly his offense can change when the jumper falls. Even allowing for the decline, what James is doing at this age remains extraordinary. Wednesday was his sixth triple-double since turning 40; every other player in NBA history has combined for one after reaching that age. Miami coach Erik Spoelstra, who won two championships with James, offered his own assessment before facing him. “Father Time always wins,” Spoelstra said . “But right now, he’s giving Father Time hell.” Philadelphia’s roster should allow James to pick his moments more carefully than he could on teams that needed him to carry the scoring load every night. On Wednesday, with Embiid unavailable and Brown lost for the second half, the Sixers needed more from him and got a performance worthy of the player who has spent more than two decades dominating the league. James may no longer wear the cape every night. As Miami discovered, he still knows where to find it. title: LeBron James reacts to 1st 76ers triple-double after Cup win over Heat
summary: LeBron James reacts to his first triple-double with the Philadelphia 76ers after an NBA Cup win over the Miami Heat
content: PHILADELPHIA -- When LeBron James grabbed his 10th rebound, the Xfinity Mobile Arena crowd grew to a crescendo. The crowd knew it. The rebound clinched the first triple-double in a Philadelphia 76ers uniform for James and the 126th of his storied career as the Sixers knocked off the Miami Heat 111-104 in the NBA Cup. James finished with 25 points, 12 assists, and 10 rebounds including a hot stretch in the second quarter. He scored 14 in the second frame on a perfect 5-for-5 shooting and he knocked down a deep triple before playing to the crowd. The viral "LeBron, LeBron, LeBron" song played over the PA speakers and James had his signature moment in a Sixers uniform. "I'm just trying to play the game the right way," James said. "I don’t think my job is to dominate the game every night for this ball club. We have a finals MVP, we have a regular season MVP. We got an up and coming superstar point guard, a young fella in VJ who's up and coming as well. My dues is paid, and what I've done. If they need me to dust off the cape from time to time, I can still accomplish that, but that's not my job. I don't think that's my job, but they need it. I can do it at any given moment." To James' point, he doesn't have to be the man in Philadelphia. That's what Jaylen Brown, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey, and VJ Edgecombe are for, but when James has to dust off the cape and be that guy he's been his entire career, he can do so. The 3-point shooting, especially, was something to behold against the Heat. He shot 4-for-6 from deep on the night for a guy who entered shooting only 27.5% from deep on the season. "Just the work," James said of his shooting. "The work I've been putting in throughout my career. I've shot over, I don't know, how many over 10,000 reps, you know? So, like, it's not—the work has been put in, and I'm not ever worried about anything part of my game." The difference for James is just reps and getting his legs underneath him. He may still be a terrific player and somebody who impacts the game in a number of ways, but at the end of the day, James is still 41 years old and will turn 42 on Dec. 30. Getting into a rhythm takes a bit longer than it did in his earlier days. "The difference between, you know, the start of the season and now is that I’m feeling better, ramp up is feeling better," James laughed. "I’m about to be 42 years old in a month. (Expletive), it takes a little bit longer for the ramp up, but feeling pretty good as of late. I'll never be second guessing myself or whatever case may be because I know the work I put in." James and the Sixers will take on the Indiana Pacers to finish the NBA Cup on Friday. content: The Charlotte Hornets fell to the Chicago Bulls Wednesday night 107-105, going 0-4 in NBA Cup Group Play in Eastern Conference Group C with a point-differential of -71. title: Stan Van Gundy changes tune on Miami Heat: 'I think they're legitimate contenders'
summary: Stan Van Gundy changes tune on Miami Heat: 'I think they're legitimate contenders'
content: It only took a month for Stan Van Gundy to change his view on the new-look Miami Heat . Even after Wednesday night’s 111-104 loss to the Philadelphia 76ers at Xfinity Mobile Arena that ended Miami’s winning streak at seven games, the Heat has still won 10 of its last 13 games following an 0-4 start to the season. “I think they’re legitimate contenders,” Van Gundy said to the Miami Herald. “I wouldn’t have put them there. content: Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images Stephen Curry is set for a crucial injury re-evaluation as the Golden State Warriors look for clarity on when their superstar could return to action. The four-time NBA champion has been sidelined since suffering an oblique abdominal tear during the Warriors’ 115-108 defeat to the Houston Rockets. According to ESPN’s Anthony Slater, Curry will undergo his next medical assessment as Golden State continue to navigate life without their leading scorer. Stephen Curry injury update gives Golden State Warriors important recovery checkpoint Curry suffered the injury early against Houston, leaving the game with 6:25 remaining in the first quarter after experiencing discomfort in his right abdominal area. An MRI subsequently confirmed an oblique tear, with the Warriors initially ruling him out for at least two weeks. Friday’s re-evaluation will offer a clearer picture of his recovery, although it does not automatically mean he will be cleared to return. Before his injury, Curry was enjoying another excellent campaign, averaging 27.8 points, 3.9 assists and 3.7 rebounds across 10 games. He was also shooting 50 per cent from the field and 45.7 per cent from three-point range. His absence has exposed just how much Golden State rely on his offensive production, with Steve Kerr admitting the team need to make adjustments. Speaking on the Tom Tolbert Show, the Warriors coach acknowledged that their previous approach placed too much responsibility on Curry. “We’ve recognized that the way we were running our offense was too Steph-dependent, and so we’ve tweaked a few things,” Kerr said. The numbers underline that problem, with Golden State recording a plus/minus of +45.5 per game with Curry this season compared to -53.8 without him. The Warriors have also been without Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody, while Kristaps Porzingis has stepped away from basketball because of an illness. Golden State did manage to beat the Boston Celtics 88-87 after a difficult five-game road losing streak, but they still need Curry back if they are to compete consistently in the Western Conference. His assessment should provide an important indication of the next stage of his recovery, with the Warriors keen to avoid rushing their franchise cornerstone back before he is ready. (Photo by Joshua Gateley/Getty Images) Getty On Wednesday, the Minnesota Timberwolves did what only the Indiana Pacers have done to the Oklahoma City Thunder over the last three seasons. With a 113-106 win in Oklahoma City, Minnesota is just the second team since the 2023-24 season with a winning record against the Thunder. Last night, the Wolves improved to 14-5 on the season, placing them just one game behind the second-seeded San Antonio Spurs. While the win was important, the bigger takeaway was LaMelo Ball’s health. In the closing minutes of Wednesday’s game, Ball, who was acquired in the offseason from the Charlotte Hornets, appeared to injure his ankle after contesting a shot attempt from Oklahoma City’s Alex Caruso. Timberwolves Suffer Potential Injury Setback in Win Getty OKLAHOMA CITY, OKLAHOMA – NOVEMBER 25: LaMelo Ball #1 of the Minnesota Timberwolves handles the ball during the second half against the Oklahoma City Thunder at Paycom Center on November 25, 2026 in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. (Photo by Joshua Gateley/Getty Images) Ball landed awkwardly on his left ankle with 2:39 left to play in regulation. The 25-year-old held his ankle in pain as he stayed on the ground for a while. Ball was eventually helped to the locker room. After the game, Wolves head coach Chris Finch raised alarm when asked about Ball’s injury. “It looked pretty bad, but I’m not sure,” Finch said after his team’s win in Paycom Center, according to Wolves broadcaster Alan Horton. Ball has been crucial to the Wolves’ success without star guard Anthony Edwards, who is expected to be sidelined at least several more weeks as he recovers from a knee injury. In Edwards’ absence, Ball has led the Wolves to an impressive 11-4 record, with the star guard averaging 18.0 points, 5.0 rebounds and 5.6 assists per game. But Minnesota’s top player in Wednesday’s win was forward Jaden McDaniels, who shined with 32 points just two nights after recording a career-high 34 points in a win over the Brooklyn Nets. If Ball is forced to miss time, McDaniels will step into a considerably increased role. Wolves React to Ball’s Injury While there is no official update on Ball’s injury as of Thursday morning, Wolves insider Jon Krawczynski noted that Ball appeared to be doing well after the team defeated the Thunder. “Once the Wolves locker room opened to media after a 113-106 victory over the Thunder, Ball was all smiles,” Krawczynski reported for The Athletic. “The Timberwolves did not give an update on his injury, expecting to give it further examination after returning home to Minneapolis. But Ball was as animated as ever, laughing and joking with his teammates while he iced both ankles. If his demeanor is any indicator of the severity of the injury, he may have avoided a worst-case scenario.” Said Wolves guard Ayo Dosunmu, who recorded 16 points, four assists and four 3-pointers in the seven-point win: “I’m just praying for him, hoping nothing is too serious, hoping he’s able to shake back like I know he would. I know that he wants to be out there and compete.” Ball was critical in Wednesday’s game, where the Wolves trailed by as many as 11 points in an arena that has not been kind to opponents in recent years. Ball registered 19 points and cashed five of nine 3-point attempts. Now, the Wolves await the official word on Ball’s injury. title: Today in Boston Celtics history: Bradley born; West debut; Douglas trade
summary: Today in Boston Celtics history, Avery Antonio Bradley was born in Tacoma, Washington in 1990.
content: Today in Boston Celtics history, Avery Antonio Bradley was born in Tacoma, Washington in 1990. Bradley played his college ball with the University of Texas Longhorns before he was picked up by the Celtics with the 19th overall selection of the 2010 NBA Draft, beginning his NBA career with his name on the injured list due to surgery on his ankle. The Texas alum was soon a meaningful part of the team's backcourt rotation once he was able to get back on the court. The defensive specialist joined a ball club with hopes for contending for an NBA title, and holding his own while he did it. Over the course of seven seasons with Boston, the Tacoma native racked up two All-Defensive team honors. He was dealt to the Detroit Pistons at the end of the 2016-17 NBA season to make room for the signing of veteran forward Gordon Hayward's contract with the Celtics. Bradley averaged 12.1 points, 3.1 rebounds, 1.7 assists, and 1.1 steals per game with Boston. Debuts It is also the date of former Boston guard Delonte West's debut with the team. An alumnus of St. Joseph's University, West was selected by Boston with the 24th overall pick of the 2004 NBA Draft. The Washington, District of Columbia native played his inaugural game for the team in a 98-96 loss to the Cleveland Cavaliers that same year. West scored 7 points, 1 rebound, and as many assists in just nine minutes of floor time. Transactions Finally, it was also on this date that fellow D.C. native Sherman Douglas was traded to the Milwaukee Bucks for Alton Lister and Todd Day in 1995. The former Syracuse point guard played parts of 5 seasons with the Celtics, averaging 11.1 points, 2.2 rebounds, and 6.8 assists per game with the team over that stretch. "I haven't paid much attention (to Milwaukee)," said Douglas at the time of the trade via the A.P. "But I know they have two great players. I like their chances. I think they'll be right there. title: Updated 2026 NBA Cup West Group B standings after Thunder lose to Timberwolves
summary: Updated 2026 NBA Cup West Group B standings after Oklahoma City Thunder lose to Minnesota Timberwolves.
content: For the first time since its invention, the Oklahoma City Thunder will not participate in the knockout stage of the 2026 NBA Cup. Their 113-106 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves on Wednesday ensured that wouldn't be the case. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander tried his best to do a one-man carry job with 32 points and five assists. Heck, Ajay Mitchell pitched in with an efficient 25 points. But the Thunder came up short in the clutch once again. The Timberwolves were led by Jaden McDaniels' 32 points and 10 rebounds. This was OKC's last leg of the 2026 NBA Cup West Group B play. Every team played four games throughout November as part of that. Here's a look at the finalized mid-season tournament standings: 1. Minnesota Timberwolves 3-0, plus-39 point differential 2. Memphis Grizzlies 2-1, plus-18 point differential 3. Oklahoma City Thunder 2-2, plus-29 point differential 4. LA Clippers 1-2, minus-43 point differential 5. New Orleans Pelicans 0-3, minus-43 point differential As a reminder, there are six groups of five teams for the NBA Cup — three in each conference. At the end of the month, all six group winners, plus two top wildcard teams, will advance to an eight-team knockout stage. The higher-seeded team will host in the quarterfinals and semifinals. The finals will be played in Indiana at Butler's collegiate home gym. A bunch of money is tied up in the NBA Cup rewards. The quarterfinal losers will receive an additional $53K per player; the semifinal losers will receive $106K per player; the finals loser will receive $212K per player; and the NBA Cup winner will receive $530K per player. The Thunder had finished in the top four in the last two years. They lost to the Milwaukee Bucks in the 2024 NBA Cup finals and lost to the San Antonio Spurs in the 2025 NBA Cup semifinals. Both happened in Las Vegas — when those rounds were still hosted there. title: NFL honors John Madden with Thanksgiving-themed coins, Madden uniform patch for Thursday slate
summary: In the years since Madden's death in 2021, the league has continued to celebrate the broadcaster's connection to the holiday.
content: Five years after the death of John Madden, the NFL is keeping the memory of the broadcaster's connection to Thanksgiving alive. The league announced last week that a Madden coin, featuring Madden's silhouette on one side and a six-legged “turducken” (a chicken stuffed in a duck, stuffed in a turkey) on the other, will be used for coin flips for the three NFL games on Thanksgiving Day. All players in those games — Detroit Lions-Chicago Bears , Dallas Cowboys-Philadelphia Eagles and Buffalo Bills-Kansas City Chiefs — will wear patches on their uniforms with the Madden silhouette. The Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers, who played on Wednesday (or "Thanksgiving Eve," as the league calls it), also wore the patches. Stencils honoring Madden will be placed in the end zones and along the sidelines of the three home fields during the matchup, and panels on the stadium wall will feature Madden in his coaching days with the Oakland Raiders. Today’s NFL games will each feature an exclusive John Madden Thanksgiving-themed coin for the pregame coin flip 🪙 Teams will also wear a corresponding patch of Madden’s silhouette on their jerseys 👤 pic.twitter.com/CsK9COHVWc — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) November 26, 2026 Along with those Madden-themed additions, the MVP of each game will receive a trophy fashioned to look like a turkey leg-football amalgamation. The Thanksgiving MVPs will also earn a $10,000 donation from the NFL Foundation to a high school or youth football program in their name. 5th annual John Madden Thanksgiving Celebration takes place NEXT week across the @NFL ! Each of the 3 Thanksgiving Day games will feature the following: 🏈Commemorative coin w/ a silhouette of Coach Madden on one side & a Turducken on the reverse 🏈Jersey patch of Coach Madden… pic.twitter.com/0HeUO5JLIx — NFL Media (@NFLMedia) November 20, 2026 Madden, one of the defining figures of the sport as both a coach and broadcaster, died in 2021 at the age of 85 . Alongside longtime broadcasting partner Pat Summerall, Madden called NFL games for decades on CBS and later Fox, becoming associated with Thanksgiving games thanks to his enthusiasm for turduckens and turkey legs. The league first introduced the specialized Madden patches and coins in 2023, two years after the football legend's death, and have continued the tradition over the past few years.

title: 4 predictions for Kansas City Chiefs vs. Buffalo Bills in Week 12
summary: Take a look at our staff predictions for the Kansas City Chiefs' matchup against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving Day in Week 12.
content: The Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills are set to face off in a highly anticipated Thanksgiving Day showdown at Highmark Stadium that could be one of the best games of the 2026 NFL regular season. Both teams are competing for the top spot in the AFC and the winner of today's holiday showdown is likely to have a key advantage in playoff seeding — which could help them punch a ticket to Super Bowl LXI in February. Take a look at our staff predictions for Kansas City's matchup against Buffalo: Ed Easton Jr.'s prediction The Kansas City Chiefs face their biggest challenge of the season on Thanksgiving, with a chance to take control of the AFC and defeat a longtime rival. The offense will be tested by the weather conditions expected at kickoff and whether Patrick Mahomes will try to pass through them. The running game will be the focus once again, with Emmett Johnson starting in place of Kenneth Walker for a third consecutive game. Andy Reid's offensive creativity will be key to the offense's progress. Defensively, the Chiefs will need to contain the running game, including Josh Allen's improvisation and James Cook's consistency. The passing game could still be a factor, but it will be chaotic, especially if the defensive line continues to set the pace over the last few weeks. The low-scoring contest could call for a clutch field goal attempt in bad weather for Harrison Butker. Final score: Chiefs 13, Bills 10 Sam Teets' prediction In terms of physical ability, Josh Allen stands alone atop the current quarterback hierarchy. However, the usually turnover-adverse former MVP has thrown interceptions in four straight games, including two last week against Miami’s struggling secondary. Mansoor Delane’s return to form positions Kansas City to take advantage of Allen’s recent turnover tendencies. Bills running back James Cook enters Thanksgiving weekend with rushing scores in nine consecutive games. Rookie defensive tackle Peter Woods is listed as questionable. His return would reinforce a thin interior that is still holding strong by only surrendering 95.5 rushing yards per game. The Bills have one of the stingiest defenses, only allowing 20.8 points per game. Part of that is because the defense ranks among the top ten in turnovers forced through 11 weeks. Patrick Mahomes needs to play a clean game while his offensive tackles find a way to deal with Greg Rousseau. Expect heavy doses of Josh Downs and Emmett Johnson. Final score : Chiefs 27, Bills 24 Jon Ediger's prediction The Kansas City Chiefs play their biggest game of the season on Thanksgiving Day as they look to tie the Buffalo Bills for the AFC's best record. This week's matchup is expected to be cold and wet, so expect both teams to lean on the run game. Running back Kenneth Walker is out for the third straight game with a groin injury, but Emmett Johnson has proven himself more than capable of stepping up in his place. Johnson will receive a heavy workload on Thursday and could be the difference-maker in what will likely be a low-scoring game. Like the Bills, Kansas City's defense will also need to focus on stopping the run. Quarterback Josh Allen is one of the NFL's best scramblers, and running back James Cook is the AFC's leading rusher. Both Allen and Cook can make life miserable for the Chiefs' front seven if they can't contain the ground game. This game will be a far cry from the aerial shootout we've come to expect from a Mahomes-Allen showdown. Final score: Chiefs 24, Bills 20 John Dillon's prediction These teams are so well-matched, but I have a hard time believing that Kansas City will secure a win over Buffalo without arguably its best offensive player in Kenneth Walker III. Don't get me wrong, I think that the Chiefs will put up a good fight at Highmark Stadium, and I expect the final score will be relatively close, but Kansas City's inability to keep its star rusher on the field will ultimately doom the team to failure in this Thanksgiving Day showdown. This week, I'll predict that Steve Spagnuolo's defense will keep Josh Allen and the Bills in check until the fourth quarter, but ultimately come up short on a goal line stand that sends the Buffalo crowd home happy. While I still think that the Chiefs will win an eventual playoff rematch against the Bills, I'm not sure Kansas City has what it takes to earn its ninth win without Walker. Final score: Chiefs 12, Bills 14 This article originally appeared on Chiefs Wire: 4 predictions for Kansas City Chiefs vs. Buffalo Bills in Week 12

title: 5 Bills to watch vs. Chiefs
summary: Buffalo can take a commanding lead in the AFC with a win on Thursday
content: The Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs in the Thanksgiving nightcap this year, and what a game it should be. The 9-1 Bills are the current No. 1 seed in the AFC playoff picture. Thanks to tiebreakers, the 8-2 Chiefs trail the 8-2 Denver Broncos in the AFC West, so Kansas City is currently the No. 5 seed in the conference. However, a win over the Bills would go a long way towards ensuring that the AFC playoffs run through Arrowhead Stadium. The Bills are coming off a sloppy divisional win over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. The Chiefs, on the other hand, thoroughly thrashed the Arizona Cardinals. Kansas City has won three games in a row; Buffalo has won six consecutive games. Unless there’s a tie, someone is going to take a loss for the first time in a long time this week. If Buffalo wants to emerge with a win over their bitter conference rival, they’ll need some big performances from their key players. While everyone wants to talk about the quarterbacks in this game, we’re intentionally leaving both Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes out of the columns this week. Those two are pretty obvious. There are plenty of other players worthy of mention, though. Here are five Bills to watch in this critical AFC contest. _____________________________________________________________________________ RB James Cook III Regardless of the weather, Cook is a tremendous key to Buffalo’s success. After a slow start on Sunday, Cook extended his streak of scoring at least one touchdown and rushing for at least 75 yards to nine games, which is a new NFL record. He had previously shared the record at eight games with John Rigging and LaDainian Tomlinson. Cook surpassed the 1,000-yard rushing mark for the fourth consecutive season, and he joins two Hall of Fame former Bills in Thurman Thomas and O.J. Simpson as the only players to achieve that feat in franchise history. The sledding won’t be easy against an outstanding Kansas Cigy tush defense that allows just 3.7 yards per carry on the season, but in a game that’s set to feature horrendous weather, finding space and keeping the offense ahead of the sticks will be of the utmost importance. TE Dalton Kincaid It’s something we’ve said ever since the Bills made Kincaid their first-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. When the big tight end is healthy, Josh Allen’s life is much easier. When he doesn’t play, Allen doesn’t have nearly as much space to operate in the passing game. Last week, Allen threw for 304 yards without Kincaid, but it took 45 passing attempts and some ugly possessions to hit that milestone. If Kincaid is healthy, it gives the Bills their full cadre of pass-catchers against an elite defensive unit. Allen’s quarterback rating when targeting Kincaid was 149.2 last season. Since Kincaid joined the club, Allen has a passer rating of 99.9 with Kincaid in the lineup and 91.2 without him. Allen averages 237 passing yards per game with Kincaid in the lineup; he averages 206 passing yards per game without him. He has thrown 77 touchdowns against 29 interceptions in 47 games with Kincaid, and he’s thrown 14 touchdowns against 9 interceptions in the ten games Kincaid has missed in his career. No. 86 is a big part of Buffalo’s offense, and having him on Thursday will go a long way towards helping the Bills earn a victory. OLB Bradley Chubb Greg Rousseau is obvious. Someone else has to offer some juice in the pass rush, and while I’m tempted to spotlight rookie T.J. Parker, I think it has to be the veteran edge rusher to come in and make a play. Chubb has been pretty quiet this season, totaling just 1.5 sacks, 10 quarterback hits and 14 pressures while playing on 69% of the Bills’ defensive snaps. With the Miami Dolphins last season coming off an ACL injury, Chubb totaled 8.5 sacks, 22 pressures, and 20 quarterback hits. No matter how many good things the Bills have to say about him, they definitely expected more when they handed him a three-year deal worth $43.5 million this offseason. I expect that the Chiefs will look to double-team Rousseau, and they’ll likely leave Chubb blocked by one man. Chubb has to win that matchup and impact Patrick Mahomes in some way. DL Deone Walker The big fella doesn’t have a quarterback hit or a takcle for loss since before the bye week. He has just one sack, which he notched against C.J. Stroud during Buffalo’s Week One win over the Houston Texans. Sure, the job of the nose takcle involves doing a lot of “lunch pail” work that often goes unnoticed, but I would love to see Walker collapsing the pocket on Mahomes from the interior in the way that we’ve had to watch Chris Jones collapse the pocket on Josh Allen from the defensive tackle spot so many times over the years. Thursday night would be a nice time for Walker to dominate. It would be a great addition to his burgeoning resume in what has been a very good second professional season. S Cole Bishop With the defense settling down over the last month, defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard can really start to use his chess pieces to their athletic strengths. Bishop can operate at every level of the defense for the Bills, and I would love to see Leonhard deploy him in a variety of ways. Use him to guard Travis Kelce. Use him as a deep-third centerfielder when Mahomes expects newly-acquired Amani Hooker to pkay that role. Use him as a blitzer off the edge to create pressure on the run game and the pass game. Bishop is an elite athlete who is allowing a career-low 55.8% of the passes thrown while he’s the closest man in coverage to be completed. Bishop has a chance to be eating a turkey leg on National television after this one because he can change the game in a variety of ways. Look for him to notch his first interception of the season while also collecting his second sack of the season at some point in this game.

title: Aaron Glenn Is Taking This Jets Dolphins Revenge Game Personally
summary: New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn is taking this Miami Dolphins rematch opportunity personally in Week 12. The post Aaron Glenn Is Taking This Jets Dolphins Revenge Game Personally appeared first on HEAVY.
content: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - OCTOBER 25: Head Coach Aaron Glenn of the New York Jets and Head Coach Jeff Hafley of the Miami Dolphins embrace after the game at MetLife Stadium on October 25, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) Getty This is the first revenge game opportunity of the season for the New York Jets. A chance for redemption against an opponent the Jets have already played, the Miami Dolphins. It sounds like head coach Aaron Glenn is taking this one personally. During his opening statement to the media, Glenn went out of his way to deliver a message. “Other than that, when it comes to this game, the one thing that sticks out in my mind is this team came down in our building and they punched us in the mouth in the first quarter, and it wasn’t good. I still feel the effects of that. In the second half though, our guys came out and they played their (expletive) off and we look forward to going down there, starting this game off on the right foot and our guys will be ready to play,” Glenn responded. ESPN’s Rich Cimini, after the press conference, said, “It’s unusual for Glenn to take this approach. He usually stays in the present and refrains from using the past for motivation. But he’s not wrong; the Jets did get punched in the mouth by the then-winless Dolphins.” Felt Like the Beginning of the End Glenn didn’t use this word, but he might as well have: embarrassing. On Sunday, October 25, it felt like a do-or-die game for Glenn. The Jets were hosting, at the time, a winless Dolphins team that had never held a lead to that point in any game this season. There were no excuses for Glenn, who entered that game 2-4; you had to win. Not only did he not win, but the Dolphins, who, to reiterate, had not held a lead all season, got the ball first and immediately took it 76 yards in seven plays to take a 7-0 lead over the Jets. It was a sign of things to come. The Jets lost 28-25, and the season felt lost. I host a daily Jets video talk show on YouTube called “Boy Green Daily.” The majority of Jets fans who either call into my show or leave comments told me that was the final nail in the coffin for Glenn. Anyone who still held out hope that he could turn this ship around abandoned ship after that loss. For what it’s worth, Cimini believes there is still a path for Glenn to save his job. “If the Jets split their last 6 games, 3-3, & finish with 6 wins, I’m sorry, Jake [Asman], I think there’d probably be a pretty good chance that [Aaron Glenn] would be coming back with a 6-11 record,” Cimini revealed on the “Jets Collective” podcast. . @RichCimini said if the #Jets "split their last 6 games, 3-3, & finish with 6 wins, I'm sorry @JakeAsman , I think there'd probably be a pretty good chance that [Aaron Glenn] would be coming back with a 6-11 record." @BrandonTierney explained why he is a little open to seeing… pic.twitter.com/SbSR7O5gX9 — Jets Collective (@NYJetsHMA) November 25, 2026 Jets Are Battling Against History The Jets haven’t beaten the Dolphins in Miami since December 28, 2014. That was 12 years ago. The Jets have lost 10 in a row in Miami when playing the Dolphins. Interestingly, Geno Smith was the Jets’ quarterback in that game, and Rex Ryan was his head coach. It was an amazing performance by Smith, one of the best of his career. The former West Virginia product had the perfect cast. He completed 20-of-25 passes for 358 passing yards with three touchdowns and zero interceptions. Smith had a perfect 158.3 quarterback rating. Smith was asked about that performance during his media availability this week. “That was so long ago man. So long ago. It was a good day that day and we have to focus on this game and take it one step at a time,” Smith responded. title: Aidan Hutchinson Update: Lions Star Out vs. Bears on Thanksgiving and for the Season After Tearing His ACL Celebrating a Sack
summary: The Detroit Lions have established themselves as one of the strongest teams in the NFL this season, improving to 8-2 while extending their winning streak to six games. However, their impressive run has been marred by a significant setback on the defensive side: Aidan Hutchinson’s injury.
content: What Happened to Aidan Hutchinson, and When Will He Return? Latest on Lions Star’s Injury and Why He’s Out in Week 12 vs. Bears on Thanksgiving The Detroit Lions have established themselves as one of the strongest teams in the NFL this season, improving to 8-2 while extending their winning streak to six games. However, their impressive run has been marred by a significant setback on the defensive side: Aidan Hutchinson’s injury. The Lions are preparing for the Thanksgiving game against the Chicago Bears, with first place in the NFC North on the line. While Dan Campbell’s squad will look to maintain its momentum, Hutchinson’s absence is significant due to his impact as a pass rusher. What Happened to Aidan Hutchinson? Hutchinson suffered a torn ACL in his right knee during Detroit’s win over the New England Patriots in Munich. The injury occurred during the first quarter when he celebrated a sack against Drake Maye. Hutchinson had brought down Maye on New England’s opening drive and jumped into the air to celebrate the play, but he landed awkwardly and immediately went down. He did not return to the game and was later spotted leaving the stadium on crutches. Further medical examinations confirmed that he had torn his right ACL. That is why Hutchinson will remain unavailable for Detroit’s Week 12 game against the Bears. When will Aidan Hutchinson return? Hutchinson will miss the remainder of this season, and there is no confirmed return date, as his recovery depends on his rehabilitation progress and medical clearance. ACL injuries generally require several months of recovery, but the timeline can vary. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator The Lions lost more than an ordinary defensive starter in Hutchinson, as he has established himself as one of the NFL’s most disruptive edge rushers, recording 49 career sacks. He was selected by the Lions with the No. 2 pick in the 2022 NFL Draft. According to TruMedia, Hutchinson recorded a 17.0% pressure rate among edge rushers since the 2025 season. He ranks No. 17 in the PFN EDGE Impact with an 82.2 grade. Losing a player capable of producing at that level creates additional responsibilities for the remaining members of Detroit’s defensive line, but the Lions have shown that they can still generate pressure without Hutchinson. In the Tampa Bay Buccaneers game, Detroit’s pass rush recorded four sacks against Baker Mayfield. That performance offered some hope for Campbell’s defense, but replacing Hutchinson’s overall production remains a difficult challenge. The Lions head coach himself addressed the losses of Hutchinson and Jack Campbell. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor “When you have guys like Hutch and Jack Campbell, the talent speaks for itself,” Campbell told former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Bill Cowher in his CBS interview. “The production speaks for itself. Of course, that’s a huge loss as it pertains to competitive football. “But when you’re around these guys, and you draft them, and you’ve been with them for four years, five years, and you see the growth. They were puppies when they came in, and now they’re full-grown dogs. They’re on the hunt nonstop.” The Lions will look to keep up their dominance against the Bears, who are on a five-game winning streak. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: Amon-Ra St. Brown has his say on Jameson Williams’ backflip celebration after controversy
summary: Amon-Ra St. Brown has backed Jameson Williams’ decision to continue doing flips as part of his celebrations after a touchdown.
content: Photo by Nic Antaya/Getty Images Amon-Ra St. Brown has backed Jameson Williams’ decision to continue doing flips as part of his celebrations after a touchdown. Following the injury to the Detroit Lions’ star defensive lineman, Aidan Hutchinson, head coach Dan Campbell asked players to stop celebrating by doing a backflip. A week after the injury, Jameson Williams scored a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and hit a front flip. Campbell went on 97.1 The Ticket Show to give his take on what he felt about Williams’ celebration. “Well, I said no backflips,” Campbell said. “Listen, I’ve got a million things going on. We’re trying to get this stuff schemed up and make sure that we’re right with everything, but no, all good.” Overall, Williams had a great game against the Bucs, as he recorded 4 receptions for 93 yards. His TD came from a 57-yard pass from quarterback Jarred Goff. Amon- Ra St. Brown explains why Jameson Williams should continue celebrating the way he wants Amon-Ra St. Brown is himself known for his creative celebrations after a touchdown. Even in the game against the Bucs, the wide receiver had his own celebration that went viral online. The 27-year-old has also done the backflip celebration in the past, which is why he did not have a problem with his teammate doing it. “I love it. I love Jamo. Keep celebrating, Jamo. Don’t let anyone tell you different. I mean, at the end of the day, look, everyone’s going to say something if you get hurt doing anything. It’s like, ‘Oh, you should have done this.’ But being an athlete, that’s all I’ve got to say. Just be an athlete. Know what you can and can’t do. Know your limits. And Jamo’s been flipping for a long time, so I’ve got nothing to say to Jamo, man. Keep being you,” said the Lions WR on the St. Brown podcast. On social media, Williams’ front flip was widely discussed as his landing was not the cleanest. Fans would definitely not want another player to be ruled out due to an injury while celebrating. With the Lions already having suffered a serious injury, their hope is that Williams moves to a safer celebration, but it remains to be seen if he changes his ways and finds something different. title: Arizona Cardinals must make commitment to experienced coaching staff
summary: A look at the Cardinals' inexeprienced coaching staff and its impact on player development.
content: When Arizona Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur spoke to the media Monday, shortly after news broke about the firing of defensive coordinator Nick Rallis, the questions addressed many levels of the decision made with six games remaining in the season and the schedule being less daunting than the first 11 games. It came amid consistent outside noise about the draft results with Monti Ossenfort as general manager since 2023 and the apparent lack of development, especially among defensive players selected in the first three rounds. Never mind that the 17 players selected in the first three rounds have missed 227 games because of injuries and that all except quarterback Carson Beck and cornerback Max Melton have spent a total of 22 times on injured reserve. The Cardinals currently have eight of those players on injured reserve or physically unable to perform. Those absences result in significant losses of talent and continuity, something that is difficult to achieve in the NFL, but yet remains gravely important in the development of a roster. When LaFleur was asked about the apparent lack of development in high defensive draft choices and the reason for that, his answer was notable as much for what he didn’t say as for what he said: “Not yet, but searching for those solutions. We have to coach better. We have to get these guys (to) perform at the level that we know that they're capable of because they want to. These guys are made of the right stuff. We have the right guys in that locker room. We have good dudes that want to do right. We have to get it out of them.” What he didn’t say was whether the right assistant coaches are also present. They might be, but it’s hard to judge after 11 games on a staff that has 10 coaches in their first season with the Cardinals, including six who are first-time NFL coaches. Three first-time Cardinals are position coaches on defense, including NFL first-timer Zac Etheridge (cornerbacks). Outside linebackers coach Matt Feeney and defensive backs coach Cristian Garcia are the only holdovers from Jonathan Gannon’s last staff, but Garcia was the linebackers coach in 2025. Consider this: defensive lineman Darius Robinson has had a different line coach in each of his three seasons. In defensive lineman Dante Stills’ four seasons, he’s had three position coaches. Defensive lineman Walter Nolen III and cornerback Will Johnson (now on IR) have had two position coaches in their two Arizona seasons. LaFleur also said something notable after being asked about simplifying things on defense where it’s been theorized that Rallis’ defense asked too much of younger players. He said, “That's the easy ... I mean it's always, 'Hey, get back to the fundamentals. Simplify things.' You get real simple against a real good defense and find out what happens too. And I say that respectfully, but there is a balance there.” He then got to the heart of the matter, saying, “You watched the Niners last night (against the Vikings) and a lot of guys there have been doing a lot of things for about 10-plus years now and a quarterback that has really fit pretty well into that system for them and just gotten better through time. We're not there yet for numerous reasons, but I'm interested in building those habits and building those foundations so that when that time is there, we're able to make the plays in those big-time games.” There’s the rub. A lack of continuity in coaching has been the hallmark of more than a century of Cardinals football, whether it was in Chicago, St. Louis or Arizona. I won’t get too deep or far back into the weeds here, while nonetheless pointing out that only two Cardinals head coaches (Jim Hanifan and Ken Whisenhunt) have lasted six seasons. Bruce Arians is the all-time leader with a mere 50 victories. The 49ers have had six head coaches with 100 or more games in their shorter history, led by Kyle Shanahan’s 174, while Whisenhunt is the only Cardinal that reached 100 (102), including playoff games. Three 49ers head coaches, including Shanahan have at least 100 career victories. He hit that milestone Monday night. Sticking to more recent history, LaFleur is the fifth Cardinals head coach since 2017, the same year Shanahan and Sean McVay ( Rams ) were hired. The Seahawks have two: Pete Carroll and Mike MacDonald. Most important is the decidedly different approach to building a staff compared to the Cardinals. The rarely talked about process of head coaches being hired in the NFL is the commitment from the organization to provide an ample budget for assistants. The latest results are not new; it’s a pattern from an organization that within the last decade, according to sources, fired two assistants to be able to pay an experienced coach and then paid less to the replacements. Here’s a snapshot of the staffs of the division rivals on offense and defense: 49ers : 21 coaches, 10 with at least 10 years of NFL experience (222 years total) and three with 10-plus in San Francisco (32). Of those 21, there are three offensive assistants and three handling defensive quality control. They also have: Assistant head coach Chris Foerster, also offensive line Offensive run game coordinator Joe Graves Offensive pass game coordinator Leonard Hankerson, also wide receivers Assistant head coach/defense Matt Eberflus Defensive run game coordinator Johnny Holland Defensive pass game coordinator Jerry Gray Longtime coaches Eberflus and Gray are two of the four first-time 49ers along with veteran defensive coordinator Raheem Morris and defensive quality control coach Angel Matute, also a first-time NFL assistant, the only one on their staff. Rams: 22 coaches, nine with at least 10 years of NFL experience (151 years total) and three with 10-plus in Los Angeles (30). They also have: Assistant head coach Kliff Kingsbury Associate offensive coordinator Dave Ragone, also quarterbacks Senior offensive assistant Eric Yarber, also wide receivers Defensive run game coordinator Giff Smith, also defensive line Defensive pass rush coordinator Drew Wilkins Defensive pass game coordinator Jimmy Lake, also defensive backs Senior offensive assistant Brian Johnson Senior defensive assistant Robert Wright Kingsbury is in his first season with the Rams. They have four coaches in their first NFL season, but three are assistant position coaches in addition to Wright: Robert Woods, receivers; Brian Allen, offensive line; Michael Hunter, defensive backs. Seahawks: 25 coaches, nine with at least 10 years of NFL experience (143 total) and none with that many years in Seattle because Macdonald is in his third season as head coach. They also have: Assistant head coach Leslie Frazier Pass game coordinator Jake Peetz, also quarterbacks Pass game strategist Daniel Stern Senior offensive assistant John Benton, also offensive line Senior offensive assistant Thomas Hammock, also running backs Offensive run game coordinator Justin Outten Senior defensive assistant Kirk Olivadotti Defensive run game coordinator Chris Partridge Defensive pass game coordinator Kark Scott, also defensive backs Stern and Hammock are two of eight coaches in their first year with the Seahawks as are offensive coordinator Brian Fleury (11 NFL seasons) and inside linebackers coach Zach Orr (10 NFL seasons). The other four include two offensive assistants, one defensive assistant and one defensive quality control coach. The overall significant number is the three teams have 28 assistants with at least 10 years of NFL experience with a total of 516 years. Then, there’s the Cardinals, a staff with only two assistants that have 10-plus years in the NFL: Interim defensive coordinator Teryl Austin (23) and offensive coordinator Nathaniel Hackett (18). They do not have an assistant head coach, which each of the other teams have, or any run or pass game coordinators. The other three division teams total 11. Cardinals fifth-year coach Connor Senger is a pass game specialist. Prior to the departure of Rallis, Austin was the only coach with a senior role in his title. The Rams and Seahawks total six. The Cardinals have 19 total assistants, including Wendy Laurent, the Bill Bidwill Fellow (first NFL season). Most glaring is that the Cardinals have 10 assistants in their first Cardinals year, including six in their first NFL year. Of those six (including Laurent), four are main position coaches: Etheridge; Matt Schaub, quarterbacks; Matt Merritt, running backs; and Pete Kwiatkowski, defensive line. The other is offensive quality control coach Brett Ekkens. The other four first-time Cardinals are Hackett, tight ends coach Jake Moreland, inside linebackers coach Rod Wilson, and defensive quality control coach Brent Jackson. While many of the NFL fledglings had previous careers in college coaching, the adjustment to the pro game is significant and success, if it happens, takes time. One other example aside from the NFC West is the commitment the Giants made when hiring John Harbaugh as head coach this year. The Giants have 21 assistants, including eight with 10 or more years of NFL experience (149 total) and have an assistant head coach, a senior offensive assistant, an offensive pass game coordinator, defensive run game coordinator, defensive pass game coordinator, two offensive quality control coaches, one defensive quality control coach, one defensive assistant and a quality control analyst. The Giants are currently 6-3-1 and in first place in the NFC East, despite playing with their third quarterback of the season. With only those four teams as examples, their 10-plus-year assistants total 221, 151, 149 and 143 years while the Cardinals total is 41. For overall perspective, in addition to what those job responsibilities are, the titles are often justification for being paid more. That’s commitment. That’s doing all an organization can do to achieve success in a league where it’s so hard just to win a game. There’s never a guarantee for good outcomes, but it creates a path for improvement and hope. Those are lessons Cardinals owner Michael Bidwill should heed. title: Art Rooney II backs Steelers’ Mike McCarthy, rips Aaron Rodgers in scathing statement
summary: Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II threw his support behind Mike McCarthy, while taking a shot at Aaron Rodgers.
content: It’s not the best time to be Mike McCarthy , thanks to a scathing interview from disgruntled quarterback Aaron Rodgers on Friday afternoon. Rodgers ripped the Pittsburgh Steelers ‘ head coach and tried to ruin his reputation on a major platform. But after he went scorched earth on The Pat McAfee Show , Rodgers was released. Since Rodgers’ interview, McCarthy has become a laughingstock on social media, and the Steelers have become a laughingstock around the NFL . Whether it be McCarthy’s sleeping habits or love for ice cream sandwiches , he’s been the butt of countless jokes. Despite the drama and whirlwind surrounding the team, Steelers owner Art Rooney II is standing firmly behind McCarthy and saying he’s their coach of the future. MORE: Wildest Moments from Aaron Rodgers’ explosive Pat McAfee appearance Steelers Fully Support Mike McCarthy Jan 27, 2026; Pittsburgh, PA, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II (left) listens at a press conference introducing Mike McCarthy (right) as the new Pittsburgh Steelers head coach at PNC Champions Club at Acrisure Stadium.. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) “I just want to say that I have 100 percent confidence in Mike McCarthy , and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season, and beyond,” Rooney said before taking a swipe at Rodgers. “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” MORE: Mike McCarthy ice cream sandwich assistant becomes most famous man in Pittsburgh Of course, if the Steelers completely collapse and miss out on the playoffs, it will be interesting to see if the support holds firm. Players have reportedly been backing up Rodgers’ claims, and if they are true, the side show could be enough to force Rooney to cut McCarthy loose. If there’s one thing we know about the Rooney family, it’s that they don’t want a circus. And anyone someone is causing distractions, they may not be longed for Pittsburgh.
