title: Bears record on Thanksgiving: Full list of wins, losses for Chicago on NFL holiday
summary: Here's a deeper look at the Bears' history on Thanksgiving.
content: Bears record on Thanksgiving: Full list of wins, losses for Chicago on NFL holiday originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . While the Chicago Bears are not a mainstay on the NFL's Thanksgiving schedule, they are no strangers to playing on the Holiday. As an NFC North rival to the Detroit Lions , the Bears frequently find themselves playing in front of the country on the big stage. Whether the Bears are contenders or underperforming, Chicago has developed a rivalry with the Lions that gives them a chance to play in Detroit every Thanksgiving. Besides the two teams that play on this day every year, no other team has played more often on Thanksgiving than the Bears franchise. That goes back all the way to 1920, when the first Thanksgiving football games were played. Here's a deeper look at the Bears' history on Thanksgiving. MORE : Which NFL teams always play on Thanksgiving? Bears record on Thanksgiving The Bears have a 20-16-2 record on Thanksgiving, as they are one of just three franchises to reach the 20-win mark on the Holiday. Only the Dallas Cowboys and Lions have more victories on Thanksgiving, and both of those teams play a home game on the day every season. MORE : Why do the Lions always play on Thanksgiving? How many times have the Bears played on Thanksgiving? The Bears have played on Thanksgiving 38 times, dating back to when they were the Decatur Staleys and the Chicago Staleys, before they changed their name to the Bears in 1922. Most of the Bears' Thanksgiving games have come against either the then-Chicago Cardinals or the Detroit Lions. The Bears and Lions played 12 straight years on Thanksgiving from 1922 to 1933, with the Bears holding that edge 7-4-1 in that span. Most of Chicago's Thanksgiving games, though, have come against the NFC North rival Lions in Detroit. Those two teams have played on the Holiday 19 times, and the Bears hold a slight 10-9 advantage in those games. Other Bears matchups on Thanksgiving include one game against the Green Bay Packers , a few games against the Cowboys and a game against the short-lived Dallas Texans . title: Blake Corum supplants Kyren Williams as the Rams' top tailback
summary: It's been slowly building throughout the season.
content: It's been slowly building throughout the season. On Wednesday night, it became abundantly clear. Blake Corum has become the Rams' top tailback. On his 26th birthday, Corum had a career night. Thirty-two carries, 184 yards, and a touchdown. Throw in 21 receiving yards, and he had 205 yards from scrimmage. “Happy birthday, man," coach Sean McVay told reporters after the game. "He was on the set of Netflix so we didn't even get to enjoy it with him. So, I know that kind of pissed me off, honestly." Corum's gains have come at the expense of Kyren Williams. Despite a report that he's been dealing with turf toe for a month, this week was Williams's first appearance all year on the injury report. And while the fact that Corum got the start last night and 58 snaps while Williams was limited to 38 may have had something to do with the toe, as Mike Tomlin says, "One man's misfortune is another man's opportunity." Corum seized the opportunity on Wednesday night, as part of a very un-Rams-like offensive output that included 241 rushing yards and 132 passing yards. For the season, Williams has 662 rushing yards and an average of 4.4 yards per carry. Corum has 731 yards rushing with a 5.4-yard average. Lurking in the background (but soon moving to the foreground) is the business side of the situation. Corum is in the third year of a slotted, third-round rookie deal. He's making $1.582 million in 2026, and he's eligible for a second contract as soon as the regular season ends. Williams is making $11 million per year, on a deal that runs through 2028. They'll need to reward Corum at some point, which could force them to make a decision about Williams. That's clearly coming. Last night's breakout showing in a standalone game shows that it's coming quickly.

title: Broncos RB Jonah Coleman sweeps NFL’s weekly awards after 3-touchdown game
summary: Broncos RB Jonah Coleman was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week, the FedEx Ground Player of the Week and the Pepsi Rookie of the Week!
content: Denver Broncos running back Jonah Coleman's trophy case is quickly filling up after his Week 11 performance against the Las Vegas Raiders . Coleman ran for 111 yards, caught four passes for 18 more yards, and rushed for three touchdowns in a 38-24 win over the Raiders. Coleman was named the AFC Offensive Player of the Week on Wednesday, then he won FedEx Air and Ground Player of the Week honors later the same day. After that, Coleman swept weekly awards by winning the NFL's Pepsi Rookie of the Week, which the league announced on Thursday. Your NFL Rookie of the Week 👏 Congrats, @JonahColeman8 ! pic.twitter.com/AzyNslynnf — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 26, 2026 Coleman has taken Denver by storm in his rookie season. When he was selected in the fourth round of the 2025 NFL draft, Coleman was listed as the third running back on the depth chart behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. His work ethic caught the eye of coach Sean Payton, who called the back a "pleasant surprise" at training camp back in August. Another one for the rook. RT to congratulate @JonahColeman8 on being named a @FedEx Air & Ground Player of the Week! pic.twitter.com/uAovj84KFd — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 25, 2026 After a Week 2 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in which Coleman scored his first NFL touchdown, he went on injured reserve for four weeks with an ankle injury. After coming back in Week 7, Coleman quickly moved up the depth chart to the starting role after an injury to Harvey and Dobbins' growing ineffectiveness. Coleman has been the centerpiece of several key plays during the Broncos ' current six-game win streak, culminating in his award-winning game against Las Vegas. Coleman looks to be the featured back during Friday's game against the Pittsburgh Steelers, which is projected to be a nightmare for passers . Way to go, rook! title: Broncos vs. Steelers: 5 things to know about Pittsburgh’s squad
summary: We asked Steelers Wire five questions about their squad ahead of Friday's showdown with the Broncos.
content: It's certainly been an interesting week as it pertains particularly to the Denver Broncos and Pittsburgh Steelers ' Week 12 matchup on Friday. With the suspension of running back J.K. Dobbins and the benching of Steelers quarterback and NFL legend Aaron Rodgers both coming on Tuesday, the matchup will feature Mason Rudolph under center for Pittsburgh while Jonah Coleman continues to lead Denver's backfield. With all the drama that unfolded, we went Behind Enemy Lines with Curt Popejoy of Steelers Wire to ask him five questions about Pittsburgh and where they stand heading into this game. You can view our questions and Curt's answers below. 1. What has this season done for the legacy of Aaron Rogers, presumably that this is his final season? Ultimately, the legacy of Rodgers won’t have much to do with a couple of mediocre seasons with the Steelers. Him being deactivated for this week is historic in it’s the first healthy scratch of his career but this is a blip on the radar. 2. What is the biggest strength of the Steelers going into Week 12? The biggest weakness? The best thing the Steelers do is play defense. We don’t know if Alex Highsmith or Nick Herbig will play but even without them, the defense has carried this team all year. As for a weakness, it is the wide receiver group. No one can get open; the best athlete is a rookie and the team’s highest-paid wideout is trying to poke defenders in the eyes. 3. Who has been an underappreciated player on offense and defense this season for the Black and Gold? On offense, it continues to be tight end Pat Freiermuth. He could be one of the more productive tight ends in the league but the team doesn’t see it that way. On defense, I’m going with inside linebacker Payton Wilson. He is on pace to set the team’s season record for tackles but he doesn’t get the recognition he deserves. 4. What are three keys on Black Friday for the Steelers to win? With Mason Rudolph at quarterback, it breaks down like this. 1 - Run the football. Have to get Jaylen Warren going. 2 - Keep Rudolph upright. He will stand in the pocket and throw the ball but he can’t take a lot of big hits. 3 - Pressure Bo Nix. I’m confident in the run defense but the pass rush has been up and down. Making life hard on Nix is the way they get the Broncos offense off the field. 5. Final score, who wins and why? I was ready to give this one to the Steelers because they are at home but the late quarterback change is a total curveball. This team is scrambling for an identity and I’m not sure this was the week to make a big move. Steelers 24, Broncos 28. The Broncos will make their way to the East Coast later this week to face the Steelers with Rudolph under center on Friday at 3:00 p.m. ET (1:00 p.m. MT) on Prime . title: CJ Stroud reacts to Texans rookie Marlin Klein's performance vs Colts
summary: Texans quarterback CJ Stroud reacts to rookie tight end Marlin Klein's performance against the Colts, including his first NFL touchdown.
content: When the Houston Texans drafted tight end Marlin Klein in the second round of the 2026 NFL Draft, they were clearly taking a risk on someone who did not have a lot of playing time in college. In fact, he recorded only 38 catches and one touchdown in his entire college career. Things started out slowly for Klein as he learned his role in the offense and on special teams. However, something seemed to click during Houston’s Thursday night win against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 11 when he had four catches for 26 yards and his first NFL touchdown. Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud reacted to Klein’s performance and his growth so far. "It was cool to see the young guy do a good job and I think he's learning. He's learning fast and he has a lot of talent. Just have get him on the same page with us on what we're trying to get accomplished. Whenever he's doing the right thing, he's usually pretty good,” Stroud said. “Just have to continue to let him develop and grow and that's up to our whole team to help him out. He's doing a great job and effort or physicality is not really the problem. It's just we have to find ways to make sure that he's on the same page with everybody and he's been able to do that these past couple weeks. Very proud of him and I'm a big fan of Marlin and what he's been able to do and continue to do great things for us." Stroud finds German TE Marlin Klein for six! @nfldeutschland INDvsHOU on Prime Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/fS7L7wS8O3 — NFL (@NFL) November 20, 2026 Klein actually ended up with the most receptions of anyone on the team in a night where Houston finally got their run game going and found some balance on the offense. Houston has a talented tight end room between Klein, Dalton Schultz and Foster Moreau, all of whom had a catch against the Colts. Having such talented players in the room has certainly helped Klein develop so far this season. The Texans and Klein take the field this Sunday at Noon on CBS. title: Commanders' Jayden Daniels weighs in on snap issues
summary: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels discusses Washington's snapping issue from Monday night.
content: The center position has been an ongoing problem for the Washington Commanders since they released former starter Tyler Biadasz last offseason. Washington missed out on former Ravens center Tyler Linderbaum and told everyone that veteran guard Nick Allegretti would be the new center. After two games, Allegretti was benched, replaced by Lucas Patrick, who was signed after the season began. But when Patrick missed the Week 10 game against the New York Giants , Allegretti was back in the starting lineup. He played well. However, for the Commanders' Week 11 game against Cincinnati, Patrick was back in the lineup. Playing on Monday night means everyone is watching. While the Commanders were impressive on Monday, upsetting the Bengals , one glaring issue remained: Washington’s center position, specifically, the snaps. Throughout the game, Patrick’s snaps were either slow, high, or both. Each time, it would throw off the timing of the play. It’s something that’s been going on all year with Patrick, but it was more evident on Monday. A chart revealed that Patrick’s snaps were the slowest in the NFL. Lucas Patrick with the ephus snap @PFTCommenter pic.twitter.com/oa6mHumlxt — Sam Schwartzstein (@schwartzsteins) November 24, 2026 Here’s a snap from Monday’s game so that you can judge for yourself. Has a nose tackle ever beaten a center this quickly? pic.twitter.com/voD1YolPfi — Grant Paulsen (@GrantPaulsen) November 24, 2026 That split second is huge, as offensive linemen are trying to protect the quarterback. On Wednesday, Daniels met with the media and was asked about Patrick’s snaps. “I’m sure Lucas goes back and looks at that and probably has a conversation,” Daniels said. “For me in the moment, man, I’m just playing ball, so I don’t really pay attention to stuff like that. So, for me, it’s like, okay, if something happens, I gotta make up for it, stuff like that. But obviously, we have talks, and we have conversations. We give each other feedback, so that's kind of the nature of this business, especially from a center to a quarterback; you gotta communicate and have those conversations.” Daniels is a pro. That’s why his teammates love him. He has every reason to be upset during the game, but you never see him showing any frustration with Patrick. As for Patrick's snaps, they need to improve, or it could be time to go back to Allegretti. Sure, Allegretti isn't perfect, but there were no snapping issues during his time at the position. Patrick's snaps didn't just become a problem on Monday night, they've been an issue all season. The Commanders are back in action on Sunday, facing the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. This article originally appeared on Commanders Wire: Commanders' Jayden Daniels weighs in on snap issues

title: Could Patriots promising offseason acquisition already be on hot seat?
summary: So far, veteran edge rusher Dre'Mont Jones' run with the Patriots hasn't gone as well as expected.
content: New England Patriots edge rusher Dre’Mont Jones should be under a watchful eye by the team coming out of their Week 11 bye. With just seven games remaining in the 2026 season, Jones has plenty to prove after not playing up to the standard expected of him throughout the year so far. Jones was one of the Patriots ’ marquee free-agent signings last offseason and was expected to rival the production that K’Lavon Chaisson provided the team in 2025, as the latter recorded 7.5 sacks that season. After recording a career-high seven sacks last year, Jones entered the current season with expectations to potentially lead New England in sacks and register the first double-digit sack season of his career. However, Elijah Ponder, who was a key backup for the team last season as a rookie, has played considerably better than Jones, as he has already recorded 7.5 sacks this year and is on pace to eclipse the 10-sack milestone. Meanwhile, rookie Gabe Jacas has also been highly productive with 3.5 sacks and an interception this season. Both players' production has made Jones’ down season even more pronounced. Through nine games played, Jones has recorded just 1.5 sacks, though he has registered 26 quarterback pressures this year. Jones has the final seven games of the year to generate a significant amount of sacks and bring a noticeable spark to New England’s defense. Otherwise, his standing with the organization will be deserving of close scrutiny, and will warrant him potentially becoming a candidate to be traded moving forward. title: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer dubbed an unexpected hot seat candidate

title: Detroit Lions picks vs Bears: Who'll come out on top on Thanksgiving?
summary: Will the Detroit Lions keep their six-game win streak going against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving? Six Free Press sports writers make their picks.
content: Grab a turkey leg – no turducken, since this game’s on CBS, not Fox – and settle in for the Detroit Lions ’ 87 th Thanksgiving Day game, as they host the Chicago Bears on Thursday, Nov. 26. The 1 p.m. start will mark the 21 st meeting between the Lions and Bears on Turkey Day (second behind only the 23 games between the Lions and Packers ), with the Bears owning an 11-9 edge in the holiday series (and a 3-2 edge at Ford Field on the holiday). Still, the Lions had the edge the last time they met on Thanksgiving, with a 23-20 win in 2024, and have beaten former offensive coordinator Ben Johnson’s squad in both reunions since. MAN IN THE MIDDLE: Lions will see whole new Bears defense in Thanksgiving game thanks to Jeffery Simmons Will the Lions keep that streak, not to mention their six-game win streak this season, going? Six Free Press sports writers make their picks: Detroit Lions predictions vs Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Dave Birkett In their long Thanksgiving history, the Lions haven't played many games bigger than this. The Lions and Bears are two of the three best teams in the NFC with identical 8-2 records and similar playing styles. The Lions are at home and have the best running back in football. The Bears are healthier and still riding the euphoria of their big trade deadline acquisition. In a game between two evenly matched teams, I see this one coming down to who has the ball last. The pick: Bears 31, Lions 30. Carlos Monarrez I’ve written that I won’t pick the Lions to lose again, until they finally do. But this one’s tough to resist. These teams are both 8-2, but the Lions have taken advantage of the NFL’s easiest strength of schedule, while the Bears have battled through the NFL’s hardest strength of schedule – and scored 34 against Seattle’s top-ranked defense. I’ve giving the Lions this game purely on homefield advantage. The pick: Lions 32, Bears 25 (OT). Christian Romo Don't expect to glean anything meaningful from the result of this game. Both of these teams are playing on a short week in front of a national audience, with the Lions missing their two best defensive players and the Bears 0-2 vs. the Lions under Johnson. The Lions could get blown out and still end up winning the division, while the Bears could put up a stinker and still be Super Bowl favorites. The Jan. 3 rematch in Chicago will probably come with real stakes – hello again, NBC? – but consider this one a midseason exhibition between two teams with similar résumés and a strong desire to enjoy a long weekend. The Bears are favored by less than a field goal because many consider them to be one of the two best teams in the NFC (along with the 9-1 San Francisco 49ers). But Detroit has done nothing but exceed expectations over the last six games, so why not make it a seventh? The pick: Lions 28, Bears 27. Rainer Sabin The last time Ben Johnson visited Ford Field, the Lions humiliated the Bears in his second game as head coach. Johnson certainly remembers that 52-21 beatdown delivered by the same organization that served as the launchpad for his career ascent from quality control coach to wunderkind play-caller. Johnson will be eager to finally exact revenge in this pivotal divisional showdown, and he now has superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to support his mission. Simmons gives Chicago the edge in this matchup and helps Johnson earn his first victory against his former team in a game that goes down to the wire. The pick: Bears 27, Lions 24. Jeff Seidel This is going to be an absolutely wild, fascinating, and incredibly important game. And it comes at the perfect time for the Lions because they have been playing tremendous football. Sure, Ben Johnson will bring out some wrinkles and find some creative ways to score. He certainly knows this coaching staff, these players and this scheme. But he will end up overthinking it and go back to the Windy City with his third straight loss to his mentor. All of that, plus, more than anything, it’s at home for the Lions. The pick: Lions 31, Bears 28. Shawn Windsor Jeffery Simmons has five sacks in three games since joining Chicago and turned the Bears into the most complete team in the NFC North ... so far. And while Ben Johnson will have his team amped and ready to beat the Lions, Dan Campbell will have his guys ready, too. They escape in the end when Jared Goff finds Sam LaPorta in the end zone. The pick: Lions 23, Bears 20. This article originally appeared on Detroit Free Press: Detroit Lions picks vs Bears: Who'll come out on top on Thanksgiving?

title: ‘I Don’t Think Another Team Wants Him’ — Packers Legend Clay Matthews Predicts We’ve Seen the Last of Aaron Rodgers After Steelers Release
summary: Clay Matthews heard how Aaron Rodgers’ time in Pittsburgh ended and saw a problem for any team considering bringing him in next. The Packers legend offered a bleak assessment of his former teammate’s future during Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve coverage of the game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams.
content: ‘I Don’t Think Another Team Wants Him’ — Packers Legend Clay Matthews Predicts We’ve Seen the Last of Aaron Rodgers After Steelers Release Clay Matthews heard how Aaron Rodgers’ time in Pittsburgh ended and saw a problem for any team considering bringing him in next. The Packers legend offered a bleak assessment of his former teammate’s future during Netflix’s Thanksgiving Eve coverage of the game between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams. Clay Matthews Doubts Another Team Will Bring In Aaron Rodgers With Rodgers released by the Steelers and with his criticism of Mike McCarthy dominating the conversation, Matthews questioned whether another franchise would be willing to take that chance. “I think this is the last time we’ve seen him in the league. I don’t think another team wants him as a quarterback,” Matthews said . The question put to Matthews was straightforward. Had Rodgers already played his final NFL game? His answer focused on what a potential employer would have to consider after watching Pittsburgh’s situation unravel. Co-panelist Michael Irvin also weighed in and added, “How do you bring Aaron in when you’re seeing how this is ending, and if it doesn’t work out for you and your club, you can imagine it’s going to end like this, Aaron Rodgers on Pat McAfee and all of these things.” Matthews and Irvin were offering their assessment of Rodgers’ market. They did not identify a team that had rejected the quarterback or announce that Rodgers had retired. The concern is another possibility of another public breakup. For a franchise weighing a late-season quarterback addition, Matthews believes the way this relationship ended could be difficult to overlook. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer This is also a harsh forecast from someone who shared a locker room with Rodgers in Green Bay. Meanwhile, Irvin made it clear that he appreciated the quarterback’s place in NFL history, calling him “one of the greatest quarterbacks we’ve ever had in this National Football League.” “For him to end his career like this, walking off the football field like this, that’s very sad,” Irvin futher added. Steelers Move Forward With Mason Rudolph After Rodgers’ Release Pittsburgh officially released Rodgers on Wednesday, Nov. 25, after announcing the previous night that Mason Rudolph would start against Denver on Black Friday. The change came with the Steelers at 6-4. Rodgers then delivered a scathing assessment of McCarthy on “The Pat McAfee Show” , including allegations about the coach sleeping during meetings and failing to prepare adequately. Those comments helped turn a quarterback change into a much wider examination of Pittsburgh’s leadership. McCarthy subsequently said the benching followed an ultimatum from Rodgers that fell outside a player’s responsibilities. He declined to detail their private conversations and maintained that he could lead the Steelers forward. There were performance questions as well. Through Week 11, Rodgers ranked No. 29 among 33 quarterbacks in PFN’s QB Impact rankings with a 67.1 grade. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor He finished his 2026 Steelers stint with 220 completions on 361 attempts for 2,241 yards and 16 touchdowns across 10 starts. Pittsburgh had brought him back after he started 16 games for the team in 2025. For Matthews, though, the public fallout was central to the question of what happens next. His comments effectively asked a prospective team to consider how a reunion or fresh start might end if expectations went unmet. Pittsburgh has already chosen Rudolph for its next game. Rodgers’ next opportunity depends on another team either claiming him off waivers or, if he clears, deciding he is worth a free-agent deal. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: 'Don't you change': Bill Cowher praises Dan Campbell
summary: Dan Campbell has made Thanksgiving football much more enjoyable for millions of people across the country by making the Detroit Lions more competitive in recent years. The way he has led his team has won over even more fans along the way, including former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach and NFL Today analyst Bill Cowher. When you think of…
content: Credit: CBS Sports Dan Campbell has made Thanksgiving football much more enjoyable for millions of people across the country by making the Detroit Lions more competitive in recent years. The way he has led his team has won over even more fans along the way , including former Pittsburgh Steelers head coach and NFL Today analyst Bill Cowher. When you think of Dan Campbell, you think of him as the ultimate football tough guy. But he hasn’t been afraid to wear his heart on his sleeve . And when Cowher gave him his flowers for an interview for The NFL Today on CBS ahead of the Lions hosting the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Day, he couldn’t help but get emotional. This is awesome Dan Campbell got emotional when @CowherCBS gave him his flowers #nflt https://t.co/Zg2IFfrBwv — NFL on CBS (@NFLonCBS) November 25, 2026 “I’d love to give thanks to you and what you represent, the journey that you’ve taken from a player to an assistant coach to climbing that ladder and landing here in Detroit; you embody what this place is all about. Yeah, you speak about resiliency, that’s Dan Campbell. You speak about grit, that’s Dan Campbell. You think about passion, that’s Dan Campbell,” Cowher said. “Thank you for being you. You’re authentic, man. And I don’t want you to ever change. Not only in the National Football League but this city, we need more people like Dan Campbell to continue to be a part of this society. As you keep your strive and pursuit for excellence is what’s made this country great, and you represent every element of that. Thank you for being you, and don’t you dare change. You bite the knees off on your way to getting that championship. Don’t you change, man.” After seeing Bill Cowher coach up Dan Campbell like that, with the emotion and intensity and pride on his own face, it’s almost a shame that the former Steelers coach never did return to the sidelines after his retirement after the 2006 season. That was an inspiring, powerful message. If you could ever get the two of them in the same locker room, players would run through any brick wall they could. title: How the Eagles and Cowboys have changed since their Week 7 matchup
summary: Joe Milton is Philadelphia's starting quarterback, and Mike Pettine leads Dallas' defense. Here's what changed since their Week 7 meeting
content: A little more than a month after suffering a 38-21 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Monday Night Football, the Philadelphia Eagles will get another opportunity against their NFC East rivals on Thanksgiving afternoon at AT&T Stadium. The Eagles failed to record a sack or quarterback hit in the Week 7 loss, while Tanner McKee completed 14 of 22 passes for 129 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Philadelphia has since made a quarterback change, while Dallas has turned to a veteran defensive assistant to direct its defense. With both teams preparing for their second meeting of the regular season, here's what's changed since October. Joe Milton replaced Tanner McKee Milton will make his third consecutive start after replacing McKee, giving the Eagles a quarterback with the arm strength to challenge Dallas vertically and the athleticism to extend plays outside the pocket. Milton has thrown for 310 yards in two starts, including 141 yards in Philadelphia's Week 11 win over Pittsburgh. The Eagles will need more production through the air against a Dallas offense capable of scoring in bunches. Mike Pettine took over the Dallas defense The Cowboys have a new defensive play-caller in Pettine, who helped Dallas hold Tennessee's offense to three first-half points in his debut. Philadelphia offensive coordinator Sean Mannion has an additional layer of preparation this week, with the Eagles having just one game of film to evaluate how Pettine intends to utilize his personnel. Philadelphia's pass rush is generating momentum After failing to disrupt Dak Prescott in October, Philadelphia recorded five sacks against Pittsburgh in Week 11. Jonathan Greenard, Jalyx Hunt, Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis will be among the players tasked with generating pressure without forcing defensive coordinator Vic Fangio to sacrifice coverage resources against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. The Eagles have additional options in the secondary The addition of veteran defensive back Kenny Moore II gives Fangio another option in the slot, while Riq Woolen could play a significant role on the outside. Quinyon Mitchell's availability will be critical against a Dallas receiving corps that presents challenges at multiple levels of the field. Cooper DeJean's versatility also gives Philadelphia flexibility when the Cowboys move Lamb inside. Dak Prescott is heating up Prescott enters Thanksgiving with nine touchdown passes over his past two games, including four against Tennessee in Week 11. Dallas boasts the NFL's second-ranked passing offense, and Philadelphia's ability to disrupt Prescott's timing will be as important as any personnel adjustment the Eagles have made since their October loss. title: Eagles vs. Cowboys: 5 storylines to follow on Thanksgiving Day
summary: Joe Milton headlines 5 Eagles-Cowboys Thanksgiving storylines
content: Thanksgiving and the Dallas Cowboys have been attached at the hip for generations. The Philadelphia Eagles are getting another opportunity to play a part in that tradition. There is something different about a divisional rivalry taking center stage on a holiday, particularly when the two teams have so much familiarity with one another and so little patience for giving the other an inch. This year's meeting carries plenty of intrigue beyond the usual NFC East animosity. Philadelphia is coming off a much-needed victory , while Dallas has been putting together an eventful stretch of its own. With the season entering its final stretch, Thursday's game gives both teams a chance to make a statement in front of a national audience. Here are five storylines surrounding the Eagles-Cowboys Thanksgiving matchup as kickoff nears. Joe Milton vs. his former team A couple of months ago, Joe Milton was on the Cowboys' practice squad. Now, he's preparing to make his third consecutive start for the Philadelphia Eagles , his second on the national stage. It's an unusual twist for a quarterback who spent training camp competing for a place behind Dak Prescott before Dallas ultimately went with Sam Howell. Dallas has undergone some changes since Milton was there, including a switch from Christian Parker to veteran Mike Pettine handling the defensive play-calling duties. The Cowboys haven't exactly become an impenetrable unit, either. They surrendered 346 yards and 30 points to the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. That may suggest Milton and Philadelphia could find an opportunity to find some favorable matchups. A unique stat about the Cowboys' five wins There's more to a team's record than the numbers in each column. Opponents, circumstances and the quality of those victories all help provide a better picture of how good a team really is. The Cowboys' recent offensive production has been impressive, but their 5-6 record leaves them with considerable work to do in the NFC playoff race. A victory over Philadelphia would move Dallas back to .500 and provide additional momentum entering December, while an Eagles victory would prevent Dallas from completing its first regular-season sweep of Philadelphia since 2021. That's worth remembering when looking at the Cowboys' 5-6 record entering Thanksgiving. Dallas has won five games, but none of those victories came against a team with a winning record. That doesn't mean Dallas hasn't earned its victories, nor does it guarantee Philadelphia will take advantage of the opportunity. However, it does raise a legitimate question about the Cowboys' standing among the NFC's contenders. A Thanksgiving win would also bring Dallas back to .500, but changing the narrative around the Cowboys' season may come only by stacking quality wins. Quinnen Williams' league-leading 18 tackles for loss The Dallas defense has had its share of problems, but Quinnen Williams has been a significant bright spot. He has recorded 18 tackles for loss through 11 games, leading the NFL, while adding eight sacks and 13 additional quarterback hits. Philadelphia allowed three sacks against Pittsburgh, and Williams' production creates another difficult assignment for an offensive line that has struggled to consistently protect its quarterbacks. The Eagles need to minimize negative plays on early downs and prevent Williams from putting Milton in difficult passing situations. He's been disruptive against both the run and the pass. The Eagles are well aware. In the first meeting between these two teams, he recorded four tackles, three tackles for loss, one sack, and another quarterback hit. The Eagles will have to account for him throughout Thursday's game. Williams can change a drive with one disruptive play, and Philadelphia cannot afford to let him dictate the terms of the matchup. Philadelphia's perfect Thanksgiving record against Dallas The Eagles have enjoyed considerable success on Thanksgiving, compiling a 6-1 record in seven appearances. Their history against Dallas on the holiday is without blemish. Philadelphia has won both previous Thanksgiving meetings. The Eagles' only Thanksgiving defeat came in 2015, when they lost 45-14 to the Detroit Lions . The results of all seven games can be found below. 1939 - Eagles 17, Pittsburgh Pirates ( Steelers ) 14 1940 Eagles 7, Steelers 0 1968 - Eagles 12, Detroit Lions 0 1989 Eagles 27, Cowboys 0 2008- Eagles 48, Arizona Cardinals 20 2014 - Eagles 33, Cowboys 10 2015- Lions 45, Eagles 14 Sometimes, records don't matter in a rivalry game, and anything can happen. The Eagles will have an opportunity to extend their perfect mark against their division rival. The first meeting came in 1989, when the Eagles shut out Dallas 27-0 in the infamous Bounty Bowl. Thursday obviously will mark Philadelphia's first Thanksgiving appearance since that loss. Eagles' recent history against the Cowboys in Arlington The Philadelphia Eagles haven't enjoyed much success on their trips to Arlington lately. They're 2-8 in their last 10 road games against the Cowboys, with their victories coming in 2017 and 2024. That recent history makes Thursday's Thanksgiving matchup another difficult assignment for Philadelphia, particularly with Dallas looking to protect its home field. The Cowboys are also favored by entering the holiday matchup on the sportsbooks. Philadelphia will have to overcome more than its recent road struggles to leave AT&T Stadium with a victory. The Eagles have already lost to Dallas once this season, and the Cowboys have another opportunity to make life difficult for their division rival in front of a national audience. title: Emmanuel Acho shares why he thinks the Steelers won’t fire Mike McCarthy despite Aaron Rodgers comments
summary: Aaron Rodgers went scorched earth on Pittsburgh Steelers’ Head Coach Mike McCarthy. The four-time NFL MVP was benched by his team after a disagreement with McCarthy, then went on Pat McAfee’s TV show to expose what he believes was unprofessionalism from his coach.
content: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers went scorched earth on Pittsburgh Steelers’ Head Coach Mike McCarthy. The four-time NFL MVP was benched by his team after a disagreement with McCarthy, then went on Pat McAfee’s TV show to expose what he believes was unprofessionalism from his coach. Rodgers said that McCarthy has slept through team meetings, has an ice cream sandwich assistant, and once said “one, two three Packers” during a Steelers team huddle. These comments put McCarthy’s future as Steelers’ head coach in question, but analyst Emmanuel Acho explains why he thinks he will not lose his job. Emmanuel Acho says why he thinks Mike McCarthy’s job is safe Rodgers’ most serious complaints about McCarthy have yet to be corroborated by his teammates, or any former players who have played under the Super Bowl-winning Head Coach. And with the Steelers well in the playoff hunt with a 6-4 record, Acho thinks that the team’s relative success this season will be enough to keep him in his job despite this embarrassing saga. Speaking on Speakeasy, he said, “Think about this. You’re still 6-4. “The Houston Texans started 0-4, so you’ve still got games on them. The Patriots ain’t got a quarterback. I’ll take Mason Rudolph over whoever the Patriots have at quarterback. They’re done. The Titans, they’re done. “So why would you fire him? As bad as Mike McCarthy is – and I’ll talk about Mike McCarthy momentarily – as bad as Mike McCarthy allegedly is, he was 6-3 five days ago, and he’s 6-4, they are firmly in the playoff picture.” The Steelers are just one win back of Super Bowl-contending Cincinnati Bengals in the brutally tough AFC North, and if they maintain their current pace without Rodgers, they will make it to the postseason. It would be foolish for them to part ways with McCarthy with that level of team success because of Rodgers’ outburst, and for now, it appears that the Steelers are sticking by him. title: ESPN analyst believes Bears DT Jeffery Simmons has good chance to win NFL award
summary: This major NFL award is actually in play for Jeffery Simmons this season.
content: ESPN analyst believes Bears DT Jeffery Simmons has good chance to win NFL award originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . A lot of teams made big moves before the 2026 NFL trade deadline this year, but no team made a more impactful addition than the Chicago Bears . They swung a blockbuster trade with the Tennessee Titans , acquiring superstar defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons in exchange for multiple first-round picks. But so far, it's been worth it. Simmons has been awesome for the Bears. Things are going so well that ESPN analyst Ben Solak believes Simmons has a real chance at winning the NFL's Defensive Player of the Year Award. While he has to stay hot through the end of the season, Solak sees a pathway for Simmons to win this award. ESPN analysts believe Jeffery Simmons can win DPOY for the Bears in 2026 "More likely: He ends up with around 14 (sacks). The last defensive tackle to win the award -- Aaron Donald -- did so in 2020 with 13.5 sacks. If the Bears win the division and Simmons gets to that number, I think he'll do it," Solak writes. Simmons is averaging 1.66 sacks per game with the Bears so far, and he's sure to continue to dominate, just maybe not at that high of a level. But if he did, he'd compete for the league lead in sacks. Currently, Will Anderson Jr. of the Houston Texans leads the NFL with 11.5 sacks. Greg Rousseau of the Buffalo Bills is second with 10 sacks, while Boye Mafe and David Bailey have 9.5 sacks each. Simmons, through 11 weeks, has nine sacks. He's the sack leader among defensive tackles, and since coming to the Bears, he's been a true game-changer for their defense. MORE : Lions may have found their 1 answer to life without Aidan Hutchinson A defensive tackle winning Defensive Player of the Year doesn't happen often, but Simmons seems to have a real chance this year. Solak believes the Bears will need to win the NFC North and for Simmons to reach 14-plus sacks for a chance at winning this award. Seeing the Texans and Anderson Jr. miss the playoffs, while Rousseau cools off a bit, could open the door for Simmons to win this NFL award. Simmons and the Bears face the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving, and with both teams 8-2, the winner will have a big advantage in the divisional race this season. If Simmons can be a game-wrecker this week and the Bears win, he could start making a strong case as a top-tier Defensive Player of the Year candidate, if he's not already one of the top candidates for the award entering Week 12. Any team that signs him now deserves what it gets.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Rodgers simply hasn’t been the same player in recent years that he was during his prime. That reality, paired with his recent tirade against Mike McCarthy, could make NFL teams think twice before considering signing him. Multiple ESPN insiders weighed in on what’s next for Rodgers. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler seemed to agree that other teams probably won’t call about signing Rodgers this season. “While there are teams with needs — think of the Patriots, who just lost Drake Maye, and the Eagles, playing without Jalen Hurts — it’s hard to imagine any expressing interest,” Fowler wrote. “Yes, even at a minimum salary. The production (or lack thereof) does not offset the headache.” If NFL teams aren’t interested in Rodgers now, it’s hard to imagine they’ll change their minds in the future. Meanwhile, Pittsburgh must simply move on and prepare for their next matchup with Mason Rudolph at quarterback. title: ESPN reporter recounts what she saw Mike McCarthy doing during Aaron Rodgers’ explosive interview
summary: ESPN’s Pittsburgh Steelers reporter Brooke Pryor was at the facility for the post-practice media interaction when Aaron Rodgers’ interview about Mike McCarthy was airing. Rodgers’ appearance on the Pat McAfee Show sent shockwaves across the NFL, as the legendary quarterback did not hold back when criticising his now-former head coach.
content: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images ESPN’s Pittsburgh Steelers reporter Brooke Pryor was at the facility for the post-practice media interaction when Aaron Rodgers’ interview about Mike McCarthy was airing. Rodgers’ appearance on the Pat McAfee Show sent shockwaves across the NFL, as the legendary quarterback did not hold back when criticising his now-former head coach. But it appears someone within the Steelers organisation got word of Rodgers’ intentions before he joined the show, as they stopped airing the programme at the Steelers’ practice facility before Rodgers even came on. Mike McCarthy overheard all Pittsburgh Steelers reporters hearing Aaron Rodgers’ criticism On an emergency episode of ESPN’s Leaguewide, Pittsburgh Steelers reporter Brooke Pryor recounted her experience at the Steelers’ practice facility as Aaron Rodgers’ interview aired. After the Steelers changed the channel to avoid airing the Pat McAfee show in the lobby, the reporters huddled around one phone to hear Rodgers’ comments. Unbeknownst to them, HC Mike McCarthy happened to walk through the lobby at the time, catching wind of everything Rodgers was saying and how the reporters were listening to it. “We were waiting in the lobby to go into the locker room,” Pryor recounted on ESPN. “And there’s a TV in the lobby where, most afternoons, the Pat McAfee Show is airing. At 1:40, or just a couple of minutes before, a staffer changed the channel. They changed it to, I believe, E!, and they were airing reruns of How I Met Your Mother. So, no sports. “That meant all the reporters – there were about 30 of us in there – were left without a way to watch. One person got their phone out and put it on full volume, and we were all huddled around this person’s phone listening to what Rodgers was saying. I have a picture of it. “And Rodgers, as we know, comes out scorched earth, talking about the snoring in meetings, skipping meetings, all of these allegations. My jaw dropped, and it’s silent in this room except for Rodgers coming through this phone. “All of a sudden, my friend hits me, and I look up. Mike McCarthy is walking from the hallway where the locker room is, around us, making his way up to the second floor of the Steelers facility. “And he’s listening to us listen to his quarterback flame him in the most ruthless interview I’ve ever heard, on the loudest mic in the world. And I just thought, ‘I can’t believe this is happening right now.’ It was crazy.” To make matters even more awkward for everyone, McCarthy then had to stand in a room and address the same reporters he saw keenly listening to Rodgers’ comments. And not just address them, but also answer questions related to the comments Rodgers made about him and the team during one of the most stressful moments of his career. To his credit, McCarthy didn’t try to attack Rodgers personally, thus putting an end to any war of words that may have come about had he responded in a more aggressive manner. title: Everything Texans QB C.J. Stroud said ahead of Week 12 vs. Ravens
summary: Here's everything Houston Texans Pro Bowl quarterback C.J. Stroud said ahead of Week 12's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.
content: Here's everything Houston Texans Pro Bowl quarterback C.J. Stroud said ahead of Week 12's matchup against the Baltimore Ravens , including his thoughts on the defense, his connection with Nico Collins and more. Question: On having a one game at a time mentality C.J. Stroud: "You can only control what you can and focusing on whatever is in front of you. I always say like, 'Whatever you have in front of you, you have to really focus on that.' It's the game, even if it's a walk through a meeting. That'll be the focus for us this week as well." On his touchdown pass to WR Nico Collins against the Indianapolis Colts Stroud: "You don't really think while you're playing. When the ball is snapped, I won't say you're not thinking, but it's just very fast. I wasn't really thinking anything specifically. I just saw Nico win, so I was just trying my best to get him the ball. He did a good job of high-pointing the ball and making a play on it. I was just trying to get him the ball as best I could." Q: On having WR Nico Collins as a teammate Stroud: "It means the world. I love Nico as a friend, as a brother, as a teammate. Love the guy for who he is. I see how hard he works from the time I got here. He's doing a great job for us. A lot of things that don't show up on stat sheets he's doing. A lot of respect for just the leader he is and what he's been able to do these past couple years." Q: On the offensive line Stroud: "I thought it was great. I thought we could be able to get a good run game going to be more balanced. I think that's good for us. I think we can still be aggressive, throwing the ball. I think we made a lot of money with that this year. We definitely have to be able to be balanced. I definitely love how 'D-Mo' [David Montgomery] was towing the rock and getting Woody [Marks] back will definitely help that as well." Q: On the Baltimore Ravens defense "They play hard. They play hard from top down, from the safety, all the way to the backers, to the corners, to the defensive linemen. I think Roquan [Smith] leads those guys and has a standard. I think Kyle [Hamilton] is, if not, the best safety, one of the best safeties in the league and does a great job. I'm a big fan of his and what he's been able to do in his career thus far. We have to be on our P's and Q's. They play really hard." Q: On his My Cause My Cleats representation Stroud: "I have my foundation on my cleats, and then I also have another pair of cleats I'll be wearing that says 'GODFIDENT'. That just puts my confidence in the Lord, but our foundation as well. My mom has done a great job with that, my family, we're all in it together. I'm just trying to reach as many people as we can and just show the love that God has given us to others. Helping them out, that's food, clothing, whatever that could be. We just want to be of service to others, so that's what we represent and what we're trying to do on Sunday with the cleats." Q: On DE Will Anderson Jr. winning AFC Defensive Player of the Week for Week 11 Stroud: "I think he's amazing. I think he's been doing a great job. I think some of the things that also a person who doesn't really show up on a stat sheet sometimes because he's in so much attention and helps free other people up. I'm really happy for him and proud of him. I think he's one of the best football players I've ever seen with my own two eyes and just very grateful he's on my team. Just to see the man that he's grown to be over the years has been really cool." Q: On imagining facing DE Will Anderson Jr. in a game Stroud: "Yeah, I would try to line up and do as best as I could, but I thank God he is on my team." Q: On TE Marlin Klein Stroud: "It was cool to see the young guy do a good job and I think he's learning. He's learning fast and he has a lot of talent. Just have get him on the same page with us on what we're trying to get accomplished. Whenever he's doing the right thing, he's usually pretty good. Just have to continue to let him develop and grow and that's up to our whole team to help him out. He's doing a great job and effort or physicality is not really the problem. It's just we have to find ways to make sure that he's on the same page with everybody and he's been able to do that these past couple weeks. Very proud of him and I'm a big fan of Marlin and what he's been able to do and continue to do great things for us." Q: On the new additions to the offensive line this year Stroud: "[G] Febechi [Nwaiwu] has been great. Since camp, he's brought a certain tenacity and talk to the offensive line. I think [C/G] Keylan [Rutledge] is one of those as well. I think [T] Braden [Smith], same thing in the run game. I think [T] Trent [Brown] has been playing well as well. It's a good thing for me, at least, to have some depth there. I think we have to be able to play elite on all five spots. I think the more we have guys that challenge one another is good. I definitely want to get a rhythm going with the guys that we'll be rocking with. Trent has been doing great as well, along with Braden. I thought Braden did really well on Thursday. We'll continue to see where we are. I think it's a good problem to have, to have some depth." Q: On WR Marvin Harrison Jr. Stroud: "Getting him back right now is a perfect time to get him rolling. He's been running great routes. I think everybody's been seeing that. Have to find ways to get him to rock. I think he's doing a great job creating separation and we'll continue to do that for us." Q: On what The C.J. Stroud Foundation is built upon Stroud: "I think self-confidence is great, but when you, as a believer in Christ, we're called to think less of yourself, but that doesn't mean be hard on yourself, too hard. Giving yourself grace, but understanding the grace of God is greater than anything that you could do yourself. So that's what it means to me. I live by that, because sometimes I do have days where I'm not the most confident person, but I know that God has put a great talent into me. Even when I can't be strong, He's strong for me. I love the verse 1 John 4:4, it says 'Greater he was in me than he was in the world.' That gives me a lot of confidence that the Holy Spirit that's in me is stronger than my fleshly being. Even when I'm weak, I'm strong because of who God is in my life." Q: On flushing bad plays on the sideline Stroud: "It's life. You get hit in the mouth, you have to be able to respond. One thing that sometimes even I forget is the other team gets paid too. They're good opponents, they're going to have a play or two. Maybe they might have a great day, you never know. The objective is always to win the game and sulking on something or thinking bad about yourself or bad about that play isn't really going to help. It took me a long time to get that way to be able to, 'Okay, that happened, what can I do to better that and then learn from it?' I've been able to do that a little bit this season. It's not easy, but you definitely have to be able to do it because no one cares about your excuses on what happened or what didn't happen. You have to find a way to let it go and move on because there are better plays to be had." Q: On what confidence does for professional athletes Stroud: "Really confidence is almost everything, especially in the NFL. I've seen guys come from college who were great players, that were All-Americans, or did this and that in college and they come to NFL. Sometimes it could be a coach, it could be an organization, it could be whatever the case may be and they can strip their confidence from the player. Some of it can be, sadly, that people just don't know what they're doing. Secondly, it could be also that this person just got less hungry. I think it means the world. You have to be a confident person because everybody nowadays has an opinion. Rightfully so, I think people are obligated to their own opinion. It's up to you to either pay attention to it or don't. I believe that who you think you are and who God thinks you are ultimately is the most important. I really can care less. Even when you're in the combine process, you'll go to these 30 visits or some of these combine visits. You're sitting in a room with a bunch of coaches and a bunch of executives. They'll grill you on everything you've done in your life. That can strip your confidence if you're not a confident person. I choose in those moments not to really care, because I know who I am. You still respect who they are and what they've done. That doesn't mean that they're God or they're your parents. You can still have a self-respect for yourself while playing this game at elite level." Q: On his favorite part about Thanksgiving Stroud: "I think Thanksgiving is amazing. I love Thanksgiving, just to be thankful for a bunch of different things. I kind of elaborated on that on Thursday and after the game, just on what I was thankful for. I'm going to enjoy it with my family whenever we're done here. When I'm here, I'll be focused on what I need to do, then I'll go home, study a little bit, but enjoy it with the fam and just relax and try to get some good food, but not eat too much, but still enjoy myself." Q: On balancing football and life Stroud: "I'm a firm believer you can't be football all day, every day. People catch me at some random places sometimes, just being a human. They'll be like, 'What are you doing here?' I'm human like you, dog. Just like if a banker, he's not walking around thinking about banking all day. He going to the movies or watching movies. It's okay to be a person. I think sometimes the outside noise, they can make you feel like you're not focused or not locked in just because you enjoy certain things. Now I think you could do too much and be doing a lot, but I don't really have that problem, I don't think. I'll choose when I am with the family or at the movies or doing X, Y, Z. I'm going to enjoy every single second of that. Then when I'm playing or I'm in practice or in meetings or in the facility, I'm going to do everything to focus on what I can in that moment for whatever I need to do for football. You have to have a balance, but it's not a bad thing to be human." This article originally appeared on Texans Wire: Everything Texans QB C.J. Stroud said ahead of Week 12 vs. Ravens

title: Expert now claims it wasn’t actually Mike McCarthy’s decision to release Aaron Rodgers
summary: Isaiah Stanback doubts that Mike McCarthy was the decision-maker in ending Aaron Rodgers’ time with the Steelers. Some may have jumped to this conclusion due to the news of Rodgers being released coming around an hour after he publicly criticised the head coach.
content: Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images Isaiah Stanback doubts that Mike McCarthy was the decision-maker in ending Aaron Rodgers’ time with the Steelers. Some may have jumped to this conclusion due to the news of Rodgers being released coming around an hour after he publicly criticised the head coach. However, when looking at the big picture, Stanback believes that there is more to this breakdown between quarterback and franchise. Isaiah Stanback suggests that someone outside of the Steelers may have called for Aaron Rodgers’ release Analyst Isaiah Stanback shared his thoughts on Aaron Rodgers being released from the Steelers during Good Morning Football. When commenting on the fractured relationship between the legendary quarterback and his coach, Stanback raised a larger point. He believes that feelings being hurt and disrespect being shown would have impacted the stance of the people above Mike McCarthy even if the comments were directed at him. “I don’t believe this was a McCarthy decision,” Stanback theorised. “I don’t know. I can speculate like the rest of us are speculating, but I do not believe this was McCarthy’s decision.” He admitted that while Rodgers and his former coach have had their “tiffs”, their relationship has previously been compared to an “old married couple”, suggesting that they butted heads but made it work. “If that was the case and they’d had some kind of tiff, he [Rodgers] would have been bumped down to number two. Go sit down. If something happens to Mason Rudolph, cool, you come in and save the day because we’re in playoff contention.” Stanback went on to add that “coaches and organisations don’t get as emotional with decisions like this”, suggesting that he thinks it is possible the call was not made by someone from the Steelers either. The former Super Bowl champion didn’t go on to elaborate or point any fingers following his comments. title: Falcons Monitor Claims Pearce May Be Contacting Ex, Rickea Jackson
summary: The Falcons are aware of social media claims that James Pearce Jr. is contacting ex Rickea Jackson. See what coach Stefanski said and the legal risks involved.
content: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images The Atlanta Falcons are aware of social media posts claiming defensive end James Pearce Jr. is trying to contact his ex, WNBA star Rickea Jackson. Head coach Kevin Stefanski confirmed the team spoke with Pearce about the issue. A Florida plea deal bars Pearce from contacting Jackson, and any violation could bring strict punishment from the NFL. Stefanski spoke to reporters on Wednesday regarding the buzz. “I’m aware,” the coach said, according to the New York Post . He added, “We’ve spoken to James. But we don’t have much more to add.” The situation involves a TikTok video where a woman scrolls through missed calls from a number with no caller ID. The original post asked, “Why don’t you just block him?” Jackson reposted the clip and wrote, “Yes still till this day!!!” in the comments. The Plea Deal Rules Pearce, 23, signed a pretrial intervention agreement with Florida prosecutors after a serious incident in February. Police reports state he used his vehicle to block Jackson from reporting a domestic dispute. Officers alleged he pursued her in a separate car, struck her vehicle, and then fled the scene. As part of the deal, Pearce must serve six months of strict probation. He has to pass random drug tests, attend counseling, and stay away from Jackson. If he breaks these terms, he faces immediate punishment from the NFL and the possible return of the original criminal charges. The Brunswick News notes that it remains unclear if Pearce has actually tried to contact Jackson, as the calls came from an unidentified number. What Jackson Says According to reports, their relationship began at the University of Tennessee and lasted three years. She has not spoken to the person in question in almost a year. On social media, she wrote, “Almost been a year btw” with a tired face emoji. She later clarified her stance, stating, “This is ACTIVE!! I haven’t said anythinggg to or about this person in almost a year !!!! and after this I won’t say anything else ever again!!” She also noted the difficulty of proving who is behind the calls in court. Jackson wrote, “Also let’s thinkkk. Any person who brings this to a court’s attention, they will say ‘it’s not enough evidence to know it’s that particular person’ BUT obviously that person know what they know to know it’s that person….” Requests for comment to the Miami-Dade state attorney’s office and Pearce’s attorney did not get answered, per the New York Post. Team Response and Next Steps The Falcons addressed concerns after Jackson’s comments surfaced on Wednesday. However, he offered little detail on the conversation and on whether the team plans further action. At the conclusion of training camp, the NFL had already suspended Pearce for eight games due to a personal conduct policy violation. The next game for the Falcons is Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET against the Minnesota Vikings at U.S. Bank Stadium.

title: Former Steelers coach gets huge new role after Cardinals firing
summary: Once a DC with the Pittsburgh Steelers, Teryl Austin received a huge promotion with the Arizona Cardinals following the firing of DC Nick Rallis.
content: Most fans of the Pittsburgh Steelers will agree that one of the most welcomed coaching changes over the past few years was former defensive coordinator Teryl Austin stepping away from the organization. And while Austin was anything but successful during his time with the Steelers, he just received a huge opportunity with the Arizona Cardinals . According to the NFL insider Ian Rapoport, Austin will be the primary beneficiary of the team's decision to fire DC Nick Rallis, as he will be stepping up as the interim defensive coordinator, a position he previously held with the Steelers from 2022 to 2025. Sources: The #AZCardinals have fired DC Nick Rallis. Teryl Austin will serve as the interim defensive coordinator. pic.twitter.com/EDjN7Qo4em — Ian Rapoport (@RapSheet) November 23, 2026 Austin, who began his NFL coaching career with the Seattle Seahawks as a defensive backs coach in 2003, went on to coach defensive backs for the Arizona Cardinals and Baltimore Ravens. He also served as the defensive coordinator for the Detroit Lions and Cincinnati Bengals before joining the Steelers as a senior defensive assistant and secondary coach in 2019. After serving as the Cardinals' senior defensive assistant in 2026, Austin will now attempt to make the most of this new opportunity as a defensive coordinator once again in the NFL. While his tenure in Pittsburgh wasn't the smoothest, we at Steelers Wire wish him the very best with this new opportunity in his NFL coaching career. title: Giants Dodged An Aaron Rodgers Disaster Without Even Realizing It
summary: The Steelers cut Aaron Rodgers and chaos followed. Giants fans should feel lucky they never signed him. Here is the real cost of that deal.
content: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) checks with head coach Mike McCarthy after calling a timeout in the fourth quarter of the Week 3 game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cincinnati Bengals on Sept. 27, 2026, at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The New York Giants avoided a total meltdown that could have ruined their season. Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers is out of the league after a messy split. This news feels like a huge sigh of relief for Big Blue. Two years ago, Rodgers had his choice between the Steelers and the Giants. He picked Pittsburgh, and now he is gone. The Giants moved on to Russell Wilson and Jameis Winston instead. Those moves did not work out perfectly, but they were clean. Letting Rodgers go was the right play for New York. Chaos in Pittsburgh Look at the mess Rodgers left behind in Pittsburgh. The team pulled the plug on him just before Week 12. Now, there is a ton of noise coming out of that locker room. Not everyone agreed with the decision to cut him. Mike DeFabo of The Athletic reported that the choice is “not going over well with Steelers players.” Rodgers did not stay quiet either. He went on the Pat McAfee Show less than a day later. He publicly bashed head coach Mike McCarthy. He claimed McCarthy missed meetings or even slept during them. Their long history with the Green Bay Packers has finally broken. This drama is exactly what the Giants escaped. A Cleaner Path Forward New York is watching the circus from the outside. Rodgers was 41 when the Jets cut him. The Giants and Steelers both wanted him back then. The G-Men decided to wait for no one. They signed other players and started fresh. Moving to the Jaxson Dart era is much easier now. It would have been a nightmare to get rid of Rodgers later. The current roster is built for growth, not drama. The team just beat the Jacksonville Jaguars 23-18 on Sunday. That win shows they can handle pressure without a star quarterback causing trouble. The Giants face a tough test next. They play the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET at Lucas Oil Stadium. The Colts are struggling, but the Giants cannot look past them. This game is just another step in their quest for the division.

content: ‘Good Grief,’ ‘The Jokes Write Themselves’ — NFL Fans Revisit Mike McCarthy’s ‘Brutal’ Admission During Cowboys Hiring Amid Aaron Rodgers Fallout Mike McCarthy has been at the center of one of the NFL’s most talked-about storylines this week, and the fallout has sent fans back to his introductory press conference with the Dallas Cowboys nearly seven years ago, when he made a confession about the 2019 film study he had described to owner Jerry Jones. The clip found a new audience Wednesday after Aaron Rodgers went on The Pat McAfee Show and tore into McCarthy’s work habits, while the Pittsburgh Steelers, who had benched the four-time MVP late Tuesday, waived him Wednesday afternoon. Mike McCarthy’s 2020 Answer on His 2019 Film Study Resurfaces McCarthy spoke on Jan. 8, 2020, at Ford Center at The Star in Frisco, Texas, the day after Dallas announced the hire. There, Ed Werder, then ESPN’s Dallas-based reporter, asked about the claim that McCarthy had watched every play of the 2019 season and what he had learned from that study that would help him most with his new team. McCarthy answered with a confession before explaining what the study had involved instead: “I need to confess. I mean, I told Jerry I watched every play of the 2019 season, but I wanted the job. So, I haven’t watched every play of the season, but it was just I mean, you do what you got to do, right? … But it was more about tracking trends and seeing what people were doing.” SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer Following Rodgers’ interview, NFL Network’s Jane Slater posted the exchange along with her own read on it: “This soundbite always felt bigger than it was at the time. Cushioned as a joke…foreshadowing.” One fan wrote of the moment: “The jokes write themselves.” Another fan’s verdict on McCarthy’s answer was blunter: “Brutal.” Two fans replying to Slater pulled Stephen Jones into the conversation. The first wrote : “I never liked the McCarthy hire, but my goodness when Stephen Jones laughs…good grief.” The other fan answered the first with a read on that laugh, writing: “The laugh of instant regret, Jones knew that was BS and now he just heard it confirmed to the media by McCarthy as casually as he eats an ice cream sandwich.” Aaron Rodgers’ Allegations and McCarthy’s Response in Pittsburgh On McAfee’s show, Rodgers accused McCarthy of sleeping through meetings and said he had “looked into what was going on in Dallas and what happened there.” Multiple sources around the league corroborated Rodgers’ account to ESPN reporters. McCarthy pushed back when he addressed the allegations nearly two hours after Rodgers’ interview, saying: “I just think we work a lot of hours, so definitely a difference of opinion from what I was told about the comments.” NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported Wednesday that McCarthy had the full support of the Steelers organization and that no immediate coaching changes were planned. NFL reporter Charles Robinson , looking back at the 2020 exchange, wrote: “I had forgotten about this until a former GM pointed it out to me today. He said he never understood why it didn’t reflect more poorly on McCarthy and whether he’d just say what he needed to…to get an end result. The moment definitely raised eyebrows in the personnel community.” Slater also reported that several sources noted concerns about McCarthy’s time in Dallas similar to the ones Rodgers raised, though those five seasons also produced a 49-35 regular-season record and three straight playoff trips from 2021 to 2023. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: ‘I Got a Problem With Them’ — Stephen A. Smith Wants Steelers To Fire HC Mike McCarthy, GM Omar Khan After Aaron Rodgers’ Scathing Accusations
summary: Stephen A. Smith wants Pittsburgh’s housecleaning to reach the head coach’s office and the general manager’s desk.
content: ‘I Got a Problem With Them’ — Stephen A. Smith Wants Steelers To Fire HC Mike McCarthy, GM Omar Khan After Aaron Rodgers’ Scathing Accusations Stephen A. Smith wants Pittsburgh’s housecleaning to reach the head coach’s office and the general manager’s desk. The ESPN personality called for the Steelers to fire Mike McCarthy and Omar Khan before Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos if Aaron Rodgers’ accusations are true. His strongest reaction concerned Rodgers’ account of a conversation with Khan that, in Smith’s view, raised questions about how much the front office knew. Stephen A. Smith Calls for Mike McCarthy and Omar Khan To Go Smith saved his demand for sweeping changes for the closing stretch of a Thanksgiving appearance on “First Take.” After criticizing Khan’s work at quarterback, he turned to Rodgers’ claim that the two had joked in a hallway about what they had seen from McCarthy. Smith argued that an owner hearing that account should be ready to act immediately. “I got a problem with them coaching this Friday,” Smith said . He then made his condition explicit. “If this is true, and I emphasize if, if, if, if this is true, both of them are gone today. They ain’t coaching tomorrow.” Smith’s criticism of Khan extended beyond that alleged conversation. He questioned the general manager’s ability to solve Pittsburgh’s quarterback situation and pointed to the franchise’s prolonged playoff frustration. BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator The implication of his argument was clear. If leadership knew about serious preparation problems and allowed them to continue, Smith believed responsibility would extend beyond McCarthy. Earlier in the segment, Smith said he believed Rodgers’ account. He cited the quarterback’s allegations about missed meetings, walkthroughs, and insufficient film study as reasons to scrutinize the coach’s work. He also argued that players’ livelihoods made those allegations especially serious. A coach responsible for calling plays, Smith said, has obligations to the people whose careers depend on executing them. SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN’s Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer That stance followed Smith’s earlier defense of Rodgers after Pittsburgh benched him for Mason Rudolph. This time, his demand reached the front office, with Khan squarely in his sights. Steelers Prepare for Denver as McCarthy Defends His Leadership Smith’s proposed shakeup would leave Pittsburgh replacing two senior football leaders while trying to stay in the playoff race. The Steelers enter Friday’s matchup at 6-4, and the quarterback change has already given them plenty to manage. Rodgers was released Wednesday after his appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show.” McCarthy acknowledged making the decision to bench him and declined to discuss their private conversations in detail. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor The coach described a difference of opinion with Rodgers and said an ultimatum from the quarterback fell outside a player’s responsibilities. He also pointed to discussions with the team’s leadership council as an opportunity to address concerns. “I know how to win,” McCarthy said, “and that’s the facts.” There was a performance case for evaluating the quarterback position. Rodgers ranks 29th in PFN’s full-season QB Impact rankings with a 67.1 grade. Through 10 games, he completed 60.9% of his passes for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns, and six interceptions. Those numbers help explain why Pittsburgh’s offense was under scrutiny. They cannot settle the allegations about preparation that drove Smith’s demand for firings. Smith wants ownership to examine who knew what and whether anyone acted. For him, the alleged hallway conversation is what brings Khan into the argument. If Rodgers’ account holds up, Smith sees two people who should answer for it before Pittsburgh takes another snap. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: Happy Thanksgiving!
summary: What are you thankful for this year?
content: Thanksgiving greetings to everyone, and I hope this holiday finds you healthy and happy and spending the day with friends and family. The Cubs got a couple of early holiday gifts in Trevor Rogers and Teruaki Sato . As you surely know, the Bears will be playing the Lions in the first of three NFL games televised today.
