title: Inside the Bills' new stadium and its coolest features
summary: Take a tour of the Bills' new Highmark Stadium, from its canopy and snow-melt system to the features designed for Buffalo weather.
content: Millions watching Bills-Chiefs on Thanksgiving night will get an extended look at the Buffalo Bills ' new home, which opened for the 2026 season. The 60,108-seat stadium was built as an intimate, football-first venue with a steep seating bowl, an open-air design and features specifically intended to deal with Western New York weather. From a canopy covering nearly two-thirds of the seats to a massive snow-melt system and an upper deck closer to the field, here are some of the most interesting features of the Bills' new Highmark Stadium. How many people does the new Highmark Stadium hold? The new Highmark Stadium has a capacity of 60,108 . That makes it one the league’s smallest, but it can expanded to an estimated total capacity of 63,000 with standing room only tickets. The move new stadium drops capacity by nearly 10,000, with the team prioritizing premium seating and sightlines over total size. The Chicago Bears' Soldier Field is the next smallest NFL stadium with a capacity of 62,500. The old Highmark Stadium seated 71,608, making it the 11th-largest in the NFL. New Highmark Stadium places fans closer to the field than its predecessor. It features a steeper, taller seating bowl that rises roughly 120 feet and is designed to provide strong sightlines throughout the stadium. Why doesn't the new Highmark Stadium have a dome? While some NFL teams have opted for fully enclosed domes or retractable roofs, the Bills’ new home remains open-air , with a partial canopy designed to shield fans from the worst of the weather while still letting the elements play their role. The dome debate has swirled for decades. Here’s why leaders and the team chose open-air instead: Fan experience: Ownership has emphasized that Buffalo’s outdoor atmosphere is unique and should be preserved. Tradition: The Bills are synonymous with tough-weather football. Cost: A full dome or retractable roof would have added hundreds of millions more to the project. How much of Highmark Stadium is covered by the canopy? The new stadium will feature a steel canopy that covers about 64% of all seating. The roof is designed to: Protect fans from wind, snow, and rain. Amplify crowd noise by reflecting sound back onto the field. Improve comfort in one of the NFL’s harshest winter climates. How does the Bills' new stadium handle snow? Buffalo’s canopy isn’t just big, it’s high-tech. Engineers describe it as the largest and most advanced snow-melt system in the world. Hydronic heat pipes run throughout the steel decking, circulating warm fluid to melt snow and ice. Sensors automatically trigger the system when snow accumulates. Concave shape helps collect precipitation so it can melt quickly. This design prevents dangerous snow buildup while ensuring fans and players remain safe during heavy lake-effect storms. The stadium features what designers describe as the world's largest stadium roof snow-melt system. What are the coolest features inside Highmark Stadium? There are seven sensory rooms. The stadium features seven dedicated sensory rooms. Populous, the architecture firm behind the new Highmark Stadium, says is more than any venue in the world. The concourses keep fans connected to the game. Open concourses and sightlines are intended to let fans move around the stadium without feeling disconnected from what's happening on the field. Fans can get exceptionally close to the action. A General Admission Plus concourse sits just 12 feet above the field, a feature Populous describes as a first for an NFL stadium. Buffalo is built into the design. More than 35 branded areas and design elements celebrate Bills traditions, Bills Mafia and Buffalo's industrial heritage. The stadium is engineered to amplify Bills Mafia. The steep, compact seating arrangement isn't just about sightlines. It's designed to concentrate crowd energy and noise around the field. Does the new Highmark Stadium have real grass? The new Highmark Stadium has natural grass , not artificial turf. The playing surface is Kentucky bluegrass grown by Tuckahoe Turf Farms in New Jersey. The farm had approximately 80,000 square feet of Kentucky bluegrass available for the Bills to use for repairs and eventually a complete replacement of the playing surface. An NFL field covers about 57,600 square feet. The Bills installed an underground heating system beneath the natural-grass playing surface to help keep the field from freezing during Buffalo winters and create conditions that allow the grass to continue growing. The system can regulate conditions beneath the playing surface, while irrigation, drainage and a sub-air system help manage water and moisture. That's a major change from the old Highmark Stadium, where the Bills played on A-Turf Titan artificial turf. Where is the new Highmark Stadium? The new venue is built directly across Abbott Road from the old Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park. The site sits on about 242 acres and the building footprint is 1.35 million square feet. What happened to the old Highmark Stadium? The old Highmark Stadium hasn't been imploded or simply abandoned. It's being demolished piece by piece. Crews began dismantling the 53-year-old stadium this spring and have spent the summer tearing through the more than 900,000-square-foot building. The larger demolition and site preparation project is scheduled to continue through March 2027. How much did the new Highmark Stadium cost ? A new Bills stadium build was initially expected to cost around $1.4 billion as outlined in a 2021 preliminary analysis report completed by construction engineering firm AECOM for the state's economic development arm, Empire State Development (ESD). That initial project total swelled to nearly $1.7 billion by August 2023 and another $400 million in excesses were tacked on to the Bills' tab by November 2024, bringing the latest tally to approximately $2.1 billion , ESD recently confirmed. More: Bills fans paid for Highmark Stadium. Can they afford to attend? This article originally appeared on Rochester Democrat and Chronicle: Inside the Bills' new stadium and its coolest features

title: Insider Gets Brutally Honest on Patriots’ Aaron Rodgers Rumors
summary: Could the New England Patriots show interest in signing Aaron Rodgers? One insider weighed in on the situation. The post Insider Gets Brutally Honest on Patriots’ Aaron Rodgers Rumors appeared first on HEAVY.
content: One insider shot down the notion that the Patriots could be interested in Aaron Rodgers Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 22: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers reacts against the Philadelphia Eagles in the third quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Eagles defeated the Steelers 19-16. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Getty The New England Patriots are gearing up for their Week 12 action, and when they return to the field, they will be without their starting quarterback, Drake Maye. The last time the Pats played, Maye suffered a fractured fibula, which could wind up forcing him to miss the rest of the regular season. As a result, that means Tommy DeVito is the next man up for the time being. DeVito didn’t inspire confidence after filling in for Maye against the Detroit Lions, but the team has decided to stick with him, at least for now. If he continues to struggle, though, the Patriots could be forced to consider external options, especially now that a new one, Aaron Rodgers, just popped up on their radar after he got released by the Pittsburgh Steelers. And yet, while New England could use a quarterback, one insider doesn’t see Rodgers being a fit for this team. Insider Shoots Down Patriots’ Aaron Rodgers Rumors The marriage between Rodgers and the Steelers came crashing down in a matter of hours. Late Tuesday night, Pittsburgh announced that Rodgers would be getting benched in favor of Mason Rudolph for its upcoming Week 12 contest. On Wednesday, Rodgers hopped on “The Pat McAfee Show” and promptly lit up the Steelers and their head coach, Mike McCarthy, which led to his release shortly thereafter. Rodgers isn’t exactly the MVP-caliber player he once was, but he still can hold his own, even as he approaches his 43rd birthday. Through 10 games, Rodgers completed 220 of his 361 pass attempts for 2,241 yards, 16 touchdowns, and six interceptions, which isn’t necessarily great, but it is worth noting that the team is 6-4 and currently sitting in the No. 7 seed in the AFC playoff picture. There are a handful of teams across the league that could use help at the quarterback position, with the Patriots being at the top of that list. On paper, Rodgers would certainly be a sensible target for New England, but there’s a lot of other baggage that comes with him off the field (as evidenced by his appearance on “The Pat McAfee Show”), and for that reason, NFL insider Jeremy Fowler of ESPN doesn’t believe the Pats will make a push to sign him. “While there are teams with needs — think of the Patriots, who just lost Drake Maye, and the Eagles, playing without Jalen Hurts — it’s hard to imagine any expressing interest. Yes, even at a minimum salary. The production (or lack thereof) does not offset the headache,” Fowler wrote. Should the Patriots Sign Aaron Rodgers? Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – NOVEMBER 22: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers reacts against the Philadelphia Eagles in the third quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on November 22, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Eagles defeated the Steelers 19-16. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) Rodgers has barely been a league-average quarterback over the past few seasons, which has made dealing with his off-field antics a tougher ask. For whatever reason, the Steelers insisted on reuniting with Rodgers over the offseason, but it really isn’t much of a surprise to see that things have gone south given what we know about him. On the field, Rodgers is probably an upgrade over DeVito, but the off-field concerns are tougher to justify with his performance declining due to his age. New England obviously wants to stay in the hunt for a playoff spot, even without Maye on the field, but for now, the team doesn’t seem interested in bringing in an external option, which means a move for Rodgers likely won’t be happening anytime soon. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Insider Gets Brutally Honest on Patriots’ Aaron Rodgers Rumors appeared first on HEAVY .

title: Jackson’s Future In Miami Looks Grim Despite Sunday’s Start
summary: Austin Jackson's contract year struggles are real, and rookie Kadyn Proctor won't take his spot this week as the Dolphins face a tough test against the Jets.
content: Credit: David Santiago-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins are staring down a massive decision at right tackle, and the writing is on the wall for Austin Jackson. Yahoo Sports NFL reports that Jackson is in the last year of his contract while the coaching staff actively weighs a change at the position. This is a bad week and likely the end of his time in South Florida. Proctor Stays Put for Now While some reports suggest Proctor is the heir apparent to the right tackle spot, Head Coach Jeff Hafley shut down that talk before practice on Wednesday. Per Sports Illustrated , Proctor will not be moving to right tackle this week and might not make the switch at all this season. The team is sticking with Jackson for now, barring an injury that forces him out of the upcoming game against the New York Jets. Hafley did not say exactly what is wrong with Jackson, only that the player would be limited in practice on Wednesday. The coach added that Jackson is expected to line up at his spot at right tackle when the Jets visit Hard Rock Stadium on Sunday. This leaves the Dolphins in a weird spot, relying on a player who has struggled all season while holding a rookie guard back from his natural progression. Looking Beyond the Current Roster The front office is clearly weighing long-term options while trying to win the next game. If the team moves on from Jackson, they have seen other players step up elsewhere in the league. Chukwuebuka Godrick started three games for the Kansas City Chiefs last season, and Caedan Wallace has two career starts on his resume with the New England Patriots. Wallace started one game at left tackle and the other as a sixth offensive lineman, showing he can handle different roles. The Dolphins also have a pass rush to worry about on the other side of the ball. Rookie pass rusher David Bailey is the second overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft and is tied for third in the NFL with 9.5 sacks. During their first meeting in Week 7, the Dolphins limited him to four tackles and half a sack over 61 snaps, with Bailey recording those statistics. The team faces the Jets this Sunday at 1 p.m.

title: Jayden Daniels: Brandon Aiyuk and I put the past behind us
summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and Brandon Aiyuk were once Arizona State teammates and close friends, but Aiyuk seemed to burn those bridges this year, when he posted several critical comments about Daniels on social media.
content: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and Brandon Aiyuk were once Arizona State teammates and close friends, but Aiyuk seemed to burn those bridges this year, when he posted several critical comments about Daniels on social media. After Aiyuk signed with the Commanders this week, however, Daniels said that's all behind them. "I'm a grown man, he's a grown man," Daniels said. "Things happen. You don't know what he was going through. You don't know what I was going through at that time." Daniels said he looked up to Aiyuk when they were at Arizona State together and thinks they can have a good relationship as teammates again. "That's somebody that looked out for me when I was 18 years old, helped me out when I first got to ASU," Daniels said. "So, like I said, I know the character and the person he is. He was man enough to settle our differences and just move forward from there. That's like a brother to me. Like I said, we've been knowing each other for some time, looked out for me, took care of me. So, just put the past behind us." As for the social media posts that Aiyuk made, Daniels said he was never angry about that. "I prayed for him because he's like family to me," Daniels said. "I think that was a very dark moment in his life." Daniels declined to go into specifics about recent conversations with Aiyuk but said he hopes Aiyuk will be a good addition to the Commanders. "That's between us, personal, but yeah, we did chat," Daniels said. "He works hard. Before his knee injury he was All-Pro, very explosive, big catch radius, so excited for him to have a fresh start, new opportunity to prove himself day in and day out." Aiyuk hasn't played in more than two years, but he was once one of the best receivers in the NFL. If Aiyuk can play at anything close to the level he used to play at, he can be a significant addition to the Commanders' offense. Daniels is excited about that possibility.

title: Jayden Daniels talks how he repaired relationship with Brandon Aiyuk
summary: Jayden Daniels reveals how he and new teammate Brandon Aiyuk repaired their relationship.
content: Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels and Brandon Aiyuk are close. They became friends back in 2019, when Daniels was a freshman quarterback at Arizona State, and Aiyuk was a receiver. They’ve remained close over the years, and when Aiyuk was going through contract negotiations with the San Francisco 49ers in 2024, he hinted at potentially reuniting with Daniels in Washington. After injuring his knee in Oct. 2024, Aiyuk later feuded with the 49ers. Earlier this year, he aired his grievances on social media, and even donned Commanders’ gear. Aiyuk made it clear he wanted to play for Washington, reportedly even buying a home in Northern Virginia. But amid those numerous social media videos over the summer, he even took aim at Daniels and his mother, who represents the quarterback as his agent. The friendship seemingly cooled and reports out of Washington indicated that the Commanders were no longer a possibility for Aiyuk if he were released. However, ESPN NFL insider Jeremy Fowler reported last week that Daniels and Aiyuk had patched up their differences. Earlier this month, Aiyuk hired Drew Rosenhaus as his agent, applied for NFL reinstatement (the 49ers had him on the reserve/left squad list), and on Monday, he finally got his wish as the 49ers released him. The Commanders were linked to Aiyuk as soon as he was released. On Thursday, the two sides made it official, with Aiyuk joining Washington’s practice squad . Daniels met with the media on Thursday and was asked about how he repaired his relationship with Aiyuk. “I mean, I’m a grown man, he’s a grown man,” Daniels said. “Things happen, I don’t, and you don’t know what he was going through. You don’t know what I was going through at that time. So, he just sit up there. That’s somebody that looked out for me when I was 18 years old, helped me out when I first got to ASU and stuff like that. So, like I said, I kinda know the character and the person he is. He was man enough to settle it out set our differences and kinda just move forward from there. That’s, it’s a brother to me. Like I said, we’ve been knowing each other for some time, looked out for me, took care of me. So, kinda just put the past behind us.” It’s good that Daniels and Aiyuk repaired things. Now, Aiyuk will have to win over an entire locker room, as there will undoubtedly be some questions about him. “He’s gotta prove to the locker room the type of guy he is, his character, high-character guy, stuff like that. So, it’ll be fun, but it’ll be a process.” There are no guarantees for Aiyuk. He must be on his best behavior to eventually win a spot on Washington’s 53-man roster. But it’s good to have the quarterback on your side. This article originally appeared on Commanders Wire: Jayden Daniels talks how he repaired relationship with Brandon Aiyuk

title: Joe Milton vs. Dak Prescott: How the quarterbacks compare in Week 12
summary: Joe Milton has thrown for 310 yards in two starts, while Dak Prescott has nine TD passes in two games. Here's how the quarterbacks compare
content: Joe Milton will make his third consecutive start for the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving, facing a Dallas Cowboys team led by one of the NFL's hottest quarterbacks. Milton helped Philadelphia end a seven-game losing streak with a win over Pittsburgh in Week 11, while Dak Prescott enters Thursday's matchup at AT&T Stadium with nine touchdown passes over his past two games. The two quarterbacks are at vastly different stages of their careers, with Prescott directing one of the league's most productive passing attacks and Milton still establishing himself as an NFL starter. Here's how the quarterbacks compare entering Week 12. Joe Milton Milton has thrown for 310 yards in two starts since replacing Tanner McKee, completing 11 of 21 passes for 141 yards against Pittsburgh. Milton was sacked three times against the Steelers but avoided throwing an interception. The former Tennessee quarterback's arm strength gives offensive coordinator Sean Mannion opportunities to stretch opposing defenses, particularly with DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks back in the lineup. Philadelphia hasn't consistently generated explosive passing plays, and Dallas presents an opportunity to change that. Milton's biggest challenge Thursday will be maintaining his efficiency on early downs and recognizing pressure against a Cowboys defense now directed by Mike Pettine. Philadelphia can help its young quarterback by establishing Saquon Barkley and avoiding obvious passing situations. Dak Prescott Prescott completed 28 of 33 passes for 325 yards and four touchdowns against Tennessee in Week 11, adding another rushing touchdown. The veteran quarterback completed 84.8% of his passes and averaged 9.8 yards per attempt, continuing a productive stretch for a Dallas passing offense that ranks second in the NFL. With CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens leading the receiving corps, Prescott has two wide receivers capable of winning against man coverage and generating explosive plays downfield. Philadelphia failed to register a sack or quarterback hit against Prescott in their October meeting, making pressure a significant point of emphasis for Vic Fangio's defense. Who has the advantage? Prescott enters the matchup with the clear advantage in experience, production and command of his offense. Milton doesn't necessarily need to match Prescott's passing numbers for the Eagles to win. Philadelphia needs its quarterback to protect the football, capitalize on opportunities downfield and sustain enough drives to keep the Cowboys' offense off the field. The longer Philadelphia can remain balanced offensively, the better its chances of preventing Thursday's matchup from developing into a high-scoring affair. This article originally appeared on Eagles Wire: Joe Milton vs. Dak Prescott: How the quarterbacks compare in Week 12

title: Leonard Fournette calls out NFL hypocrisy as he eviscerates Mike McCarthy and backs Aaron Rodgers
summary: Leonard Fournette has launched a furious attack on Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy while defending Aaron Rodgers amid their ongoing fallout. Fournette also highlighted what he sees as media hypocrisy: players are routinely held accountable for their actions while coaches escape the same scrutiny.
content: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Leonard Fournette has launched a furious attack on Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy while defending Aaron Rodgers amid their ongoing fallout. Fournette also highlighted what he sees as media hypocrisy: players are routinely held accountable for their actions while coaches escape the same scrutiny. Rodgers was initially benched in favour of backup quarterback Mason Rudolph after the Steelers’ frustrating defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles last weekend. The 42-year-old then publicly criticised McCarthy in an interview with Pat McAfee, giving Pittsburgh no choice but to release him on Wednesday. Fournette was particularly critical of reports that McCarthy had fallen asleep during team meetings when he should be setting the standard for everyone in the building. He also praised Steelers players for supporting Rodgers and suggested the media often takes a different approach when criticism is directed at coaches. Fournette ranted: “When you have players backing up Aaron Rodgers , saying he falls asleep in meetings… you’re supposed to be the example; you’re supposed to be the head. On with your a–! I’m glad these players are coming out saying this and I’m glad Aaron Rodgers came out saying this because, when it’s the players’ fault, the media is on the players’ a–; people believe everything the coach tells them.” The former Jacksonville Jaguars and Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back then suggested Rodgers has little reason to stay quiet after everything he has achieved. Fournette believes the four-time MVP had every right to reveal what has happened behind the scenes in Pittsburgh. Fournette continued: “Aaron Rodgers is a Hall of Famer in the back end of his career, has made all the money and got everything. He does not give a d— about what anybody is talking about. He’s about to spill the beans. Not only that, [McCarthy] has a personal ice cream sandwich assistant. Coach, get your fat a– on.” Fournette’s comments add to the growing criticism surrounding McCarthy following Rodgers’ departure. The Steelers head coach now faces questions not only about his handling of the quarterback, but his coaching of the entire team. title: Lions-Bears / Cowboys-Eagles Thanksgiving Day NFL game chat
summary: Join us at Buffalo Rumblings to chat Lions vs. Bears and Cowboys vs. Eagles as the games unfold on Thanksgiving Day
content: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-NOVEMBER 28: Running back Jahmyr Gibbs (26) of the Detroit Lions carries the ball during a game between the Detroit Lions and the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving Day in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Thursday, November 28, 2024. (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Thanksgiving Day is finally here, and with it comes a featured course of football all day long. First, the Detroit Lions host the Chicago Bears in a game that should have Buffalo Bills fans’ attention even through their meals this afternoon. It’s a fantastic matchup of two 8-2 teams vying to win the NFC North in what may be the NFL’s strongest division. The Bills defeated the Lions in Week 2 for Thursday Night Football , and they’ll battle the Bears in Week 15 for a Saturday spotlight game in primetime. Many see Chicago as a favorite to represent the NFC in Super Bowl LXI. The mid-afternoon game features the Dallas Cowboys hosting the Philadelphia Eagles. It’s a game with a far different vibe and two NFC East teams with losing records. The Cowboys still have a chance at the playoffs, mathmatically, but it’s bleak at best without winning their division thanks to the quality of teams in the NFC North. This evening, the Buffalo Bills host the Kansas City Chiefs in what should be another incredible game between two of the best teams in the AFC and this era’s greatest quarterbacks in Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes. We’ll of course have a separate, dedicated open thread for Bills-Chiefs in primetime this evening, but for now enjoy this space to chat all things Lions, Bears, Eagles, and Cowboys… and maybe some Turkey Day talk! We here at Buffalo Rumblings wish you all a happy, healthy, and safe Thanksgiving with your family and loved ones. As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

title: Matt LaFleur pays Rams defense huge compliment after loss
summary: Matt LaFleur says the Rams' defensive front is as good as any in the NFL right now.
content: The Los Angeles Rams ' defense rose to the occasion in their 26-13 victory over the Green Bay Packers on Thanksgiving Eve, putting a haul to Jordan Love and his passing offense. The Rams were able to force three turnovers while limiting Green Bay to only one touchdown, largely thanks to their ability to put Love on the ground. Their defensive line, led by Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett, put pressure on Love all night long, forcing errant passes and landing three hits on the quarterback. Byron Young picked up the team's lone sack of the evening. After the game, Packers head coach Matt LaFleur gave the defensive line high praise, calling them one of the best fronts in football. "That's as good of a defensive front as you're going to see in the National Football League," said LaFleur via the AP's Greg Beacham . What makes their work even more impressive is their ability to generate pressure without blitzing, allowing defensive coordinator Chris Shula to use his dime defense to schematically eliminate successful route patterns by flooding the field with defensive backs. These strategies led to the Rams holding the Packers to no points in the second half, allowing the offense to kill the clock with an effective rushing attack. With the plethora of injuries plaguing the team, that strategy might be their best chance to win a Super Bowl. This article originally appeared on Rams Wire: Matt LaFleur pays Rams defense huge compliment after loss

title: Maxx Crosby reacts to Aaron Rodgers getting released by the Steelers
summary: Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby reacts to the release of quarterback Aaron Rodgers by the Pittsburgh Steelers after an interview with Pat McAfee.
content: The Pittsburgh Steelers made a surprising announcement, releasing Aaron Rodgers. The move occurred soon after the four-time NFL Most Valuable Player appeared on The Pat McAfee Show and shared harsh criticism of Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. That decision brought a firestorm of reactions from everyone in the league, including Raiders DE Maxx Crosby. "That’s crazy. I don’t know what happened or transpired, but I’m sure there’s more to the story, and you know how it goes: people are going to be digging," said Crosby. The 6-4 Steelers will now turn to Mason Rudolph to lead the offense against the Denver Broncos during their Thanksgiving Day game. To his credit, level of play couldn’t be the reason for Rodgers’ release because he had 220 completions for 2,241 yards and 16 touchdowns through ten games. Meanwhile, Crosby expressed his praise for Rodgers and the unfortunate ending of his stint in Pittsburgh. "Aaron Rodgers is one of the greatest QBs to ever play this game. If that’s his final ride, that’s not his ideal way of going out," Crosby continued. "He’s a first-ballot Hall of Famer. He’s somebody who changed the game and was very innovative. I have a ton of respect for him, and I wish him the best.” Raiders DE Maxx Crosby reacts to Aaron Rodgers getting cut by the Steelers: “Aaron Rodgers is one of the greatest QBs to ever play this game. If that’s his final ride, that’s not his ideal way of going out. He’s a first-ballot Hall of Famer. He’s somebody who changed the game… pic.twitter.com/L37YYyMhDN — Vegas Sports Today (@VegasSportsTD) November 25, 2026 Rodgers and Crosby faced each other on the field only once. It occurred on October 20, 2019, when the Green Bay Packers defeated the Oakland Raiders 42-24. Rodgers threw for 424 yards and five touchdowns, while Crosby had one sack in that game. title: Meet the Wives and Girlfriends Cheering on the Chicago Bears
summary: Several members of the NFL squad are married, including linebacker D’Marco Jackson and defensive back Elijah Hicks
content: D’Marco Jackson and Carley Jackson in 2024; Elijah Hicks and Jordyn Hicks with their son in 2025. Credit: D'Marco Jackson/Instagram; Elijah Hicks/Instagram The Chicago Bears have the full support of their wives and girlfriends this Thanksgiving in their matchup against the Detroit Lions . Several members of the NFL squad are married, and so is the team’s head coach, Ben Johnson, who tied the knot with his wife, Jessica Johnson , in 2014. The couple have since welcomed three children. From their game-day rituals to their lives off the field, here’s what to know about the wives and girlfriends of the Chicago Bears. 01 of 11 Janessa Johnson, Jaylon Johnson’s wife Jaylon Johnson and Janessa Johnson with their kids in 2025. Credit: Jaylon Johnson/Instagram Jaylon Johnson and his wife, Janessa Johnson, met as middle schoolers in Fresno, Calif., remained friends through high school and eventually reconnected as adults via social media. The Bears defensive back later recalled their first date in a May 2026 interview with Essence . “The way she talked to me and about me was something I’d never experienced before,” he said. “From that day forward, I knew God placed her in my life for a reason.” The couple tied the knot in the Dominican Republic in May 2026 in front of 50 guests, with their two daughters serving as flower girls, per The Knot . “She’s an amazing mom, a great friend, and a joy to be around,” Jaylon told Essence . “We go through every emotion together, and that’s what marriage calls for.” 02 of 11 Carley Jackson, D’Marco Jackson’s wife D’Marco Jackson and Carley Jackson in 2024. Credit: D'Marco Jackson/Instagram Linebacker D’Marco Jackson and his wife, Carley Jackson, began dating in 2019, shared the news of their engagement in February 2023 and announced that they had eloped in July 2024. They welcomed a second child in 2026. 04 of 11 Emily Kmet, Cole Kmet’s wife Cole Kmet and Emily Kmet in 2024. She played soccer for the University of California, Berkeley and met Elijah when they were both students there. The couple got engaged in 2023 and married in May 2024. They welcomed their first child, son Elliot , in June 2025. In March 2026, Elijah told ChicagoBears.com that both his father-in-law and his son inspire him on the football field. “My wife, her dad is Sean Elliott. He’s won an NBA championship, so now I need to win a championship,” Elijah said. “I need to win the Super Bowl so I can tell my son, ‘Your grandpa and your dad won at the highest level.’ So it’s inspiring to me too, to be able to continue to get better.” 07 of 11 Erin Moriarty, Ozzy Trapilo’s girlfriend Ozzy Trapilo and Erin Moriarty in 2026. title: Multiple NFL Insiders Expecting Dallas Coaching Change
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are still alive in the playoff race, but they’re not where they thought they’d be by Week […]
content: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys are still alive in the playoff race, but they’re not where they thought they’d be by Week 12, sitting below .500 with a 5-6 record. Yet that’s still good enough for second place in the NFC East. However, considering the Cowboys entered the season with playoff expectations, it’s safe to say this campaign has been a disappointment. Brian Schottenheimer’s offense is still top-notch, but his failure to find a competent defensive coordinator has plagued him throughout his two years on the job. Schottenheimer’s 12-15-1 record isn’t strong enough to blindly stick behind. In fact, some feel like the Cowboys are bound to make a coaching change before the 2027 season kicks off. Read Next 5 Bold Predictions for Philadelphia Eagles vs Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day Playoffs or Bust for Brian Schottenheimer? Nov 22, 2026; Arlington, Texas, USA; Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer watches game play against the Tennessee Titans during the fourth quarter at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images The Cowboys have just six games left this season, but only two are against teams with a losing record. In other words, they have a lot of work cut out for them down the stretch, especially if they still have dreams of securing a playoff spot. Recently, ESPN NFL insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano both cast doubt on the Cowboys sticking with Schottenheimer for a third season in 2027. Fowler even suggested that Schottenheimer could be facing a scenario where he gets fired if he can’t bring the Cowboys to the playoffs. “The vibes out of Dallas leadership are not great. The Christian Parker move was not universally well-received in the building. This might be a case where coach Brian Schottenheimer needs a playoff berth to ensure a third season.” Jeremy Fowler on Brian Schottenheimer Meanwhile, Graziano also believes Schottenheimer is on very thin ice in Dallas, thanks in part due to the high expectations bestowed upon the team, which feels like an annual game of deception at this point. “And I agree on Schottenheimer. The Cowboys are more patient with coaches than their reputation would lead you to believe, but they had very high hopes for this season. If it fizzles out because they blew the defensive coordinator hire, and Schottenheimer gets to the end of the year with another losing record, I think there would be some smoke there.” Dan Graziano on Schottenheimer The Cowboys are supposed to be a dominant team, but they haven’t shown signs of consistently outsmarting or outplaying their opponents under Schottenheimer. The writing is already on the wall, eventually the job posting will be listed too. The question this time becomes whether owner Jerry Jones will be more willing to actually open up the pocketbook for a big name, despite recent comments suggesting otherwise . title: NFL insider shares anonymous Steelers players’ replies to Aaron Rodgers’ Mike McCarthy comments
summary: Aaron Rodgers’ controversial rant about head coach Mike McCarthy has reportedly received a co-sign from someone else in the locker room. Aaron Rodgers’ time with the Pittsburgh Steelers has come to an unfortunate and bitter end.
content: Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers’ controversial rant about head coach Mike McCarthy has reportedly received a co-sign from someone else in the locker room. Aaron Rodgers’ time with the Pittsburgh Steelers has come to an unfortunate and bitter end. After news broke that the team was ready to bench the former MVP, he took matters into his own hands. Rodgers did an interview with Pat McAfee airing out all of head coach Mike McCarthy’s dirty laundry. Rodgers and McCarthy worked together for years, even winning a Super Bowl together during their time with the Green Bay Packers. It seems that the QB has very little respect for his long-term HC, though. His comments revealed the extent of his disdain for McCarthy’s behaviour, and it would seem that he isn’t the only player feeling this way. Jordan Schultz says anonymous Pittsburgh Steelers player told him that everything Aaron Rodgers said is true Pittsburgh has lost two games in a row, and this essentially seems to have led to the decision to bench Rodgers. In his interview, the QB revealed that he learned about his benching from a teammate rather than McCarthy himself. Rodgers accused the coach of sleeping through meetings, missing team meetings and walkthroughs, and failing to properly prepare. Additionally, he also claimed that McCarthy had lost the locker room by leading a chant about the Packers instead of the Steelers. It is hard to know how much of this has been embellished, but one NFL insider says that one player told him that it is all true. “It’s been a s*** show. Happy it’s out there tbh,” one unnamed Steelers star said, as per Jordan Schultz’s post on X . He added that another voice in the locker room told him, “Aaron has made all the money in the world. He can say all that. We can’t. But it’s all true.” If this is all as real as it seems to be, then Mike McCarthy’s job could and should be in some serious jeopardy. There are those who are suggesting that the quarterback has been embellishing the truth to make himself look good. If other sources are backing him up, though, this could become a very bad look for the Steelers head coach. title: NFL Network's Daniel Jeremiah shares encouraging take on Jets organization
summary: NFL Draft expert Daniel Jeremiah sees good things coming to the Jets.
content: Optimism has been in short supply around the New York Jets for quite some time. After years of disappointing seasons, failed quarterback experiments, and organizational resets, fans have understandably grown tired of hearing about what might happen next. Here's a silver lining for that dark cloud. One respected NFL draft analyst believes there are legitimate reasons to think the franchise could be approaching a breakthrough. NFL Network draft wiz Daniel Jeremiah recently offered an encouraging assessment of the Jets' outlook, suggesting the organization could be in position to make a significant jump next season. "I could see a world where the Jets are a playoff team next year. They have a lot of young talent on offense and an elite defensive piece to build around. Plus a million draft picks." For general manager Darren Mougey, the challenge now is turning those ingredients into a competitive roster. The Jets have accumulated significant draft capital and young talent, but the upcoming offseason will be an important test of whether the organization can finally turn its rebuilding efforts into meaningful progress. Of course, optimism about the future doesn't erase the franchise's current reality. The Jets own the NFL's longest active playoff drought, having missed the postseason for 15 consecutive seasons. Their last appearance came after the 2010 season, when they reached the AFC Championship Game before falling to the Pittsburgh Steelers. New York isn't expected to end that drought this season, leaving another offseason of questions and roster decisions ahead. Still, Jeremiah's assessment offers a different perspective on an organization that has spent far too long searching for a reason to believe. The Jets have plenty left to prove, particularly at quarterback and in turning their draft assets into meaningful results. But if Mougey can make the right moves and the young talent continues to develop, perhaps Jeremiah's playoff prediction won't sound quite so far-fetched. Jets Wire will continue to provide updates throughout the 2026 NFL season. This article originally appeared on Jets Wire: NFL Network's Daniel Jeremiah shares encouraging take on Jets organization

(Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images CB Mansoor Delane Delane was able to bounce back from his injury woes and was dominant against the Cardinals. He didn’t make any crazy plays, but he also didn’t make mistakes, which is exactly what you want from a CB1. The Chiefs will be playing on Thanksgiving against the Buffalo Bills, which will be the biggest game of Delane’s early career. Safety A.J. Haulcy We finally got the A.J. Haulcy game. The rookie showed out against the Houston Texans, ending the game with an impressive interception and led the team in run stops. Indianapolis still got destroyed in this game, like usual, but Haulcy truly stood out. Next game will be against the New York Giants, another game where Haulcy can get a turnover. WR Zavion Thomas Next up is Zavion Thomas, and he had a really good game last week. He had two receptions for 56 yards, with one being a huge completion for the Bears, and he also got a 30-yard run. In the battle with Barion Brown, who we will get to, Thomas was utilized much better and did really well when called upon. Another one of our Thanksgiving games, Thomas and the Bears will be playing against the Detroit Lions, and maybe Thomas can have yet another big play. TE Bauer Sharp It was nice to see Sharp get a target this week, but once again, we are not seeing enough usage. WR Barion Brown As I mentioned earlier, Thomas and Brown faced off last week, and Thomas clearly won. Brown had some moments on special teams, but his usage on offense wasn’t great, and he did much worse on an identical run that Thomas took for 30 yards. The Saints offense is all over the place, so Brown will need to rely on special teams to make a difference. LB Harold Perkins The Falcons were on their bye week, and their first game back will be against the Minnesota Vikings. It will be the Kirk Cousins revenge game, so now it’s Perkins’ job to stop that from happening. QB Garrett Nussmeier Did not play because Patrick Mahomes is healthy. EDGE Jack Pyburn Did not play.

title: Washington Commanders officially sign Brandon Aiyuk to practice squad
summary: The Commanders signed Brandon Aiyuk, former 49ers receiver and Jayden Daniels’ college teammate, to their practice squad
content: UPDATE: The Commanders have officially announced the signing of receiver Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad. They also added cornerback Ambry Thomas to the practice squad, and released receiver Malik Heath from the practice squad in a corresponding move. It’s clear that Aiyuk will need some time to get used to the Commanders’ offensive system and to get into NFL game shape, and he’ll also need to help run the Washington scout team. His activation will come in time and try to help the Commanders down the stretch in their attempt to win the NFC East. We have made the following roster moves: – Signed WR Brandon Aiyuk and CB Ambry Thomas to the practice squad – Released WR Malik Heath from the practice squad — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) November 26, 2026 The Commanders have signed receiver Brandon Aiyuk to their practice squad, ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported on Wednesday. The free agent, who was released by the San Francisco 49ers and formally cleared waivers, met with the Commanders at the team’s complex on Wednesday . Per Schefter, Aiyuk signed contract to join the team’s practice squad. Free-agent WR Brandon Aiyuk is signing with the Washington Commanders practice squad, per his agent Drew Rosenhaus. Aiyuk once again becomes teammates with his Commanders QB Jayden Daniels. pic.twitter.com/jt8diY95o3 — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) November 25, 2026 This move was telegraphed somewhat, with the Tuesday release of running back Craig Reynolds to open up a spot. Aiyuk will have an opportunity to work himself back into game shape after more than two years on the shelf. The Commanders can elevate him when ready, or they can sign him to the active roster at a time of their choosing. He can be elevated three times before Washington has to formally activate him. Washington has been Aiyuk’s preferred destination, a point that was clear when he started wearing Commanders gear in social media posts over the summer. Some quick background: The 49ers drafted Aiyuk in the first round back in 2020 and then inked him to a four-year, $120-million contract in 2024. Then things got messy. Aiyuk suffered a serious knee injury during the 2024 campaign and didn’t play after that. The 49ers took issue with Aiyuk’s choice to rehab away from their facility, and it created a schism and a rift that was never repaired. The 49ers voided Aiyuk’s guarantees and placed him on the exempt/did not report list. Then Aiyuk went on a social media tirade, torching 49ers GM John Lynch and head coach Kyle Shanahan. He also took some shots at Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels – Aiyuk and Daniels were good friends and teammates at Arizona State – and his mother. They have reportedly mended fences, which set the stage for this signing. Commanders GM Adam Peters was also involved in the Aiyuk draft pick when he was in San Francisco. Aiyuk had 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns in 2023, shockingly his last full season in the NFL. There’s no doubting Aiyuk’s talent, though it has been some time since that has led to production. How long it takes for Aiyuk to get ready is to be determined, but Washington needs him to get prepared fast to keep this good thing going. It’s hard to imagine he’ll be ready for Sunday’s road game against the Arizona Cardinals, especially with his need to catch up learning the Commanders system. And there’s great shape and football shape, which are two totally different things. Let us know your thoughts about this Brandon Aiyuk signing in the article comments below:

title: Packers fans, NFL Twitter rip refs over officiating in game vs Rams
summary: The Packers' performance on the field was frustrating enough for fans, but the officials' calls and penalties didn't help matters, either.
content: The Green Bay Packers certainly didn't lose their Week 12 game to the Los Angeles Rams because of the officials. No, the Packers did that all to themselves thanks to their offensive and defensive failures from start to finish in their deflating 26-13 loss at SoFi Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 25. You can't put it on the refs when you have three turnovers on offense, have miscommunications between players about assignments, your defense can't stop the opponent on third downs and allows 241 rushing yards. That's all on Matt LaFleur's team . But Packers fans and many in the NFL world watching the standalone game on Thanksgiving Eve were still frustrated with the refs, a repeated trend all season. Not all the plays led to the same level of outrage and they weren't all questionable. But they built up for Packers fans over the course of the game coupled with the team's poor play. The first came on a defensive pass interference call against Brandon Cisse on the Rams first possession. There was some contact as the players made their way down the field, and whenever that happens there's a chance the yellow flags can come out. And that's what happened. Pass interference against Cisse for a huge 37-yard penalty. It led to a Rams field goal. 100% not DPI pic.twitter.com/QiQUcaEBev — Jared Smith (@jaredsmithbets) November 26, 2026 That is a pathetic call on Cisse Barely touched him and it was uncatchable anyway — Eli Berkovits (@BookOfEli_NFL) November 26, 2026 Ball was overthrown and Cisse barely breathed on him lmaooooo every week bro — Ryan (2026 WS CHAMPS) (@BrewPack8) November 26, 2026 This is teach tape for DBs on tight coverage. The NFL refs are teach tape on how to make fans hate a sport by calling this PI https://t.co/nd7uxzSpf7 — Austin Krueger (@AustinKrueger_) November 26, 2026 But that was only the start of frustration for the Packers, who ended up with eight penalties on the night, and their fans. The next came on a Devonte Wyatt roughing the passer on the Rams’ ensuing drive. The Packers' defensive tackle came around the end and while he made contact with his hand on Matthew Stafford's helmet, also something that the refs will typically call, a flag wasn't thrown until the Rams' quarterback appeared to petition to the nearest referee. The Rams received 15 free yards and they were in their watch another field goal. That again sparked plenty of reaction online, including from a prominent member of the NFL fraternity. Devonte Wyatt Called For Roughing The Passer On Matthew Stafford. Stafford Sure Seems To Like That Call. Soft Freaking League. 🙄 pic.twitter.com/cpo0FcyzB5 — SM Highlights (@SMHighlights1) November 26, 2026 Former Super Bowl-winning and All-Pro offensive lineman Jason Kelce, now an analyst for ESPN, called out the league with a social media post using a picture of Charmin brand of toilet paper. "Ultra soft" is featured on the graphic. https://t.co/KQV9NfP7W9 pic.twitter.com/L06TYUOHy7 — Jason Kelce (@JasonKelce) November 26, 2026 Shop Packers tickets on StubHub And this was harder for some to swallow later on when Packers QB Jordan Love was hit after a throw without a call. Myles Garrett smashes Love after the throw but god forbid Devonte Wyatt tap Stafford. — Peter Bukowski (@Peter_Bukowski) November 26, 2026 Jordan Love clobbered again. No call. Announcers laugh about it. Because it's a joke. — Bruce Irons (@BruceIronsNFL) November 26, 2026 But what had fans and social media most upset was a holding call against defensive back Javon Bullard in the third quarter. A Rams touchdown on third down had just been overturned by replay following a long drive, which seemingly would have set up a field goal with the game tied at 13-13. But it didn't matter in the long run because the officials later announced a flag on Bullard on the same play. So, while the Rams didn't get a touchdown at that moment, they were awarded a first down and would punch it into the end zone moments later. Fans on social media were befuddled by this appearance of a flag based on the timing - after a booth review - and what a replay showed. It didn't appear Bullard touched anyone. Compare this to Garrett slobbering Love after the pass and pancakes him. https://t.co/EzzFvghaBN — Bruce Irons (@BruceIronsNFL) November 26, 2026 How does the NFL review a play call with no penalty during the play than after the review come to realization that there’s a defensive holding? I’ve never seen that before. NFL and Vegas be playing in peoples faces. — Breiden Fehoko (@BreidenFehoko) November 26, 2026 I’m sorry the foul was on Bullard?! pic.twitter.com/F6UHnWDZu5 — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) November 26, 2026 Where https://t.co/DzEqNCfDUE — Eric Hubbs (@BarstoolHubbs) November 26, 2026 This was the phantom holding call on Javon Bullard to extend the drive Explain to me how this isn’t rigged? #Packers pic.twitter.com/PPQPVfwWT3 — Tony Clements (@TonyCMKE) November 26, 2026 This is why they got a fresh set of downs? @nfl come on man https://t.co/Ga4h7PZIGr — Kurt Benkert (@KurtBenkert) November 26, 2026 While we're at it... How about a replay of the defensive holding on Bullard? https://t.co/87taXXFqdx — Drew Olson (@DrewOlsonMKE) November 26, 2026 Picture 1: Several OL past the line of scrimmage on a pass play, no flag. Clip 1: "Defensive Pass Interference" on #7, Javon Bullard. Like, what are we doing @NFLOfficiating ?? pic.twitter.com/Y7rHDSgegT — Easton Butler (@Easton__Butler) November 26, 2026 Ahhh no wonder they didn’t show the replay https://t.co/jhwBjGndua — Danielle (@toepacktoe) November 26, 2026 Have the Packers gotten screwed by more calls than every other team in 2026 or am I crazy? — Bill Simmons (@BillSimmons) November 26, 2026 The Packers certainly didn't help themselves by their play on the field but did the refs assist the Rams along the way? Honestly could easily argue 3 points on the phantom PI call, 3 points on the weak roughing call and 4 points on the phantom holding call. That’s 10 points from the refs for L.A. — Andy Herman (@AndyHermanNFL) November 26, 2026 This article originally appeared on Milwaukee Journal Sentinel: Packers fans, NFL Twitter rip refs over officiating in game vs Rams Our editors independently choose our recommendations. title: Packers most to blame for deflating Thanksgiving eve loss to Rams
summary: The Green Bay Packers met their nightmare scenario in Week 12. Green Bay no-showed against Los Angeles in a 26-13 beatdown on Thanksgiving Eve. This tough loss will have a number of negative impacts on the Packers moving forward . Not only did Green Bay fall behind in the NFC North division standings, but they also lost to a team they’ll be […] The post Packers most to blame for deflating Thanksgiving eve loss to Rams appeared first on ClutchPoints.
content: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images Packers most to blame for deflating Thanksgiving eve loss to Rams appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Green Bay Packers met their nightmare scenario in Week 12. Green Bay no-showed against Los Angeles in a 26-13 beatdown on Thanksgiving Eve. This tough loss will have a number of negative impacts on the Packers moving forward . Not only did Green Bay fall behind in the NFC North division standings, but they also lost to a team they’ll be competing with for a wild card spot in the NFC playoffs. The Rams now boast a head-to-head tiebreaker with the Packers. If both teams are fighting over one playoff spot at the end of the season, the Rams will win that tie. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur did not hold back his feelings when talking about what this loss means for this team after the game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It’s extremely disappointing,” LaFleur admitted. “Like I told the team, it’s always 1-0, but we’re in a 1-game season from here on out. We dug ourselves a hole.” So what exactly went wrong on Wednesday night? And where does Green Bay go from here after falling to 6-5 on the season? Here are the Packers most to blame for their crushing Thanksgiving Eve loss to the Rams. Packers pass game couldn’t create chunk plays, made too many mistakes Lon Horwedel-Imagn Images The X-factor that has kept Green Bay competitive this season was their explosive passing attack. Unfortunately, it completely vanished on Thanksgiving Eve. The Packers only managed 189 passing yards against the Rams. Green Bay’s inability to create huge chunk plays through the air completely neutralized their attack, turning the game into a low-scoring slugfest. Love’s pair of interceptions in the second half did not help matters at all. His first interception was arguably the more devastating turnover. Green Bay was driving inside LA territory down by just one score at 20-13. Sadly, that interception caused a huge momentum swing and took away Green Bay’s best chance at scoring points in the second half. The second interception was bad too, but the first one set the Rams on their path to victory. It is worth noting that Christian Watson left this game with a concussion . His absence made it easy for LA to lock down Matthew Golden on route deep down the field. At this point, it is unclear how long it will take for him to clear the NFL’s concussion protocol. But that’s a worry for another day. Green Bay made the smart decision to air the ball out against LA. Remember, the Rams are without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. So there was a path for the Packers to run away with this game if the passing game started cooking. Instead, it turned to disaster. If the Packers cannot bully a team like the Rams, how will they fare against an actually elite offense that can run up the points? When the big plays aren’t there, the Packers don’t have a second gear to shift into and can easily fall behind. That should have fans worried as the Packers attempt to fight their way into a competitive NFC playoff picture. LA dominated Green Bay on the ground on both sides of the ball Another reason why the Packers have been relying on their passing attack is their atrocious running game. That ended up becoming a huge problem against the Rams. Green Bay could only manage 51 rushing yards throughout the entire game. They did not try very hard to run the ball, only attempting 14 carries. And even then, their best plays came with Love scrambling or on designed wide receiver runs. Meanwhile, LA did nothing but run the ball down Green Bay’s throat the entire game. The Rams finished with 241 rushing yards, including a career-high 32 carries for 184 yards and a touchdown by Blake Corum . It should be no surprise that time of possession skewed heavily in favor of the Rams in this one. LA had the ball for 40:40 while Green Bay only had it for 19:20. Green Bay’s lack of a running game prevented them from playing complementary football. It’s hard to imagine that Josh Jacobs being active would have made much of a difference either. Matt LaFleur did not have the Packers ready to play Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Packers were simply outmatched in every phase against the Rams. That includes LaFleur looking like an inferior coach when compared to Sean McVay. Green Bay lost the penalties battle, committing eight for 78 yards. They also lost the turnover battle, losing a fumble in addition to Love’s two interceptions. And beyond those basic stats, the Packers just didn’t have that many answers from a schematic perspective. LaFleur deserves a large chunk of the blame here. Yes, Green Bay’s offensive line has struggle a lot this season and injuries have played a big role. Still, that does not excuse LaFleur from failing to work around that issue. It will be interesting to see if talk of LaFleur being on the hot seat intensifies in the coming weeks. title: Packers Winners and Losers: Week 12 vs. the Rams
summary: The best and worst as the Packers suffer their second straight loss.
content: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Thanksgiving Eve, the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams faced off in a game which had heavy impact on the playoff chances for both teams. RG Kevin Zeitler made his first start for the Packers. EDGE Micah Parsons made his long awaited return after sustaining a torn ACL during the 2025 season. It was also another chapter in the Matt LaFleur vs. Sean McVay saga, and, for the first time since the two both became NFL head coaches, McVay and the Rams came out victorious, 26-13. Let’s take a look at what worked, and what didn’t. Winner: Micah Parsons It feels so good typing these words right now. After wondering what the heck was taking so long with the return of the Packers star edge rusher after a December 2025 ACL tear, it was revealed that the damage was much more severe than many of us realized . Last night, finally healthy, Parsons made his first start of the 2026 season, playing about 37% of total defensive snaps. And he looked…great! Parsons nearly got to QB Matthew Stafford a few times, and then just before halftime, we all got to see the sack we’d been waiting 346 days for. With how things have been called all year for the Packers, I was certain this would be flagged for roughing the passer. Parsons finished the night with 1 sack and 2 QB hits, and was credited with 4 pressures on 26 snaps. Good stuff, and it’ll only get better. Welcome back, @MicahhParsons11 ! 📺: Netflix pic.twitter.com/YLmftoOBeY — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 26, 2026 Winner: Christian Watson WR Christian Watson was the only reliable pass catcher for the Packers last night, and he was knocked out of the game in the first half after taking a nasty blow to the helmet, which saw Rams S Kam Kinchens ejected. Prior to the hit, Watson was the only one able to hold onto the ball or…do anything right, really. The routes were nice. The hands were strong. He finished the night catching all 4 targets for 65 yards and 1 TD. His concussion status will be one to monitor as the Packers head into their next game next Sunday. CHRISTIAN. WATSON. 📺: Netflix pic.twitter.com/wXV7uZYgFw — Green Bay Packers (@packers) November 26, 2026 Loser: Tucker Kraft The Packers have had a problem with TE Tucker Kraft all season, and now, it’s got me begging them to stop giving him the ball. Kraft has had some pretty egregious drops this year, has played like he’s scared of getting hit, and has just been generally BAD. Last night, he logged his second fumble of the year, and the Rams were able to turn it into 3 more points. Kraft finished the night catching 3 of 5 targets for 24 yards. They don’t really have any other options at TE, so I guess we just hope for the best? And cry a little? Landman PUNCH. Rams force a turnover. GBvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/Rc7QYWZ47f — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Loser: Matthew Golden Last night was the first time I’ve seen QB Jordan Love visibly angry, and it came on the heels of an interception that seemed to have been caused by WR Matthew Golden running the wrong route. Golden has been great this year. He even showed flashes of that last night with his big 39 yard gain, but this error killed any sort of momentum the Packers were developing. Golden finished the night with 1 catch on 5 targets for 39 yards. Shannon Sharpe calls out matthew golden pic.twitter.com/6XsPpO7422 — NBA Hoops (@Thechat101) November 26, 2026 Loser: Bo Melton It may not be a good idea to stop running and then just watch as the defender intercepts your quarterback. Rams get a pick off Love again. Defense is COOKING. GBvsLAR on Netflix pic.twitter.com/JjAiSSCGb3 — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Loser: Brian Gutekunst We can blame the quarterback (not really), we can blame the offensive line, we can blame the receivers, we can blame the run defense, we can blame the head coach! At the end of the day, this goes back to GM Brian Gutekunst, who put the team together. Now—there are things he can’t control, like the drops, and the injury bug flying through the locker room. But the poor depth at offensive line has been the catalyst for almost all of the bad things to happen to the Packers offense this season. Jordan Love has been running for his life. He’s being hit while throwing. The RB room doesn’t stand a chance. The receivers have had almost no time to get open. An even mediocre offensive line fixes a lot of this. By failing to put together an o-line group that can sustain any sort of run game, any sort of passing game other than “sling it and hope for the best”, Brian Gutekunst has bungled the 2026 roster. The 6-5 Packers make their next appearance next Sunday, December 6, against the 3-7 New Orleans Saints. The game is at 1 pm ET/12 pm CT, and yes, that’s a threat.
