title: Rams aren't the Super Bowl team we expected -- they're better
summary: The Rams that were supposed to win the Super Bowl lost their stars and don't exist anymore. The team that replaced them might just be more dominant.
content: The Los Angeles Rams running back Kyren Williams (23) scores a touchdown during an NFL football game against The Green Bay Packers on November 25th, 2026 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- The Rams were supposed to win the Super Bowl with Matthew Stafford throwing to Puka Nacua and Davante Adams in one of the highest scoring offenses in football. Nacua is done for the season. Adams hasn't played since October. Stafford threw for 140 yards on Wednesday night. And the Rams pushed the Green Bay Packers around and controlled the clock for 40 minutes and 40 seconds. The Rams; 26-13 win on Thanksgiving Eve was their fifth straight, and for the first time this season, the Rams would be in the playoffs if the season ended today. That would have sounded like a modest goal in August, when they were the prohibitive Super Bowl favorites. But the team that carried those expectations never took the field all at once, and it doesn't exist anymore. What exists now is something Sean McVay has never coached before: a team that runs the ball 45 times, wins time of possession by more than 20 minutes and dares you to do something about it. Nobody has yet. The Rams' injury list reads like a depth chart of a preseason favorite. Nacua and cornerback Jaylen Watson are done for the season after seven games. Defensive tackle Poona Ford is done after six, and tight end Terrance Ferguson after three. Starting interior offensive linemen Steve Avila and Coleman Shelton have been out since starting the first nine games. Adams, Avila and Shelton are all expected back at some point, but the Rams know the roster will likely be a revolving door, with players seemingly going down each time they take the field. On Wednesday, the Rams lost tight end Davis Allen and offensive lineman Bill Murray, who will be reevaluated this week. The Rams' injury woes began around the time they lost to the lowly Arizona Cardinals at home to fall to 2-4 on Oct. 18. They haven't lost since. Despite the injuries, they have reeled off five straight wins to improve to 7-4, the same record they had through 11 games the last time they won the Super Bowl. If the Rams hoist the Vince Lombardi Trophy at SoFi Stadium at the end of this season, they will do it as a completely different team than the one that began it. McVay has been forced to abandon his traditional pass-heavy identity and lean into a physical, ball-control style that looks more like Bill Parcells' 1990 New York Giants than any of McVay's high-octane teams. Most of the promotional material heading into this season featured Nacua and Adams. But if the Rams make the playoffs, it will be because they have one of the league's best rushing attacks, averaging more than 142 rushing yards per game behind Blake Corum (731 yards, 5.4 yards per carry) and Kyren Williams (662 yards, seven touchdowns). Against Green Bay, the Rams ran for 241 yards, including 184 on 32 carries from Corum. The Rams ran 71 plays to Green Bay's 44. That's the 1990 Giants' Super Bowl XXV blueprint, nearly to the second. According to OptaStats, only twice in the 21st century has an NFL team run the ball 30 or more times in the second half, piled up 145 or more rushing yards, held the ball for at least 23 minutes and allowed zero points. Both were by the Rams in the last 11 days. For all the talk about the Rams' running backs, the defense has carried this team during the winning streak. The Rams have held four of their last five opponents to 13 points or fewer, including the Chargers to nine, the Cardinals to six and the Packers to 13. They haven't allowed a rushing touchdown in six straight games, the longest active streak in the NFL. They have held opponents under 65 rushing yards in four straight games, which is also the longest active streak in the league. They have allowed four touchdowns in their last six games. And they haven't allowed a first-quarter touchdown in 12 straight games dating to last season, a franchise record. Nate Landman forced a fumble, his eighth as a Ram and the most in the NFL since he arrived in 2025. Jaylen McCollough and Emmanuel Forbes Jr. intercepted Jordan Love, giving the Rams eight different players with an interception this season, the most in the league. Kobie Turner returned after five weeks on injured reserve as the Rams honored the legendary "Fearsome Foursome" by wearing their iconic blue and white uniforms and unleashing theitr modern day version led by Myles Garrett, Aaron Donald, Braden Fiske, Byron Young an Turner. For the first time this season all five core pass rushers for the Rams took the field together. The most damning thing about Wednesday night from Green Bay's perspective is that the Packers knew exactly what was coming and still couldn't stop it. "Our inability to stop the run, which is exactly what we knew that they were going to try to do, that's a recipe for disaster," Packers coach Matt LaFleur said. "And tonight it was." That's what an identity looks like. It isn't a trick that works once. It works even when the other side knows it's coming. For nearly a decade, McVay has been the NFL's most imitated offensive mind, the play-action, pre-snap motion, make-the-defense-guess architect who turned unknown receivers into All-Pros. This version of McVay is running the ball 45 times and daring you to stop it. The Rams have run for 200-plus yards in back-to-back games for the first time since 1984, when Eric Dickerson was setting the single-season rushing record. Over the last five games, they've outrushed opponents 895-261. Last week, they closed out the game with a 12-minute, 15-second drive. "The game honors toughness," McVay said. "I think we're playing tougher. … It's almost like body blows. As the game goes on, those hit a little bit harder than maybe they do earlier on in the game, and that's when you're able to get 45 carries off." Corum spent his birthday putting together one of the best rushing performances in franchise history. His 184 yards were the most by a Ram since Todd Gurley ran for 208 in 2018, and according to ESPN, they were the second-most by a player on his birthday in NFL history, behind only Bo Jackson's 221 in 1987. He was the first Ram with 30 carries in a game since Gurley in 2015, and he has scored a touchdown in seven straight games. Williams added a rushing touchdown of his own, the 43rd of his career, tying Dan Towler for fifth in franchise history. They did it behind an offensive line that was being rebuilt during the game. With Avila and Shelton already out, David Quessenberry, Keagen Trost and Justin Dedich all rotated in, with tight ends Colby Parkinson and Max Klare playing all over the formation. "We were able to control the line of scrimmage," Stafford said, "which was the recipe for success today." Stafford, playing in his 250th career regular-season start (just the sixth quarterback in NFL history to reach that mark), completed 16 of 23 passes for 140 yards and an interception. A year ago, that line would have been a crisis. Now it's a supporting role, and Stafford seems fine with it. "Some weeks it's handing the ball off a bunch of times," Stafford said. "Other weeks it's throwing the ball a little bit more. We're playing as a team right now." That's the real reason the Rams are still Super Bowl contenders, just not for the reasons anyone expected in August. This team doesn't need any one star. A ball-control offense and a defense that won't let you run travel well in January, when the weather turns and the margins shrink. And the reinforcements are coming. Think about what this offense looks like when Adams comes back to a defense that's already slanting fronts and sending defensive backs at the line just to slow down the run game, and when Avila and Shelton return to a line that has learned how to win without them. Is there a concern? Of course. The passing game is the question nobody in that locker room is pretending to have answered. If the Rams fall behind by two scores in a playoff game, can a team built to win 26-13 win 34-31? Stafford knows it, too. "There are some opportunities for us to be better and cleaner, especially in the pass game," he said, "and I'll obviously work to be that for us." The last time the Rams were 7-4, in 2021, they were built for the moment through blockbuster moves: Stafford, Von Miller, Odell Beckham Jr. This team was built by whoever was left standing. McVay quoted his old college coach at Miami (Ohio), Terry Hoeppner, after the game: "Have a plan, work the plan, plan for the unexpected." The Rams that were supposed to win the Super Bowl this season don't exist anymore. The ones that do might be better built to win it.

title: Rams CB Calls Out Refs With 11-Word Message Over Kamren Kinchens’ Controversial Ejection vs. Packers
summary: Kamren Kinchens was sent off for a hit on Christian Watson. Another Los Angeles Rams defensive back, watching from the sidelines with a season-ending injury, had a rather different take on the decision.
content: Rams CB Calls Out Refs With 11-Word Message Over Kamren Kinchens’ Controversial Ejection vs. Packers Kamren Kinchens was sent off for a hit on Christian Watson. Another Los Angeles Rams defensive back, watching from the sidelines with a season-ending injury, had a rather different take on the decision. The Rams safety was ejected during the first half of Wednesday’s Thanksgiving Eve clash against the Green Bay Packers after a collision with wide receiver Watson left him being evaluated for a concussion. The league reviewed the play and ruled that Kinchens had left his feet and made helmet-to-helmet contact. But Jaylen Watson, who is currently on injured reserve, wasn’t buying the decision. The two-time Super Bowl champion took to social media with a pointed message for the officials, questioning whether playing physical defense had become a problem in the NFL. Jaylen Watson Takes Aim at Officials After Kamren Kinchens’ Ejection The Rams and Packers entered their Thanksgiving Eve matchup with identical 6-4 records, making the Netflix showdown an important one in the NFC playoff race. Kinchens’ departure added another complication for Los Angeles, particularly with the secondary already dealing with injuries. The incident happened with 1:54 remaining in the first half. Facing fourth-and-1, Packers quarterback Jordan Love lofted a pass towards Watson, who was tracking the ball near the sideline. Kinchens arrived at full speed and collided with the receiver, making contact around the head and neck area. Watson remained down for several moments before getting up and walking to the locker room for a concussion evaluation. He was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the game. IMPROVE YOUR TEAM: PFN’s Free Fantasy Trade Calculator The NFL’s decision to eject Kinchens came from the league office, with executive vice president of football operations Troy Vincent making the final call. The reasoning, communicated during the Netflix broadcast, was that the Rams safety had left his feet and made helmet-to-helmet contact. The play also produced an unusual officiating sequence. Kinchens was called for unnecessary roughness, but the penalty was offset by offensive pass interference against Packers receiver Matthew Golden. As a result, Green Bay did not receive an automatic first down, and the down was replayed. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor The decision did not go over well with Watson. “So basically, if you hit somebody too hard, it’s a flag,” Watson wrote on X , as he recovers from a shoulder injury and surgery that has effectively ended his season. Jaylen Watson wasn’t too happy with the ejection issued against Kamren Kinchens for the hit on Packers’ star Christian Watson. It remains to be seen if the NFL retroactively changes the distinction. But for this game, the Rams had to move forward without Kinchens in the lineup. He is ranked 58th in PFN’s Safety Impact Score with a grade of 71.2 entering Week 12. His availability and consistently solid production in the spot have been invaluable to a Rams team already dealing with a ton of injuries. His absence, though, did not derail the side on the night. They forced three turnovers and eventually pulled away for a 26-13 victory, their fifth consecutive win. The result moved Los Angeles to 7-4, while Green Bay fell to 6-5. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: Rams grind out 26-13 win over Packers on Thanksgiving Eve
summary: INGLEWOOD, Calif. — Blake Corum turned 26 on Wednesday and celebrated with a career-best performance, carrying the ball 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown as the Los Angeles Rams controlled the clock and the trenches in a 26-13 victory over the Green Bay Packers . It was the NFL’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game,…
content: Nov 25, 2026; Inglewood, California, USA; Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) throws a pass during the first quarter against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images INGLEWOOD, Calif. — Blake Corum turned 26 on Wednesday and celebrated with a career-best performance, carrying the ball 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown as the Los Angeles Rams controlled the clock and the trenches in a 26-13 victory over the Green Bay Packers . It was the NFL’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, and the Rams used it to extend their winning streak to five and improve to 7-4. Corum’s 32 carries were the most by a Rams running back in Sean McVay’s decade in charge. He scored for the seventh straight game, and Kyren Williams added a touchdown and 46 yards on 12 carries as Los Angeles finished with 241 rushing yards. Brandon McManus contributed four field goals. Matthew Stafford needed only 16 completions on 23 attempts for 140 yards (and one interception) as the Rams leaned on the ground game against an injury-thinned receiving corps. The teams were tied 13-13 at halftime. Green Bay had clawed back from an early deficit behind a Christian Watson touchdown catch, but the second half belonged entirely to the Rams. Los Angeles outscored the Packers 13-0 after the break, held Green Bay to just 55 rushing yards, and dominated time of possession (40:40 to 19:20). Jordan Love finished 17-of-29 for 198 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. The Packers fell to 6-5 after their second straight loss. The night was not without controversy. Rams safety Kamren Kinchens was ejected for a helmet-to-helmet hit on Watson late in the second quarter; Watson was ruled out with a concussion after catching four passes for 65 yards and the score. Micah Parsons, returning from a torn ACL, recorded a sack for Green Bay, but the Packers could not generate consistent offense once the Rams established their rushing rhythm. The result carries clear playoff weight. Both teams entered at 6-4 in a crowded NFC wild-card race; the head-to-head win and the possession edge now give the Rams a clearer path. Los Angeles hosts the Kansas City Chiefs next, while Green Bay travels to face the New Orleans Saints.

title: Rams jump ahead of Seahawks in NFC playoff race after win vs Packers
summary: The pressure is on for Seattle to win on Sunday.
content: It may only be Week 12 of the NFL season, but the Seattle Seahawks are officially in must-win mode for the rest of the year. Not only do they need to keep the San Francisco 49ers within striking distance, and hope they stumble along the way, but now the loathsome Los Angeles Rams are back in the picture. On Wednesday night, the Rams trounced the Green Bay Packers 26-13 on prime time. This was a critical piece of the NFC playoff puzzle, as both LA and Green Bay were 6-4, with the Packers occupying the final Wild Card spot. Since the Rams won, they now move ahead of both Seattle and Green Bay to take the No. 7 seed. Should the season magically end this exact moment, the Rams would be in the playoffs and the Seahawks would not. Fortunately, no such witchcraft exists to end the NFL regular season prematurely. But this does put even more pressure on the Seahawks to win on Sunday over the 49ers. If they do, they will jump the Rams and take the No. 7 spot for themselves as they own a better in-division record tiebreaker over Los Angeles. However, should they lose they will fall even further out of playoff contention. There is a world of difference between 7-4 and 6-5, and down in the muck with Green Bay. This article originally appeared on Seahawks Wire: Rams jump ahead of Seahawks in NFC playoff race after win vs Packers

title: Rashee Rice addresses preparation for the Bills' physical defense
summary: During his press conference, Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice addressed the Buffalo Bills' physical defense | @EdEastonJr
content: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice recently spoke with reporters. He addressed the Buffalo Bills ' physical defense going into tonight's matchup. "Obviously, your main objective is to catch the ball, so catch the ball first," said Rice. "Try to react as fast as you can to protect yourself. And when it comes to being able to get up from tough hits, kind of you gotta, you know, take time in the weight room to be able to take certain hits like that in the game because you're going to get hit regardless in football." Rice took a big hit in last Sunday's victory over the Arizona Cardinals; he is more than welcoming the challenge against Buffalo. "Very competitive games. They're a great challenge for us. Going to be a good challenge for the offense," said Rice. "Every game we play versus those guys is a fun game, and we just kind of come at each other's necks the whole time, and we're two big football teams that want to win really bad." Buffalo's defense ranks 11th in total yards allowed (320.4 yards per game) and 9th in points allowed (20.8 points per game) entering tonight's game. "We have to be able to have our hands available, be explosive off the ball," said Rice, "and just kind of be able to react, and that they're going to be aggressive on the front line." Through 8 games this season, Rice has 36 receptions for 427 receiving yards and 2 touchdowns, averaging 11.9 yards per catch. This article originally appeared on Chiefs Wire: Rashee Rice addresses preparation for the Bills' physical defense

title: Ravens’ Mike Green explains how he sets up tackles to finish sacks
summary: Ravens linebacker Mike Green reveals the complex strategy and teamwork required to consistently sack NFL quarterbacks.
content: Getting to the quarterback in the NFL is not as simple as beating an offensive tackle and running toward the backfield. Mike Green knows that better than most, and the Ravens outside linebacker offered a detailed look at the strategy behind pass rushing during his appearance on the team's The Lounge podcast. Speaking with hosts Ryan Mink and Garrett Downing, Green explained that a successful pass rush depends on several things happening together. A defender can have the right move, but that does not guarantee an opportunity to bring down the quarterback. “There's a bunch of things that go into getting sacks,” Green said. “A lot of things have to go right. Not only if your move works or not, you got to make sure that our coverage is locked down.” Green explained that strong coverage gives the pass rush more time to get home. Defenders also have to work together, maintain their rush lanes and make sure the quarterback does not get rid of the football before they can finish the play. “You got to make sure that the defensive line is rushing together, and you got to just make sure that it's a third-and-long situation and the quarterback is dropping to a certain depth,” Green said. Another important part of the job is setting up the offensive tackle. Green said pass rushers cannot simply rely on the same move over and over because offensive linemen are constantly adjusting to what they have seen. “I think that's probably one of the key things to be a really good pass rusher,” Green said. “You have to set up the tackle and you have to be in the right situations and in the right place at the right time.” For an edge defender, repeatedly threatening the outside shoulder of an offensive tackle can force the blocker to change his positioning. Green's explanation illustrates why he considers the spin move a change of pace. Its effectiveness can depend on how the tackle has responded to his previous rushes. He described the matchup as a back-and-forth game in which both players are trying to anticipate what the other will do. “You want to do moves based off what he does, and he wants to stop your moves based off what you previously have done,” Green explained. “So it's just like you're playing this back-and-forth game.” That is also why Green does not rely on his spin move every time he rushes the passer. He views it as a changeup that can be more effective after he has shown an offensive tackle other moves. “I'll probably just say whenever I just need to change up,” Green said. “Sometimes I'm like, no, I shouldn't do it at all. Sometimes we're just like, yeah, you know, I should probably do it a little bit more than often. But I kind of just think it just depends on the type of game it is, what the offense is doing, and where we are in the game.” Green also emphasized the importance of coverage, an area that has contributed to Baltimore's defensive inconsistency this season. When opposing quarterbacks can identify an open receiver immediately after the snap, even a successful move at the line of scrimmage may produce little more than a pressure. Improvements in the secondary could create additional finishing opportunities for Green and the rest of Anthony Weaver's front. Green's explanation provides a glimpse into the preparation and decision-making behind his recent production. His growing sack total is the result of more than individual athleticism; it also reflects the timing, teamwork and technique required to consistently pressure NFL quarterbacks. This article originally appeared on Ravens Wire: Ravens’ Mike Green explains how he sets up tackles to finish sacks

title: Rome Odunze looking to feast on Lions' defense on Thanksgiving
summary: Former Washington star Rome Odunze has a great chance to put together a huge day against the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving.
content: Since the Chicago Bears selected Rome Odunze and quarterback Caleb Williams in the top ten of the 2024 NFL draft, the tandem has never beaten the Detroit Lions. Now, tied with their NFC North rivals atop the division at 8-2, they have an opportunity to vault into first place with a victory on Thanksgiving. In his third season in the Windy City, Odunze battled through some drops early in the year, but has looked increasingly confident over the last month, and has hauled in 36 catches for 573 yards and a touchdown on the year, while losing out on some of his target share to 2025 second-round pick Luther Burden III. As they head to the Motor City on Thursday, Williams and Odunze will not only have a chance to earn their first win over the Lions and right the late-game blunders of former head coach Matt Eberflus in a 2024 loss, but they can also rack up some gaudy numbers in the process. What a route by Rome Odunze 👏 TBvsCHI on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/eR58ZzU4Ma — NFL (@NFL) November 9, 2026 The Lions have allowed 2,331 passing yards so far this year, the tenth-most in the NFL, and facing coach Ben Johnson's offense in his second year at the helm has proven to be a difficult challenge for all defensive coordinators this season. For Odunze specifically, who is averaging 15.9 yards per reception, the Lions' tendency to play a lot of man "Rome is looking to play fast, and his superpower is being able to make contested catches," Johnson said of Odunze in the preseason. "He’s making plenty of separation, and I’m really pleased to see him and Caleb’s ball placement and going up for the ball as needed. I look forward (to) sinking into that." With just his lone score on the year, Thursday also feels like a prime spot for Odunze to find the end zone, as Detroit's 21 passing touchdowns allowed are the third-most in the NFL. This article originally appeared on Huskies Wire: Rome Odunze looking to feast on Lions' defense on Thanksgiving

title: What Romeo Doubs returning to practice means for the Patriots
summary: The veteran wide receiver was back in action on Wednesday.
content: The New England Patriots offense is still missing some of its most important players, including quarterback Drake Maye, due to injury. However, in the last three days, it saw two starters return to practice: after left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker made his comeback on Monday , wide receiver Romeo Doubs was back in action on Wednesday . Both have now officially been designated to return from injured reserve and are eligible to rejoin New England’s active roster as soon as this week’s game against the Los Angeles Chargers. How else does this impact the team, though? Let’s find out. Window open We will speak about the on-field impact of a potential Doubs return to the Patriots’ 53-man roster as soon as it happens. For now, however, let’s focus on the return designation and what it means for the team As noted above, Doubs has now been designated to return from injured reserve to New England’s active roster. He is allowed to carry that status for 21 days, and he can be activated at any point during those three weeks. If the Patriots opt against that move by December 16, however, he will have to return to IR and stay there for the remainder of the season. Given the limited nature of return designations — more on that topic shortly — the Patriots would not have brought Doubs back to practice if they didn’t feel good about his ability to return to the 53-man team and eventual game day squad. There are still questions about the timing, especially given that he will have only two practice opportunities this week due to the Thanksgiving break on Thursday. At least theoretically, however, an activation could happen as soon as this week. Roster crunch Given those aforementioned questions about Doubs’ return, the Patriots might opt to play things safe and keep him on injured reserve until next week. If so, they would h ave bought themselves some extra time to find what will have to be two open roster spots at one point. Besides Dubs, after all, the aforementioned Alijah Vera-Tucker is also in line to return. Given that he already was back at practice on Monday, his activation appears to be closer than his teammates’. Either way, at one point the Patriots will have to create two roster spots to bring both starters back into the mix. How they will do is anybody’s guess, but there are options. Drake Maye, for example, might be a candidate to be moved to injured reserve himself given that his fractured fibula is expected to keep him out at least six weeks — longer than the four-week minimum stay on IR. Offensive lineman Walter Rouse, who remains in concussion protocol two weeks after first entering it, is another player to watch. In addition, the Patriots also might decide to simply cut some back-end-of-the-roster players. One spot left We’ve been seemingly speaking about it ad nauseam this season, but that is the nature of the Patriots’ 2026 campaign. So, here it goes again: NFL teams are permitted to return eight players from injured reserve during the regular season, plus two more if they qualify for the playoffs. Leaving those two extra spots to the side for now, the Patriots are now down to their final return spot. Doubs, after all, has become the seventh player to be brought back off IR, joining fellow wideouts A.J. Brown and Mack Hollins, fullback Reggie Gilliam, and offensive linemen Marcus Bryan, Greg Van Roten and Alijah Vera-Tucker. With one spot remaining, only one of RB TreVeyon Henderson, RG Mike Onwenu, ED Quintayvious Hutchins, LB Khalil Jacobs and S Dell Pettus will be able to return during the regular season. Of course, should Drake Maye join that list, he would be the top candidate to be brought back both in status and expected length of recovery. For the time being, though, we have one spot and at least five players vying for it — if they are physically possible to return in the first place.

title: Seahawks news: 3 players who need to step up most after bye week
summary: Here is a look at the three players who need to step up most for the Seahawks down the back half of the 2026 season.
content: The Seattle Seahawks approach the final stretch of the 2026 NFL season coming out of their bye week with an opportunity to regroup, address areas of their attack that need to be fixed on both offense and defense and make a playoff run. While Seattle has several established playmakers on its roster, three important players in particular who have not played up to par this year will need to step up most as the team looks to remain in contention for another Super Bowl win at the end of the season. 1. Rashid Shaheed, WR Shaheed entered the 2026 season with expectations to have an increased role in Seattle's offense, but his production has underwhelmed thus far this year. Despite his explosive speed and big-play potential, he has struggled to become a consistent part of the passing attack. Shaheed has recorded 171 receiving yards this season and has yet to score a receiving touchdown on the year. One of the biggest concerns for Shaheed has been his lack of increased involvement in the Seahawks offense that was expected to materialize this season, as he's averaged just four targets per game. Seattle needs to make a greater effort to scheme up additional opportunities for him, particularly with downfield routes that allow him to exploit open space and stretch the field. Getting Shaheed more involved on short and intermediate routes will also help establish his rhythm and make him a more consistent weapon that will be needed for the team moving forward, especially if they secure a playoff berth. 3. Sam Darnold, QB The Seahawks will ultimately go as far as Darnold takes them when it comes to him playing quality football. His ability to protect the ball, make timely decisions and deliver in critical situations will determine how far this team can go. Darnold has had a noticeably down year in 2026, as he's completed a poor 60.2% of his passes for 1,478 yards and 10 touchdowns through seven games played thus far. The most concerning part of his play has been the nine interceptions that he has thrown this year, which is fourth-most in the league. Reducing his interceptions must be a priority for him after the bye week. However, Darnold also needs to become more dynamic as a playmaker, extending plays and finding ways to create opportunities in all three phases of the field when the pocket breaks down. If he is able to combine his aggressive mentality with improved decision-making and bold plays that create momentum in the game and bring life to the offense, Seattle will have a legitimate opportunity to compete for another Super Bowl championship this year. 2. AJ Barner, TE Barner has the capability to emerge as a legitimate receiving option in Seattle's offense. His versatility and ability to create mismatches make him an intriguing weapon who deserves a larger role in the passing game. However, he too has not put up numbers on the year and needs to get more involved in the offense. Barner has recorded only 229 receiving yards and a REC touchdown across 10 games played this season, which does not put him on track to finish with even 500 REC yards on the year -- a total he eclipsed last season. The Seahawks need to utilize him more frequently in the intermediate areas of the field. Giving Barner additional opportunities will provide Darnold with another reliable option in the receiving game, take pressure off of Darnold and add more variance to the offense. Establishing a stronger connection with Barner will also help Darnold avoid forcing throws into coverage and reduce his interceptions on the year. This article originally appeared on Seahawks Wire: Seahawks news: 3 players who need to step up most after bye week

title: Who is singing the national anthem for Bears-Lions on Thanksgiving?
summary: An "Off Campus" star will kick things off in Detroit on Thanksgiving with the national anthem for Bears vs. Lions.
content: Although there is no Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade on Thursday -- it has been moved to Saturday thanks to high winds and heavy rain on the East Coast -- there are still plenty of holiday traditions to observe, starting with back-to-back-to-back NFL games . The Detroit Lions kick things off by hosting the Chicago Bears at 1 p.m. ET in a game that will be aired on CBS. Both the Bears and Lions sit with an impressive 8-2 record atop the NFC North, so there are no worries that the on-field action will be hotly contested. We also know that the halftime will be high energy as the Wu-Tang Clan is taking to the field for the performance at the break. But who is getting things started with the national anthem? That would be actor and singer -- and Michigander -- Antonio Cipriano. Cipriano is one of the stars of the Prime Video series Off Campus , which returns for its second season on April 28, 2027. Actor, recording artist, and Michigan-native - Antonio Cipriano - will perform the national anthem ahead of the Lions Thanksgiving Day game against the Bears at Ford Field. pic.twitter.com/uR758JwvCV — Detroit Lions (@Lions) November 1, 2026 Bears-Lions kicks off at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. This article originally appeared on For The Win: Who is singing the national anthem for Bears-Lions on Thanksgiving?

title: Skip Bayless’ scathing Mike McCarthy nickname resurfaces after Aaron Rodgers sleeping claims
summary: Skip Bayless’ old criticism of Mike McCarthy has resurfaced after Aaron Rodgers accused the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach of falling asleep during team meetings. The NFL pundit gave McCarthy the nickname ‘Mike McSleepy’ back in 2021, and his comments have taken on a new relevance following Rodgers’ recent allegations.
content: Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images Skip Bayless’ old criticism of Mike McCarthy has resurfaced after Aaron Rodgers accused the Pittsburgh Steelers head coach of falling asleep during team meetings. The NFL pundit gave McCarthy the nickname ‘Mike McSleepy’ back in 2021, and his comments have taken on a new relevance following Rodgers’ recent allegations. Rodgers claimed McCarthy arrived late to a quarterbacks’ meeting, fell asleep twice while snoring loudly and then walked out without explanation. The former Green Bay Packers quarterback suggested this was not an isolated incident, as similar behaviour had taken place during their previous years together. However, this is not the first time McCarthy has faced questions about his alertness during games and meetings. Bayless famously took aim at the coach on Fox Sports’ Undisputed after the Dallas Cowboys suffered a 23-19 defeat to the New York Giants in January 2021. The Cowboys entered that game at 6-9 and needed a victory to keep their playoff hopes alive. Instead, they lost to the Giants and missed the postseason, prompting Bayless to deliver a lengthy rant about McCarthy’s role on the sideline. “What have I had a problem with all year long? I’ve sat over here and said this 100 times this season. I keep asking: What does Mike McCarthy do on the sideline? He doesn’t call plays; he doesn’t overrule or rule on special teams; he just sort of stands over there with his hands in his pockets, blinking and looking around like, ‘Am I the head coach?’ I’m not sure. “Mike McCarthy is Mike McSleepy. He has challenged two plays the whole year and I’m saying, ‘Who is he and what is he doing over there?’ You know what a pond looks like with a frog on a lilypad; he’s like a big old bullfrog on a lilypad just sunning himself on Sunday afternoon.” Bayless’ comments have resurfaced amid the growing controversy surrounding McCarthy’s treatment of Rodgers and the 42-year-old’s departure from Pittsburgh. The old ‘Mike McSleepy’ nickname now feels particularly relevant given the allegations Rodgers made. Read more: Stephen A. Smith tells Aaron Rodgers what he should do next after Steelers release How the weather forecast is having surprise impact on Buffalo Bills vs. Kansas City Chiefs Thanksgiving ticket prices Leonard Fournette calls out NFL hypocrisy as he eviscerates Mike McCarthy and backs Aaron Rodgers

title: Sources back Rodgers’ claims on McCarthy: “It’s all true”
summary: Multiple NFL sources have corroborated key parts of Aaron Rodgers’ account of his time with Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy, according to ESPN. Rodgers went on The Pat McAfee Show Wednesday and said McCarthy snored through meetings, missed walk-throughs, fell behind on film, and once broke a Steelers halftime huddle by saying “1-2-3 Packers.” One…
content: Nov 22, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy on the sidelines against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images Multiple NFL sources have corroborated key parts of Aaron Rodgers’ account of his time with Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy, according to ESPN. Rodgers went on The Pat McAfee Show Wednesday and said McCarthy snored through meetings, missed walk-throughs, fell behind on film, and once broke a Steelers halftime huddle by saying “1-2-3 Packers.” One source told ESPN’s Brooke Pryor, “It’s all true.” McCarthy himself later acknowledged the “Packers” line, calling it an “embarrassing moment.” Other reporting fills in the background of the split. Sources told NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo that Rodgers asked to take over offensive play-calling and was turned down; a possible compromise of having quarterback coach Tom Arth relay the plays never materialized. A separate source told ESPN’s Adam Schefter that McCarthy “crossed” Rodgers, prompting the public comments. Rodgers has also said similar issues existed during McCarthy’s earlier tenures in Green Bay and Dallas. The Steelers waived Rodgers Wednesday afternoon after benching him Tuesday night for Friday’s game against the Broncos. Organization sources say McCarthy retains full support and will remain head coach. Mason Rudolph is set to start in Denver as the 6-4 Steelers chase a playoff spot.

title: Stats and Snaps – 2026 Week 11, Commanders vs Bengals
summary: The Cardiac Commanders keep post-season hopes alive with their nail-biting finish is as many weeks
content: The story of the Commanders’ season has been playing up to the level of the best teams in the league and playing down to the level of some of the worst ones. Until Week 9, they have struggled to find ways to win close games. For the second week in a row, the Commanders pulled off a game winning drive after the two minute warning. While it may be too early to pronounce a turnaround to the disappointing 2026 season, fans who have kept hope alive for a return to 2024 form would have recognised the calm determination and surgical precision Jayden Daniels showed as he led the team into field goal range with 39 seconds remaining. Over the past few games, the Commanders’ identity has finally started to come into focus. In addition to a magician at QB, Daronte Jones’ aggressive defense is emerging as a strength. The Bengals rank 4 th in total points. Prior to facing the Commanders, they were averaging 30.9 point per game. The Commanders are one of only three teams to hold them to under 27 points, along with the Jaguars and Texans. That level of defense, and a quarterback who is up to any challenge, can allow them to compete with the best teams in football, if they can just stay out of their own way. Drew Stevens’ 26 yard field goal with time expiring sealed the Commanders’ first back-to-back win since the divisional round of the 2024 playoffs. They need to keep stacking the wins to catch up with the division-leading Giants and keep their playoff-hopes alive. Fortunately, they only need to tie the Giants’ win total to win the division, thanks to the Week 10 win giving them the advantage of the head-to-head tiebreaker. The Commanders only play two opponents with winning records in seven remaining games, while the Giants have yet to run the gauntlet of the 49ers, Seahawks and Lions. Hopefully the Cowboys stay out of the mix. But the Commanders may have the opportunity to settle the matter if Jerry’s boys make it close by the Week 18 rematch. There is still a lot of football left to play. Against the 7-2 Bengals, the Commanders did what they needed to do to keep their season alive. They will need to keep building on the winning formula of aggressive defense, ball control and executing when it matters to get off of life support and hit the post-season with momentum. Fans who still have doubts just need to rewatch the final two minutes of Monday night’s game. To drive that message home, let’s take a look at who stood out – it’s a long list – whose play left room for improvement – shorter list – and where they all lined up in the Commanders’ 22-20 upset of the Cincinnati Bengals in primetime. Technicalities: Stats were sourced from the official NFL gamebook via NFLGSIS, Pro Football Reference (PFR), Pro Football Focus (PFF) and ESPN’s total QBR. In cases where advanced stats are scored differently, I have chosen preferred providers (eg. QB pressures – PFF, yards before contact – PFR). Where differences in advanced stats result from judgment calls (eg. Coverage yards allowed, broken tackles) I have gone with a modified consensus approach. When there is fundamental disagreement between sources, the stats won’t be reported. Minor differences between sources that support the same conclusion are reported. If advanced stats are reported without attribution of source, it means there was consensus. As always, official NFL stats override conflicting data from other sources. 2026 reference ranges for the advanced metrics used in the Stats and Snaps were published in the Week 10 Stats Roundups ( Offense , Defense ), to help readers get a sense of what are good or not so good numbers for the different positions. BIGGEST PLAYS OF THE GAME These plays had the largest impact on teams’ scoring potential within a drive, as judged by Expected Points Added (EPA). Threshhold: EPA = +/- 2.20 Biggest Plays for Commanders Q4, 0.23, 2 nd and 10 at WAS 50: Jayden Daniels pass complete deep middle to Antonio Williams for 42 yards. EPA 3.66 Q4, 6:48, 2 nd and 20 at WAS 25: Jayden Daniels pass complete deep middle to Stefon Diggs for 29 yards. EPA 3.15 Q2, 0:54, 2 nd and 7 at CIN 38: Jayden Daniels pass complete deep middle to Chig Okonkwo for 32 yards. EPA 3.12 Q3, 13:44, 1 st and 10 at WAS 39: Jayden Daniels scrambles up the middle for 47 yards. EPA 3.12 Q1, 1:03, 4 th and 1 at CIN 45: Joe Burrow left end for no gain (tackle by Frankie Luvu). EPA -2.2 Biggest Plays for Bengals Q2, 3:02, 3 rd and 11 at CIN 22: Joe Burrow pass complete short middle to Samaje Perine for 44 yards. EPA 4.2 Q2, 2:00, 2 nd and 7 at WAS 31: Joe Burrow pass complete deep left to Tee Higgins for 31 yards, touchdown. EPA 3.82 Q2, 8:34, 4 th and 2 at WAS 37: Joe Burrow pass complete short middle to Mike Gesicki for 11 yards. EPA 3.05 Q1, 3:52, 3 rd and 9 at CIN 19: Joe Burrow pass complete short right to Samaje Perine for 17 yards. Samaje Perine fumbles, ball out of bounds at CIN-36. EPA 2.37 Q4, 0:50, 4 th and 14 at WAS 37: Evan McPherson 56 yd field goal good. EPA 2.21 OFFENSE JD5 completed 23/35 (65.7%, ADOT 7.8 yds) for 289 yds, with no TDs or INTs, while taking 3 sacks for 11 yds. Two of Jayden’s completions for 64 yds occurred on the the final drive, with 39 seconds remaining, to set up the game winning field goal. It was his second game winning drive of the season. According to PFF, he faced pressure on 35.7% of dropbacks. He ran the ball 6 times for 55 yds (9.2 Y/A) and 2 first downs, with a long of 47 yds (33.3% success rate 33.3%). Jayden’s effort was good for a 58.6 total QBR, ranking him 13 th among starting QBs in Week 11. While not used extensively, the two backs given opportunities were well above the league average of 2.2 YBC/att this week. Not surprisingly, both were at or near the top of the league in rushing success rate in Week 11. Jacory Croskey-Merritt was just behind Jayden in total yardage, with 54 yds on 13 att (4.2 Y/A), 1 TD, and 4 first downs. He achieved a healthy 2.5 YBC/att on his carries. Bill’s 76.9% rushing success rate was the highest among all NFL players with more than 10 rushing attempts in Week 11. He also caught 2/3 targets for 23 yds, with a long reception of 18 yds. All 23 yards were gained after the catch. He led the team at an impressive 11.5 YAC/rec, and was the Commanders’ second most productive receiver at 2.30 Y/RR. Austin Ekeler had 7 attempts for 41 yds (5.9 Y/A) and 2 first downs. In most weeks, his 71.4% rushing success rate would lead the team and sometimes the league. Ekeler found plenty of room to run, averaging 4.1 YBC/att. Ekeler caught 2/3 targets for 3 yds. Rachaad White did not touch the ball. Antonio Williams earned a Pepsi Rookie of the Week nomination for his best game as a pro, catching 9/11 targets (81.8% rec, ADOT 8.7 yds) for 122 yds, including receptions of 22 and 42 yards, constituting the game winning drive. He was the Commanders’ most productive receiver, at an impressive 3.05 Y/RR. Williams gained 63 yards after the catch, for a whopping 7.0 YAC/rec. He caught his only contested target. Stefon Diggs caught 4/6 targets for 45 yds. He was moderately productive at 1.25 Y/RR. Treylon Burks caught 2/3 targets for 30 yds. Van Jefferson dropped his only target, a perfectly thrown deep pass, which hit him in the hands. Luke McCaffrey was main used as a run blocker He received the second highest PFF run blocking grade on the team (85.5). Chig Okonkwo was second on the team in receiving yards, with 66 yards from 4 receptions and 5 targets. He was the Commanders’ third most productive receiver at 2.13 Y/RR. Chig gained 34 yards after the catch, placing him second on the team at 8.5 YAC/rec. He caught his only contested target. A week after his breakout game as a receiver, Ben Sinnott was used primarily as a blocker, with more than 1/3 of his offensive snaps taken from the fullback alignment. He had no touches against the Bengals. John Bates spent 19/21 offensive snaps as a blocker. He was penalized 10 yards in the 3 rd quarter for holding. LT Brandon Coleman allowed 2 hurries in 40 true pass blocking snaps. His 5.0% pressure rate allowed was in the above average range for OTs. His 66.0 run blocking grade was well below his 80.9 season average, but still above the NFL season average of 64.9. LG Chris Paul posted a personal best 89.0 run blocking grade. It was the Commanders’ highest mark in Week 11. Paul allowed pressure (2 hurries) on 5% of true pass blocking snaps, which is a little below average for guards, based on Week 10 season stats. Paul was penalized 5 yds for a false start in the 3 rd quarter. Lucas Patrick cleared the concussion protocol and returned to the lineup at C this week. He allowed 2 QB hits in pass protection. His 5% pressure rate in pass protection was nearly twice the acceptable rate for centers. His 76.7 run blocking grade was his highest this season. RG Sam Cosmi allowed 2 hurries in pass protection, for a sub-standard 5.0% pressure rate. It was his second worst game in pass protection this season. Cosmi’s 57.9 run blocking grade fell below his 67.2 season average. RT Josh Conerly Jr only allowed 1 pressure in pass protection. Unfortunately, it was a sack. It was the first sack he has allowed in pass protection this season and broke his streak of 11 games without allowing one. Even with the sack, Conerly’s 2.5% pressure rate in pass protection was the lowest on the OL last week and his second lowest mark of the season. 2.5% pressure rate is above the 90 th percentile for OTs as a season stat. His 85.2 run blocking grade was a personal best, and third highest on the team last week. Conerly committed a 5 yard false start in the first quarter and a 10 yard holding infraction in the fourth. They were his 9 th and 10 th penalties this season. DEFENSE This was by far the best overall pass-rush performance by the edge rushers this season. Every player was above the 70 th percentile for their position at pressuring the QB. None of the EDs made a run stop. K’Lavon Chaisson led the group in impact per opportunity, with 0.5 sack and 2 QB hits in 17 pass rush attempts, for an elite-level 17.6% pressure rate. Chaisson added 1 tackle and 1 assist. Chaisson dropped into coverage on a group-leading 34.6% of pass plays. He allowed 2 receptions on 2 targets. There was disagreement on the yardage allowed (ie. Which receptions were his), but the consensus was not great (PFR: 11 yds, 1.22 Y/Cov Snp; PFR: 21 yds, 2.33 Y/Cov Snp). Odafe Oweh applied the pressure, with 4 QB hurries per PFF (16.0% pressure rate), but otherwise kept off the stat sheet. He did not drop into coverage. Joshua Josephs got the most playing time of his rookie season to date. In 24 defensive snaps, he registered 2 QB hits for a strong 15.4% pressure rate. He dropped into coverage 4 times (23.5% of pass plays) without allowing a reception on 1 (PFR) or 2 (PFF) targets. Dorance Armstrong had 2 tackle assists. He generated 3 QB hurries in 22 pass rush attempts (13.6% pressure rate). Not to be outdone, the interior defensive linemen also generated high levels of pressure, with 3 of the 5 exceeding the 90 th percentile of pressure rate for their positions. Tim Settle led the interior defenders with 2 tackles, 3 assists, 1 TFL, 1.5 sacks, 2 QB hits. His team-leading 21.1% pressure rate is off the charts for iDL. He was second on the team with 3 total defensive stops. Shy Tuttle had 2 tackle assists, one of which contributed to a run stop. He generated 2 pressures in 16 pass rush attempts. His 12.5% pressure rate is outstanding for iDL, and even more so for a nose tackle. While not a designated starter, Charles Omenihu took the most snaps on the interior. He had 1 tackle assist, 1 QB hit and 3 hurries for an off-the-charts 15.4% pressure rate. The tackle assist contributed to a run stop. Johnny Newton made 1 tackle for a run stop, and generated 1 hurry in 13 pass rush attempts. His 7.7% pressure rate is just below average for iDL. He had 1 missed tackle. Rotational DE Deatrich Wise did not register any stats in limited action. Last week Sonny Styles led the group. Against the Bengals, Frankie Luvu tagged in with monster performance featuring 5 tackles, 7 assists, 4 total defensive stops. In 14 blitzes, he registered 1 QB hit and 1 hurry (14.3% pressure rate). His 21.0% run stop rate even eclipsed Styles’ 16.7% mark against the Giants. Both numbers are in the elite range for LBs. His coverage was not quite as good as his run defense and pass rush. Despite some disagreement about the numbers, there was general consensus that he had a rough afternoon in 30 coverage snaps (PFF: 79 yds, 2.63 Y/Cov Snp; PFR: 72 yds, 2.40 Y/Cov Snp). Sonny Styles came back down to earth after his big day against the Giants, with a fairly average 8.3% run stop rate. He had a solid, well rounded performance, featuring 3 tackles and 2 assists, with 2 stops. He generated 2 hurries in 17 blitzes (11.8% pressure rate). Like Luvu, there was a little variance in the coverage numbers. But there was consensus that he his performance was a little below average performance (PFF: 3 rec, 22 yds, 0.96 Y/Cov Snp; PFR: 4 rec, 27 yds, 1.17 Y/Cov Snp). Kain Medrano squeezed a lot of action into 5 defensive snaps. He was credited with 1 tackle assist, 0.5 sack, 1 QB hit, which equates to making a play on the ball on 60% of defensive snaps. He was not targeted in 3 coverage snaps. Trey Amos tied for second on the team in combined tackles, with 3 tackles and 3 assists. He made 1 stop and had 1 missed tackle. He had a tough day in coverage, which is not unexpected against the Bengals high power passing attack. Trey conceded 5 receptions for 56 yds and 1 TD in 44 coverage snaps, spread out between 5 different receivers. On a positive note, he only conceded 1 reception for 7 yds to J’Marr Chase and 1 for 31 yds to Tee Higgins. His 1.27 Y/Cov Snp rate of yardage allowed is around the 20 th percentile for CBs. Other CBs have fared worse. Amos committed the Commanders’ only penalty on defense. He was flagged for a 10 yard holding penalty in the 3 rd quarter. Rasul Douglas had a great performance in coverage, filling in for injured starter Amik Robertson. He did concede a TD to TE Colbie Young, but aside from that his coverage numbers in 44 snaps ranged from very good (PFR: 5 rec, 28 yds, 0.636 Y/Cov Snp) to nearly total shutdown level (PFF: 4 rec, 12 yds, 0.27 Y/Cov Snp), depending on whose numbers you believe. Douglas was officially credited with 4 tackles, 1 assist and 2 pass breakups. Two of the tackles were defensive stops. Original Redskin Fabian Moreau held up well in 10 coverages snaps. His coverage numbers ranged from 1 rec for 3 yds (PFF 0.3 Y/Cov Snp) to no targets and receptions (PFR). Mike Sainristil played 4 defensive snaps without disaster striking. He is credited with 1 tackle for a defensive stop and 1 reception allowed for 6 yds. Nick Cross continued his campaign of disruption with 1 tackle, 3 assists, 0.5 sack and 1 QB hit. He made 1 run stop, and generated pressure on 50% of 4 blitzes. There was some disagreement on his coverage numbers. PFR counted 3 rec for 34 yds in 40 coverage snaps (0.85 Y/Cov Snp), which is not terrible for a nickel safety. PFF counted 5 rec for 54 yds (1.35 Y/Cov Snp), which is a sub-par outing for any coverage defender. Jeremy Reaves tied with Amos for second most combined tackles, with 5 tackles, 1 TFL and 1 assist. He allowed 3 receptions for 47 yds in 42 coverage snaps to tight ends Mike Gesicki and Drew Sample, with 1 pass breakup. His 1.19 Y/Cov Snp rate of yardage allowed is below the 10 th percentile for safeties. Quan Martin made 1 tackle and 2 assists with 1 stop. There was disagreement on his coverage figures, with PFR counting 1 reception for 19 yards, and PFF counting no receptions. SPECIAL TEAMS Luke McCaffrey returned 3 kickoffs for 65 yds (21.7 Y/A). He attempted 1 punt return for -1 yd and made 1 fair catch. He made 1 tackle in coverage. Drew Stevens earned a Pepsi Rookie of the Week nomination for his perfect performance featuring successful field goal attempts from 25, 26, 36, 40, and 41 yds and 1 extra point. Tress Way punted 4 times for 167 yds (41.8 Y/A), with 1 returned for 5 yds (Net 40.5 Y/A). He landed 3 of 4 attempts inside the Bengals 20 yard line. Tyler Ott has avoided attention for 10 straight games, which is what you want from a long snapper. Rachaad White returned 2 kickoffs for 48 yds (24.0 Y/A). Mike Sainristil led the coverage units with 2 tackles. Tyler Owens and Ale Kaho made 1 tackle apiece. Colson Yankoff made 1 tackle and missed 1. Jordan Magee , Kain Medrano and Joshua Josephs made tackle assists. Quan Martin had 1 missed tackle.

title: Steelers owner calls Aaron Rodgers 'insubordinate' and a bad teammate
summary: Steelers owner Art Rooney II talked to the media on Thursday and doubled down on his support of head coach Mike McCarthy.
content: It might be Thanksgiving but the Pittsburgh Steelers are still hard at work, preparing to take on the Denver Broncos . Oh, and Steelers owner Art Rooney II is hard at work doing damage control after the whole Aaron Rodgers/Mike McCarthy debacle of the last 36 hours. Rooney II did an interview with Steelers beat writer Gerry Dulac and he condemned what Rodgers did and doubled down on his support of McCarthy. “He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure," Rooney said. “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond. The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” Now the Steelers have to try and put all this aside and focus on this week's game to try and salvage their season and any hopes of making the playoffs with Mason Rudolph as the starting quarterback. This article originally appeared on Steelers Wire: Steelers owner calls Aaron Rodgers 'insubordinate' and a bad teammate

title: Steelers President Art Rooney expresses full confidence in Mike McCarthy
summary: Steelers President Art Rooney II backs Mike McCarthy amidst Aaron Rodgers saga.
content: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Wednesday was one of the wildest days in the history of the Pittsburgh Steelers. After benching Aaron Rodgers late Tuesday night, the four-time MVP went on The Pat McAfee Show and aired out a lot of grievances largely pertaining to head coach Mike McCarthy. Among the issues Rodgers put on blast were McCarthy routinely falling asleep in meetings, being late for walkthroughs and meetings, not knowing the gameplay, and breaking down a team huddle vs. the Eagles by saying, “1-2-3 Packers.” Several insiders have noted that players have backed up these claims made by Rodgers, which led many to believe McCarthy’s days in Pittsburgh could and should be numbered. However, Team President Art Rooney II expressed faith in the Steelers’ head coach. “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney said via Gerry Dulac . “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that.” The Steeles will face the Broncos on Black Friday in their first home game since they defeated the Cleveland Browns 27-6 to secure a 6-2 record. title: Stephen A. Smith calls out the NFL after what he saw during Packers’ loss to the Rams
summary: Fans may have forgotten that there is actually football being played in the NFL amid the media storm that has been created by Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. Wednesday night saw the Los Angeles Rams leapfrog the Seattle Seahawks to the second spot in the NFC West with their victory over the Green Bay Packers.
content: Allen J. Schaben / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images Fans may have forgotten that there is actually football being played in the NFL amid the media storm that has been created by Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. Wednesday night saw the Los Angeles Rams leapfrog the Seattle Seahawks to the second spot in the NFC West with their victory over the Green Bay Packers. It was a convincing win for Sean McVay’s team, who have finally found their form following the turbulent start to the year. Although focus has quickly reverted back to the situation in Pittsburgh, Stephen A. Smith was keen to vent his frustrations surrounding Kamren Kinchens’ ejection at SoFi Stadium. The ESPN analyst was baffled by the decision to throw the Rams’ safety out of the game. Stephen A. Smith left furious by Kamren Kinchens’ ejection in Rams victory Packers wide receiver Christian Watson suffered a concussion following a big hit from Kinchens. The officials deemed the hit was to the head of the wideout, despite the safety leading with his shoulder. “I don’t agree with that. I did not agree that warranted an ejection or anything like that. I know my brother Ray Lewis is losing his mind, because he’s like, ‘D*** it, we’re men! What are they doing?’ You know, taking everything away from them when it comes to the defence and what it’s allowed to do,” Smith said on First Take. “Do we have that footage of that hit? Do y’all have that? Show that to us, please. Tell me where the illegal hit is on this. What is this? That would seem like a good one to me. Look at that. Come on y’all, right in the shoulders! What’s up? I mean, why is that an ejection? Why?” “It was on the left shoulder, and it was just a devastating hit. He caught the ball, he was in bounds, and I hit him on the shoulder. I just put a hat on him, you know, let him know. I mean, I saw no problem with that hit, zero. At the very least it’s a penalty, not an ejection. I’m like, what are they talking about? It landed on his shoulder. He just got popped silly, that’s all.” The level of officiating has come under real scrutiny this season. This is not even the first time this week that NFL fans have been left frustrated by the referees. Fans were baffled by the Cincinnati Bengals being penalised on Monday night after Joe Burrow was hit late by a Washington Commanders defender. This incident, in particular, only highlights the emphasis the league is putting on protecting so-called defenseless players. However, Travis Kelce has suggested no player should be defenseless when on the field in such a physical game. There are some real concerns over the direction of the game with calls like this being made. title: Stephen A. Smith does not hold back on Aaron Rodgers controversy
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers epitomized dysfunction on Wednesday. After the team announced late Tuesday night that four-time NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers would be benched and made inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos, Rodgers decided to burn everything down on his way out of the building. The 42-year-old called into The Pat McAfee Show Wednesday…
content: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers (8) gets his bearings after being sacked in the fourth quarter, Sunday, September 7, 2025, in East Rutherford. The Pittsburgh Steelers epitomized dysfunction on Wednesday. After the team announced late Tuesday night that four-time NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers would be benched and made inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos, Rodgers decided to burn everything down on his way out of the building. The 42-year-old called into The Pat McAfee Show Wednesday afternoon and said that Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy would fall asleep in some of their team meetings, would miss others, and, in his estimation, lost the locker room when he ended a chant with “one, two, three, Packers!” Rodgers’ comments sparked reactions across sports media and, interestingly enough, several media members and former Steelers players said that their sources around the organization confirmed Rodgers’ assertions. On Thursday, ESPN’s Stephen A. Smith, a Steelers fan himself, came into the First Take studio despite the Thanksgiving holiday just to address the situation. Smith started his tirade with calling out McCarthy’s lack of postseason success, noting that he only has one playoff win over the last eight years, in which he has coached the Green Bay Packers and Dallas Cowboys. Smith then turned his attention to Rodgers. “I am in no way condoning what Aaron Rodgers did,” Smith said. “I’m saying, what the hell has happened to us? Can we not take it? See, this insatiable appetite to throw this man under the bus because we haven’t liked his personality. When has Aaron Rodgers done this? “This insatiable appetite to throw this man under the bus because we haven’t liked his personality […] hasn’t he earned the right for somebody to ask, ‘Damn, why would he do this?'” — Stephen A. Smith weighs in on Aaron Rodgers’ comments about Mike McCarthy on ‘The Pat McAfee Show’ — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 26, 2026 “When has anybody done this? The man has been in the National Football League for 22 years. Hasn’t he earned the right for somebody to ask, damn, why would he do this?” Regardless of how Smith feels, the Steelers have released Rodgers and are reportedly standing by McCarthy and giving the coach the full support of the organization. If Pittsburgh gets blown out by Denver on Friday, however, it’s hard to imagine McCarthy will remain the coach if everything Rodgers claims is true. The post Stephen A. Smith does not hold back on Aaron Rodgers controversy appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

content: The annual Dallas Cowboys game is now as much a part of Thanksgiving Day tradition as mashed potatoes and 2026 is no different. The Cowboys (5-6) will host the rival Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) on Thursday, Nov. 26, at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. The game is at 2:30 p.m. MT/ 3:30 p.m. CT on FOX and FOX Deportes. title: Tom Brady, Mike Vrabel exchange verbal jabs in fun back-and-forth
summary: Coach Mike Vrabel and former quarterback Tom Brady shared a hilarious back-and-forth at Rob Gronkowski's Patriots Hall of Fame ceremony.
content: Former New England Patriots quarterback Tom Brady had a hilarious exchange with Mike Vrabel when the two met at Rob Gronkowski’s Patriots Hall of Fame induction ceremony. They may not be teammates anymore, but it proves the playful trash talk never goes away. Brady and Vrabel were teammates with the Patriots from 2001-2008. During that time, they won three Super Bowls together. Vrabel also had the unique recognition of catching 10 career touchdown passes from Brady. This included back-to-back touchdown receptions in Super Bowls XXVIII and XXXIX. The latest episode of Forged in Foxborough showed things coming full circle when Brady and Vrabel reunited for Gronkowski's ceremony. “No, Mike. Not Coach. He didn’t earn Coach yet,” Brady said. “Oh, man, the beef is real. The beef is rea. Is the rivalry real between you two or what? I gotta know, “ Gronkowski asked. “Why? Because I’m good at jokes?” Vrabel asked. “Are you good at jokes? I don't know. I heard you’re not," Gronkowski responded. The fun back-and-forths show the bond between the Patriots' legends. Who wouldn't want to be a fly on the wall for the full conversation that evening? Follow Patriots Wire on Twitter and Facebook . title: Tom Brady names the four quarterbacks he would invite to his ideal Thanksgiving dinner
summary: Tom Brady joined in the Thanksgiving Day fun by answering some interesting questions that gave the fans an idea of how he celebrates the holiday now that he is retired. The seven-time Super Bowl champion is arguably the greatest QB.
content: Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images Tom Brady joined in the Thanksgiving Day fun by answering some interesting questions that gave the fans an idea of how he celebrates the holiday now that he is retired. The seven-time Super Bowl champion is arguably the greatest QB. He has played in four Thanksgiving Day games and knows what it is like to compete on what is an auspicious holiday for the entire nation. Brady, who is known to be a student of the game, learned from some skilled players at the quarterback position. When asked who he would like to invite to his Thanksgiving dinner, Brady named some legends, while also snubbing some. “Joe Montana, Steve Young, Peyton Manning and I’ll go Roger Staubach,” Brady answered when asked in a rapid-fire question round on Fox. Tom Brady explains why he picked the four QBs to have Thanksgiving Dinner Undoubtedly, there aren’t many QBs who have done more in the NFL than Brady. What separated him from the others was his willingness to learn, and his reasoning behind naming the four on the list was also that. “I’m here to learn, I just think these guys can spread a lot of knowledge. They would have some amazing stories, probably a lot that I could take to the booth with me,” added Brady. Brady’s list had a total of nine Super Bowl wins between them, which shows that they had a lot to contribute to the game. More interestingly, the four QBs had different paths to get to the top, which would lead to some brilliant stories on the dinner table. Steve Young was the backup to Joe Montana during their time together with the San Francisco 49ers. Meanwhile, Staubach played in an entirely different era, when the game was completely different from Brady’s time. His selection of Peyton Manning stems from the rivalry the two had when they played against each other. Manning defeated Brady’s New England Patriots in the AFC Championship Game twice, and on both of those occasions, he went on to win the Super Bowl. It’s safe to say that the discussion during Brady’s Thanksgiving Dinner would have been completely about football and not anything else if this was actually something that the QB had planned. title: Two former teammates slam Aaron Rodgers for Mike McCarthy comments
summary: Former Packers players Greg Jennings and T.J. Lang criticized Aaron Rodgers for how he handled his Steelers departure.
content: Aaron Rodgers' scorched earth approach with Mike McCarthy was like the drop of a bomb. The fallout from its explosion has carried further than just the current Pittsburgh Steelers roster . Former Green Bay Packers players from the Rodgers and McCarthy era – 2006 to 2018 – have started to weigh in on how the veteran quarterback handled his split from the Steelers . Greg Jennings, the wide receiver who spent seven years in Green Bay, and guard T.J. Lang, an eight-year Packer, both expressed their surprise at Rodgers' approach. Neither player confirmed the quarterback's stories about McCarthy, and both had their criticisms for his explosive appearance on ESPN's "Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday, Nov. 25. AARON RODGERS: Veteran QB goes scorched earth on Mike McCarthy after Steelers benching Rodgers' scathing comments about McCarthy came hours after the coach benched the quarterback in favor of Mason Rudolph late Tuesday, Nov. 24. In the aftermath of the "Pat McAfee Show" appearance, Pittsburgh waived the veteran quarterback ahead of Week 12. Here's what Jennings and Lang said about Rodgers' comments: Greg Jennings expresses shock, calls out A.J. Hawk The former Packers wide receiver said he could not corroborate any of Rodgers' stories about McCarthy during the time they shared in Green Bay. He also noted his surprise at the lack of questions for A.J. Hawk, a former linebacker for the Packers who spent the 2006 through 2014 seasons in Green Bay and a mainstay on the "Pat McAfee Show." "A large part of me just wanted someone to ask A.J., who was sitting right there, 'A.J., do you recall any of this stuff?' Please, someone, ask A.J., 'Can you confirm, or can you second any of this?'" Jennings said on FS1. The former receiver said he also reached out to some of his other previous teammates in Green Bay, who also said they could not confirm any of Rodgers' stories about McCarthy. Greg Jennings takes a shot at A.J. Hawk over Aaron Rodgers' 'McAfee Show' interview: "A large part of me just wanted someone to ask A.J., who was sitting right there, do you recall any of this stuff?" 🏈 📺 🧀 https://t.co/TDCzKtxMIn — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 25, 2026 T.J. Lang says Rodgers' approach was hypocritical Lang, who spent the final two years of his career with the Lions, made an appearance on Detroit sports radio station 97.1 The Ticket on Wednesday, Nov. 25. He said Rodgers' decision to air out all of his grievances publicly was the exact kind of behavior the quarterback used to call out. "I think it's despicable," Lang said. "I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has b----ed about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates. Airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. "He has blacklisted I don't know how many former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he was sick of it." TJ Lang on his former teammate Aaron Rodgers https://t.co/0oiS3PybCn — 97.1 The Ticket: (@971theticketxyt) November 25, 2026 The two-time Pro Bowler also cast doubt on some of Rodgers' comments, given that the Steelers chose to bench, then release the quarterback. Lang specifically called Rodgers out for saying he and Steelers general manager Omar Khan shared laughs about McCarthy's miscues as the head coach behind his back. "Then why would Omar Khan side with Mike McCarthy? Why would Omar Khan allow Mike McCarthy to bench Aaron Rodgers and basically side with Mike McCarthy?" Lang said.
