title: Ultimate Fan: Running the ball and stopping the run will be key to success over Steelers
summary: Happy Thanksgiving, Ultimate Fans! What a weekend for football, complete with NFL drama and everything! A few short days ago we were salivating over the chance to sack Aaron Rodgers and then he went and sacked himself…making the Broncos’ game Friday more interesting to say the least. Or as our awesome UFGer noted, “more unpredictable!” […]
content: DENVER, COLORADO - NOVEMBER 22: Bo Nix #10 hands off to Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos during the first quarter of a game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Empower Field At Mile High on November 22, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Happy Thanksgiving, Ultimate Fans! What a weekend for football, complete with NFL drama and everything! A few short days ago we were salivating over the chance to sack Aaron Rodgers and then he went and sacked himself…making the Broncos’ game Friday more interesting to say the least. Or as our awesome UFGer noted, “more unpredictable!” Another huge thanks to this week’s contributor, Wrenchman1122, who’s been pulling for this team for a loooonnnnngggg time, and he’s ready for another Super Bowl run. (and since it’s Thanksgiving, let me just say a huge thanks to ALL of you — the contributors and the commenters — who come here every week to give and react to such excellent insights and fun commentary. I say it every year and I mean every time — I LOVE THIS SERIES MORE THAN ANY OTHER POST I WRITE!) But now let’s kick off this Thanksgiving football weekend with a bang! GO BRONCOS! Heading to the Steel City for #BlackFridayNFL 🍂 pic.twitter.com/WgVtzRESdt — Denver Broncos (@Broncos) November 26, 2026 Week 12: Broncos at Steelers MHR – Broncos are 8-2, coming off a win over the Raiders, sitting alone atop the AFC West and knocking on the door to the overall No. 1 seed in the AFC. How good is life for a Broncos fan right now? Wrenchman1122: It’s been a heck of a ride so far, especially the one-score games. Life is pretty darn good in Broncos Country right now! What I love most is that this team is winning in different ways. We have Nix who keeps growing, an offense with multiple weapons, and a defense that can make life miserable for anybody. Beating the Raiders is always sweet and with first place in the West all to ourselves and looking to catch the Bills? Even better! MHR – Big news on a short week – JK Dobbins suspended and Aaron Rodgers benched. While the Dobbins news may not impact the offense all that much, Rodgers’ decision has been…interesting. In general how do these two pieces of info impact the kind of game the Broncos should play on offense and defense? Likewise, with the short week and East Coast game, does this push Payton toward a simpler, run-heavy game plan? Wrenchman1122: I like our chances if we make them play our game. A different theory, this week – pass early to set up the run as Pittsburgh has a good run D and the secondary can be taken advantage of, especially on quick hits with Waddle in motion or Sutton bodying up the defender. And let’s keep using Engram and his speed, which was evident last week against the dreaded Raiders. The weather will play havoc with specific planning, and with Rogers being benched and ultimately released, I’d expect plenty of runs and quick throws to help Rudolph get settled. We need to stop the run…if we can stop the run, we have an excellent chance. The short week, East Coast game and weather may create a simpler game plan, but we have the advantage of a mid-season form Nix versus Rudolph who has only started a handful (19?) games. MHR – Jonah Coleman has seemed like “the guy” a few times this season and then he broke it open on Sunday. Granted, the Raiders have one of the worst run defenses in the league, but what are your thoughts on Hat Trick Coleman and making him the bell cow back? And have we seen the last of Dobbins in Denver? Wrenchman1122: I’m all in on Jonah Coleman. Sure, the Raiders weren’t exactly known for stopping the run, but you still have to go out there and do it. Three touchdowns, 111 yards rushing, and the way he ran with authority, vision, and determination tell me we’re watching something special develop. What impressed me most wasn’t just the numbers; it was how he took over when the game was on the line. That’s what you want to see from a running back. I believe Coleman has earned the opportunity to be the bell cow. Feed the hot hand! He’s physical, runs with a purpose, and seems to get stronger as the game goes on. He’s also giving this offense something it desperately needs: a dependable running game that takes pressure off Bo Nix and opens up the passing attack. As for Dobbins, I wouldn’t write him off just yet. He’s been a good player for Denver, but this is a business, and opportunities have to be earned. With the recent suspension and Coleman’s emergence, the situation has certainly changed. Here’s my bottom line – Broncos Country has been waiting for an offense that can run the ball, control the clock, and finish games physically. Coleman might be exactly the missing piece we’ve been looking for. Between Bo Nix, this defense, and a running game that’s starting to find its identity, I like what I’m seeing. (Love the Hat-Trick reference). Jonah Coleman has been named FedEx Air & Ground NFL Player of the Week for his performance in the Broncos' win. Coleman is the first rookie to take home the honor this season. pic.twitter.com/eJiPwFHp1d — Zac Stevens (@ZacStevens) November 25, 2026 MHR – The Broncos really do have a lot of offensive targets to use, and Bo Nix alluded to that after the Raiders game in talking about Evan Engram’s big day, noting that he, like many others on the team, “probably want to get the ball more.” Of all the receiving threats – Sutton, Waddle, Bryant, Engram, Mims… – who do you think are the best for this offense and is it possible to have too much of a good thing and still keep all of it? Wrenchman1122: I love this problem. When was the last time we could honestly say the Broncos had this many weapons on offense? Jaylen Waddle brings something Denver hasn’t had enough of: game-changing speed. He forces defenses to respect the deep ball and opens things up underneath for everyone else. I was impressed with Engram’s game last week. We finally were able to be reminded of what he can do. He’s a matchup nightmare for linebackers and safeties, and I want to see him become a bigger part of the weekly game plan. Defenses can’t take away everybody. Double Sutton, and Waddle can burn you. Take away the deep ball, and Engram can work the middle. Crowd the middle, and Bryant or Mims can make you pay. Add Jonah Coleman establishing a legitimate running game, and suddenly this offense becomes awfully difficult to defend. MHR – I thought the Raiders game was one of Nix’s best, even if the stat line wasn’t particularly impressive. What did you like, what should Nix and the offense build on, and what still needs work – particularly as we gear up for what could be a major showdown for the AFC with the Bills in a month? Wrenchman1122: I thought Bo showed real growth against the Raiders. What I liked most was his patience, decision-making, and willingness to take what the defense gave him rather than forcing plays. The connection with his receivers is continuing to develop, and the running game is finally giving this offense another dimension. That’s what we need to build on. What still needs work is consistency, especially on third downs, red-zone execution, and avoiding unnecessary turnovers. Against a team like Buffalo, you can’t afford to leave points on the field. I believe Bo is growing into the quarterback we hoped he would be, and I wouldn’t trade our guy for anybody. MHR – Matt Peart, not Alex Palczewski or Ben Powers, started the game at left guard, and Bo Nix got sacked just once. Payton indicated that “Powers is still important to what we’re doing” but is Peart the answer at left guard? Or was that a one-week patch? Wrenchman1122: I think Peart earned another look at left guard. The line played well against the Raiders, and keeping Bo upright has to be priority No.1. One game doesn’t make Peart the permanent answer, but I’d like to see what he can do with another opportunity. Powers remains an important piece. Not sure he’s 100% and Palczewski provides valuable depth. Ultimately, let the best five linemen earn their spots. In addition to a Tom Jackson tribute, this is basically a @Island2_1 and @jonahcoleman8 highlight video … What a ******* game! #LAVvsDEN #BroncosCountry #RIP57 https://t.co/16kt8RahDe — Doctor of Words (@docllv) November 25, 2026 MHR – Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback while Rodgers will be inactive on another team! It’ll be Rudolph’s 20th career start. Does the QB change make Pittsburgh more dangerous or less? How should Vance Joseph attack a QB who just got the keys midweek? Wrenchman1122: I think the quarterback change makes Pittsburgh a little more unpredictable, but I wouldn’t necessarily say more dangerous. Rudolph has experience and has shown he can win games, so Vance Joseph can’t afford to take him lightly. The key is to make him uncomfortable early. Bring pressure, disguise coverages, mix up the looks, and force him to make quick decisions. At the same time, Denver has to stay disciplined and not give up easy plays by getting too aggressive. I want to see our defense set the tone, create a turnover, and make Rudolph prove he can beat us. If the Broncos control the line of scrimmage and get after him, I like our chances. MHR – Ja’Quan McMillian. This guy is unbelievable. On a defense with a future HOF cornerback and All Pro edge rushers and d-linemen, J-Mac just goes and does it all anyway. What impresses you about him and is he just getting more expensive by the game for George Paton? 😉 Wrenchman1122: McMillian is everything you want in a Broncos defender. His instincts, toughness, versatility, and ability to make plays in big moments are impressive. What I love most is that he plays with a chip on his shoulder and never seems intimidated by the moment. Honestly, J-Mac reminds me a little of Rod Smith. Maybe it’s the underdog mentality, the work ethic, or the way he constantly proves people wrong. He may not get the headlines that Surtain and the pass rushers get, but he’s a huge part of what makes this defense special. George Paton has an important decision ahead of him because McMillian is making a strong case for a well-deserved payday. He’s a player I’d like to see wearing orange and blue for a long, long time. MHR – While the Broncos’ defense has turned in amazing plays to win a lot of games this season, there are still some holes…especially defending the run and the middle of the field. Are you concerned? Is this a personnel problem or just an issue of giving up a few big plays here and there? Wrenchman1122: As good as this defense has been, I think there are areas that still need improvement. The biggest thing this defense needs to clean up is eliminating the two or three explosive plays it seems to give up each game. Championship defenses don’t just make big plays; they limit the opponent’s opportunities to make them. Singleton has played extremely well in the middle, but his pass coverage can still be an issue at times. My biggest concern, however, is depth. Injuries are inevitable, and we need to know the next man up can maintain the same level of play. I don’t think it’s time to panic, but these are areas that need attention. Come playoff time, teams will expose any weakness they can find, and we need all three levels of this defense playing at a high level. MHR – Special teams last week turned in two blocked punts. And Crawshaw and Lutz have been spectacular. Is Special Teams a true strength for the Broncos that can be the difference-maker in closer games and/or playoffs down the stretch? Wrenchman1122: Absolutely. Special teams can be a major difference-maker, especially in tight games and the playoffs. Two blocked punts show the aggressiveness and preparation of this unit, while Crawshaw and Lutz have been outstanding. Just as importantly, it forces opposing teams to spend valuable practice time preparing for what Denver can do on special teams rather than focusing entirely on our offense and defense. I consider special teams a real strength for Denver and potentially a deciding factor down the stretch. MHR – Not to get too far ahead, but what is your hope for this team this season? Wrenchman1122: My hope is to see Denver make a legitimate run at the Super Bowl. I think this team has the talent, coaching, and defensive identity to compete with anybody. The biggest thing is consistency, staying healthy, and continuing to develop on offense. I want to see the defense remain aggressive, the offense take another step forward, and this team learn how to win the close games against the best competition. At a minimum, I want a playoff run that gives Broncos Country something to be excited about. The optimist in me wants the 49ers again in Super Bowl LXI. title: ‘Unserious Organization,’ ‘He’s a Disgrace’ — Steelers Fans Rip Owner Art Rooney II for Supporting HC Mike McCarthy Despite Aaron Rodgers’ Revelations
summary: Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II publicly threw his full support behind head coach Mike McCarthy on Thanksgiving, and many fans online are furious about it. Rooney’s comments came after a rough stretch in Pittsburgh.
content: ‘Unserious Organization,’ ‘He’s a Disgrace’ — Steelers Fans Rip Owner Art Rooney II for Supporting HC Mike McCarthy Despite Aaron Rodgers’ Revelations Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II publicly threw his full support behind head coach Mike McCarthy on Thanksgiving, and many fans online are furious about it. Rooney’s comments came after a rough stretch in Pittsburgh. The Steelers lost 19-16 to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday for their second straight loss, dropping to 6-4. The week since has been dominated by tension between McCarthy and quarterback Aaron Rodgers, who called out the head coach for falling asleep and missing meetings, not watching film, losing the locker room, and more after he was benched for Mason Rudolph. Pittsburgh promptly waived Rodgers after his bombshell interview. Rooney stood by his coach, and the reaction online was harsh. Steelers Fans Blast Art Rooney II for Backing Mike McCarthy “I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he’ll be our coach this season, next season and beyond,” Rooney said . “The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination [that] can’t be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can’t live with that. … Mike’s as healthy as the rest of us. Health was not an issue. I’m not sure where that part comes.” Rooney put no blame on McCarthy, and instead called out Rodgers. “There’s maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload,” Rooney said. “He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don’t do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that’s for sure. In general, I think, historically, what’s in the locker room stays in the locker room. That’s the way it’s always been. That’s the way it should be as far as I’m concerned.” Many fans expressed frustration over Rooney’s comments. Matt King, an influencer, was blunt. BUILD YOUR TEAM’S DRAFT: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator “This is how you stay a bad organization. Good luck with the dude that sleeps in meetings,” he wrote. Other fans focused on what Rooney’s words could mean for the players. One fan wrote that “Art just told the entire locker room that he does not have the players best interest in mind,” and added, “So sad.” Another fan made a similar point, writing that Rooney is essentially telling the locker room that “he could care less [if] this guy is doing his job, but he’s not paying him not to coach.” Some fans looked ahead to the offseason. One predicted the Steelers are “gonna lose the [locker] room, if they haven’t already,” and added that “expect trade requests.” They also called the Steelers an “unserious organization, from the owner to the GM, to the HC.” The anger was not limited to McCarthy. Plenty of it landed on Rooney himself. One fan asked, “Can the nfl owners get together and kick out Rooney PLEASE.” Another fan reached back into Steelers history to make the point, saying, “He’s a disgrace to the great men that built this franchise before him.” The numbers have not been kind to Rodgers this season. Pro Football Network’s QB Impact Score gives him a grade of 67.1 through Week 12 of the 2026 season, which ranks 29th of 33 graded quarterbacks. Rooney’s message leaves little doubt about where the team stands. McCarthy is staying, and the owner sees Rodgers’ insubordination as the only problem. For a 6-4 team coming off back-to-back losses and a drama-filled week, the bigger question is whether the locker room and fan base accept that answer. Based on Thursday’s reaction, many fans online have already made up their minds. This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network .

title: Washington Commanders vs. Arizona Cardinals Week 12: Gimme Him
summary: There is one player the Washington Commanders would love to steal from the Arizona Cardinals ahead of their Week 12 matchup.
content: The Washington Commanders head west in Week 12 when they face the Arizona Cardinals at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, Arizona, at 4:25 p.m. EDT. The Commanders are fresh off an upset victory over the Cincinnati Bengals and now sit just two games out of the top spot in the NFC East, while the Cardinals sit squarely at the bottom of the entire NFC. Arizona has won just three games this season, all over teams with losing records, and all on the road. The Cardinals are in a bit of a rebuild right now after releasing former starting quarterback Kyler Murray in the offseason and recently trading Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens , leaving Carson Beck as the starting quarterback with Josh Johnson to back him up. Due to injury, Johnson is expected to start against his former team in Week 12. In this week's edition of "Gimme Him," where Washington hypothetically steals one player from the upcoming opponent, that player is tight end Trey McBride. Please don't misunderstand, Chig Okonkwo is good, and Ben Sinnott is excellent in his role, but McBride is one of the top tight ends in the NFL right now, and Jayden Daniels would wildly benefit from having a guy like McBride at his disposal. There aren't very many 1,000-yard receiving tight ends in the NFL, and his 87 receptions for 689 yards rank best among all tight ends in 2026. McBride also has five touchdowns, tied for fifth among tight ends, and his production puts him on pace for his third consecutive 1,000-yard season. To compare, Okonkwo has 31 receptions for 329 yards and zero touchdowns this season, while Sinnott has five receptions for 48 yards and a touchdown. We wouldn't get rid of either of them because they are good at their jobs, but having McBride provides a true elite tight end. Okonkwo and Sinnott would be excellent depth at the position. The Commanders have a very real opportunity to bring their record to .500 on Sunday when they face the Cardinals, even without stealing Trey McBride. Arizona is not a good team, and getting another win will put them that much closer to ending the season with more wins than losses. title: Four-time MVP Rodgers released and may have played last NFL game
summary: Aaron Rodgers is replaced as the Pittsburgh Steelers' starting quarterback, then criticises head coach Mike McCarthy before being released with immediate effect.
content: Aaron Rodgers has thrown 16 touchdown passes and six interceptions from 10 games this season [Getty Images] Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers may have played his last game in the NFL after being released by the Pittsburgh Steelers. In a brief statement published on Wednesday afternoon local time, the Steelers announced Rodgers, the NFL's four-time Most Valuable Player, was no longer with the franchise. That came after a tumultuous 24 hours, which began with the Steelers announcing at 23:10 local time on Tuesday that Rodgers had been replaced as their starting quarterback. He then appeared on US sports TV programme the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, saying he would not rejoin the team. "That ship has sailed," said Rodgers, who turns 43 next week. During the 34-minute interview, he said he discovered he had been replaced from team-mate Pat Freiermuth. Rodgers was also critical of Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy, including accusing him of snoring while he slept through team meetings. They won the Super Bowl together with the Green Bay Packers in 2011 and, during Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, Rodgers said that McCarthy ended the half-time huddle with a chant of "one, two, three, Packers". When asked by reporters on Wednesday about that claim, McCarthy admitted there was "an embarrassing moment". The 63-year-old was in charge for most of Rodgers' 18-year spell with the Packers and left in 2018. He then coached the Dallas Cowboys from 2020-2024. Tension had developed between the pair over play-calling and Rodgers said he told McCarthy "try to bench me or don't change the play-caller, then you should just release me". McCarthy later said "there was an ultimatum made that was clearly outside his job description", adding it was his decision to let the player go. All this came after the Steelers said that Mason Rudolph will start Friday's home game against the Denver Broncos and that Rodgers would be inactive, so would not serve as back-up to the 31-year-old. Rodgers, who joined Pittsburgh in 2025 after two years with the New York Jets, was "99% sure" he was going to retire after leading the Steelers to last season's play-offs. McCarthy's appointment persuaded him to play one more year but Rodgers told the talk show on Wednesday the season had not been "what I signed up for". Although the Steelers have a 6-4 record, they have had two straight defeats after losing 19-16 at Philadelphia on Sunday. Analysis - an unceremonious end to an illustrious career? Pittsburgh's brief statement confirming Rodgers' release is likely the unceremonious end to an illustrious career. While Rodgers was unable to claim a second Super Bowl win with Green Bay, he was named the season MVP in 2011, 2014, 2020 and 2021. Only Peyton Manning (five) has won the award more times. Rodgers had said his 22nd year in the NFL would be his last, and he has been let go at a crucial stage in the season. The Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) lead the AFC North division, with Pittsburgh third, but with seven games left the Steelers occupy the final play-off spot for the AFC Conference. Although Pittsburgh are 6-4, they have had to grind out some of those wins as they have struggled offensively. They rank 22nd for both points and passing yards per game. Rodgers is undoubtedly past his best, but his form has only dropped slightly from last season and the team's struggles are by no means entirely down to him. The Steelers' depth among their wide receivers is thin. Michael Pittman is out injured and DK Metcalf has not delivered the production expected when he was brought in with Rodgers before the 2025 season. Metcalf, 28, was even ejected during Sunday's loss at Philadelphia, meaning Rodgers had to lean on debutant Max Hurleman with the game on the line. It is not as if Pittsburgh had a hot-shot rookie quarterback pushing for an opportunity. Rudolph is in his ninth season and has started each as a back-up. But this week's discussions with Rodgers forced McCarthy's hand and the manner in which the situation unraveled cannot be a complete surprise given Rodgers has clashed with team management, coaches and team-mates throughout his career. While McCarthy hopes Rudolph can spark the Steelers' offence, Rodgers is now free to join another team. Several have had quarterback issues this season through injuries and poor form, and with more than a third of it left, there is time for Rodgers - one of the greatest quarterbacks of all time - to come aboard and make an impact. The Indianapolis Colts are one of those teams having released Daniel Jones last week, but they are out of play-off contention. That leaves the New England Patriots as an intriguing alternative. Drake Maye will be out for at least six weeks after suffering a fractured fibula and at 5-5 are just outside the AFC's play-off spots - one below Pittsburgh. The Patriots have Super Bowl pedigree having reached last season's big game and Rodgers would relish the chance to deny McCarthy and his former team. It would also give him the opportunity to follow his former adversary Tom Brady and get one last shot at finally emulating Brady and Manning by becoming a multiple Super Bowl winner himself. title: Why do the Lions and Cowboys always play on Thanksgiving?
summary: There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. The teams playing the night game change annually, but you might notice that the Lions always host the first game of the day, and the Cowboys always host the second game. How did […]
content: Detroit Lions fans dress for Thanksgiving game against the Chicago Bears, Thursday, Nov. 28, 2019 at Ford Field. Detroit Lions fans | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co There are three NFL games today. The Lions host the Bears, the Cowboys host the Eagles, and the Bills host the Chiefs. The teams playing the night game change annually, but you might notice that the Lions always host the first game of the day, and the Cowboys always host the second game. How did that come to be? The Lions played their first Thanksgiving game in 1934. It was their first season in Detroit. They had previously been located in Portsmouth, Ohio, where they were known as the Portsmouth Spartans. A radio executive named George Richards bought the franchise and moved it to Detroit. The Lions were having difficulty gaining any sort of popularity in their new home city. Richards came up with the idea of scheduling their team’s big game against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving. The Lions were 10-1 at the time, and the Bears were 11-0. This was before the days when the league dictated the schedule to its teams. The teams themselves could schedule the times of their games. Richards used his connections in the radio business to get the game broadcast nationally. Even thought Detroit lost, it was a huge success. The Lions sold the game out, and they have played on Thanksgiving ever since with the exception of World War II years despite some calls for them to lose the game during the dismal Matt Millen Era. Thanksgiving gained a second traditional team in 1951. For the next thirteen years, the Green Bay Packers traveled to Detroit to play the Lions on Thanksgiving. Vince Lombardi ended the arrangement. Lombardi cited the end of an agreement that paid the Packers $10,000 extra for playing the game, the difficulties of playing games on a short week every year, and having to face a rival in front of an electric crowd on the road every season. Of course since the teams are in the same division, the Packers remain a frequent Thanksgiving opponent for Detroit. So how about the Cowboys? In the mid-1960’s the NFL was looking to add a second Thanksgiving game. It was not entirely clear it would work outside Detroit, where Thanksgiving NFL was already a tradition. The Dallas Cowboys were a six year old team with no history of winning. General manager Tex Schramm was a visionary. (He was a driving force behind other innovations like instant replay, the flags on goal posts, the NFL-AFL merger, and too many others to name). He jumped at the opportunity. The Cowboys hosted their first Thanksgiving game in 1966. They kept the game annually until the 1970’s when the league hatched a plan to alternate between the Cowboys and the then St. Louis Cardinals . The Cowboys were to host the second game in even years and the Cardinals in odd years. The Cardinals only hosted two home Thanksgiving games, however, which took place in 1975 and in 1977. The games weren’t competitive, and attendance was relatively poor. Then commissioner Pete Roselle put an end to the experiment, and made a deal with Schramm that the Cowboys would keep the game from then on. Dallas has hosted the second Thanksgiving game ever since. With two permanent Thanksgiving hosts, why does the third game rotate? In 2006, the NFL added a third game in primetime. The Chiefs defeated the Broncos that night. By this time, a Thanksgiving game had become a desired timeslot. Unlike the experiments in Dallas and Detroit decades earlier, the 30 other teams in the league would probably all love to become the permanent host of the primetime Thanksgiving game. Since everybody wants it, the league has not given the game to a single team. The matchup changes every year and in recent years has usually been a division rivalry (although not this year). The last major change to Thanksgiving games came in 2014 when the NFL’s current TV deal kicked into effect. CBS and FOX both get to broadcast one game on Thanksgiving afternoon. Prior to the current TV contract, CBS could only show games where an AFC team was on the road. That meant one AFC team had to play at either Detroit or Dallas every Thanksgiving. The league’s new TV deal allowed AFC road games to be flexed to FOX and NFC road games to be flexed to CBS. The new arrangement allowed for greater scheduling flexibility. Both Detroit and Dallas could be given NFC opponents, and one of the afternoon games could be flexed to CBS. In theory either the Detroit or Dallas game could also be flexed to prime time, but that has yet to happen. This year the NFL added a game on Thanksgiving Eve. Since 2023, there has also been a game on Black Friday so the number of marquee games this weekend has continued to rise.

title: Why Lions might franchise tag Brian Branch instead of signing a contract extension
summary: The Lions might not extend their DB this offseason, but a franchise tag is in play.
content: Why Lions might franchise tag Brian Branch instead of signing a contract extension originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Detroit Lions are facing off against the Chicago Bears on Thanksgiving, and defensive back Brian Branch is going to be key to stopping this high-powered Bears offense. For Branch himself, this week is a huge opportunity to further prove himself in a contract year. Set to hit the open market after 2026, alongside tight end Sam LaPorta, the Lions will have a difficult decision to make with Branch this upcoming offseason. ESPN's Bill Barnwell believes that, instead of a contract extension for Branch, he might be in line for the Lions' franchise tag. The reason why is simple: it's more affordable for Detroit to use the tag on Branch to give them more time to figure out a long-term deal. Why Brian Branch might be franchise tagged by Lions "With the safety franchise tag projected to come in at $22.2 million, the Lions might see tagging him as a logical way to continue their relationship while they negotiate a long-term extension," Barnwell writes. With the Lions having plenty of offseason questions to solve, once the 2026 season comes to a close, being able to tag Branch and figure things out over an extended period of time would be much easier than trying to work out an extension. Since Branch has had an up-and-down NFL career so far, seeing what Branch can do to close out the 2026 NFL season could give the Lions reason to sign him to a long-term deal. But even if he doesn't finish strong, the Lions could still elect to tag him to avoid letting him hit free agency, where he'd surely get plenty of competitive offers from other teams looking for upgrades. MORE : Lions may have found their 1 answer to life without Aidan Hutchinson Barnwell highlighted Branch as someone with a lot on the line for the remainder of the 2026 season, as a strong finish could lead to a contract extension sooner rather than later. However, even a lackluster second half of 2026 shouldn't stop the Lions from trying to keep Branch, as they have too many issues in the secondary not to try and keep arguably their best defensive back in-house. Branch has a lot on the line this year, although he's most likely going to get tagged by the Lions. LaPorta's future is up in the air as well, and he could get tagged, which could complicate Branch's future with the team. While the Lions could still choose LaPorta over Branch, with the team's more questionable secondary, tagging Branch would make a lot of sense as a way to guarantee they have at least one more season out of the star defensive back. title: Barkov and Marchand Spark Panthers in 5–3 Win Over Senators Ahead of Tough Weekend Slate
summary: The Florida Panthers received an immediate boost of offense and veteran leadership on Wednesday night as captain Aleksander Barkov and forward Brad Marchand made their much-anticipated returns to the lineup
content: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Florida Panthers received an immediate boost of offense and veteran leadership on Wednesday night as captain Aleksander Barkov and forward Brad Marchand made their much-anticipated returns to the lineup, combining for four points in a 5–3 victory over the Ottawa Senators at Amerant Bank Arena . Both players had been sidelined since early October due to left knee injuries but returned ahead of their initial recovery timelines. Barkov wasted no time making an impact, scoring a goal, while Marchand showcased his playmaking skills with three assists, helping Florida regain its offensive rhythm. Instant Impact From Two Key Returns The return of Barkov and Marchand provided head coach Paul Maurice with a dynamic lift just as the schedule intensifies. Barkov seamlessly rejoined the top-six forward group, while Marchand’s presence added playmaking instincts that were crucial in generating consistent pressure against Ottawa. Aleksander Barkov: Scored in his first game back since early October, delivering a vital boost on both ends of the ice. Brad Marchand: Recorded three assists in his return, orchestrating the offense and setting the tone for Florida’s success. Roster Shuffle: Waivers, Vilmanis, and Devine Accommodating the return of these high-impact veterans necessitated some tough roster decisions. Florida lost forward Cole Reinhardt to the Vancouver Canucks after placing him on NHL waivers, creating the necessary roster space for Barkov and Marchand. Meanwhile, forward Sandis Vilmanis has continued to garner praise for his consistent play, contributing energy and secondary scoring as a regular NHL contributor. Additionally, forward Jack Devine has navigated recent recall and loan moves with the American Hockey League , providing Florida with valuable organizational depth as roster spots become increasingly competitive. What’s Next for Florida The Panthers won’t have much time to celebrate Wednesday’s victory, as they face a demanding back-to-back test this weekend: Friday, Nov. 27, 2026: at Washington Capitals Location: Capital One Arena (Washington, D.C.) Time (EST): 3:00 PM Saturday, Nov. 28, 2026: vs. Tampa Bay Lightning Location: Amerant Bank Arena Time (EST): TBD With Barkov and Marchand back in the fold, the Panthers are hoping to build on this momentum as they navigate a challenging stretch ahead.

title: The Calgary Flames’ Most Important Young Defenseman Might Not Be in the NHL Yet, Or Even the AHL
summary: As much fun as it’s been watching Zayne Parekh and Simon Nemec this season, I’m just as interested in what’s […]
content: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As much fun as it’s been watching Zayne Parekh and Simon Nemec this season, I’m just as interested in what’s happening with another young defenseman in the Calgary Flames’ organization. Carson Carels might not generate the same kind of offensive highlights as Parekh, but there’s a chance he ends up being just as important to Calgary’s rebuild. The Flames selected Carels sixth overall in June’s NHL Draft after the Manitoba product recorded 20 goals and 73 points in 58 games with the Prince George Cougars of the Western Hockey League (WHL). He finished tied for fourth in scoring among WHL defensemen and recorded another 10 points in 10 playoff games. The 18-year-old has since made the jump to collegiate hockey at the University of North Dakota, where he recorded four assists through his first 10 games. I wouldn’t be too concerned about the drop in offensive production, though. Some of the things that make Carels such an exciting prospect have very little to do with how many points he puts up. Carson Carels Brings Something Different to Calgary’s Blue Line Despite recording the second-highest single-season point total by a defenseman in Cougars history last season, Carels spent much of his time in Prince George developing his defensive game under former Flames head coach Jim Playfair and former NHL forward Mark Lamb. In a June interview published on the Cougars’ website , Carels credited Playfair with helping him develop better habits in his own zone. His ability to close gaps quickly, take away passing lanes and play physically without sacrificing mobility is a big part of what made him such an attractive prospect heading into June’s draft. Flames director of player development Ray Edwards spoke about Carels’ versatility in an August interview with NHL.com , projecting him as someone capable of playing big minutes against the opposition’s best players and being trusted late in games regardless of whether the Flames are protecting a lead or chasing a goal. Considering the young offensive talent Calgary already has on its blue line, I think there’s tremendous value in having someone capable of taking on that kind of responsibility. I’d love for the Flames to eventually have Parekh and Nemec driving offense on separate defensive pairings. I’ve also been a fan of giving Parekh opportunities to play on his off side, which would give Calgary even more flexibility when putting those pairings together. What’s exciting about adding Carels to that group is that the Flames could have three defensemen capable of generating offense at a high level without needing all three to be deployed the same way. Carels could be taking on some of Calgary’s toughest defensive assignments and still contributing plenty offensively. Flames Fans Should Be Excited To Watch Carels at the World Juniors Carels became the fifth-youngest defenseman to represent Canada at the World Juniors last season. The only four who did it at a younger age were Jay Bouwmeester, Chris Joseph, Matthew Schaefer and Scott Niedermayer. Carels recorded one assist through five games as Canada went on to win bronze, playing alongside Parekh, who put up an incredible 13 points in seven games. I’m really interested in seeing how much more responsibility Canada is willing to give Carels if he returns to the tournament this year, especially after he’s spent a few months playing against older competition at North Dakota. He’s exactly the kind of defenseman I’d want on the ice against some of the best forwards the Americans and Swedes could bring to the tournament. Flames fans also have a reason to be following North Dakota throughout the season, as Carels is continuing his development alongside fellow Calgary first-round pick Cole Reschny. Between Parekh, Nemec and the strides Yan Kuznetsov has been making, Calgary doesn’t need to rush Carels into the NHL. I’d much rather see him spend some time at North Dakota developing into someone capable of taking on significant defensive responsibility when he arrives. If Carels becomes the kind of player Edwards envisions, the Flames could have one hell of a young blue line in a few years. title: Canucks Ice Time: Which Players Does Malhotra Trust Most?
summary: The Vancouver Canucks have a mix of veteran and young talent, which can lead to interesting disparities in ice time. […]
content: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Vancouver Canucks have a mix of veteran and young talent, which can lead to interesting disparities in ice time. Who does Head Coach Manny Malhotra trust the most to handle the tough minutes? Who is on thin ice? Most Trusted Veterans Malhotra and the Canucks want to win every game. Therefore, the seasoned players are getting a lot of game time. Sometimes, it can border on being too much ice time for some of the veterans. It does say a lot about how much the head coach trusts these players, though. Filip Hronek Filip Hronek is averaging 26:47 of ice time per game, which is fourth in the NHL. He has also played the most cumulative minutes in the league. As the Canucks defensive core has three players 23 and younger, it does make sense that they are being sheltered a bit, which means that Hronek has to do the heavy lifting. Hronek has played over 30 minutes in four games, which is tied for the most in the NHL, with fellow minute-munchers Zach Werenski and Matthew Schaefer . There is a concern that the Canucks are overplaying Hronek and, in the process, not giving younger players enough ice time. However, as younger defenders are still learning the game, there is a balance to be struck. Malhotra clearly trusts Hronek, even though he has had his share of defensive lapses this season. Elias Pettersson (Forward) It is indisputable that Elias Pettersson has been a critical part of this team. He plays in all situations and, for the most part, has been solid this season. His production has been higher, and he has taken the most faceoffs in the NHL. He has averaged 20:42 per game and has played over 20 minutes in 15 out of 24 games. The most prominent part of Pettersson’s game is his work on the penalty kill. Out of the 34 power-play goals the Canucks have surrendered, Pettersson has only been on the ice for eight of them. His two-way game is genuinely impressive, and he has blocked 32 shots this season, by far the most among Canuck forwards. While he still has a ways to go in his offense, Malhotra trusts Pettersson’s two-way capabilities, and without him in the lineup, the defensive zone coverage has been staggeringly poor. Brock Boeser and Filip Chytil Rounding out the forward group is the ice time of Boeser and Chytil, who have recorded an average of 19:38 and 19:21 of ice time this season. I don’t think Boeser’s role on the team has to be reiterated. He is a smart player who can use his hockey IQ to make up for his lack of foot speed. Like the veteran Pettersson, he plays in all situations and will always be a player who closes out competitive games. He is also the undisputed leader of this team . The interesting player to watch is Filip Chytil . Before this season, his highest season-average in ice time was 16:42. What has made Malhotra play Chytil so much more this season? Firstly, he has the highest average even-strength minutes among Canuck forwards. Chytil has a play style that Malhotra clearly likes, and that is straight-line speed and play-driving. He is not afraid to go to the dirty areas and move the puck up ice quickly in transition plays. Arguably, he has the most offensive talent in the Canuck forward group. While Pettersson eats up a lot of power-play minutes, Chytil is the even-strength king on the team. He is quite fun to watch when he is healthy. How Are the Young Defensemen Faring? In terms of ice time, the three young Canuck defenders are doing pretty well. Zeev Buium and Tom Willander have the second- and fourth-most average ice time on the team, at 21:58 and 20:15, respectively. Elias Pettersson , or D-Petey, has an average of 18:32 a night. Zeev Buium Buium is supposedly the defender of the future and one of the cornerstones of the rebuild. Yet, his season has been quite the roller coaster. He had a tough start to the season, leading to a demotion to the third pairing. He has rebounded and found some stability, and his confidence has grown over time. His puck movement is stellar when his confidence is high. I am surprised that he does not get more power-play time compared to Filip Hronek. Malhotra is trusting him a lot more now, as he has played over 25 minutes in his last three games. However, Buium does not play on the penalty kill. If he did, his numbers could be very close to Hronek’s. Tom Willander Willander has been a good story for the Canucks. He has come into his own as a stable defender. According to Natural Stat Trick, his Corsi-for percentage (CF%) is highest among Canucks defensemen at 49.19. That means that with him on the ice, the Canucks are generating more chances and allowing fewer opportunities against. Willander is not necessarily the most flashy player out there, but his breakouts are clean, and his defensive zone retrievals are consistently able to turn into clean zone exits. Those quiet plays feed into what Malhotra says is the “nothingness” of the game. He has the makings of a calm and collected two-way defender. D-Petey D-Petey’s season has been an up-and-down one. At some point, he was probably the most impressive out of the three young defenders. Now, the playing field has gotten a bit more even. His physical play and penalty-killing time are valuable, but in those tougher minutes, especially on the PK, he has a lot to learn. The penalty kill has been a massive struggle for the entire team, and a lot of it is because the team is too puck-focused. That leads to a lot of chasing and less being in the right positions. Early on in the season, he also had an offensive flair in his game. That has since dropped off a bit, but it is good to know that he has it in him. Players on Thin Ice There are a number of players that have not gotten that much ice time, and based on their play, it is understandable the reason why. Marco Rossi Given the talent on this roster, it is highly unlikely that he will get scratched, but there are signs that Malhotra does not trust Rossi as a second-line center. Rossi is being deployed as a third-line center right now, with limited minutes at even strength. In the last game against the Detroit Red Wings, Rossi had the least amount of ice time at even strength, with only 11:19. Ty Mueller and Jacob Quillan , who were AHL call-ups, had 14:23 and 13:13, respectively. For those two to get more ice time than Rossi says a lot, especially when Pettersson is injured. Malhotra has been critical that he doesn’t get to the inside of the ice often enough, calling him a perimeter player. Rossi’s average of 15:21 per game is his lowest average since the 2022-23 season. Whoever is Playing Third-Pair, Right Side The Canucks have rotated the defensemen on the third-pair, right side, a lot. Luke Schenn , Victor Mancini , and Cameron Crotty have played in that role this season. Victor Mancini has the highest average ice time among the three, with 12:25. However, he struggled mightily on the penalty kill, allowing five power-play goals against in 11:36 of penalty-killing time. That represents 25.86 power-play goals against per 60 minutes. That was likely a main reason why Mancini was sent down to the minors: to improve his defensive positioning. Veteran defenseman Luke Schenn is getting old. The 37-year-old has averaged 12:02 of ice time this season and has played in 15 of 27 games. Schenn’s foot speed is not good, and Malhotra has tried to give other players a chance to play in his spot. Those experiments have not been successful, as Schenn seems to be the best player for the job as of right now. At least he can kill penalties more consistently. He has only given up two power-play goals in 17 minutes of penalty-killing time. Cameron Crotty has only averaged 8:54 of ice time and has not looked good in his limited minutes. He was brought in from waivers, and that experiment has largely failed. He allowed two power-play goals in 3:14 of penalty-killing time, and that was probably enough for Malhotra to play Schenn over him again. Balancing Results With Player Development While we can say that the results of the 2026-27 season are not that important in the grand scheme of things, no team wants to continually lose games. For the most part, the veterans are playing the best hockey on the team, and thus, they are getting a lot of ice time. It is also important to understand that a lot of the veterans will likely be the first ones to get traded . It is critical to showcase their value. There are signs that the coaching staff is increasingly trusting the young players a bit more, especially the three young defensemen. However, players like Jonathan Lekkerimäki , Linus Karlsson , and Liam Öhgren are players who could use some more ice time. Once the trades start going down, we will see if the younger players will get their time to shine. title: Chicago Blackhawks May Have Already Found Connor Bedard’s Long-Term Running Mate
summary: As frustrating as it must be for Chicago Blackhawks fans to see Connor Bedard dealing with another shoulder injury, they’ve […]
content: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect As frustrating as it must be for Chicago Blackhawks fans to see Connor Bedard dealing with another shoulder injury, they’ve had plenty of reasons to be excited about some of their other young forwards lately. Frank Nazar has been playing some great hockey, but it’s 22-year-old Russian forward Roman Kantserov who’s been making NHL history. After recording his first career NHL hat trick as part of a four-point performance in Sunday’s 6-3 victory over the Vancouver Canucks, Kantserov scored twice in Wednesday’s 3-1 victory over the Seattle Kraken. He’s now up to 15 goals and 20 points through his first 25 NHL games. No Blackhawks player has scored more goals through the first 25 games of a season in the NHL’s modern era, dating back to 1943-44. Considering the Blackhawks selected Bedard first overall in the 2023 NHL Draft, there wasn’t nearly as much attention being paid to what they did with the 44th overall pick that year. There’s a chance we look back on that draft in a few years and talk about how Chicago acquired two of its most important offensive players in the span of two days. Roman Kantserov’s Game Should Complement Connor Bedard’s Kantserov spent the past three seasons playing against men in the Kontinental Hockey League (KHL) before making the jump to North America. He helped Metallurg Magnitogorsk win a Gagarin Cup in 2024 before leading the KHL with 36 goals last season. His 36 goals and 64 points in 63 games were both single-season records for a KHL player under the age of 22. What I really like about Kantserov as a potential long-term linemate for Bedard is his willingness to get into areas of the ice where he can take advantage of the opportunities created by more dynamic puck carriers. Despite being listed at 5-foot-9, Kantserov doesn’t need to operate exclusively around the perimeter to be an effective offensive player. After Sunday’s game, he spoke about how he’s had to adjust his game since arriving in the NHL, getting closer to the net and looking for rebounds and deflections rather than relying as heavily on his ability to score from distance. Two of his three goals against Vancouver came on the power play, while Alex Vlasic set him up near the net for the other. Kantserov completed the hat trick by burying a rebound off a Patrick Kane one-timer. Against Seattle, he scored from down low in the right circle after Sam Rinzel found him with a pass on the power play before adding an empty-net goal. We know how dangerous Bedard can be with the puck on his stick, both as a shooter and a playmaker. Putting someone alongside him who can consistently find those openings in defensive coverage and finish the opportunities he creates could make life pretty miserable for opposing defensemen. Chicago’s Young Forwards Are Giving Fans Plenty To Look Forward To Bedard is expected to need roughly four months to recover from Monday’s right shoulder surgery, meaning we’re going to get a pretty good look at what some of Chicago’s other young forwards can do without him in the lineup. Kantserov is already showing he doesn’t need to play alongside Bedard to produce at the NHL level, and Nazar has been making a pretty strong case for himself as an important piece of Chicago’s future, too. The Blackhawks have now won three consecutive games for the first time this season, with Kantserov scoring five goals across the past two. As much as the focus of Chicago’s rebuild has understandably been on Bedard, its success will ultimately depend on the organization’s ability to surround him with enough talent. Kantserov is giving Blackhawks fans plenty of reasons to believe they’ve already found one of those guys. title: Hawks Hits: Road Redemption, Kantserov’s Pace, Newcomer Impact
summary: Last time the Chicago Blackhawks went on a three-game road trip, they were outscored 18-6 combined in three lopsided losses […]
content: Last time the Chicago Blackhawks went on a three-game road trip, they were outscored 18-6 combined in three lopsided losses to the Florida Panthers, Tampa Bay Lightning, and Carolina Hurricanes. At the time, the Hawks were 4-13-1 through their first 18 games in the 2026-27 regular season. Once the team returned home, the situation was so dire that GM Kyle Davidson held a press conference to discuss his sinking rebuild and the Blackhawks biggest issues. Considering the internal preseason expectations for Year 5 of Davidson’s rebuild, the opening month couldn’t have gone much worse. But since Davidson’s presser on Nov. 11, the Blackhawks are now 5-1-1 in their last seven games, thanks to a perfect 3-0 Pacific Northwest road trip, capped by a 3-1 win over the Seattle Kraken at Climate Pledge Arena on Wednesday. Sure, the competition was much less strenuous than the Southeastern road trip, but the Blackhawks still deserve credit for the road turnaround and taking care of business against the Kraken, Vancouver Canucks, and Calgary Flames. They outscored those three opponents 13-7 during the road trip. After failing to win away from the United Center in their first nine attempts (0-8-1), the Blackhawks earned their first three road wins in five days. They pushed through in overtime against Calgary, took down the Canucks in a track meet, and earned a hard-fought, scrappy victory over Seattle. Wednesday’s win wasn’t the prettiest, with Seattle leading 30-19 in shots on goal and 32-25 in scoring chances, but the Blackhawks defended well overall and didn’t allow many high-danger scoring opportunities. The Kraken’s only odd-man rush, a 2-on-1 from center ice in, was negated with a perfect sliding play from Artyom Levshunov . Head coach Jeff Blashill didn’t like his team’s puck play for most of the game, but acknowledged they gave themselves a chance to win by playing responsible defense and checking hard for 60 minutes. “I think our guys are getting rewarded for good, solid play,” Blashill said. “It hasn’t always been perfect, tonight I didn’t think we were our best with the puck, especially through the first two periods. But we defended really hard, and we checked hard.” Goaltender Spencer Knight , who stopped 29 of 30 shots faced and was credited with 1.98 goals saved above expected, agreed with Blashill’s sentiment. Knight credited the players in front of him for blocking shots time and time again and making the correct defensive reads. “I thought there was a lot of buy-in today,” Knight said. “A lot of commitment to play a good road game and commitment to play the right way. We stuck with it throughout the game. It was fun for me to see.” After a 9-2 drubbing to the Carolina Hurricanes earlier this month, Knight, usually a soft-spoken, mild-mannered member of the locker room, called out his teammates for poor defensive effort early in the season, which left the Blackhawks goaltenders in horrific situations too often. Knight’s frustration was justified, and the rest of the group got the message. The Blackhawks have been much improved defensively over their last seven games, including Wednesday in Seattle. Knight’s comments and tone have changed drastically, as has the spirit around the team. Hawks Hits vs. Seattle. 1. Kantserov 50-goal Pace With two more tallies on Wednesday, Roman Kantserov now leads the Blackhawks and all NHL rookies with 15 goals and 20 points in 25 games this season. The 22-year-old winger is currently on pace for 50 goals, a feat that’s only been achieved four times by a first-year player in league history. Kantserov’s three-game road trip was simply extraordinary, racking up six goals and eight points in the Pacific Northwest. The closer to the Motherland, the better he plays, it seems. He scored in all three games and is tied for sixth in the NHL in goals, ahead of notables like Connor McDavid and Auston Matthews . Fittingly, Kantserov has become just the third player in the past 30 years to record 15 goals in their first 25 games, joining fellow Russians Evgeni Malkin and Alex Ovechkin . If Kantserov can impact the Blackhawks rebuild as Malkin and Ovechkin did for their respective teams two decades ago, it’s going to be a fun ride. Furthermore, Kantserov has scored the most goals by a Blackhawks skater through 25 career games in the NHL’s modern era, with only Bill Mosienko scoring more way back in 1944. He’s also recorded a point in eight straight road games. Kantserov’s nine road goals in November are tied for the third-most by an NHL rookie in a single month. Most of Kantserov’s goals this season have come from the net front, but he scored in two different ways on Wednesday. First, he ripped a one-timer from a sharp angle into the top corner of the net, scoring the eventual game-winner on the power play. Then, with the Blackhawks clinging to a late 2-1 lead, Kantserov stripped Kraken forward Matthew Wood in the defensive zone and impressively hit the empty net from nearly 200 feet away. Kantserov’s bulldog mentality and elite goal-scoring traits were on full display during the three-game road trip, and it’s put him in some special conversations. Kantserov hasn’t just been the NHL’s best rookie this season; he’s been the Blackhawks best player. 2. Glendening’s Debut After joining the team for practice on Tuesday, Luke Glendening’s veteran experience and familiarity with Blashill immediately thrust him into a fourth-line center role in his Blackhawks debut just one day later. Despite little time to get acclimated, Glendening fit in seamlessly on the Blackhawks penalty kill and in defensive situations against the Kraken. He’s well accustomed to Blashill’s pressure-styled penalty-kill system from their time together in Tampa Bay, and it showed. Glendening did his job well on Wednesday, winning 11 of 15 faceoffs and helping the Blackhawks go 4-for-4 while shorthanded. The 37-year-old won most of his faceoffs on the penalty kill and selflessly stepped in front of Seattle shooters, recording three blocked shots. The Blackhawks have been the NHL’s worst faceoff team all season, having won only 42.2 percent of their draws as a team entering Wednesday. Glendening was brought in to help in that department, and he did his part in Seattle. Chicago won 32 of 62 faceoffs against the Kraken, marking one of the few times they’ve been at or above 50 percent in a single game this year. Glendening also helped the Blackhawks outhit Seattle 29-23, tallying a team-high six hits in 13:11 of ice time. Blashill wants his team to become harder to play against in all three zones, and Glendening’s willingness to be physical is another positive impact he can provide. So far, so good for Glendening with his new team. 3. Kane’s Injured Again… Patrick Kane extended his point streak to six games with an assist on Kantserov’s power-play tally, but unfortunately, his night ended shortly after. With the Blackhawks ahead 2-0 late in the third period, Kane blocked a shot in the defensive zone and immediately dropped to the ice. The 38-year-old couldn’t put much pressure on his right skate and headed down the tunnel into the locker room. Kane did not return for the final 3:01. Blashill didn’t have much of an update on Kane during his postgame media session, but it would be crushing for the Blackhawks to lose him for any stretch of time. Since returning from a three-game absence earlier this month, Kane has played his best hockey of the season and been a huge reason for the recent turnaround. Kane’s playmaking and creativity have been terrific in the last seven games, but he’s also been more involved defensively than usual. That was apparent again in Seattle, as Kane, an unlikely candidate, recorded three blocked shots. Sadly, his final one might have some lasting effects, but that’s the self-sacrificing style Blashill wants from his players. “It doesn’t come without some risk, and I certainly don’t want a guy like Patrick to miss time or anything like that,” Blashill said. “But it is part of the game now, and it’s part of the commitment to winning that you have to have.” 4. Willing Shot Blockers Knight referenced the Blackhawks buy-in during his postgame media session, and it was obvious in the final minutes. With the game on the line, the forwards and defensemen jumped in front of every shot attempt and did everything possible to hold onto the one-goal advantage. It didn’t go unnoticed. “It’s something the coaching staff has emphasized,” Knight said about the players in front of him blocking shots. “I think over the course of [the season], guys have started getting comfortable with just doing that and buying into doing that. For me, it’s pretty motivating to see, just because when that happens, it shows sacrifice, and it makes you want to play more for the guys.” The Kraken led 68-55 in shot attempts on Wednesday, but only 30 found their way through to Knight. The Blackhawks led 19-7 in blocked shots in Seattle. Stepping in front of opposing shots is another way Blashill wanted the Blackhawks to become harder to play against, with Knight often seeing too much rubber earlier this season. He’s been pleased with the progression in that aspect. “Early in the season, we weren’t committed enough [to block shots], and I think we’ve gotten much better at it,” Blashill said. “We’re in lanes, and we’re way more committed to blocking shots. It’s one of those things that’s a little bit contagious. 5. Fourth Line Chips In Mentioned not too long ago in this postgame column was something along the lines of the Blackhawks, especially now without Bedard, needing more offensive contributions from their bottom-six forward group. Well, they’ve gotten it over the last couple of weeks. Fourth-line winger Cole Smith opened the scoring early in the third period with his third goal of the season, and he’s now recorded at least one point in four of the last five games. Glendening also provided a tremendous net-front screen on Ethan Del Mastro ‘s point shot, which Smith deflected into Seattle’s net. Smith, Glendening, and Jordan Greenway served as the fourth line against the Kraken, and they were an effective trio in their first look together. The Blackhawks led 8-6 in shots on goal, 5-2 in scoring chances, and 1-0 in goals for at even strength with the fourth line on the ice. They nearly added a second goal later in the third period, as Glendening beat Seattle netminder Joey Daccord, but the puck glanced off the post. On both sides of the ice, the fourth line was crisp, and that’s a much-welcomed development for the Blackhawks. Glendening’s style seems to be a perfect fit, along with Smith’s pace and Greenway’s heavy 200-foot game. For more Blackhawks news, visit Chicago Hockey Now and like our Facebook Page . title: Panthers’ Brad Marchand, Aleksander Barkov react to dominant return vs. Senators
summary: The Florida Panthers have sorely missed Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand during their lengthy injury absences — and Wednesday’s win showed exactly why. The two-time Stanley Cup champions combined for four points in their respective returns to the lineup as the Panthers defeated the Ottawa Senators 5-3 at Amerant Bank Arena. Marchand assisted on […] The post Panthers’ Brad Marchand, Aleksander Barkov react to dominant return vs. Senators appeared first on ClutchPoints.
content: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Panthers’ Brad Marchand, Aleksander Barkov react to dominant return vs. Senators appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Florida Panthers have sorely missed Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand during their lengthy injury absences — and Wednesday’s win showed exactly why. The two-time Stanley Cup champions combined for four points in their respective returns to the lineup as the Panthers defeated the Ottawa Senators 5-3 at Amerant Bank Arena. Marchand assisted on Florida’s first goal of the game and added two more helpers, while Barkov scored into the empty net late in regulation. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It was great to be out there, but even better seeing ‘Barky’ back again,” Marchand told reporters afterward, including NHL.com’s George Richards. “You saw that we can be a really good team.” “I feel like I got better once the game started going,” Barkov added. “The second, third period were better. Obviously it takes time to get used to playing against a really good team. There’s not much space on the ice. You have to kind of figure it out.” With Barkov and Marchand back in the lineup , the Panthers have arguably the deepest top nine in the National Hockey League. The former slotted back in on the top line alongside Sam Reinhart and Carter Verhaeghe, while the latter reunited with Anton Lundell and Eetu Luostarinen, a trio that was terrific in the 2025 Stanley Cup Playoffs. Barkov was back on the top power-play unit — with Reinhart, Seth Jones and the Tkachuk brothers — while Marchand skated with the second man advantage group. The pair had each played just two games this season before Wednesday following early-campaign injuries in October, but looked no worse for wear against a strong Senators team. Ottawa is tops in the Atlantic Division at 16-7-3, while Florida improved to 14-8-3, good for fifth in the division and now four points back of the Sens. Maybe nobody was happier than head coach Paul Maurice to have two of his most important players back in the fold. “The impact that those two men have on our team is seen in the game and it’s not just the big stuff,” the bench boss said, per Richards. “Barkov was 70 percent on his face-offs (16-for-23), was on the penalty kill, was on the power play. Big face-offs at the end of the game. He greatly affects the game. And Brad just generates, is just so quick on his edges and his hands are so fast. He can make those plays.” With a nearly healthy roster, the Panthers will hope they can get back to the level that saw them march to three consecutive Stanley Cup Finals between 2023-25. Up next is a visit to Washington to play the Capitals on Friday afternoon. MORE FLORIDA PANTHERS NEWS Are Aleksander Barkov, Brad Marchand returning from injury for Panthers vs. Senators?

title: Pete DeBoer reunites Mathew Barzal with Bo Horvat and it pays off for Islanders
summary: The Islanders’ first crack at remaking their top line after Kyle Palmieri’s injury was going back to an old standby.
content: The Islanders’ first crack at remaking their top line after Kyle Palmieri’s injury was going back to an old standby. Mathew Barzal was on Bo Horvat’s right wing for the first time this season, with Simon Holmstrom to Horvat’s left, as coach Pete DeBoer juggled his lines for Wednesday’s 3-2 shootout win over the Blues . All four lines looked different from the disastrous loss to the Maple Leafs two nights prior. The second line of Emil Heineman, Brayden Schenn and Victor Eklund was reunited. Bo Horvat celebrates after scoring the game-winning shootout goal in the Islanders’ 3-2 win over the Blues on Nov. 25, 2026, at UBS Arena. Corey Sipkin for New York Post Calum Ritchie was at right wing in his first game back in the lineup, completing a third line with Anthony Duclair on the left and Jean-Gabriel Pageau at center. Matias Maccelli was dropped to the fourth line on Casey Cizikas’ right, with Ondrej Palat at left wing. “I liked all our lines tonight,” DeBoer said, with three of the four having a positive shots-for margin on the evening, per Natural Stat Trick. “It wasn’t perfect but that was a really tight-checking game. There wasn’t a lot of room there. … We’ll see going forward but I liked everybody out there tonight.” Horvat and Barzal have played surprisingly little together since the 2023-24 season, when they were mainstays on the Islanders’ top line. Largely due to Barzal’s injury, they had just 18 games on the same line in 2024-25, then just 16 games together last season with both healthy. During nearly 300 minutes together at 5-on-5 last season, though, the pair had a 54.64 expected goals percentage. DeBoer said during an optional pregame skate that the Islanders were still working through possibilities, though their lineup largely mirrored the way they’d practiced Tuesday. The Islanders were still in wait-and-see mode Wednesday morning on Palmieri as he continued to see doctors, but the tone was pessimistic after the winger suffered a right knee injury Monday night. “It’s heartbreaking,” DeBoer said. “Same as [Alexander Romanov], same as what [Ryan Pulock’s] dealing with, really. If you would’ve told me at the 20-game mark that those three guys would all be facing what they’re facing, or faced already, it’s heartbreaking because all three of them went through long summers and rehab, things like that.” Asked whether surgery was a possibility for Palmieri, who tore the ACL in his left knee a year ago, DeBoer said, “I think everything’s on the table. We won’t know until he sees the doctors.” Logan Stanley played Wednesday after missing practice Tuesday for maintenance. Defenseman Kashawn Aitcheson was held out of the lineup in AHL Hamilton on Wednesday as a disciplinary measure because he was late to a treatment appointment, coach Jay McKee told local reporters. The Islanders held a pregame ceremony to honor Cizikas for reaching the 1,000-game mark .
