title: Anita DeFrantz, first Black woman to medal in Olympic rowing and a trailblazer at the IOC, dies at 74
summary: DeFrantz won a bronze medal with Team USA in 1976, becoming the first Black woman to win a medal in the sport, before becoming the first American woman elected to the IOC.
content: Anita DeFrantz, an Olympic medalist and pioneering member of the International Olympic Committee, died Wednesday, the IOC announced Thursday. She was 74. As a member of Team USA rowing, DeFrantz earned bronze with the USA women's eight at the 1976 Olympics in Montreal, becoming the first Black woman to win an Olympic medal in the sport. DeFrantz was elected to the IOC in 1986 in a trailblazing move, making her the first American woman and the first Black member to join the committee. In a statement , IOC president Kirsty Coventry described DeFrantz as "a mentor, a friend and a true inspiration." "I feel an immense sense of loss at Anita's passing," Coventry said. "From my earliest days in the Olympic Movement, she showed me what courageous leadership looked like, and what was possible for women in sport. She broke barriers long before many of us had the opportunity to follow, and I will never forget that the path I have been privileged to walk was made possible by trailblazers like Anita." Coventry, who was elected into office in 2025, chose to receive the Olympic torch from DeFrantz ahead of the 2026 Milan Olympics. Per the statement, DeFrantz described having a woman as IOC president as "exactly how the world should be." The IOC added that it will fly the Olympic flag at half-mast at the committee's headquarters in Switzerland for three days in DeFrantz's honor. DeFrantz, who grew up in Indianapolis, competed for Team USA from 1975 to 1980. She was team captain of the women's eight in 1976, leading the team to bronze in the sport's Olympic debut. As a member of the 1980 Olympic team, DeFrantz challenged the U.S. boycott of the Moscow Games that year, suing the U.S. Olympic Committee and testifying before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee. That effort earned her the Bronze Medal of the Olympic Order from the IOC that year. In the lead-up to the 1984 Olympics in Los Angeles, DeFrantz was the vice president of the LA 84 organizing committee. She remained president of the LA84, which developed youth sports programs, for 28 years after the Games concluded. With the IOC, DeFrantz joined the organization's executive board in 1992, and became the first female vice president of the committee in 1997. DeFrantz ran for IOC president in 2001, becoming the first woman to do so, but lost the election. She remained with the IOC, serving on the IOC executive board again from 2013 to 2017, and again serving as vice president from 2017 to 2021. DeFrantz was inducted into the U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Hall of Fame in 2025. In a joint statement, United States Olympic and Paralympic Committee CEO Sarah Hirshland and president Gene Sykes described DeFrantz as "a giant of the Olympic Movement." "Anita DeFrantz was one of the most consequential Olympians our nation has ever known. To those of us fortunate enough to work alongside her, she was also a mentor, a truth-teller and a steady source of wisdom and grace," the statement read. "For all of her historic firsts, what we will miss most is Anita herself: her quiet strength, her sharp mind and her warmth. She asked the hard questions, always with kindness, and always brought the conversation back to the athletes. She made each of us, and this organization, better. "Her legacy lives on in every Team USA athlete who speaks and is heard, and in every girl who finds her place in sport. On behalf of the entire Team USA family, we extend our deepest love and condolences to Anita's family, friends and colleagues around the world." U.S. Rowing honored DeFrantz and her contributions in a statement as well. "Though she is gone, DeFrantz's legacy and contributions to rowing and Olympic sports will continue to resonate with our community for years to come," the statement read. "We remember her extraordinary legacy and extend our condolences to her family, friends, and the rowing community."

title: Anita DeFrantz, Olympic medalist and pioneering IOC member, dies at 74
summary: Anita DeFrantz was the fifth woman, and first American woman, to serve as an IOC member.
content: July 12, 2025; Colorado Springs, CO, USA; Olympian Anita DeFrantz during the U.S. Olympic & Paralympic Hall of Fame Class of 2025 Induction Ceremony at The Broadmoor. Mandatory Credit: Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Anita DeFrantz, an Olympic rowing medalist who became one of the most influential people and a pioneering Black woman in the Olympic Movement over four decades, died Wednesday at age 74. The IOC called DeFrantz "a trailblazer for women in the Olympic Movement" and said "her legacy of courage, leadership and commitment to equality will live on." “I feel an immense sense of loss at Anita’s passing,” IOC President Kirsty Coventry of Zimbabwe said. “Anita was a mentor, a friend and a true inspiration to me, and to so many others around the world. From my earliest days in the Olympic Movement, she showed me what courageous leadership looked like, and what was possible for women in sport. She broke barriers long before many of us had the opportunity to follow, and I will never forget that the path I have been privileged to walk was made possible by trailblazers like Anita.” U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Committee CEO Sarah Hirshland called DeFrantz a "giant of the Olympic Movement." "Anita DeFrantz was one of the most consequential Olympians our nation has ever known," Hirshland said. "To those of us fortunate enough to work alongside her, she was also a mentor, a truth-teller and a steady source of wisdom and grace." Hirshland said that DeFrantz's "quiet strength, her sharp mind and her warmth" will be missed the most. "She asked the hard questions, always with kindness, and always brought the conversation back to the athletes," Hirshland said. "She made each of us, and this organization, better. Her legacy lives on in every Team USA athlete who speaks and is heard, and in every girl who finds her place in sport. On behalf of the entire Team USA family, we extend our deepest love and condolences to Anita's family, friends and colleagues around the world. Thank you, Anita, for pulling for all of us.” U.S. Rowing posted , “Though she is gone, DeFrantz’s legacy and contributions to rowing and Olympic sports will continue to resonate with our community for years to come. We remember her extraordinary legacy and extend our condolences to her family, friends, and the rowing community.” DeFrantz went from winning an Olympic women's eight bronze medal in 1976 to becoming an IOC member in 1986. She was the first American woman to hold IOC membership, fifth woman overall, and the first African American member. In 1997, she became the first woman to serve as an IOC vice president. In 2001, she became the first woman to run for the IOC presidency (an election won by Belgian Jacques Rogge). She also served as vice president of the 1984 Los Angeles Olympic Organizing Committee. For 28 years after those Olympics, she was president of the LA84 Foundation, which developed youth sports programs that defined the legacy of the Games. DeFrantz, also a 1980 Olympic team member, challenged the U.S. boycott of the 1980 Moscow Games. She testified before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, arguing that American athletes should be permitted to go, and sued the U.S. Olympic Committee over the decision. For her efforts, she was awarded the Bronze Medal of the Olympic Order by the IOC in 1980. DeFrantz, born Oct. 4, 1952, grew up in Indianapolis with three brothers. She was introduced to rowing in the early 1970s as a Connecticut College sophomore. A few years later, while a Penn law student, she was team captain as women's rowing made its Olympic debut at the 1976 Montreal Games, earning a bronze medal in the eight. She called rowing the "noblest of sports" and the "ultimate team sport." "Unlike other sports, we can't say, 'OK, I need a couple of strokes off, I'll get back with you,'" she said upon being inducted into the U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Hall of Fame in 2025 . "We're in it together, and that taught me so much." She loved the Olympic Movement, saying "it's based on values, not entertainment, but the values of fair play and mutual respect." She advocated for athletes and fought for female representation, both for athletes and administrators. When DeFrantz competed at the Olympics, there were 1,260 women to 4,813 men in Montreal. At LA 2028, there will be more female athlete quota spots than male athlete quota spots for the first time in Olympic history. IOC membership went from five women and more than 80 men when DeFrantz joined in 1986 to 46 women and 60 men following elections during the Milan Cortina Winter Games. In March 2025, DeFrantz traveled to Costa Navarino, Greece, to cast her vote in the election where Coventry became the IOC's first female president. "I was just really proud that I could make her proud," a teary Coventry said on the day she was elected. "Women like her paved the way for women like me." In July 2025, Coventry returned the favor, traveling to Colorado Springs to introduce DeFrantz as she was inducted into the United States Olympic and Paralympic Hall of Fame. title: Anita DeFrantz, women's Olympic trailblazer, dies at 74
summary: Anita DeFrantz won a bronze medal in rowing at the 1976 Summer Games and was the first American woman to serve on the International Olympic Committee.
content: Olympic rowing medalist and former International Olympic Committee member Anitz DeFrantz has died at the age of 74. The IOC announced the death of DeFrantz , the first African-American and the first American woman to hold a seat on the committee, on Thursday, Nov. 26. "I feel an immense sense of loss at Anita’s passing," IOC President Kirsty Coventry said. "Anita was a mentor, a friend and a true inspiration to me, and to so many others around the world. From my earliest days in the Olympic Movement, she showed me what courageous leadership looked like, and what was possible for women in sport." DeFrantz captained the United States' rowing team at the 1976 Olympics in Montreal, earning a bronze medal in the women's eight. She served as vice president of Los Angeles' 1984 Olympic organizing committee and was elected to serve on the IOC in 1986. DeFrantz, an outspoken advocate for women's sports, spent a total of 13 years on the IOC's executive board, becoming the organization's first female vice president in 1997. She also chaired the IOC’s Women and Sport Commission for nearly two decades. "With the death of Anita DeFrantz, the Olympic Movement has lost a great trailblazer and an outstanding advocate for the Olympic values," IOC honorary president Thomas Bach said. "Personally, I am losing a longstanding and wonderful friend. Our friendship started at the beginning of the 1980s, when we both stood up against the boycott of the Olympic Games Moscow 1980, and both lost this fight. It showed how much we were thinking alike; and this brought us very close together. In the many years after, I had the privilege of working with her very closely in the IOC. I will be forever grateful for her inspiration and support, in particular when we were serving together on the Executive Board for many years." Most recently, DeFrantz was inducted into the U.S. Olympic and Paralympic Hall of Fame in 2025 for her career characterized by courage, service and pioneering leadership. She was also honored for her service to the Olympic movement at the 2026 Milano Cortina Winter Games by participating in the torch relay, handing off the flame to Coventry, the IOC's first female president. "Receiving the Olympic flame from Anita was a moment full of emotions," Coventry said at the time. "She really led the way for female leaders in sport globally." title: British Olympian wins the 90th Manchester Road Race

content: MANCHESTER – Sam Atkin , a two-time Olympian from England, won the 90th Manchester Road Race Thursday morning, finishing first on the 4.737-mile course in 20 minutes, 57 seconds, three seconds off the course record. Atkin, 33, who is based in Colorado and competed in the Tokyo and Paris Olympics, ran in the race for the first time. Edwin Kurgat , last year’s winner and course record holder, finished second (21:01) and Morgan Beadlescomb, the 2023 winner, was third (21:03). Diane van Es of the Netherlands won the women’s race in 24:03. Florencia Borelli was second (24:23) and Annie Rodenfels third (24:23). There were 14,449 people registered for the race this year, the biggest number in years. It was windy and chilly at the start but the rain held off.

title: Campbell Wright is first American to win a biathlon World Cup standalone race
summary: Campbell Wright won the season-opening 20km by a wide margin.
content: Campbell Wright became the first American to win a biathlon World Cup standalone race, taking the season-opening 20km individual in Kontiolahti, Finland, on Thanksgiving. Wright, a 24-year-old with a best individual Olympic finish of eighth last February, was the only man in the field of more than 100 to shoot clean (20 for 20) on Thursday and won the 46-minute race by a comfortable 1 minute, 20 seconds. In 2025, Wright became the first American to win two individual medals at one World Biathlon Championships, earning silvers in the 10km sprint and the 12.5km pursuit in Lenzerheide, Switzerland. American Lowell Bailey previously won a race at the 2017 World Championships. In biathlon, World Championships also count in the World Cup standings. Wright will be the second American to wear the World Cup points leader’s yellow bib after Tim Burke in 2009 and 2010. Wright was born and raised in New Zealand with parents who were born in the U.S. Wright placed 32nd and 75th in two 2022 Olympic events while competing for New Zealand as the only teenage male biathlete at those Games. He also worked as a barista during the offseason. Wright, a dual citizen, then moved to Lake Placid, New York, spent time training with the American team and switched representation to the U.S. in 2023. "Not too bad, eh?" title: Alisson Becomes First LFC Goalkeeper to Register Assist in Champions League History
summary: Still breaking records.
content: Liverpool's goalkeeper #01 Alisson Becker (R) and Liverpool's forward #09 Alexander Isak celebrate at the end of the UEFA Champions League league phase football match between Club Brugge and Liverpool at Jan-Breydel Stadium in Bruges on November 25, 2026. (Photo by NICOLAS TUCAT / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images A rather inexplicable statistic has emerged following Liverpool FC’s 3-0 away win over Club Brugge in the UEFA Champions League. Goalkeeper Alisson Becker hoofed the ball long to Alexander Isak, who went one-on-one with veteran keeper Yann Sommer and scored. That… was somehow the first assist by a Liverpool keeper in the competition’s history. This appears to include European Cup fixtures, and not some Premier League/First Division delineation we’re so used to being subjected to exclude some all-time Liverpool greats from whatever conversations sports media wants us to have. 1 – Alisson is the first Liverpool goalkeeper to provide an assist in the UEFA Champions League. Inventive. pic.twitter.com/1bHLTFuwYC — OptaJoe (@OptaJoe) November 25, 2026 Other interesting statistics: This was Alisson’s fourth assist for the club. His previous three? All of them were for one Mohamed Salah. Of course, Alisson also has a goal to his name, with the memorable header in the dying seconds against West Brom seared into everybody’s minds. This assist was almost exactly like those Salah goals, a long, accurate ball, and Isak was off to the races, with only the opposition keeper to beat. The recent news that Alisson is open to an extension should be music to every Liverpool fan’s ears. The club has been blessed with some wonderful goalkeepers, and Alisson could very well be the best of them all with his complete game.

title: Analysing Arsenal ahead of Sunday’s Premier League clash
summary: A closer look at the side we’ll play this Sunday… Men's Team How can I watch Arsenal v City on TV around the globe? We go to north London to face defending Premier League champions Arsenal in a 16...
content: Analysing Arsenal ahead of Sunday’s Premier League clash A closer look at the side we’ll play this Sunday… Men's Team How can I watch Arsenal v City on TV around the globe? We go to north London to face defending Premier League champions Arsenal in a 16:30 (UK) kick-off. City come into the weekend third in the league, with 22 points from 11 games – having won seven, drawn one and lost three. With the help of Opta data, we find out more about the Arsenal team we’ll play… Recent form Arsenal sit six points clear at the top of the table, claiming 28 from a possible 33 so far this season. Their one defeat came against Brighton in September but their only draw was in their last outing – a 2-2 draw at Newcastle United last weekend. They also tied with Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday evening. However, they’ve very much enjoyed playing at home in the league this season and remain the only side yet to drop points at their home ground across all 20 sides. Men's Team Register your interest in our new PUMA x C.P. Company kit Preferred lineup Arsenal almost exclusively play 4-2-3-1 under Mikel Arteta. David Raya has established himself as one of the world’s best goalkeepers but could miss this game through injury, with Kepa Arrizabalaga the assumed stand-in. From right to left, Jurrien Timber, Ezri Konsa, Gabriel and Riccardo Calafiori appear to be the first choice back four during William Saliba’s injury absence. The likes of Ben White and Piero Hincapie may otherwise feature. In the double pivot, it’s either Bruno Guimaraes or Myles Lewis-Skelly to partner Declan Rice with captain Martin Odegaard ahead of them. Men's Team Maresca: We take the point and move on Noni Madueke has been in form on the right wing with Bukayo Saka currently out, with Christos Tzolis or Eberechi Eze on the left. Kai Havertz is the main man in the No.9 role. Manager Mikel Arteta cut his teeth in the coaching world under Pep Guardiola following his retirement in 2016 until becoming Arsenal boss in December 2019. He ensured gradual improvement, finishing runners-up to City in 2022/23 and 2023/24 before getting their hands on the title last time out. Only two managers currently in the Premier League have overseen more than his 259 games in charge – David Moyes and Mauricio Pochettino – but he is the longest serving manager in his current job by 109 matches. In his 259 Premier League games as boss to date, he’s won 158, drawn 49 and lost 52 times. That means his 61% win rate is by far the best of any manager currently in the competition. One of the current wave of outstanding managers from the Basque country, Arteta is known for a passion and exuberance in the dugout. Head-to-head record Having won on six consecutive Premier League trips to Arsenal between 2018 and 2023, we haven’t been victorious on our last three visits. Overall, the two sides have met 58 times in the Premier League with Arsenal winning 25 and City 20. Seven of our victories have come at Arsenal’s home. Interestingly, we have won 12 of our last 14 Premier League games against reigning champions, completing the double over Liverpool last season. We lost the Community Shield 3-0 to them in August but we did have the upper hand over Arsenal in meetings last season, with a late, late equaliser at the Emirates earning them a point before we won 2-1 at the Etihad in April. How they defend Resolutely. There’s no doubt their defence is what their success last season was built upon. In fact, David Raya has won the last three Premier League Golden Glove awards since moving to Arsenal and is in pole position for this one too. They conceded just 27 times last season and have only let in seven so far more than a quarter of the way through the campaign. That record is again the best in the league so far, while they have the meanest defence inside the box and in the first 15 minutes of games. However, they are a little more susceptible to set pieces than last season with their two goals conceded from corners only putting them mid-table in the Premier League. Only two sides have committed fewer fouls than them so far and seen fewer yellow cards too. How they attack With 17 goals so far, they’re the seventh most prolific side in the division. That matches their place in the table for big chances created (28) and is slightly better than their ninth place for amount of shots (151). They’re nowhere near as threatening from set pieces this season as last, with just two goals from those situations so far. Martin Odegaard is a central figure in everything they do. Since the 2023/24 season, only Bruno Fernandes (41) and Mohamed Salah (35) have more Premier League assists than Odegaard (25). Meanwhile, Kai Havertz has enjoyed playing against us recently having been involved in four goals in our last four games. With 514 passes per match, they are the fifth most possession focused side in the league, with City top on 634. Havertz, Odegaard and Saka all have three goals each, with several others chipping in too. City v Leeds: Tickets on sale now Don’t miss out on our exciting clash with Leeds this December. Enzo Maresca’s men comes up against Daniel Farke’s team on Wednesday 2 December, kick-off 19:30 (UK). Tickets are on sale to Premium, Matchday and Junior Members with one previous purchase at the Etihad Stadium. It’s four tickets per Member with an additional three for Season Ticket Members. You can also make a special night of it with a hospitality experience under the Etihad lights. Our hospitality packages start from £130 per person in City Hall, with places in Crossbar all the way through to Backstage available. BUY TICKETS NOW

title: Andoni Iraola optimistic over Victor Munoz knee injury after Liverpool beat Club Brugge
summary: Andoni Iraola remains optimistic over Victor Munoz's knee injury after the winger limped off during Liverpool's 3-0 Champions League win against Club Brugge. Despite the £34.5 million summer signing leaving the pitch in significant discomfort, the manager offered a hopeful update ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash with Everton.
content: SOCCER CL DAY5 CLUB BRUGGE VS LIVERPOOL FC - AFP Andoni Iraola remains optimistic over Victor Munoz's knee injury after the winger limped off during Liverpool's 3-0 Champions League win against Club Brugge. Despite the £34.5 million summer signing leaving the pitch in significant discomfort, the manager offered a hopeful update ahead of Sunday's Premier League clash with Everton. Munoz limps off in Liverpool win Iraola says he remains optimistic regarding Munoz's fitness after the winger was forced off with a knee injury during Liverpool's 3-0 Champions League victory over Club Brugge on Wednesday night. The 23-year-old suffered the blow in the closing stages of the first half in Belgium. Although Munoz looked in significant discomfort as he departed, he was able to limp off the pitch without needing a stretcher. His premature exit proved to be the sole concern on an otherwise comfortable European evening for Liverpool, leaving the club waiting anxiously to learn the extent of the damage. Iraola offers hopeful post-match injury update Speaking after the win in Belgium, Iraola admitted that seeing Munoz forced off dampened the mood despite the convincing scoreline. However, the Liverpool boss revealed that the winger's outlook had already improved by the time the match concluded. "It was the worst part of the game, definitely," Iraola said, as quoted by Metro . "He was in a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive after the game had finished. In the moment it was very, very painful. After the game I spoke with him and he was a little bit more optimistic." Liverpool cruise past Brugge despite setback Munoz joined Liverpool in the summer after completing a £34.5 million transfer from Osasuna. The club's medical staff will now evaluate how the joint reacts before determining whether the issue is minor or more serious. "It was a knock on the knee so now we have to assess him if the knee presents well tomorrow and it's just a knock or, obviously, it's very early to tell if there's something more than a knock," Iraola explained. Despite losing Munoz before the interval, Liverpool still produced a clinical display to dispatch Club Brugge. Two goals from Alexander Isak, alongside a strike from Florian Wirtz, sealed the 3-0 triumph and made it four wins in five Champions League matches this season. Munoz faces race for Everton clash Attention now turns swiftly to Thursday's assessment as the Reds await clarity on whether Munoz has avoided a lengthy spell on the sidelines. Iraola's side return to Premier League action on Sunday with an away fixture against Everton. Whether the £34.5 million winger recovers in time to feature this weekend remains to be seen.

title: Andoni Iraola provides Liverpool injury update after Club Brugge win
summary: Víctor Muñoz Injury Update After Liverpool Beat Club Brugge 3-0Liverpool came away from Belgium with a 3-0 win over Club Brugge, but the main talking point was Victor Munoz and the knee injury that ...
content: Andoni Iraola provides Liverpool injury update after Club Brugge win Víctor Muñoz Injury Update After Liverpool Beat Club Brugge 3-0 Liverpool came away from Belgium with a 3-0 win over Club Brugge, but the main talking point was Victor Munoz and the knee injury that forced the youngster off before half-time. Munoz went into an aggressive challenge with Jorne Spileers and came off second best after what looked like a clash of knees. He stayed down in obvious pain, Liverpool’s medical staff were called on, and the delay was long enough to raise concern on the pitch and on the bench. A stretcher was brought out, which usually tells you plenty. In this case, it was not needed. Munoz left the pitch under his own steam, albeit with a heavy limp and clear discomfort. That matters. Players who can walk off are not automatically fine, but it does suggest the situation may be less serious than it first looked. IMAGO Andoni Iraola gives early Victor Munoz verdict Iraola did not overplay it after full-time. He said what he knew and no more. “[Munoz’s injury] is the worst part of the game, definitely,” Iraola said post-match. He added: “He was with a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game had finished. “It has been a knock on the knee, so now we have to assess him. Then if he presents well tomorrow and it’s just this knock… but obviously it’s very early to tell if there is something more than the knock. “But in the moment it was very, very painful. After the game, I talked to him and he was a little bit more optimistic.” Liverpool injury concern before Merseyside derby That is the sensible reading of it. Painful, yes. Serious, not confirmed. Liverpool will assess him properly, and timing is the issue here. The Merseyside derby at the Hill Dickinson Stadium is next, and availability remains uncertain. This is awkward for Liverpool because they were already missing Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch in Bruges. Squad depth helps, but losing another option before a derby is hardly ideal. Club Brugge 0-3 Liverpool as Alexander Isak strikes again Before Munoz went off, Liverpool had already taken control. Dominik Szoboszlai supplied Alexander Isak for the opener after 13 minutes, with the striker finishing from close range. Florian Wirtz made it 2-0, and Isak added his second to complete a straightforward 3-0 win. The result was comfortable. The Munoz injury was not. For now, Iraola’s post-match comments offer Liverpool some encouragement.

title: Andoni Iraola provides Victor Munoz injury update after Liverpool’s win at Club Brugge
summary: Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz scored the goals as the Reds eased past Club Brugge 3-0 in Belgium
content: Andoni Iraola has provided an update on Victor Munoz after the winger was forced off injured in Liverpool’s 3-0 win over Club Brugge . The only downside on a night the Reds they kept their first clean sheet in the Champions League this season, Munoz took a heavy blow to the knee and was replaced by Rio Ngumoha in the 42nd minute. The Spaniard, who scored his third Premier League goal in the routing of Manchester United on the weekend, was in visible agony as he was being treated but Iraola has revealed that the pain had subsided by the end of the match. “He was with a lot of pain when he left the pitch. He was a lot more positive when the game has finished,” said Iraola. Liverpool’s Victor Munoz (right) leaves the pitch (Bruno Fahy/PA) “It has been a knock on the knee so now we have to see how it presents tomorrow and see if it is just a knock – but it is very early to tell if there is something more. “In the moment it was very painful and after the game I talked to him and he was more optimistic.” Iraola was nevertheless delighted with his two £100m men Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz as the pair’s goals edged Liverpool closer to Champions League qualification.. Isak scored at either end of the game to take his tally to 10 for the season – on target in his last six away games – with Wirtz continuing his good form with a sixth in five games for club and country. Victory lifted Liverpool into fifth place on 12 points – in the two seasons of the new format, 16 has been enough to guarantee the top-eight finish needed to avoid a two-legged play-off in February. “I am very pleased with the result and the performance overall. The result, 3-0, you can think it was an easy game but I don’t think it was,” said Iraola. On Isak, he added: “Obviously he is in a great moment right now. In the first half especially he helped us a lot in the link-up, we were finding him very easily. “The way they pressed was very aggressive and you have to find the last line straight away. Alex was helping us a lot in those situations. “In the second half it was more about defending a little bit lower. We knew they would push forward and give spaces to exploit. “Sometimes they were leaving him one-v-one against the centre-backs and in one of those moments he has killed the game.” Florian Wirtz (left) impressed once again (Virginie Lefour/PA) Isak said he was “in a good place…hopefully it gets better from here”. He added on TNT sports: “The attack in general is beginning to click. We have a lot of different combinations and whoever comes in we have a dangerous attack. It feels good.” Isak and Wirtz are starting to form a profitable partnership, but Iraola believes the overall team performances are helping them flourish. “Both are now in a good place,” he said. “When the team overall is playing well and we are getting good results, everyone looks a little better. When everything collectively is not there, everyone looks a little bit worse. “The important part is they help the team to play well, to win games, to get results, and if we play well then we have chances, we are solid, everyone will play their part and will look better. Alex and Flo right now are in a good moment.”

title: Anthony Gordon makes history! Barcelona star smashes RARE Cristiano Ronaldo & Karim Benzema records during Champions League masterclass against Sabah
summary: Anthony Gordon continues to justify his hefty price tag at Barcelona after a historic night in the Champions League saw him eclipse a long-standing record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. The England international was the catalyst for a dominant Blaugrana display in Azerbaijan, proving exactly why the Catalan giants moved so decisively for his signature last summer.
content: Anthony Gordon continues to justify his hefty price tag at Barcelona after a historic night in the Champions League saw him eclipse a long-standing record held by Cristiano Ronaldo. The England international was the catalyst for a dominant Blaugrana display in Azerbaijan, proving exactly why the Catalan giants moved so decisively for his signature last summer. Gordon inspires dominant Barcelona victory in Baku Gordon delivered a Man of the Match display on Wednesday night as Barcelona cruised to a 4-1 Champions League triumph over Sabah at the Baku Olympic Stadium. The England winger struck twice in Azerbaijan to spearhead another commanding European victory for the Catalan side. His latest brace continued an impressive debut campaign in Spain following his £69m transfer in May. Having arrived amid initial scepticism, Gordon now boasts five goals and five assists across all competitions, rapidly establishing himself as a standout summer acquisition. Shattering Ronaldo and Benzema's Champions League records Finding the net twice against Sabah saw Gordon become the first player in Champions League history to score six away goals in a single country within one calendar year. That tally eclipses the previous benchmark of five shared by former Real Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo, who achieved the feat in Turkey in 2013, and Karim Benzema, who matched it in England in 2022. The double also handed Gordon the all-time Champions League record for the most away goals scored by an English player in one nation. His latest strikes in Azerbaijan added to the four goals he registered in the country for Newcastle against Qarabag during last season's competition. Relentless attacking mindset fuels Baku love affair Gordon's clinical edge in Baku underlined the aggressive philosophy driving Barcelona's European campaign, with the attacker insisting the visitors refused to ease off even after taking control of the tie. Speaking after the final whistle, he said: "Even when we were 3-0 up, we didn't stop attacking. We kept trying to score. That's our style, and I think it's very important." Despite walking away with the Man of the Match trophy and a pair of historic records, the former Newcastle forward admitted he left the pitch slightly frustrated at missing out on a treble. He added: " Baku must be a very special place for me ... I should have scored another hat-trick tonight, but I wasted that chance with my left foot." Deportivo trip and Manchester City clash await Barcelona now turn their attention to an away trip to Deportivo this weekend, where Gordon will aim to build on his tally this term. Maintaining that sharp attacking rhythm will be vital as the Catalan side look to carry their momentum forward. European action then resumes on December 8, when Barcelona host Manchester City at Camp Nou. With Gordon in record-breaking form on the continental stage, the fixture offers another major test for the summer signing.

title: Antonee Robinson on Fulham's development, Pochettino at Man United, Guardiola for USMNT and trophy dreams
summary: USMNT left back Antonee Robinson spoke to NBC Sports about a variety of topics, as the Fulham star is hopeful of trophies for club and country.
content: LONDON — Fulham and USMNT star Antonee Robinson was relaxed and reflective as he took some time to chat with NBC Sports at Fulham's Motspur Park training base ahead of the busy festive period coming up in the Premier League. The marauding left back praised the way new manager Alvaro Arbeloa has tweaked Fulham's style of play and explained how they're creating more chances and have clicked in recent weeks. Their impressive draw at Manchester City last weekend stretched their unbeaten run to five league games and Fulham are extremely fun to watch. Robinson praises Arbeloa, explains how his role has changed "The form has really picked up. The first few games with a new manager and new players it's difficult to have everything figured out straight away," Robinson explained. "There were times when even if we were playing good we were getting picked out for little mistakes. The team has adapted and the manager has done really well picking out problems and seeing where we need to improve. He said from the start he liked a lot of the things we were seeing in the games, we just needed to tidy up on a few things." "For me personally I feel like I've been a lot higher on the pitch," Robinson continued. "He picks one full back to be high and wide and then the other side it is the winger and with Sander [Berge] and Shea [Charles] playing together and being a bit more solid in the midfield has helped us a lot. Like I said, the fact there was a lot of underlying things at the start of the season where even if we weren't winning games, he was still really happy with us and told us to 'keep building the belief, keep building our identity' and it's a long season... "The fact we've kept to his ideals and carried on pushing through and now we are starting to reap the benefits of that, it instils confidence in us as a team." Robinson on Pochettino: “He is such a personable guy, a great manager” On the international stage Robinson reflected on a positive 2026 World Cup for the USMNT, as he was a key part of the team which inspired so many new fans as they reached the last 16. He hopes they can kick on and succeed at the Gold Cup this summer, then hopefully the 2028 Copa America being held in the U.S. before taking a big step forward at the 2030 World Cup. Robinson, 29, also spoke of his belief that former USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino will turn things around at Manchester United after leaving the U.S. side unexpectedly. "It was a great experience," Robinson said when asked about playing for Pochettino. "He is such a personable guy, a great manager and fills the team with a lot of confidence and belief and the kind of passion he has for the game I feel like he really instilled that in our team. That translated into the World Cup and us playing pretty well. You can understand why when Man United came along he felt like it was time to change project. That is up to him. I think everyone wishes him all the best and know that despite the bad start they've just had they know the quality he's got and what he can do to turn things around. Hopefully things go well for him." With Man United linked with a new left back in January, it's no surprise Robinson's name has come up in transfer reports considering he has just over 18 months left on his Fulham contract and played so well under Pochettino for the USMNT. Time will tell how that all plays out when it comes to Robinson's future at club level. US Argentine head coach Mauricio Pochettino gestures past defender #05 Antonee Robinson during the 2026 World Cup Group D football match between USA and Paraguay at the Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood on June 12, 2026. (Photo by Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images) AFP via Getty Images Pep Guardiola next for USMNT head coach? “I think it’s an attractive job” - Robinson When asked about who U.S. Soccer should be looking at to replace Pochettino, Robinson admitted that a manager of the ilk of Pep Guardiola (heavily linked with replacing Pochettino) makes sense given the direction the USMNT are heading in. "Hopefully someone who can carry on the good exciting football that we've done and someone who gets results and someone who can figure out how we win any game we are faced with and can deliver results," Robinson said of what a new USMNT manager should have. "You'd put him [Guardiola] and Poch and other people like that in the same category of managers. I'm not necessarily sure who would be the best fit. It would be interesting for Pep as that would be his first international managerial stint, it is different going from club to international and you have less control than you would at a club. It's going to be interesting and hopefully someone of a Pep caliber would definitely be interested because I think it's an attractive job. I feel like we've got very good players so they're taking on a good team." NEW YORK, NEW YORK - SEPTEMBER 18: Former manager Pep Guardiola attends the match between New York City Football Club and New York Red Bulls at Yankee Stadium on September 18, 2026 in the Bronx borough of New York City. (Photo by Jordan Bank/Getty Images) Getty Images Reflective Robinson eager to win more silverware to put extra gloss on a superb career Off the pitch Robinson is an impressive character. From card tricks to playing the piano to acrobatic back flips when he scores goals, USMNT and Fulham legend Tim Ream once described Robinson as having 'more talent in his pinky finger than I've got in my whole body!' So has Robinson got any new skills? "I'm putting all of my energy into getting better at golf, because I'm crap at that!" Robinson laughed. Given his talent for just about anything, he'll likely be on the PGA Tour soon. As for his main targets and goals for the rest of his career, Robinson was reflective on just how far he's come from a youngster at Everton going out on loan to Bolton Wanderers and Wigan Athletic to becoming one of the most consistent left backs in the Premier League over the last five years. "When I look back to when I was younger and before I made my way in the pro game, I don't think if you'd have told me I would have played in two World Cups, played in 100 or so Premier League games, played for my national team so many times, that I would have believed it. So I think it's about taking pride in what I've already achieved and enjoying that." He also revealed winning silverware at Fulham, and some more with the USMNT, is a huge aim. "And at the same time when I finish I want to play as many games as I can at the highest level," Robinson continued. "Try and win trophies which I feel like at some point Fulham is overdue one. The past few years we've had a good few cup runs that have fell short when they shouldn't have. "So hopefully this season the FA Cup comes along. Playing at the top level for as long as I can, hopefully win some trophies, playing with the national team to the best I can and hopefully win some more trophies with them too." MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 21: Antonee Robinson of Fulham in action during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester City and Fulham at Etihad Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Manchester, United Kingdom. (Photo by Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Offside via Getty Images) Offside via Getty Images

title: Arrested at training! Vasco da Gama forward David Correa detained by police as club considers terminating his contract
summary: Vasco da Gama forward David Correa was sensationally arrested by police on Thursday morning in the middle of a first-team training session. Officers executed a pretrial detention warrant as part of a wider investigation, leaving the Brazilian club to weigh up the future of the 31-year-old attacker.
content: Olimpia v Vasco da Gama - Copa CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2026 - Getty Images Sport Vasco da Gama forward David Correa was sensationally arrested by police on Thursday morning in the middle of a first-team training session. Officers executed a pretrial detention warrant as part of a wider investigation, leaving the Brazilian club to weigh up the future of the 31-year-old attacker. Shock arrest during Vasco training session The Brazilian football community was left in a state of disbelief on Thursday morning when police officers arrived at the Vasco da Gama training ground to detain forward Correa. Agents from Leblon’s 14th Police Precinct carried out the arrest under a pretrial detention warrant linked to a major operation by the Espirito Santo Civil Police. Witnesses saw the player, who was dressed in his full training kit at the time, being led away by authorities in what has quickly become one of the most high-profile scandals in the Brasileirao this season. The investigation targeting the 31-year-old is wide-ranging and carries severe implications. Authorities confirmed that the operation is focused on alleged drug and weapons trafficking and money laundering, which has been under scrutiny for several weeks. ESCÁNDALO EN EL FÚTBOL BRASILEÑO 🚨⚽ Así fue el momento en que la policía llegó al centro de entrenamiento de Vasco da Gama para detener al delantero David Corrêa da Fonseca 😳 El futbolista fue arrestado por presuntos vínculos con tráfico de drogas y armas, lavado de dinero,… pic.twitter.com/KKXISTxcgI — ABC Deportes (@ABCDeportes) November 26, 2026 This dramatic escalation follows a previous court order in late October that required the player to hand over his passport. The situation has intensified significantly with reports suggesting the probe also involves allegations of attempted murder and the potential bribing of witnesses, as noted by ABC Deportes . Legal avenues and contract suspension options Following the arrest, Vasco da Gama are now exploring their legal rights regarding Correa's employment. Under Brazil’s Consolidation of Labor Laws (CLT), the club has the immediate authority to halt certain financial obligations while the player remains in custody. This includes the suspension of his salary, contributions to the employee severance fund (FGTS), and other prorated benefits. The club is carefully navigating the General Sports Law, which offers a specific framework for professional athletes who are unable to fulfil their duties due to personal legal issues unrelated to their sporting activity. Specifically, Article 88 of the General Sports Law stipulates that if an athlete is unable to participate for more than 90 consecutive days for reasons that are entirely their own responsibility, the club may formally suspend the special sports employment contract. For this to take effect, Vasco would need to provide formal notice and register the suspension within the National Registration System of the Brazilian Football Confederation. While the player’s defense team can seek a habeas corpus petition, the club is prioritising the protection of its own interests during the ongoing judicial process. The path to contract termination While suspension is an immediate option, the total termination of Correa's contract for cause is a more complex matter under Brazilian law. Currently, the club can only move for a termination for cause once a final conviction has been reached with no further avenues for appeal. As Correa is presently only under investigation and has not been convicted of any crime, the "innocent until proven guilty" principle remains a significant hurdle for the Rio-based outfit. If the club chooses to part ways immediately, they would likely have to negotiate a mutual agreement or pay the full sports termination compensation required by current legislation. Correa, who has been a regular for Vasco since 2024, had already sat out the club's recent fixture against Bragantino before this week's events took place. His absence from the pitch is now set to be indefinite as the legal proceedings in Espirito Santo unfold. For Vasco da Gama, the focus now shifts from the training pitch to the boardroom and the courts, as they decide how to handle the future of a player who has contributed six goals throughout the current campaign but now faces a fight to clear his name against a litany of serious charges. Police raided Correa's home On September 1, 2029, Brazilian police raided the home of Correa in the upscale Barra da Tijuca district and the club's training ground as part of a major investigation into alleged drug and arms trafficking. The cross-state operation, codenamed "The Troop", involved around 100 officers, according to the Associated Press. The operation resulted in four arrest warrants and 15 search warrants being executed. Vila Nova right-back Hayner Cordeiro was also investigated as authorities looked into suspected links between professional footballers and organised crime networks. Meanwhile Correa left Vasco's training facility without answering questions from reporters.

title: Arsenal has doubts over giving key man a new contract
summary: Arsenal have been offering new contracts to several members of their first team in recent weeks, and more players are expected to receive improved deals at the Emirates Stadium. The Gunners have enjoy...
content: Arsenal has doubts over giving key man a new contract Arsenal have been offering new contracts to several members of their first team in recent weeks, and more players are expected to receive improved deals at the Emirates Stadium. The Gunners have enjoyed considerable success on the pitch in recent seasons, rewarding the efforts of a squad that has worked hard to maintain high standards. Much of that progress has come under Mikel Arteta, whose players have continued to work towards making the team competitive. The club want to maintain that progress, and securing the futures of key members of the squad remains part of their plans. However, not every contract situation is straightforward. There is one player Arteta would reportedly like to see commit his future to Arsenal, but there are concerns within the club about whether to offer him a new deal. Arsenal have doubts over Odegaard’s next contract That player is Martin Odegaard, although Football Insider reports that there are doubts at board level about the prospect of handing him a new contract. Arsenal are reportedly concerned that the midfielder may not develop much further and could begin to decline, with the feeling that he is no longer performing at the highest level of his game. Those concerns appear to have influenced the club’s thinking, despite Odegaard remaining a regular member of the team. The situation creates a difference between Arteta’s reported preference and the board’s position. While the manager would like to secure the midfielder’s future, the decision-makers at the club are understood to be more cautious about committing to another deal. Martin Odegaard v Brentford. (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) Gunners assess Odegaard’s long-term future Odegaard has remained involved in the first team, but Arsenal do not currently view his performances in the same way as those of some of their other players. The club reportedly have doubts about whether he can continue to improve and maintain the level expected of him. That does not mean Arsenal are necessarily preparing for his departure. Rather, the concern is whether offering him a new contract would be the right decision for the club at this stage. The Gunners have been rewarding several players for their contributions , but Odegaard’s situation appears to be different. title: Bap suggests reducing the number of teams relegated from the Brasileirão
summary: Flamengo president Luiz Eduardo Baptista, known as Bap, criticized the Brazilian Championship’s current relegation format, which sends four teams down to Série B each year.According to ge, the exec...
content: Bap suggests reducing the number of teams relegated from the Brasileirão Flamengo president Luiz Eduardo Baptista, known as Bap, criticized the Brazilian Championship’s current relegation format, which sends four teams down to Série B each year. According to ge, the executive said during the "CBF Summit Academy" that the current model is financially unsustainable for Brazilian football. In the Flamengo president’s view, the high turnover hurts both promoted and relegated teams. Newly promoted teams commit to long, expensive contracts to compete in the top flight, risking financial damage they may not recover from if they quickly return to the second division, while established clubs lose the ability to pay their bills after relegation. According to ge, Bap presented Flamengo’s proposed alternative for restructuring the competition. The idea is to gradually reduce the number of relegated teams—to three in one season, then setting the limit at just two from the following season onward. In addition to reducing the number of relegations, the executive suggested creating a financial safety net to support relegated teams. He stressed that relegation cuts revenue by 70% to 80%, making budget adjustments extremely difficult without that support. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇧🇷 here.

title: Barcelona duo make strong case for bigger role under Flick after impressive performance vs Sabah
summary: Barcelona’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Sabah was not a routine win for Hansi Flick.This is because the likes of Alejandro Balde and Karim Adeyemi delivered performances that strengthened thei...
content: Barcelona duo make strong case for bigger role under Flick after impressive performance vs Sabah Barcelona’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Sabah was not a routine win for Hansi Flick. This is because the likes of Alejandro Balde and Karim Adeyemi delivered performances that strengthened their claims for greater involvement, showing the German manager that his squad possesses valuable alternatives during a demanding run of fixtures. With Lamine Yamal unavailable and Raphinha starting on the bench, Flick made several changes to his starting line-up in Azerbaijan. As such, Balde, Adeyemi, Gavi, Jules Kounde and Gabriel Jesus were among those given opportunities to impress, and two players in particular made the most of their minutes. Adeyemi delivers in Lamine Yamal’s absence Adeyemi was one of Barcelona’s most influential attacking players , combining direct running with effective pressing and movement. Karim Adeyemi was unstoppable against Sabah. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) Selected to occupy the position usually associated with Yamal, the German winger showed that Barcelona can maintain their attacking threat without relying exclusively on their teenage star. Apart from the brilliant goal he scored from Balde’s cross, Adeyemi also helped initiate the move for Anthony Gordon’s opener, provided the assist for Barcelona’s second and then finished the third himself, which strengthens his case for a more prominent role under Flick. Balde brings attacking quality back to Barcelona Furthermore, Balde also used the opportunity to show why he remains an important option on the left flank. After limited playing time earlier in the season, the defender brought greater energy and attacking intent to Barcelona’s build-up. His intelligent forward passes helped create opportunities for Gordon, while his outstanding low delivery for Adeyemi’s goal showed the quality he can provide in the final third. Alejandro Balde delivered an assist for Karim Adeyemi’s goal. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) The injury that forced Balde off was an unfortunate setback, particularly after such an encouraging performance. Barcelona will now need to assess his condition before determining when he can return. Flick gains valuable options before demanding fixtures Barcelona’s slow start against Sabah was indeed a concern, with the home side hitting the post before the visitors established control. However, the attacking contributions of Adeyemi and Balde, among others, helped Flick’s team recover. The result also improved Barcelona’s goal difference in the Champions League, which will be an important consideration in the league phase. Now, with Manchester City, Como and Sporting CP approaching in the Champions League next, Flick will need contributions from across his squad, and it is encouraging to see Adeyemi and Balde have provided compelling evidence that they deserve more opportunities.

content: FC Barcelona filed a pre-trial conciliation request following Florentino Pérez’s comments about the Negreira case in May, giving him a chance to retract them. Because Pérez refused to withdraw his remarks, Barcelona “will continue to defend its interests,” said club president Joan Laporta. Pérez said the case is an “unprecedented case of corruption” and the “biggest scandal in history.” A report from The Athletic mentions that Barcelona will also file a case against Florentino Pérez because of those quotes. “We consider we have to defend Barça’s interests when barbarities like that are said around, and especially coming from the biggest representative of another football club. I saw that in Madrid’s general assembly they kept talking about Barça in the same terms. They are obsessed with talking about Barça. In the end we will end up asking them for royalties, because they are boosting their image thanks to Barça,” said Laporta.

title: Barcelona hopeful 23-year-old star’s ankle injury is not serious after Sabah scare – report
summary: Barcelona are hopeful Alejandro Balde has avoided a serious injury after the left-back was forced off during Wednesday’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Sabah in Baku. According to SPORT, the ini...
content: Barcelona hopeful 23-year-old star’s ankle injury is not serious after Sabah scare – report Barcelona are hopeful Alejandro Balde has avoided a serious injury after the left-back was forced off during Wednesday’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Sabah in Baku . According to SPORT , the initial outlook is encouraging, although the club is still waiting for medical tests to establish the extent of the problem. The injury came on a night that had offered Balde a significant opportunity to reassert himself. Making his first start of the season, the defender produced one of Barcelona’s strongest individual performances before an ankle problem cut his appearance short. Balde makes his opportunity count in Baku Balde had endured a frustrating period with limited minutes this season, making his return to Hansi Flick’s starting line-up particularly important. He responded with an energetic display on the left, providing Barcelona with width and attacking penetration. Alejandro Balde injured his ankle against Sabah. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) His contribution was most evident in the move that led to Karim Adeyemi’s goal. Balde advanced down the flank and delivered a low ball into the area, allowing the German forward to finish from close range. Ankle inflammation raises concern, but early outlook is positive Balde was unable to continue after suffering a heavy twist to his ankle . The resulting inflammation affected his ability to accelerate, prompting him to request a substitution rather than risk aggravating the problem. Building on that, the aforementioned outlet confirms Barcelona feel the injury is not serious, although an ankle sprain remains a possibility. Notably, the club’s medical staff still need the inflammation to settle before they can make a more precise assessment. Furthermore, Hansi Flick also acknowledged after the match that the extent of the injury was not yet known. Alejandro Balde made his first start of the season yesterday. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) The defender is now expected to undergo examinations on Thursday, November 26, with those tests intended to establish both the diagnosis and a potential recovery timeline. Medical tests will determine Balde’s next step The timing is unfortunate for Balde, who had finally been given a starting opportunity after falling behind in the competition for minutes. His performance offered a positive reminder of his skills, although one strong display will not automatically settle his place in Flick’s plans. The current priority is to understand whether the ankle issue is a minor setback or something that requires a period of rehabilitation. For now, Barcelona have reason to be cautiously optimistic, but no confirmed diagnosis or return date should be assumed until the medical examination is complete.

title: Barcelona may have found their defensive answers in La Masia starlet – report
summary: Barcelona extended their winning run to five matches in all competitions following a 4-1 win over Sabah in the UEFA Champions League.Apart from the stellar attacking display, a key highlight of the ni...
content: Barcelona may have found their defensive answers in La Masia starlet – report Barcelona extended their winning run to five matches in all competitions following a 4-1 win over Sabah in the UEFA Champions League. Apart from the stellar attacking display, a key highlight of the night was the debut of La Masia starlet Alex Campos. The young defender came in as a 64th minute replacement for Frenkie de Jong and had a solid enough outing. An answer to Barcelona’s defensive problems? Alex Campos made his debut against Sabah. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) It is no secret that Barcelona are struggling defensively. Even Hansi Flick looked visibly frustrated after the team conceded a goal against Sabah. The team simply lacks enough depth in central defence. But as reported by Diario SPORT , Flick may have found his answer in the form of Campos. With Andreas Christensen still struggling with injuries, Pau Cubarsi carrying a knock and the likes of Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde often required elsewhere, Barcelona have been crying out for a reliable centre-back. De Jong has done well to chip in, but he is not a natural in this position, leaving Flick with Gerard Martin as the only other option. Campos’ cameo in Baku may prove to be a first step towards him becoming a real alternative for Barcelona. The report frames the youngster as a potential example of Barcleona solving the defensive problem from within. The Catalans have a solid track record of doing so, having previously solved multiple problems for giving chances to academy players such as Marc Casado, Marc Bernal, Fermin Lopez and Cubarsi himself. What does Campos bring to the table? Campos is rated highly by Bojan. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As far as his profile is concerned, Campos is quite similar to Cubarsi. Originally a midfielder before Barcelona converted him into a central defender, Campos’ natural qualities include playing out from the back and the ability to join attacks. He is also a genuine threat from set-pieces and is very efficient on the ball. Under Juliano Belletti, however, his defensive game has improved enormously and he is now regarded as a solid, reliable operator in central defence. Campos is also quite versatile, as he can perform both as a left and a right sided centre-back. He is comfortable filling in as a holding midfielder as well. Perhaps more importantly, Campos rarely loses his composure. He is already held in high regard by the likes of Bojan Krkic and Belletti and it will be interesting to see if he is used more often by Flick in the coming weeks.

title: Barella praises Bellingham: “He’s my favorite player right now”
summary: Inter Milan midfielder Nico Barella praised Jude Bellingham during an interview ahead of Inter’s match against Stuttgart, which ended with the Italian team earning a 2-0 victory. “Jude Bellingham is good at everything he does, he is a very complete midfielder. He is very good when you watch him, but when you play against him, […]
content: Inter Milan midfielder Nico Barella praised Jude Bellingham during an interview ahead of Inter’s match against Stuttgart, which ended with the Italian team earning a 2-0 victory. “Jude Bellingham is good at everything he does, he is a very complete midfielder. He is very good when you watch him, but when you play against him, you fully realize how amazing he is. He is my favorite player right now,” said Barella. Barella was rumored to be on Real Madrid’s radar a few years ago, when Los Blancos were scouting the market for a Toni Kroos replacement. However, it’s clear that he’s now a crucial player for Inter, so he will likely play there most of his prime.

title: Bayern Munich handed Michael Olise injury boost

content: Bayern Munich handed Michael Olise injury boost Bayern Munich have received a welcome boost on the injury front, with Bild reporting that Michael Olise has resumed running training. The Frenchman suffered a bruised foot in Friday's 1-1 draw with 1. FC Köln and subsequently missed Wednesday's 2-1 defeat to LOSC Lille in the Champions League. With Bayern dealing with several injury problems in attack, the German champions will be hoping to welcome the influential winger back as soon as possible. However, it's currently unclear if Olise will be fit in time for Saturday's Bundesliga clash with Hamburger SV. In addition to Olise, Manuel Neuer, Alphonso Davies, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari also missed Wednesday's game. Neuer, Kane and Saibari are all set to remain sidelined long term.

title: Bolton Wanderers 1-3 West Bromwich Albion - fans' verdict
summary: Here are your thoughts after West Bromwich Albion won 3-1 at Bolton Wanderers on Wednesday to close the gap at the top of the Championship.
content: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after West Bromwich Albion won 3-1 at Bolton Wanderers on Wednesday to close the gap at the top of the Championship. Here are some of your comments: Trotters fans Andrew: We are going to struggle but we are always there, so no need to panic just yet. David : Lack of class at this level plus individual errors and naivety are killing us. We need to learn quickly or it's going to be a long winter. Jordan : Bolton are far too passive, sitting deep and waiting to be punished. It's starting to feel like the manager isn't capable of getting the best out of our team. Poor decisions almost every game around the starting 11 means we're almost always having to chase a game, especially at home, leaving us wide open to attack and getting punished further. We have a decent squad but need to use it better. Albion fans Nathan : Football is a funny old game at times, I thought we dominated the first half, although we only had one goal to show for all the possession. The second half Bolton were a lot better and I was worried that they were more likely to score a winner. Good teams always find a way to win so I'm glad we were able to!

title: Burnley 0-2 Birmingham City - fans' verdict
summary: Here are your thoughts after Birmingham City won 2-0 at Burnley on Wednesday to close the gap at the top of the Championship.
content: [BBC] We asked for your thoughts after Birmingham City won 2-0 at Burnley on Wednesday to make it an EFL record 24 home games without a win for the Clarets while Blues closed the gap at the top of the Championship. Here are some of your comments: Clarets fans Lynne: Tragic. No desire to push forward or take responsibility in front of goal. The fans are despondent as are the players. It's so sad to watch. Brian : The worst performance ever. Many will not renew season tickets until Pace has gone. Steve : Going backwards. Losing possession has been a problem all season, as has schoolboy defending. We are so so slow building attacks it's ridiculous. It's like we allow any team to get back in shape before we attack. Kyle Walker has been terrible and even Amdouni, who has been loved by the fans, has had stinkers in the last two games. I can see us going down again and the owners have created all this. They should resign as a board and sell up and go back to the US. Darren : Woeful, no fight in any of them. We are staring at League One football without a doubt. Mark : We were shocking. Our defence is about as useful as a chocolate fireguard. Vardy should have started, he'd have gotten on the end of Ramazani's crosses and balls into the box. It was a very lacklustre performance. On these performances we're down. Blues fans Phil : A routine win against a very poor team. In Blues' favour it's not the easiest place to visit on a cold winter evening. Gary : Good start but some sloppy play meant we needed Beadle to be on top form. Fry and Neumann excellent, Klarer has a rival for his place now, some puzzling substitutions from Davies. David : It's wins like this that win Championships and promotions. They build confidence which is so important. Daniel : Very professional performance, could have been more comfortable. Burnley had very good possession but no end product. Looking forward to upcoming games, real battle at the top now, bring it on. John : This win looks good but we could easily have lost if Burnley had taken their chances. In my opinion we were quite lucky in some ways.

title: "There are certainly options" – Eberl keeps door open to January transfers at Bayern
summary: Bayern Munich's injury problems came into sharp focus on Wednesday as a depleted side suffered a 2-1 defeat to LOSC Lille in the Champions League, bringing their unbeaten start to the season to an end...
content: "There are certainly options" – Eberl keeps door open to January transfers at Bayern Bayern Munich's injury problems came into sharp focus on Wednesday as a depleted side suffered a 2-1 defeat to LOSC Lille in the Champions League, bringing their unbeaten start to the season to an end. With key players such as Harry Kane, Michael Olise and Alphonso Davies sidelined, the defeat only added to the growing speculation over whether Bayern might strengthen their squad in January. Speaking to DAZN after the game, board member for sport Max Eberl left the door open to new signings, while stressing that any potential arrival would have to be a “perfect fit”. "We'll take a look at it. First and foremost, what's important is what the squad looks like in January," Eberl said. He stressed that the club will not “rush into anything” and instead assess the situation calmly. "There are certainly options, but whatever we do would have to be a perfect fit," Eberl added. Speaking before the game, Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund pointed out that, with several players, including Michael Olise and Alphonso Davies, expected to return in a not too distant future, there's currently no intention to make any additions to the squad in January. "That's why making signings isn't our plan at the moment. We hope the situation will look different again soon and that we can collect plenty of points with the players we already have," Freund said.

title: Champions League power rankings: Real Madrid surge – while rivals hit by injuries
summary: Real Madrid remain the lone team with an 100 per cent record, while only PSG and Arsenal are now also unbeaten after a shock loss for Bayern Munich
content: Real Madrid will head to Arsenal in matchweek six of the Champions League with the only 100 per cent record remaining in the competition after Jose Mourinho’s side made it five wins from from five this season. The 15-time winners have found form just as a couple of their main rivals have been dealt major injury blows, too, with Bayern Munich ’s Harry Kane suffering an ankle injury and Paris Saint-Germain losing Desire Doue to an ACL injury, adding to the absence of Khvicha Kvaratskhelia. It means that will back-to-back winners PSG remain top of our standings, the competition is looking rather open underneath them – as the league phase table begins to take shape and the fight for the top-eight and play-off places intensifies. We compiled our 36-team power rankings by combining team’s previous performance in the Champions League, their results in the competition so far, and the likelihood of them going all the way this season. Agree or disagree with our standings after matchweek five? Let us know and have your say in the comments below. ↔️ 1. Paris Saint-Germain Results: 6-1 vs Slovan Bratislava, 4-2 v Man City, 4-2 v Barcelona, 6-0 v Villarreal, 2-2 v Roma Fixtures: Aston Villa (a), Como (a), Galatasaray (h) Luis Enrique’s back-to-back champions have seen their star-studded attack devastated by the injuries to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue, who are both likely to be out for the rest of the season due to ACL issues. While Ousmane Dembele remains, as well as a brilliant midfield three, Enrique will have his work cut out if PSG are to remain as dangerous and retain their title this season. They dropped points for the first time in the Champions League this season as Roma secured a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes. Dembele will be without Kvaratskhelia and Doue for the rest of the season (Reuters) ↔️ 2. Barcelona Results: 5-1 v Feyenoord, 4-1 v Galatasaray, 2-4 v PSG, 3-0 v Aston Villa, 4-1 v Sabah Fixtures: Manchester City (h), Sporting (a), Como (h) Even with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha rested, the goals kept flying and a double from Anthony Gordon in the 4-1 win over Sabah made it 69 goals in 18 games in all competitions this season from Hansi Flick’s side. The LaLiga champions are well placed to finish the league phase as one of the top seeds for the knockout stages, but the big question remains how their defence will stand up against one of the top teams. Conceding four in defeat against PSG means there is still much to prove. Gordon scored twice for Barcelona against Sabah (Reuters) ↔️ 3. Arsenal Results: 1-0 vs Napoli, 3-0 v Lille, 2-2 v Bayern Munich, 2-1 v Slavia Prague, 1-1 v Borussia Dortmund Fixtures: Real Madrid (h), Real Betis (a), Sabah (h) The arrival of winter is perhaps leading to some frustration, particularly in front of goal . Arsenal remain unbeaten but they were punished for not taking their opportunities as they dropped points at home to Borussia Dortmund, a result which means their place in the top-eight is not assured yet ahead of tough games against Real Madrid and Real Betis. Viktor Gyokeres was on target against Dortmund but Arsenal dropped points (Getty) ⬆️🟢 4. Real Madrid (+2 from 6) Results: 2-1 v Inter Milan, 4-3 v Roma, 4-1 v RB Leipzig, 3-2 v AEK Athens, 5-1 v PSV Fixtures: Arsenal (a), LASK (h), Shakhtar (a) Real Madrid have come into a remarkable run of form, with a thumping win over PSV making it 10 wins in a row in all competitions under Jose Mourinho. It’s funny, in the Champions League, Real Madrid have trailed several games yet have maximum points. Now, the 15-time Champions League winners are not just managing to find a way, but they are blowing teams off the park. Jude Bellingham scored a brilliant volley in their big win over PSV (Getty) ⬆️🟢 5. Liverpool (+2 from 7) Results: 2-1 v Atletico Madrid, 6-3 v LASK, 4-3 v Villarreal, 2-3 v Fenerbahce, 3-0 Club Brugge Fixtures: Porto (h), Inter (a), Lens (h) Before Andoni Iraola’s first season, it felt like so much depended on the potential of Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz coming good in the Liverpool attack. Well, the signs of the past few weeks have been hugely promising as Isak and Wirtz continued to build their partnership in the 3-0 win at Club Brugge, with the Reds bouncing back from their shock defeat at Fenerbahce last time out. Florian Wirtz got on the scoresheet again in Belgium (Getty) ⬇️🔴 6. Bayern Munich (-2 from 4) Results: 5-0 v Bodo/Glimt, 3-3 v Viking, 2-2 v Arsenal, 2-0 v Atletico Madrid, 1-2 v Lille Fixtures: Slavia Prague (h), Manchester United (a), Real Betis (h) The major concern for the German champions is the fitness of their Ballon d’Or holder Harry Kane, who will now be out until the “business end” of the season due to an ankle injury. Bayern have plenty of games to play until then and the question is whether they can get through to the top eight without Kane to avoid an additional play-off round. A stunning 2-1 defeat at Lille, which featured some calamitous defending and a truly remarkable Aleksandar Pavlovic own goal (honestly, go and check it out ...), saw Bayern drop to 15th in the table. Kane will be out until the knockout stages of the Champions League (Getty) ⬇️🔴 7. Man City (-2 from 5) Results: 2-0 v Porto, 2-4 v PSG, 5-1 v AEK Athens, 3-2 v Leipzig, 2-2 v Napoli Fixtures: Barcelona (a), Lens (a), Sporting (a) Three defeats from four in the Premier League have well and truly taken shine off an impressive start for Enzo Maresca’s side, while uncertainty off the pitch remains as well . After another sloppy performance against Napoli and the returning Kevin De Bruyne means it is now 10 games in a row without a clean sheet. City now face a mouthwatering trip to Barcelona and likely require a result to avoid dropping out of the top eight. Manchester City drew 2-2 with Napoli (PA) ⬆️🟢 8. Como (+2 from 10) Results: 4-1 v RB Leipzig, 2-3 v Feyenoord, 4-1 v Manchester United, 9-1 v Lens, 1-0 v AEK Athens Fixtures: Real Betis (a), Paris Saint Germain (h), Barcelona (a) Up at the top of the table with the likes of Real Madrid, PSG and Barcelona, the Champions League debutants are certainly making a name for themselves. Cesc Fabregas’s stylish side didn’t quite hit the same heights against AEK Athens after their nine-goal dismantling of poor Lens, but look what comes next. Those games against PSG and Barcelona at the end of the league phase, after a tricky trip to Real Betis, are going to be fascinating. Como have four wins from their first five Champions League games, scoring 20 goals (Getty) ↔️ 9. Inter Milan Results: 1-2 v Real Madrid, 3-4 v Club Brugge, 1-0 v Shakhtar, 3-0 v Feyenoord, 2-0 v Stuttgart Fixtures: Borussia Dortmund (a), Liverpool (h), Slovan Bratislava (a) After starting with back-to-back defeats, Inter have responded with three consecutive wins. There was more good news in the 2-0 win over Stuttgart as Lautaro Martinez marked his return from injury after a month on the sidelines with a goal. Lautaro Martinez celebrated his return from injury (Getty) ⬆️🟢 10. Roma (+5 from 15) Results: 1-1 v Fenerbahce, 3-4 v Real Madrid, 4-0 v Slovan Bratislava, 2-3 v Manchester United, 2-2 v Paris-Saint Germain Fixtures: Sporting (h), AEK Athens (a), Lille (h) Sure, they absolutely bottled it against Real Madrid and Manchester United, throwing away leads on both occasions. Sure, they’ve got five points from five games in the Champions League and sit outside the top 24 in the league table. But a 2-2 draw at Paris Saint-Germain continued Roma’s impressive season under Gian Piero Gasperini; they remain unbeaten in Serie A and now have a more favourable run of games in the Champions League. On performances alone, they’ve earned a place in our top 10. Donyell Malen scored Roma’s equaliser in Paris (Reuters) ↔️ 11 . Atletico Madrid ↔️ 12. Borussia Dortmund ↔️ 13. Real Betis ⬇️ 🔴 14. Aston Villa (-6) ⬇️ 🔴 15. Manchester United (-1) ↔️ 16. Sporting ⬆️ 🟢 17. Galatasaray (+2) ⬇️ 🔴 18. Stuttgart (-1) ⬇️ 🔴 19. Club Brugge (-1) ↔️ 20. Napoli ⬆️ 🟢 21. Fenerbahce (+3) ⬇️ 🔴 22. Villarreal (-1) ⬇️ 🔴 23. RB Leipzig (-1) ⬇️ 🔴 24. Bodo/Glimt (-1) ↔️ 25. Porto ↔️ 26. PSV Eindhoven ↔️ 27. Shakhtar Donetsk ⬆️ 🟢 28. LASK (+1) ⬆️ 🟢 29. Viking (+1) ⬆️ 🟢 30. Lille (+3) ⬇️ 🔴 31. content: Champions League Team of the Week includes Hermoso, Barella and Milla There are three Serie A players in the UEFA Champions League Team of the Week, as Roma’s Mario Hermoso, Nicolò Barella at Inter and Como midfielder Luis Milla made it into the ideal XI. Every week, UEFA’s panel of experts evaluate each game and pick the best performing players for their Team of the Week. There is plenty of Serie A representation this time around, including two players who got on the scoresheet. PARIS, FRANCE – NOVEMBER 25: Mario Hermoso of AS Roma is put under pressure from Maghnes Akliouche of Paris Saint-Germain during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Paris Saint-Germain and AS Roma at Parc des Princes on November 25, 2026 in Paris, France. (Photo by Franco Arland/Getty Images) Roma defender Hermoso opened the scoring at Parc des Princes for an exciting 2-2 draw against Paris Saint-Germain , ending the reigning trophy holders’ 100 per cent record. However, the panel explains he was also chosen for “dominating his duels and making 11 recoveries” against the notorious PSG strikers. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Inter midfielder Barella was included for his performance in the 2-0 victory over VfB Stuttgart, even though the goals were scored by Petar Sucic and Lautaro Martinez.
