title: Chelsea forward wanted by European giants
summary: Chelsea Hold Firm on Estêvão as PSG Weigh January Transfer Window MoveChelsea are understood to have no intention of letting Estêvão leave, despite fresh interest from Paris Saint-Germain ahead of...
content: Chelsea forward wanted by European giants Chelsea Hold Firm on Estêvão as PSG Weigh January Transfer Window Move Chelsea are understood to have no intention of letting Estêvão leave, despite fresh interest from Paris Saint-Germain ahead of the January transfer window. The latest reports suggest the European champions are reviewing attacking targets after a damaging injury setback, with Estêvão now firmly in the frame. According to Caught Offside, PSG are assessing their options after Désiré Doué and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia both suffered serious knee injuries. That situation has forced a rethink in Paris, and Chelsea’s young Brazilian has emerged as one of the names under consideration. Photo IMAGO PSG interest puts Estêvão in focus The report states that “PSG have included Estêvão on their shortlist alongside Bayern Munich winger Luis Díaz and RB Leipzig’s Antonio Nusa.” It also adds that “Luis Enrique is reluctant to rush into the transfer market and wants to assess his existing attacking options before making a final decision.” Even so, there appears to have been early contact. Another key line in the report says PSG “contacted Chelsea regarding Estêvão’s availability, only for the west London club to quickly dismiss the possibility of a deal.” That is a significant detail. It indicates Chelsea’s position is clear, at least for now, and there is no appetite at Stamford Bridge to entertain offers. Chelsea stance on Estêvão reflects long-term plan This feels like a straightforward situation in one sense. Chelsea rate the player highly, PSG admire him, and the selling club are resisting. Estêvão is still only 19, and while “his opportunities to play regular football have been limited”, there is evidently a belief internally that his pathway should remain in west London. The reasoning is easy to follow. Chelsea invested in him because of his ceiling, and the source makes that case strongly, describing his “enormous potential, exceptional dribbling ability and creativity in the final third”. Those are attributes clubs at the top of the European game monitor very closely, especially when the player is already attracting this level of attention. Regular minutes now look crucial for Chelsea winger There is also a wider point here for Chelsea. It is one thing to reject interest, it is another to create the right conditions for development. The report argues that “Selling Estêvão at this stage of his career would be incredibly short-sighted,” and it is difficult to disagree. It goes further, adding that “Giving the Brazilian greater responsibility and consistent playing time could prove far more rewarding than any substantial transfer offer from Paris.” That may be the central issue in the months ahead. Chelsea are right to protect a major talent, but PSG’s move is a reminder that elite clubs are watching closely. If Estêvão is part of the future, Chelsea now need to show it with meaningful opportunities. Our View This is the kind of report that immediately creates anxiety because it touches a nerve. Chelsea have collected elite young talent for years, but there has to be a point where potential turns into trust. If PSG are already looking at Estêvão this seriously, then everybody in football can see what Chelsea have on their hands. The fear is whether Chelsea will handle him properly. Rejecting an approach is the easy part. The hard part is giving him a genuine route into the side, especially when attacking selections can become crowded and short-term pressure often drives decisions. If he stays on the margins, this story will not go away. It will grow. Other clubs will keep asking the same question, and sooner or later the player may ask it too. There is also a nagging concern that Chelsea sometimes speak like a club building for the future while acting like a club chasing immediate fixes. Estêvão should not become another case of waiting, watching and wondering when his moment will come. If he is as special as this report suggests, then he needs proper minutes, proper responsibility and proper backing. Watching a talent of this level become a star somewhere else after being stockpiled would be maddening. Chelsea cannot afford to treat him as a luxury asset. He has to be developed with conviction. Otherwise, interest from PSG today could become a real problem tomorrow. Source: Caught Offside

title: Christian Pulisic, Antoine Griezmann and Emma Hayes’ USWNT: Why American soccer fans have plenty to celebrate this Thanksgiving
summary: GOAL breaks down what you should be thankful for during this holiday season.
content: Thanksgiving 2026 GFX - GOAL GOAL breaks down what you should be thankful for during this holiday season. It's Thanksgiving, and we all know what that means. Turkey, gravy, mashed potatoes, stuffing - all on the menu. There's plenty to be thankful for, but that doesn't just extend to food; it extends to soccer, too. Obviously, there are more important things in life to give thanks for at this time of year, but it is also worth acknowledging the sport's role in everyday life. For some, it's an obsession. For others, it's a distraction. But, if you're reading this story, it's safe to assume that you're glad that soccer is a part of your life in some way. So, with that in mind, let's sit down, put down the fork for a moment and give thanks for all of the good things about American soccer and, just as crucially, all of the things worth being excited for on the horizon, too. The 2026 World Cup Spain helped make the 2026 World Cup a summer to remember as fans from across the globe came together in America. Yeah, it's over now, but what a ride it was! For one summer, soccer came stateside and, for one summer, America was at the forefront of the beautiful game. The scenes were unforgettable: the games, the pageantry, the fans sweeping through cities. Scotland in Boston, Algeria in Kansas, Norway's Viking Row taking over Times Square - it was a wonderfully unifying experience, one that saw fans from all over the world experience American hospitality. It also saw Americans experience a taste of the unknown as they learned about those who had arrived for a summer of fun. From a USMNT perspective, yes, the ending was rough, but the road there was full of highs. The wins over Paraguay and Australia were unlike anything the world had seen from an American team. The Turkey game, despite the defeat, had several feel-good moments. Even the Bosnia and Herzegovina game that began the downturn was full of both grit and talent that inspired onlookers all over the world. So, before we turn the page, a toast to the 2026 World Cup and a thank you to all who made it special. Copa America, Olympics and Women's World Cup on the way More tournaments will soon be arriving on American shores. And, if you liked the World Cup experience, get ready for more, because there's more coming. Just this week, it was confirmed that both the 2031 Women's World Cup and 2028 Copa America will be coming to the U.S., bringing two more major tournaments stateside. You can also tack on the 2028 Olympics, too, giving fans another huge competition worth being excited to watch for both the men's and women's sides. For years, many looked at the 2026 World Cup as the pinnacle, the end of one era of American soccer. It turns out that wasn't the case; it was a huge, huge part, yes, but it was merely the latest step on a journey that, thankfully, includes plenty of big games stateside. American stars in big places For big names to keep that recognition, they need to put themselves on the biggest stages. We've seen plenty of that from American players on both the men's and women's side. With the men, there are a total of 23 players in either the Champions League, Europa League, or Conference League. You can turn on your TV and see Christian Pulisic scoring for Milan, Tyler Adams helping Bournemouth win game after game, or Alex Freeman going toe-to-toe with Barcelona. It's become normalized in recent years, but for those of a certain age, the idea of Americans playing at that level is preposterous. Now, it's everyday. The women have always been held to that standard, and many of the familiar faces continue to keep it. Trinity Rodman remains the face of the NWSL, having signed on to be exactly that. Mallory Swanson and Sophia Wilson are back, while the Gotham FC crew routinely raises the bar. All the while, captain Lindsey Heaps is now stateside after a long European adventure. American soccer has always had stars, but there's more star power than ever before at the top of the American game. The next generation While those stars continue to do what they've been doing, there's a new generation coming up behind them that looks like it could be pretty damn good. On the women's side, there's always been a steady stream of talent, and that doesn't seem to be stopping. At just 19, Lily Yohannes is already a seasoned veteran, as is 20-year-old Claire Hutton. The Thompson sisters continue to grow into players that could dominate in their respective positions. You have players like Jaedyn Shaw, Olivia Moultrie, Riley Jackson and Jordyn Bugg who have been in and around the team. Meanwhile, the aforementioned Rodman is just 24 and has hopefully put her injury issues behind her. USWNT manager Emma Hayes is spoiled for choice, and more choices are on the way. The men have names like Cavan Sullivan, Mathis Albert and Julian Hall already contributing for club and country. After so much talk of a "Golden Generation", it appears that the 2022-26 World Cup teams may just be "the Initial Generation", one that has another crop of stars coming up behind them. We've already seen the generations blend a bit in USMNT camp, but it's just the beginning. So it seems the good news is that this isn't ending soon. There's no doom and gloom for the USMNT or USWNT, as both seem to have the stars of the next decade already lined up. International additions For fans of the domestic league, local homegrowns are always nice, but it's also great to have some star power, and both MLS and the NWSL continue to add that. Antoine Griezmann, Robert Lewandowski, Sam Kerr, and Guro Reiten all came from huge European teams this summer. They join leagues that already feature names like Lionel Messi, Son Heung-min and Temwa Chawinga. Their presence allows American fans the opportunity to see some of the world's best players up close and, let's be honest, that's a whole lot different than watching from your couch. How many kids can the names above inspire? How many fans are watching just because they're here? Growing the game means drawing in fans in as many ways as you can and, for many, the presence of big names remains the driver of American soccer's growth. Soccer on TV It often goes overlooked, but it is worth being thankful for it sometimes, too, because the truth is, there may not be a better country to watch soccer in than the U.S. No matter the time of day, there's likely soccer available somewhere and, while you'll need to pay for a streaming service or two, soccer is more accessible in the U.S. than anywhere else. There are no 3 p.m. blackouts or laws preventing the showing of soccer; it's on all the time, broadcast from all over the world. Meanwhile, leagues all over the world continue to cater to an American audience. Everyone wants a piece of the American pie, and that isn't slowing down any time soon. That means more games, more coverage, and, ultimately, more soccer. How could you not be thankful about that?

title: Confirmed: Barcelona star Anthony Gordon named UEFA Champions League Player of the Week
summary: Following his exploits in the team’s 4-1 win over Sabah, Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon has been named the UEFA Champions League Player of the Week for Matchday 5 of the league phase.Starting on th...
content: Confirmed: Barcelona star Anthony Gordon named UEFA Champions League Player of the Week Following his exploits in the team’s 4-1 win over Sabah, Barcelona winger Anthony Gordon has been named the UEFA Champions League Player of the Week for Matchday 5 of the league phase. Starting on the left flank in the away fixture in Baku on Wednesday night, the England international was the driving force behind the Catalans’ comfortable victory. Indeed, Gordon found the back of the net on two occasions on the night in Azerbaijan, giving the Blaugrana the lead in the 31st minute in the first half before adding another one six minutes into the second period. Apart from scoring two goals, the 25-year-old attacker caused problems to the home team’s defence for most of the game, justifying manager Hansi Flick’s decision to start him on the night. As such, Gordon has now been voted the UEFA Champions League Player of the Week for Matchday 5 in the league phase. The Barcelona summer signing saw off competition from Cucho Hernandez of Real Betis, Antonio Nusa of RB Leipzig, and Real Madrid superstar Kylian Mbappe, who finished second, third, and fourth, respectively. Apart from being named the Player of the Week, Gordon also makes it to the Champions League Team of the Week for Matchday 5. Since arriving at Barcelona in the summer, the 25-year-old has made a solid start , scoring and assisting five goals apiece from 17 matches across all competitions. Involved in a competition for a starting spot on the left flank with Karim Adeyemi, Gordon has been Flick’s preferred option and his performance against Sabah further strengthened his credentials.

title: 'I didn't sleep for 10 days' - AC Milan icon Filippo Inzaghi relives 2007 Champions League glory in Athens and urges Rossoneri to show 'personality' against Olympiacos
summary: AC Milan have returned to the scene of one of their most famous triumphs as they prepare for a high-stakes Europa League encounter in the Greek capital. Club legend Filippo Inzaghi has marked the occasion by reflecting on the magical night in 2007 when his brace secured European glory against Liverpool.
content: FBL-EUR-C1-LIVERPOOL-ACMILAN - AFP AC Milan have returned to the scene of one of their most famous triumphs as they prepare for a high-stakes Europa League encounter in the Greek capital. Club legend Filippo Inzaghi has marked the occasion by reflecting on the magical night in 2007 when his brace secured European glory against Liverpool. Returning to the scene of the crime As the current AC Milan squad touches down in Athens for a pivotal continental fixture, the memories of the club's 2007 Champions League triumph loom large. Inzaghi, the man whose goalscoring instincts defined that era, has opened up about the emotional weight of returning to the city where he reached the pinnacle of club football. The Rossoneri are currently in a precarious position in the Europa League, sitting on just three points after four games, while their upcoming opponents Olympiacos remain undefeated with 10 points . 'I had one of the greatest nights of my career in Athens. It's a city I associate with special memories and, for that reason, it will always hold a special place in my heart,' Inzaghi told La Gazzetta dello Sport . The 10-day insomnia of a champion The 2007 final carried immense significance for Milan, who were seeking redemption after their heartbreaking defeat to Liverpool in the 2005 Champions League final. On that occasion, Milan had raced into a 3-0 half-time lead, only for Liverpool to stage a remarkable comeback in Istanbul before winning on penalties. Recalling his memories ahead of the 2007 showpiece, Inzaghi said: 'I remember the wait for the game; I knew how important that final was and I felt that it could be a special evening.' During the match itself, he identified the second goal as his favourite moment, adding: 'The second goal the best, the moment I realised the trophy was really close.' The intensity of the occasion was so profound that Inzaghi struggled to process the reality of his achievement long after the celebrations had subsided. 'I didn't sleep for 10 days; I woke up in the middle of the night thinking that the final and my goals had been a dream,' the former Italy international revealed. Comparing World Cup and Champions League glory Having tasted success both with his club and the Italian national team, Inzaghi had also lifted the World Cup with Italy in 2006, the Azzurri's most recent triumph on the global stage. The striker played his part in that campaign, scoring a goal in Italy's group-stage victory over the Czech Republic. These achievements often lead to questions about which success carries more weight for him. 'Those are two different memories, because both enriched my football career. A World Cup victory is the highest honour for any footballer. Athens, however, had a special meaning for Milan's history. We came off a disappointing final, which I watched from the stands, but this time around I was on the pitch and able to contribute to the victory. Fate gave me a second chance and it went the way we now know it did. However, I can't rank those two glorious nights because those achievements each mean something different to me,' Inzaghi explained. A message to the modern Rossoneri Transitioning from his personal nostalgia to Milan's current challenges, Inzaghi has issued a rallying cry to the squad ahead of their match at the Georgios Karaiskakis Stadium. Milan currently sit 28th in the Europa League standings, outside the qualifying places for the next round, making victory in today's encounter crucial if they are to revive their hopes of progressing in the competition. 'I spent some extraordinary years at Milan; the bond with the fans was born out of goals and victories, but also from the commitment I always tried to give. Knowing that all this has survived the test of time means an awful lot to me. I hope they face the match with a lot of personality, and return home enjoying a great European evening. I know how much that shirt matters and how much the fans expect in a game like this. I hope the team can bring them joy and a victory,' Inzaghi concluded.

title: Dominic Calvert-Lewin signs new Leeds deal
summary: The England international has extended his stay with the club until 2029
content: Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new deal, taking his stay with the club until 2029. The England international joined Leeds on a three-year deal after leaving Everton as a free agent in 2025, and has now extended for another two and a half years. He scored 15 goals in all competitions last season and so far has six in this campaign, having rebooted his career following a difficult spell marred by injuries at Everton, and earned a recall to the England squad. Leeds said: “ Leeds United are delighted to announce Dominic Calvert-Lewin has signed a new contract with the club. “The England international has put pen to paper on a two-and-a-half-year deal at Elland Road , keeping him in West Yorkshire until the summer of 2029. “Everyone at Leeds United is thrilled Dominic has signed a new deal and we look forward to seeing him continue to impress in the famous white shirt.” Calvert-Lewin has started all 11 top-flight fixtures of this season and scored in the statement 4-1 victory over Chelsea on Saturday. Leeds currently sit seventh in the Premier League , four points off the Champions League places. He won the Premier League’s Player of the Month Award in December after scoring in six consecutive matches - becoming the first Leeds player to win the award in 24 years. His performances were recognised by Thomas Tuchel , who called him up to international duty for a 1-1 friendly draw with Uruguay in March, and he retained his place the squad for Nations League matches against Spain and Czechia. His latest England appearance was against Spain earlier this month when he stepped off the bench to win his 15th cap in the Three Lions ’ 3-2 win.

title: FIFA confirms personal, business data recently stolen by hackers
summary: FIFA on Thursday confirmed personal and business data has been stolen after its systems were hacked recently.
content: FIFA has confirmed hackers recently accessed its systems and stole personal and business data. File photo by Claudio Thoma/EPA Nov. 26 (UPI) -- FIFA on Thursday confirmed personal and business data has been stolen after its systems were hacked. International soccer's governing body said a "limited set of personal and business information" was stolen in the cyberattack. The data breach did not include documents related to the controversial FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal, the failed sell-off plan by FIFA President Gianni Infantino, the BBC reported . The Handsome Boy Hacking Club, an online group, has claimed responsibility for the attack and posted screenshots last week of FIFA documents. The group says it stole more than 12 gigabytes of data, which include identity and immigration documents, executive information, financial records, and legal documents and internal governance records. "FIFA condemns in the strongest possible terms the unlawful acquisition and publication of information, particularly personal data," FIFA said in a statement. "Such actions constitute a serious and unacceptable violation of privacy and can have significant consequences for the individuals concerned." FIFA personnel reportedly said the hackers impersonated staffers to gain access to its systems and not because of a technical failure. The hack comes three months after FIFA said "there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine FIFA and its President."

title: Former Gunner struggles on Manchester United loan
summary: Former Arsenal academy striker Chido Obi is struggling on loan from Manchester United with Eredivisie side Willem II, with the club considering a January recall.Photo by Linnea Rheborg/Getty ImagesSte...
content: Former Gunner struggles on Manchester United loan Former Arsenal academy striker Chido Obi is struggling on loan from Manchester United with Eredivisie side Willem II, with the club considering a January recall. Photo by Linnea Rheborg/Getty Images Steven Railston reports for the Manchester Evening News that Manchester United will consider recalling Chido Obi from his loan to Willem II in the January transfer window, and suggests the striker’s future “may be away from United”. United were reportedly aware from the outset that Willem II could struggle this season, which is proving the case. They sit rock bottom of the Eredivisie and winless, with only three draws to show for their league campaign. But given there reportedly wasn’t much summer interest in Obi, United still viewed this loan move as a good option at the outset. Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images Academy staff at the club believed they would be setting Obi up to fail by sending him to the English lower leagues, where they felt he would struggle with the physicality. Yet that’s seemingly been the case in the Netherlands as well, with Willem II’s recent caretaker manager Adrie Koster publicly questioning Obi’s defensive work. That’s presumably part of the reason the forward has featured so infrequently, only managing 86 senior minutes on the pitch from the first 11 matches available to him. His only start was for Willem’s reserve team in an u21 fixture. The experience has been a reality check for Obi, with Railston reporting that the player was initially frustrated to be spending the 2025/26 campaign playing youth football with United. Obi evidently felt he was capable of more, but he’s struggling to prove it in his first loan spell this season. Photo via Arsenal.com The former Arsenal striker had a fantastic, record-breaking run with the Arsenal u18s, and that led to an expectation that he was set for greatness in senior football. But even before the player left for Manchester United, there were some questions over whether he was simply benefitting from being so much more physically developed than his peers. Though Obi scored 32 goals in 18 games for Arsenal in the u18 Premier League, he never scored in any of his appearances for the Gunners’ u19s or u21s, and there was a sense that if he couldn’t dominate defenders physically, he didn’t have a backup plan. Photo via Arsenal.com Obi’s return with the United u21s is certainly not bad. He’s scored 19 goals in 40 games across all competitions, though his Premier League 2 goal record has been a bit erratic. Eight of Obi’s 11 Premier League 2 goals came in just three games, netting two against Nottingham Forest in April 2025, two against Wolves in January 2026, and four against Leicester City in February 2026. Meanwhile, Obi has failed to score in 16 of his 22 games in the competition, as well as blanking in his eight senior appearances for United and his seven senior appearances for Willem II. There remains some evidence that the young striker requires the right opponent to help him shine. At least for now. Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

title: 'He's lost a little bit of confidence' - Peter Schmeichel highlights 'sad truth' behind Senne Lammens' Man Utd struggles after Sporting errors
summary: Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel has offered a blunt assessment of Senne Lammens' current form following a difficult night for the goalkeeper in the Champions League. While the 24-year-old showcased his shot-stopping ability with a penalty save, a series of costly errors allowed Sporting to fight back and claim a 2-2 draw in Lisbon.
content: Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel has offered a blunt assessment of Senne Lammens' current form following a difficult night for the goalkeeper in the Champions League. While the 24-year-old showcased his shot-stopping ability with a penalty save, a series of costly errors allowed Sporting to fight back and claim a 2-2 draw in Lisbon. Costly errors overshadow Lammens' penalty heroics Lammens endured a difficult European outing against Sporting as two unforced errors undermined a promising start. After denying Colombian forward Luis Suarez from the penalty spot in the first half, the Belgian keeper quickly conceded a foul in the box, allowing Suarez to convert. Matters worsened after the break when Lammens spilled a high delivery into the area. Suarez reacted quickest, finishing acrobatically to earn the Portuguese side a point. Schmeichel points to World Cup hangover and defensive failings Speaking to CBS Sports , former United keeper Schmeichel declined to say if Lammens should be dropped, suggesting new boss Mauricio Pochettino's staff could spark a turnaround. "I don’t know [at what point should Man Utd drop him]," Schmeichel said. "Mauricio Pochettino has come in, he’s brought his own staff, that means he’s got a new goalkeeping coach and maybe that is something that can change it for him." Schmeichel traced the 24-year-old's dip back to Belgium's tournament exit against Spain. He added: "I don’t know if you remember in the World Cup, he came against Spain and made a bit of a mistake, [Mikel] Merino scored and they [Belgium] got knocked out, and I feel like he’s lost a little bit of confidence from that mistake, hasn’t really recovered. "As a goalkeeper when you’re not on your best form you need your defenders in front of you to help you out and the sad truth is that they haven’t been able to do that and of course, that makes it so much worse. I like him a lot but today was not a great day for him." Fernandes demands collective accountability Lammens' shaky start to the term contrasts sharply with his encouraging debut campaign at United following an £18.1 million transfer from Royal Antwerp. Despite his costly lapses in Portugal, club captain Bruno Fernandes defended his team-mate and demanded shared accountability across the squad. "It’s part of football, mistakes are part of football, and from that, you get goals," Fernandes said. "But, obviously, it’s not an individual sport, so everyone has to take the blame for everything we do good and everything we do bad. "I think the main thing and the most important thing is to understand we need to be together, in the good and in the bad moments, and it’s not going to change the belief we have in each other." Pressure mounts on Lammens as Darlow waits in the wings With his confidence dented, Lammens faces a stern test to rediscover his debut-season form under Pochettino's new goalkeeping coach. Summer signing Karl Darlow remains waiting in the wings if a change is required, with the former Newcastle and Leeds United keeper yet to make a Premier League appearance this season.

title: Inter Milan star amazed by Real Madrid’s Jude Bellingham: ‘He’s a complete midfielder’
summary: Speaking to TNT Sports Mexico, Inter Milan midfielder Nicolo Barella has heaped praise on Real Madrid superstar Jude Bellingham, hailing him as a ‘complete midfielder’.The 23-year-old England inte...
content: Inter Milan star amazed by Real Madrid’s Jude Bellingham: ‘He’s a complete midfielder’ Speaking to TNT Sports Mexico , Inter Milan midfielder Nicolo Barella has heaped praise on Real Madrid superstar Jude Bellingham, hailing him as a ‘complete midfielder’. The 23-year-old England international has been in sensational form since the start of the season and has been earning praise from all quarters – teammates, opponents, former players, and pundits alike. Barella joins in Now, it is Barella who has waxed lyrical over Bellingham and his brilliant run of performances for Real Madrid and the England national team. “Jude Bellingham is good at everything. He’s a complete midfielder,” the Italian international said. Barella in awe of Bellingham. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) Continuing, Barella added: “When you watch him play, you realize how good he is, but when you face him on the pitch, you really realize what an exceptional player he is.” Going a step further, the Inter Milan mainstay called the Real Madrid ace his favourite footballer, saying: “He’s my favourite player right now.” Bellingham in a rich vein of form Barella’s praise for Bellingham comes in the aftermath of his spectacular displays for Real Madrid and England. The 23-year-old midfielder has managed to score and assist seven goals in his last seven appearances for club and country, showcasing why he is considered one of the best in the game in his position. In terrific form. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Overall, this season, Bellingham has recorded a tally of seven goals and five assists from 18 matches in all competitions for Real Madrid, which includes his spectacular volleyed strike in the win over PSV Eindhoven earlier in the week. Having endured a difficult last season due to injuries and instability in the team, the England international appears to be back to his best under new manager Jose Mourinho. Given his form and growing stature as one of the leaders of the team, Real Madrid have already begun working on a new long-term contract for Bellingham. The Merengues have recently renewed the contracts of Arda Guler, Aurelien Tchouameni, and Thibaut Courtois, and Bellingham is seen as next in line to pen a new deal, with a verbal agreement reportedly in place already .

title: Jose Mourinho identifies key issue with Real Madrid’s squad players after PSV scare
summary: Real Madrid have secured ten successive wins in all competitions and are looking like the team to beat at the moment.However, the team is not without its faults, and it was evident in the first half o...
content: Jose Mourinho identifies key issue with Real Madrid’s squad players after PSV scare Real Madrid have secured ten successive wins in all competitions and are looking like the team to beat at the moment. However, the team is not without its faults, and it was evident in the first half of their game against PSV Eindhoven in the UEFA Champions League. The defensive duo of Antonio Rudiger and Eder Militao looked completely out of sorts , prompting Jose Mourinho to make changes in the second half. Mourinho identifies a key issue Mourinho wants more quality from his second squad. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) As reported by Defensa Central , Mourinho believes that his rotation options are simply not performing as expected. The Real Madrid coach has observed that when the fringe players come in, Real Madrid often lose their brightness and competitive edge. It is a pattern that Mourinho has noticed on multiple occasions, with the likes of Rudiger, Trent Alexander-Arnold, Alvaro Carreras and Eduardo Camavinga often failing to perform to the expected level. These players have lacked the quality and the consistency the first-choice XI has provided this season, and the 5-1 win over PSV was the latest example. Mourinho made six changes to the starting lineup, but the team struggled in the first half and conceded. He had experienced similar situations in the comebacks against Celta Vigo and AEK Athens. A necessary balancing act Mourinho is using Luis Enrique’s playbook. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Despite this shortcoming from lesser-used players, Mourinho remains committed to using the full depth of his squad. The Portuguese is working on managing a demanding schedule in December through a selection rest plan. He is determined to keep his first-choice players fresh for key matches. With Real Madrid facing a relentless run of fixtures, rotation will indeed play a key role in the month of December, and that is when Mourinho needs his second-fiddle stars to perform well. In many ways, Mourinho is applying the same roadmap used by Luis Enrique at PSG, protecting his important players in selected games. He rested Arda Guler and Tchouameni against AEK, and left Jude Bellingham on the bench against PSV Eindhoven. This is yet another indicator that Mourinho has stressed massively on ensuring the well-being of his trusted individuals. But for this formula to work, players such as Trent, Rudiger, Camavinga, and others must step up their game.

title: Joshua Kimmich lays into 'incomprehensible' handling of Jamal Musiala situation by Bayern bosses
summary: Joshua Kimmich did not hold back when discussing several recent comments from Bayern Munich bosses regarding the ongoing situation surrounding teammate Jamal Musiala
content: Bayern Munich's Joshua Kimmich has leapt to the defense of teammate Jamal Musiala after recent comments by team bosses -Credit:Alexander Hassenstein - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images Joshua Kimmich has leapt to the defense of Bayern Munich and Germany teammate Jamal Musiala, with club executives having recently faced heavy scrutiny regarding their handling of the latter’s ongoing health battle. Back in August, the 23-year-old collapsed in back-to-back preseason friendlies , after which he revealed that he had been “diagnosed with temporary, brief, but easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction.” Subsequent rest, followed by another injury setback, has limited the attacking midfielder to just 247 minutes so far this season across all competitions. Musiala said in August he was dealing with 'a neurological dysfunction' -Credit:Marco Steinbrenner/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images Musiala’s already challenging situation then took an unexpected turn when club honorary president Uli Hoeneß, CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen, and sporting director Christoph Freund all opted to publicly comment on the star’s health. Hoeneß told Bayerischer Rundfunk, via FOX Sports , “Whether [Musiala] will ever regain the level of performance he once had… “Yet he continues to receive his pay. Just imagine if FC Bayern were to call his contract into question, arguing that his current level of performance no longer aligns with the terms of the agreement.” Fast forward to Sunday, and Freund defended both Hoeneß and ex-CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge - who had also faced criticism for his comments on Musiala - before stating, via @iMiaSanMia , “I’m convinced that Jamal will once again excite us all to such an extent that we will be giving him standing ovations in the stadium, and that one day we will look back on this whole situation differently.” Dreesen also failed to dig himself out of the hole club representatives had created for him, calling Musiala “an extraordinary player” before commenting , “But there is a second responsibility, not just toward the player, but also toward the club. To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE “It’s like at any company when someone is no longer able to perform all of their duties. This is a new situation in football, a situation that we have to learn how to deal with. These absence seizures have never occurred in elite sport, particularly in football, before. I ask for your understanding on this.” Seemingly seeking to quell the growing backlash, Bayern released a statement on Tuesday, in which they clarified that they had engaged in “constructive talks with Musiala’s management.” It added, “On Tuesday, FC Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala’s management held a constructive discussion. Both sides agree that the player’s health comes first. Jamal Musiala has their full support on his road to recovery. “Given the many rumors in recent days, FC Bayern and 11WINS, the agency representing Jamal, would like to clarify: Jamal Musiala was first examined for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025. This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical department, immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared. “FC Bayern and Jamal Musiala’s management have agreed to continue their discussions in a spirit of partnership and confidentiality.” • FIFA confirms cyber attack as hackers access 'personal and business information' • Manchester City appeal verdict date 'named' for Premier League charges by ex-club advisor However, by this point, it seems the damage had been done. Speaking after Bayern’s 2-1 UEFA Champions League defeat at Lille, captain Kimmich told reporters, as per The Athletic , “Generally speaking, you have to look at the situation from different perspectives. I completely understand that this isn’t an easy situation for a club either. “What I don’t understand is the way this is being communicated publicly. It should never happen that this is played out at the expense of a player. Of course, the club is always the highest priority and is bigger than us as players, but still not bigger than the individual. “And that is an absolute no-go and not in the spirit of Bayern, especially in the current phase, where I myself have often emphasized how very, very special the club is. Even in my own situation, the club was very, very special. You could really feel that this ‘Mia san mia’ spirit was truly lived. What has happened now should simply never happen. I find it completely incomprehensible.” When given the opportunity to address Kimmich’s comments on Thursday, Dreesen said, according to Kilian Kreitmair , “I’d like to stand by what I said elsewhere: We need to focus on taking care of things, not talking… We want to resolve this internally.” Musiala’s contract, signed back in February 2025, is set to run through the summer of 2030.

title: Joshua Kimmich slams club's 'not Bayern-like' treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala
summary: LILLE, France (AP) — Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club's “not Bayern-like” treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures.Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala's performances and contract after repeated seizures caused by a neurological condition, including two on the field in preseason games, drawing protests from players' union FIFPRO.
content: LILLE, France (AP) — Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich has launched a stinging attack on the club's “not Bayern-like” treatment of his teammate Jamal Musiala, who has a condition which causes seizures. Senior Bayern figures have publicly questioned Musiala's performances and contract after repeated seizures caused by a neurological condition, including two on the field in preseason games, drawing protests from players' union FIFPRO. Now a key player has spoken out, too, and warned Bayern risks undermining its family image. “What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated in public,” Kimmich told reporters after Bayern's 2-1 Champions League loss at Lille on Wednesday. “It must never happen that the burden is placed on a player. The club is obviously the top priority and bigger than a player, but it's not bigger than a person. That's an absolute no-go and it is not Bayern-like either.” Kimmich also questioned whether Musiala's run of injuries over the last two years, including a badly fractured leg at the Club World Cup last year, had more impact on his game than the neurological condition. “It's not the case that he has problems because he's unprofessional. He's there every day trying to get the maximum out of himself,” Kimmich added. Bayern met with Musiala's agents Tuesday and clarified the timeline of events, dismissing speculation Musiala could have concealed the condition when he signed his last contract extension. Bayern said the club and Musiala's representatives both accept he was first examined for seizure symptoms in April 2025, two months after the contract extension. “This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical unit immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared,” Bayern said. Musiala went public with his diagnosis in August after collapsing on the field in two preseason games, leaving players and fans alarmed. Bayern coach Vincent Kompany said at the time the incidents were triggered by a change in the medication Musiala was taking. Musiala was rested for the start of the season and has since missed several games with a muscle issue. Musiala came off the bench in the 76th minute of Bayern's loss at Lille, which continued a bad week for Bayern. Ballon D'Or winner Harry Kane injured his ankle Friday and faces months on the sidelines, while Bayern has lost the lead in the Bundesliga and slipped to 15th in the Champions League standings. ___ See AP’s full soccer coverage here

title: Joshua Zirkzee makes his position unmistakable after Man United’s controversy-filled Sporting encounter
summary: Joshua Zirkzee has made his feelings crystal clear after Manchester United’s controversy-filled 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP.ControversyPochettino was denied his first win as United...
content: Joshua Zirkzee makes his position unmistakable after Man United’s controversy-filled Sporting encounter Joshua Zirkzee has made his feelings crystal clear after Manchester United’s controversy-filled 2-2 Champions League draw against Sporting CP. Controversy Pochettino was denied his first win as United head coach, with multiple bizarre refereeing decisions going against him and his players. Referee Szymon Marciniak ruled out an Amad Diallo goal during the second half, having adjudged Youri Tielemans to have committed a foul in the build-up. Marciniak’s whistle came just before Amad found the net, ruling out any VAR intervention. The Polish referee compounded matters by awarding Sporting a debatable first-half penalty and disallowing what would have been a late United winner for a push on goalkeeper Kaique Pereira. The decision to chalk off United’s goal seemed baffling given that he allowed a similar Suárez goal to stand when there was slight contact with Senne Lammens . Pochettino hit out at the decisions in his post-match remarks to reporters , but he chose to emphasise the positives and the fine attitude his players displayed. In an interview with MUTV , Zirkzee acknowledged how costly the referee’s shocking performance had been, but insisted it was solely down to him and his teammates to deliver the victory. Zirkzee’s verdict The Dutchman told club media, “In my opinion, there were definitely some key decisions there that didn’t really favour us. We shouldn’t look at the referee, we should look at ourselves instead, but it definitely has an impact on us, you can’t deny that.” “But the team that we have, we should come here and not look at the ref and make sure that we get the win, regardless of the decisions that he makes.” He continued, “Obviously, we did come here to win, so in a way, we’ve got some positives to take.” “But with our recent form, of course, we’re disappointed to not win. Some positives to take, we’ve just got to keep moving forward, keep going together, keep putting in the work and move onto the next game.” Zirkzee said of his return to the starting XI, “I’m very happy; every game you play for this club is an honour. I’ve been here for some time and it’s been a while since I started a game, so I’m very happy, I just wish we could have got a win.” “For where we’re standing at right now, to have a fanbase like that is just incredible. All we can do is get up the next day and make sure the next time they travel with us and the next time they watch our game, we repay it, so that’s all we can do for now.” Looking ahead to Saturday’s meeting with Brentford, Zirkzee remarked, “It’s a big test. The fans deserve a result and all we want is a result. We’ve got to dig ourselves out of the trenches.” United sit in 19th place in the Premier League table heading into the game against Brentford.

title: Joshua Zirkzee reveals Manchester United dressing room reaction to Senne Lammens howlers in Sporting draw
summary: Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee has opened up on the atmosphere inside the dressing room following Senne Lammens' difficult night in the Champions League. The Belgian goalkeeper suffered a personal nightmare in Lisbon, committing two high-profile errors that ultimately saw victory slip away against Sporting.
content: Manchester United forward Joshua Zirkzee has opened up on the atmosphere inside the dressing room following Senne Lammens' difficult night in the Champions League. The Belgian goalkeeper suffered a personal nightmare in Lisbon, committing two high-profile errors that ultimately saw victory slip away against Sporting. Costly errors and VAR drama deny Pochettino first win Mauricio Pochettino was denied his first victory as Manchester United manager following a chaotic 2-2 draw with Sporting at the Jose Alvalade. Bruno Fernandes fired the visitors into a 2-1 lead with a quickfire double early in the second half, after Lammens had saved a penalty only to rush off his line 75 seconds later and concede a second spot-kick converted by Luis Suarez. The Colombian striker later capitalised when Lammens spilled a cross at his feet with 10 minutes remaining to snatch an equaliser. United were also left fuming at Polish referee Szymon Marciniak, who blew for a free-kick just before Amad scored prior to half-time and later saw a late winner chalked off after VAR judged Patrick Dorgu had fouled the goalkeeper. Zirkzee insists Man Utd squad are backing Lammens Despite the gaffes continuing Lammens' uncertain second season in Manchester , Zirkzee revealed his team-mates chose to give the goalkeeper breathing room in the dressing room while backing his strong mentality. "In this moment, we just give him space," said Zirkzee. "Not sure if he wants to hear anything at all. But Senne’s a great kid. He's got a good head on him. "And we all know that next game he is going to be at the top of his game. And we didn't draw because of him. I'm also someone who likes to look at myself and I didn't score." Asked how important it was to show support to Lammens, the forward added: "It's everything. This team is a family, so there's no one who will suffer by themselves. Mistakes happen. Let's go on to the next one. Senne’s a great goalkeeper." Officiating frustration and an 'us against the world' mindset Controversial refereeing has now marred both of Pochettino's opening matches in charge, following Leny Yoro's wrongful eighth-minute red card at Anfield . That growing sense of injustice has fuelled a siege mentality inside the camp, though Zirkzee refused to blame the officials entirely. "Yeah, we're in a place where it can feel like that pretty quick," he said. "But as I said, we've got a locker room that's built on supporting each other and we will get out of it eventually. And if it's us against the world, so be it. "For the team that we are, we shouldn't really be looking at what the referee decides, but you cannot deny that it was some key decisions that weren't in our favour, to put it like that. "But, as I said, we shouldn't really be looking at the referee. All we have to do is look at ourselves. In the end, I think we lost because of small details, little mistakes. But we definitely have something to build on, mainly the way we started the second half. I think that's something we can build on and move on with." Brentford clash offers immediate chance to respond United now return to Premier League action against Brentford, where Pochettino will again seek his maiden victory at the helm. Cutting out costly lapses in concentration remains the immediate challenge if the squad are to turn improved displays into three points. Replicating the intensity that produced Fernandes' double after the interval in Lisbon will be vital as United look to steady their campaign and put back-to-back frustrations behind them.

title: 'A level below!' - PSG warned their squad players cannot replace injured stars Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue
summary: Paris Saint-Germain face a major attacking dilemma after losing Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue for the rest of the season. Following a frustrating 2-2 Champions League draw with Roma, former stars Daniel Xuereb and Emmanuel Petit have raised serious doubts over the squad's depth ahead of the January transfer window.
content: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-ROMA - AFP Paris Saint-Germain face a major attacking dilemma after losing Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue for the rest of the season. Following a frustrating 2-2 Champions League draw with Roma, former stars Daniel Xuereb and Emmanuel Petit have raised serious doubts over the squad's depth ahead of the January transfer window. PSG's attacking crisis exposed against Roma PSG's offensive struggles were laid bare on Wednesday night as they were held to a 2-2 draw by Roma in the Champions League. With Kvaratskhelia and Doue both ruled out for the remainder of the campaign, the club's supporting cast failed to step up when needed most. Maghnes Akliouche, Ferran Torres and Mika Godts all endured disappointing outings against the Italian side. Their underwhelming displays immediately prompted concern from former PSG striker Xuereb and ex-Chelsea midfielder Petit, who both questioned whether the current squad can cope without their injured talismans. Xuereb questions quality of PSG's deputies Xuereb, a 1984 Olympic champion, offered a blunt assessment of the players tasked with filling the void. Speaking to Le Parisien , he argued that the replacements simply do not match the match-winning quality that has defined PSG's recent success. "Those who played on Wednesday lacked penetration, one-on-one duels and runs in behind," Xuereb said. "They are excellent players, internationals. But if they don't usually play, there are good reasons for that. When Doue and Kvaratskhelia are there, they are second-string players. They are a level below. "If PSG have achieved what they have over the past two or three seasons, it is thanks to players capable of scoring at any moment. Unfortunately, they are injured." Petit urges January action over cruciate fears Petit shares those concerns and believes PSG must enter the winter transfer market to find an attacking reinforcement. Speaking as a pundit on RMC , he stressed that recovering from cruciate ligament injuries is notoriously difficult, meaning the club must plan beyond the current campaign. "They have to explore every opportunity," Petit said. "When you tear your cruciate ligaments, those are not simple injuries. Rare are the players who have returned to their previous level. So the thinking for next summer can already happen in January. You are only looking at this season, whereas I am looking ahead to next season." Crucial winter transfer window awaits PSG PSG now face a defining period as the January transfer window approaches. With Kvaratskhelia and Doue sidelined for the rest of the season, the club's hierarchy must weigh up whether to pursue an immediate attacking signing or trust the options already at their disposal. If no suitable targets are available mid-season, the pressure will remain firmly on the likes of Akliouche, Torres and Godts to rediscover their sharpness.

title: Lucas Chevalier plans to leave PSG this winter
summary: Lucas Chevalier (25) wishes to leave Paris Saint-Germain as early as the winter transfer window, according to reports in L’Équipe.Confined to the role of substitute to Matvey Safonov (27), the Fren...
content: Lucas Chevalier plans to leave PSG this winter Lucas Chevalier (25) wishes to leave Paris Saint-Germain as early as the winter transfer window, according to reports in L’Équipe . Confined to the role of substitute to Matvey Safonov (27), the French goalkeeper has still not played a single minute since the start of the season. This situation is becoming increasingly untenable for the 25-year-old, who was signed from LOSC Lille in the summer of 2025 for €40m. Aware that he is already at a turning point in his career, Chevalier now wishes to rediscover his enjoyment of the game, secure a key place in a European starting XI and find a project in which he can flourish once again. He is expected to convey this desire shortly to Luis Campos, the club’s sporting director, and Luis Enrique, his manager, with whom he is due to meet soon to discuss his future. Whether it is a loan or a permanent transfer, all options remain on the table at this stage, provided that PSG can find a replacement of a similar calibre to Chevalier, capable of stepping in for Safonov. In any case, there is a shared desire amongst all parties not to part on bad terms and to find the best solution for everyone. All that remains now is for the offers to come in. GFFN | Léo Aschi

title: Major MLS playoff overhaul confirmed as league axes wild card round and best-of-three series
summary: Major League Soccer (MLS) is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season format, with the wild card round and best-of-three first round set to be scrapped from the 2027-28 campaign. The revamped 16-team structure aims to boost regular-season intensity after the current format proved ineffective at sustaining momentum and rewarding the league's top performers.
content: Inter Miami CF v D.C. United - Getty Images Sport Major League Soccer (MLS) is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season format, with the wild card round and best-of-three first round set to be scrapped from the 2027-28 campaign. The revamped 16-team structure aims to boost regular-season intensity after the current format proved ineffective at sustaining momentum and rewarding the league's top performers. MLS set for major play-off overhaul MLS is finalising another major overhaul of its post-season structure , even as the 2026 MLS Cup play-offs get under way. Beginning with the 2027-28 season, the league will eliminate its short-lived wild card round and scrap the best-of-three first-round format, according to reports from The Guardian . The changes will condense the play-off field to 16 teams. Under the new model, the opening two rounds will be played as two-legged, home-and-away ties, while the semi-finals and final will revert to single-elimination matches hosted by the higher seed. Why the league is scrapping best-of-three Introduced in 2023, the best-of-three opening round has proved ineffective at sustaining drama or rewarding regular-season excellence. Over the past three campaigns, a staggering 35 days elapsed between the end of the regular season and the second round due to the November international break. While the 2026 World Cup break allowed MLS to push the start of this year's play-offs past the international window, the gap from Decision Day to the quarter-finals still stretched to 28 days. The league had also weighed an Australian rules football-inspired double-elimination model before settling on its latest plan. Although an MLS spokesperson did not immediately comment on the latest reports, the league confirmed its review back in August. "Major League Soccer is continuing to evaluate potential adjustments to its postseason format as part of a broader review of the league’s shift to a new competition calendar, beginning with the 2027-28 season," a spokesperson said at the time. A bid to restore regular-season intensity A primary driver behind the constant adjustments is the desire to raise the stakes of the regular season. Currently, 60 per cent of clubs qualify for the play-offs, creating an overly forgiving race. That leniency was highlighted this year when Real Salt Lake reached the first round despite winning just once in 16 matches after the World Cup. They edged out Minnesota United on Decision Day, even though Minnesota had endured a run of one victory in 18 games. The 2027-28 model will become the sixth different play-off format MLS has used since its 1996 launch. The league briefly abandoned multi-legged ties in 2019 before reintroducing extended series following its broadcast partnership with Apple, partly to guarantee lower-ranked qualifiers at least one match of post-season revenue. What's next for MLS play-offs? For now, clubs must navigate the 2026 MLS Cup play-offs under the existing system before the overhaul arrives alongside the league's new competition calendar in 2027-28. Some finer details of the revamped format still require clarification. It remains unknown how hosting order for the two-legged ties will be assigned, although the last MLS format to use home-and-away series gave the higher seed home advantage for the decisive second leg.

title: How many more points will Liverpool likely need to ensure top-eight Champions League finish?
summary: Liverpool are nicely on course to qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16 after their 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night.The Reds’ 100% start to the league phase was ended ...
content: How many more points will Liverpool likely need to ensure top-eight Champions League finish? Liverpool are nicely on course to qualify directly for the Champions League round of 16 after their 3-0 win away to Club Brugge on Wednesday night. The Reds’ 100% start to the league phase was ended by a 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce earlier this month, but they responded to that setback in Istanbul with a thoroughly impressive victory against the Belgian side, with whom they were level on points prior to the match. That result has left Andoni Iraola’s team fifth in the league phase standings with 12 points from a possible 15, with a top-eight finish seeing them bypass the bear pit of the knockout play-off round in February. Now that we’re past the halfway mark of the league phase, the 36 Champions League clubs have a strong indication as to where they’re likely to finish, and what more needs to be done to achieve their targets. Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust How many more points do Liverpool need for top-eight finish? At present, Manchester City occupy the final position for automatic passage to the round of 16, with Enzo Maresca’s side on 10 points, averaging two per game. That means the projected points tally required for a top-eight placing is 16, so Liverpool would need to aim for at least four points from their remaining three matches against Porto (home), Inter Milan (away) and Lens (home). The two Anfield fixtures are against teams placed 22nd and 34th respectively, so the Reds would be fully expected to win both of those. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The visit to the San Siro is likely to be much tougher, but LFC beat Inter at the famous venue last season, and a repeat result would probably be enough to guarantee a top-eight finish with one game to spare. That’d give Iraola the luxury of being able to rest key players for the concluding fixture against Lens, which falls between Premier League matches against Manchester United and Everton. Top-eight finish well within reach for Liverpool With Liverpool also still going strong in the Carabao Cup and plausibly making it to a two-legged semi-final in the opening weeks of 2027, any opportunity to rotate the squad in January must be embraced. The picture can obviously change over the final three matchdays, but right now it seems probable that if the Reds beat Porto and get a result away to Inter, they could be effectively or even mathematically assured of a top-eight finish by the time they host Lens. That objective is well within reach for Iraola’s side, and avoiding the play-off round in February is a must.

title: Midweek Warm-up: What a week for Bayern Munich, huh?; Don’t meet your heroes; Champions League predictions; and MORE!
summary: It’s a Champions League showdown for Bayern Munich
content: Photo: Peter Kneffel/dpa (Photo by Peter Kneffel/picture alliance via Getty Images) “What a week, huh?” “Captain, it’s Wednesday.” Bayern Munich could probably use that exchange as the unofficial motto for the last several d ays. Between the public discussion surrounding J amal Musiala, comments from club leadership, questions about his contract, and now reporting from Sport Bild’s Christian Falk and Julian Agardi (via @iMiaSan Mia ) about Vincent Kompany reassuring players and club employees regarding Musia la’s health, it has been an exhausting news cycle. According to Falk and Agardi, Kompany told his players during a dressing-room team talk that they should have absolutely no concerns about Musiala or his health, assuring them that their teammate is in excellent health and full of energy. Kompany reportedly delivered the same reassurance to several other club employees. The reassurance comes after a week in which Musiala has seemingly become the center of a wider Bayern Munich debate that has extended well beyond football. Comments and crit icism from Jan-Christian Dreesen, Uli Hoeneß, and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge regarding Musiala, his contract, and his situation have helped fuel the perception of a growing divide between the player a nd the club. What might ordinarily be an internal conversation about a player’s development, recovery, contractual future, and expectations has increasingly played out publicly, leaving Musiala at the center of a debate that is difficult to separate from the footballing realities. That is where this entire situation has become particularly uncomfortable. Musiala is not just a contract negotiat ion, a talking point for club executives, or a headline generator. He is a player recovering, trying to get back to his best, and one whose importance to Bayern Munich is difficult to oversta te. Public discourse can easily turn a complicated situation into a perceived confrontation, but that does not necessarily reflect what is happening behind closed doors. Ultimately, though, thi s is about Jamal Musiala’s health. The hope should be that he gets fully healthy, regains his confidence, and returns to the form that made him one of the mo st highly regarded talents in world football. That is what matters most, regardless of the noise, the speculation, or the conversations about who knew what and when. Will he get back to a top level? Is he worth the massive contract? Should Bayern Munich seek to renegotiate? For now, it is probably time to put th is ordeal aside, take a breath, and focus on what Bayern Munich actually has in front of it — a Champions League game. The rest can wait. Song of the Midweek: “Young Again” by Shinedown In contrast to our normal fare, here is a newer song. Released earlier this year on EI8HT , this one caught my attention, and it felt like a good little change from a lot of my reminiscing about music from years closer to my prime (hell yeah!). Enjoy: In lieu of an Entertainment Rundown As the podcast listeners know, I’ve been on the road a bit and had no time to watch anything, but there is a topic that needs to be addressed… Manuel Neuer has found himself caught up in yet ano ther controversy, and while the latest discussion surrounding the Bayern Munich captain might change how some people view him personally, it should not change how we evalua te him as a footballer. Those two things can coexist, even if football fandom often struggles to separate them. There is an uncomfortable reality in sports — exceptional athletes are not necessarily exceptional people. Players can make questionable dec isions, display narcissistic tendencies, behave selfishly, or even be genuinely unpleasant individuals, and still be extraordinary at their profession. Football does not automatically mak e someone virtuous, and talent does not require a spotless personal record. Neuer’s legacy as one of the greatest goalkeepers of his generation is built on what he has done between the posts, not on whether every decision he has made away from the pitch deserves admiration. Criticism of his conduct is fair, and fans are perfectly enti tled to reassess the person they thought they knew. But that does not erase decades of elite performances. It is another reminder of the old saying, “Do not meet your heroes.” Sometimes the person behind the legend is considerably more complicated than the image we built in our heads. That does not mean the football was any less phenomenal. Predictions When I look in the mirror I can’t believe what I see Tell me, who’s that funky dude Staring back at me? Broken, beaten down, can’t even get around Without an old man cane, I fall and hit the ground Shivering in the cold, I’m bitter and alone Excuse the b*tching I shouldn’t complain I should have no feeling ‘Cause feeling is pain As everything I need is denied me And everything I want is taken away from me But who do I got to blame? Nobody but me Yup, Bayern Munich is, indeed, broken and beaten down and not living “The Good Life” — at least not at this very moment. At some point, though, the squad has to get past t he headlines and conjecture and remember why it is here in the first place: a Champions League tilt vs. LOSC Lille. LOSC Lille is not great, let alone a powerhouse, but it has — at least — had a week not mired in controversy. In addition, while Lille does have some injuries, its front line is mostly intact. The same cannot be said for Bayern Munich, which is limping into the game. At some point, though, the pride wi thin the Bavarians has to show through all of the nonsense going on around the squad. The fight and heart will need to be on full display, and the mentality of a true champion will either be there when the whistle blows or… it won’t. Let’s bank on Bayern Munich remembering exactly who the (expletive removed) it is. And I don’t wanna be an old man anymore It’s been a year or two since I was out on the floor Shakin’ booty, makin’ sweet love all the night It’s time I got back to the good life Prediction: Lille 1-2 Bayern Munich (L) Other Champions League predictions include: Tuesday November 24th Bodø/Glimt 2-1 LASK Linz (W) Galatasaray 1-2 Aston Villa (L) Arsenal 1-0 Borussia Dortmund (L) Como 3-1 AEK Athens (W) Feyenoord 2-2 FC Porto (L) Manchester City 4-1 Napoli (L) RB Leipzig 3-0 Lens (W) Real Madrid 4-1 PSV Eindhoven (W) Slovan Bratislava 0-2 Real Betis (W) Tuesday’s record: 5-4, 1PP Wednesday, November 25, 2026 Sabah FK 0-5 FC Barcelona (W) Slavia Prague 1-2 Villarreal (W) Atlético Madrid 2-0 Viking FK (W) Club Brugge 1-3 Liverpool (W) Inter Milan 2-1 VfB Stuttgart (W) Paris Saint-Germain 2-1 AS Roma (this game will tell us a lot about PSG’s fight-or-flight mentality) (L) Shakhtar Donetsk 0-1 Fenerbahçe (W)*** Sporting CP 1-2 Manchester United (L) Wednesday’s record: 6-3, 1PP Prediction Records Total: 356-214 Perfect Picks: 50 Bundesliga Last Matchday: 5-4 Bundesliga Overall: 44-46 DFB-Pokal: 40-8 World Cup: 71-28 International Friendlies: 50-30 UEFA Nations League: 90-66 Champions League: 55-35 Club Friendlies: 5-1 Franz Beckenbauer Supercup: 1-0 Join the conversation! title: Milan List Barcelona, Bologna and Frosinone Defenders
summary: Milan are shifting their focus from the middle to the left of their defense and are stepping up their efforts to acquire a new specialist in January. They had already been linked to a pair of options ...
content: Milan List Barcelona, Bologna and Frosinone Defenders Milan are shifting their focus from the middle to the left of their defense and are stepping up their efforts to acquire a new specialist in January. They had already been linked to a pair of options before Ruben Amorim stated he was content with his center-backs. According to Calciomercato , the Rossoneri will keep pursuing Noussair Mazraoui , who already worked with their coach, but it’s too early to determine his future, as Manchester United are in a holding pattern after recently hiring Mauricio Pochettino. Milan had also been attached to Gabriele Calvani , who’s showing well at Frosinone for the second consecutive season. He generally plays as a center-back but has some experience wide too. He’s on loan from Genoa, who’s interested in their youngsters Francesco Camarda and Christian Comotto. Instead, Alejandro Balde and Juan Miranda are the latest additions to their shortlist. Jorge Mendes has offered the latter to several clubs, as he’s logged just 125 minutes thus far. However, he needs to be convinced to leave Catalunya. Instead, the Bologna man is in the midst of a career season, having already provided six assists. The Felsinei are having trouble with his extension talks and would carefully weigh €15M offers. Our Take on Milan Looking For a Fullback They have to decide whether they want a defensive or an aggressive option, as Amorim has used Mario Gila and Sankhoun Diawara wide whenever everyone was fit in the back to free up their attackers. Instead, other than Calvani, who’s not even left-footed, their rumored targets are all dynamic players. It feels like their search is in its infancy, and the right name hasn’t emerged yet.

content: Nations League: Spain-France quarter-final to be played at Mestalla 🇪🇸🇫🇷 It’s official: the Spain-France clash in the first leg of the UEFA Nations League quarter-finals will take place at Mestalla on Thursday, 25 March 2027 at 20:45 . The match will serve as a tribute and a final farewell to Valencia’s historic home from the Spanish national team before the move to Nou Mestalla. A farewell in style What had been an open secret is now confirmed. The Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) has chosen Valencia’s stadium to host the opening leg of this high-stakes tie, giving the Valencia fans one last great night of international football. Opened in 1923, Mestalla will bring down the curtain with La Roja after more than a century of history and unforgettable occasions. A tantalising rematch against Les Bleus There could hardly be a bigger fixture to mark the end of an era. Luis de la Fuente’s side will once again face Kylian Mbappé and Zinedine Zidane’s France, in a repeat of the last World Cup semi-final, which Spain won 2-0. After this meeting in Valencia, the tie will be decided three days later, on Sunday, 28 March, on French soil, with a place in the Final Four at stake. title: Pep Guardiola Admits to Being "Ashamed" After Rejecting National Team Job Offer
summary: The former Barcelona and Bayern Munich coach called time on his legendary spell as Manchester City boss at the end of the last campaign, closing the door on a 10-year stay at the Etihad Stadium.During...
content: Pep Guardiola Admits to Being "Ashamed" After Rejecting National Team Job Offer The former Barcelona and Bayern Munich coach called time on his legendary spell as Manchester City boss at the end of the last campaign, closing the door on a 10-year stay at the Etihad Stadium. During the decade-long reign, Guardiola secured a remarkable six Premier League titles for the Sky Blues, a first-ever UEFA Champions League alongside an FA Cup and top-flight success in a treble-winning season, and a multitude of domestic cup honours. But citing the mental, physical, and emotional toll of top-level football management, Guardiola stepped aside as Manchester City moved to appoint former Leicester City and Chelsea coach Enzo Maresca as his replacement. Since then, Pep Guardiola has found himself at the centre of speculation concerning his own next steps in the game, having recently confirmed that his next role would come in the form of an international job. Now, speaking during an interview with former Barcelona team-mate Romario on his YouTube channel RomarioTV , as translated by The Athletic , Pep Guardiola shone light on his decision to reject an approach from the Italian Football Federation (FICG). The FICG have been confirmed to have made an approach for Guardiola back in July - just over a month after the 55-year-old left Manchester City - but the former Etihad boss explained that the opportunity came when he needed a break from the game. Further adding that he he felt “ashamed” to decline the job from figures that he 'loves so much', Pep Guardiola explained, “I spoke with them. It was an honour. I even feel bad or ashamed to say no to a country like Italy. "It is one of the biggest honours I’ve had that they thought of me as the right man to manage Italy. But they found me in a moment when I needed to stop." Guardiola continued, “If they had come in one or two years time, probably I would have taken it. But I told (Paulo) Maldini and Leonardo (Bonucci, FICG executives at the time), who I love so much, I needed to stop and spend a bit more time with myself. "It’s been 18 years of being there every day, every day.” Pep Guardiola's ongoing commitment to Manchester City Despite leaving the club at the end of the 2025/26 season, Pep Guardiola continues to hold strong ties to Manchester City and the Premier League giants' parent company, the City Football Group (CFG). As part of the announcement confirming his departure from role of manager, City confirmed during the summer that Guardiola would take up a role as a Global Ambassador for the City Football Group. It was explained at the time that the position would involve 'giving technical advice to the clubs in the group, working on specific projects and collaborations', with Pep Guardiola having since visited clubs within CFG such as Brazilian outfit Bahia. In light of Manchester City's guilty verdict issued by the Premier League in September, Pep Guardiola also made a swift return to the Etihad Stadium, sitting with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak and other key boardroom figures for the Champions League meeting with PSG . The former Barcelona and Bayern Munich boss is believed to still have full faith and trust in those who offered him the same throughout his tenure in Manchester, and issued a statement of support shortly after the release of the verdict around the club's 115 charges.

title: Pick of the stats: Southampton v Middlesbrough
summary: Here are the key stats for Southampton v Middlesbrough.
content: [BBC] Middlesbrough will aim to extend their lead at the top of the table when they visit Southampton on Friday night (20:00 GMT). The two sides are meeting each other for the first time since Spygate but it will mean more to Boro than a grudge match. A slip up here could see any of the four Midlands teams beneath them steal their place at the apex by the end of the weekend and their automatic promotion spot to boot. It won't be easy though with Saints yet to to lose on home soil this season. Southampton are winless in their last four league games against Middlesbrough (D2 L2) since a 2-1 away win in the Premier League in May 2017. Middlesbrough have gone five away league games without a win at Southampton (D3 L2) since beating them 1-0 in September 2003. Southampton are unbeaten in their last 18 home league games (W14 D4), their best run without losing at St Mary's since going 24 in a row between December 2010 and December 2011. Middlesbrough have failed to score in each of their last two away league games, having 30 shots without success. They haven't gone three Championship away games without a goal since January 2015. ● Cyle Larin has netted 12 goals in 16 home league appearances for Southampton, averaging one every 86 minutes. It's the best ratio by a Saints player to play 500+ minutes across the Premier League, Championship and League One at St Mary's since it opened in 2001. [BBC]

title: Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg wishes to remain at Marseille; €2m release clause valid at the end of the season

content: Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg wishes to remain at Marseille; €2m release clause valid at the end of the season Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg (31) was pushed towards the exit during the summer transfer window, but held firm, rejecting a move to Newcastle United, much to the frustration of OM’s ownership, in order to remain at the Vélodrome. As per a report from L’Equipe , he has no intention of leaving the club during the January transfer window either. The publication adds that he is the only player to have offered to lower his salary amid OM’s financial struggles (an agreement could soon be reached), which will oblige Marseille to sell further players either in January or before the end of June. The situation will become clearer when OM meet with the DNCG next month. In any case, Hojbjerg, who saw the captain stripped from him over the summer, wants to remain at Marseille, at least until the end of the season. At this point, the Dane would become very accessible to any interested party. His contract, which runs until 2028, has a €2m release clause that will become valid in June, L’Équipe understands.
