title: 'We play with no fear!' - Mario Hermoso reveals Gian Piero Gasperini's training ground secret after AS Roma halt Paris Saint-Germain's winning streak
summary: Mario Hermoso scored early and earned Player of the Match honours as AS Roma ended Paris Saint-Germain's 100 per cent Champions League start with a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes. Speaking afterwards, the Spanish defender explained how Gian Piero Gasperini's fearless system empowers centre-backs to attack.
content: FBL-EUR-C1-PSG-ROMA - AFP Mario Hermoso scored early and earned Player of the Match honours as AS Roma ended Paris Saint-Germain's 100 per cent Champions League start with a 2-2 draw at the Parc des Princes. Speaking afterwards, the Spanish defender explained how Gian Piero Gasperini's fearless system empowers centre-backs to attack. Hermoso inspires fearless Roma to historic Paris point Mario Hermoso set the tone inside five minutes as AS Roma held reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain to a thrilling 2-2 draw in the first-ever meeting between the clubs on Wednesday night. Winning possession high up the pitch before finishing from Matias Soule's cut-back, the Spanish centre-back helped Gian Piero Gasperini's side end PSG's 100 per cent Champions League start despite goals from Illia Zabarnyi and Ousmane Dembele, with substitute Donyell Malen converting a late penalty after Vitinha's handball. "Everyone knows what the coach does, this is his identity, his style of playing," Hermoso told Sky Sport Italia after collecting UEFA's Player of the Match award. "We defenders get the opportunity to be protagonists, so I am very happy to come to a stadium like this, and see Roma playing in this special way, with no fear. We are on the right track and must keep taking these big steps forward." Training ground drills and Gasperini's squad rotation Gasperini sprang a tactical surprise by leaving Malen, Paulo Dybala and Bryan Cristante on the bench from the start, yet Roma's rotated line-up matched the French giants across 90 minutes. Hermoso, who also went close to adding a second open-play goal, revealed how attacking rotations are rehearsed daily. "With these team-mates who play in attack, we do try to make these moves in training sessions, everyone gets to have a go, and that means us defenders can bring something extra to the team, it's an added benefit," he explained. Addressing the bench impact, Hermoso added: "Everyone in this squad is important, we are set out in a way that we can all be protagonists. Dony, Paulo and Bryan had more minutes in this season, but they came on with the right mentality, and were ready to help get a good result." Building a winning mentality against European champions PSG only breached Roma's open-play organisation through Zabarnyi's 31st-minute corner header and Dembele's 62nd-minute spot-kick after Achraf Hakimi was fouled by Wesley. Hermoso credited Gasperini with transforming Roma's resilience in high-pressure European fixtures. "The coach gives you confidence to believe, to have this mentality of reacting to difficult moments that we suffered not just this season, but over the years," Hermoso told Prime Video . "This is important, given the way the team came in, the way we played this match against a team that has won the last two Champions Leagues. The result is a huge achievement... It's a shame we didn't win, but a point is good." Roma target knockout surge from 25th place Sitting second in Serie A, Roma now turn their focus toward climbing into the Champions League play-off spots from 25th place with five points from five games. "The most important thing is to continue to grow. We want to fight for everything – we have the mentality to do it, we have the quality too. Let's continue like this, with what the coach wants. For us, it's the right path," Hermoso concluded.

title: Pochettino confident Man United will turn things round
summary: Mauricio Pochettino is confident that Manchester United will turn things around and says he sees a united dressing room.Pochettino’s side drew 2-2 at Sporting CP in the Champions League on Wednesday...
content: Pochettino confident Man United will turn things round Mauricio Pochettino is confident that Manchester United will turn things around and says he sees a united dressing room. Pochettino’s side drew 2-2 at Sporting CP in the Champions League on Wednesday night, as the Argentine earned the first positive result of his tenure. Braces from Luis Suarez and Bruno Fernandes saw the points shared in Lisbon, a result that leaves United in the qualification places for the play-off round. Pochettino’s first fixture ended in a 4-0 defeat to Liverpool, but he saw improvement from his side at Sporting. United dealt with some questionable referring decisions in Portugal, which included conceding two penalties, a disallowed goal, and Youri Tielemans’ red card. Despite a tough start to his reign, Pochettino said he is full of motivation as he looks to get United back to the top of English and European football. “I’m happy to be here. I am so excited to be in the front and be the face of representing the club,” he said. “I think we are here because the situation wasn’t the situation that all the fans and the people expect, that is why we are here. We are here to take the responsibility from week one, and we are going to for sure improve and put again this team in the place [we belong], because of the history and everything we deserve to be. “It’s going to be tough, of course. Nothing is easy, but we have the energy and I think we have the capacity and, most importantly, we have the players and the power and the energy from our fans that is massive. And I think united all together, I think we will find a way to perform and win games.” See Also – Five of the best Premier League away kits in 2026/27 Follow The Football Faithful on Social Media: Facebook | Instagram | Twitter | YouTube | TikTok

content: Pundit tells Arsenal who to sign instead of Calvert-Lewin Arsenal have been advised to consider signing Dominic Calvert-Lewin, but pundit Joel Beya believes the Leeds United striker may not be the right choice for the Gunners. He has instead recommended that the club target a younger forward who could offer greater potential for the future. Viktor Gyokeres has not yet met expectations at the Emirates, raising the possibility that Arsenal could return to the transfer market for another striker in one of the next two windows. Several players are reportedly on their radar as they assess how to improve their attacking options. Calvert-Lewin was previously linked with Arsenal during one of the strongest periods of his career at Everton. He has since joined Leeds United and is performing well there, attracting renewed attention from people who believe he could also contribute at a club with greater ambitions. Theo Walcott has urged Arsenal to consider signing the Englishman , believing he could strengthen their forward options. However, Beya is not convinced that pursuing the Leeds striker would be the best decision. Beya questions Calvert-Lewin as an Arsenal target Beya believes Calvert-Lewin could be useful as a backup option, but he does not see him as the ideal signing if Arsenal want to take their attack forward. The pundit feels the club should focus on a younger player who could make a greater contribution over the longer term. Speaking on TalkSport , he explained his position: “I like Calvert-Lewin as a back-up striker, maybe. No disrespect, he’s obviously still doing a good job at Leeds. “I think we should be looking at the Kroupi’s of this world, we should be looking at people that are going to take us forward.” (Photo by Mike Hewitt/Getty Images) Arsenal urged to consider younger striker Beya’s comments suggest that Arsenal should look beyond players who could provide immediate cover and prioritise a forward with room to develop. His preference is for a younger option who could become an important part of the team’s future. Calvert-Lewin’s current form at Leeds means he remains a possible option, particularly if Arsenal want an experienced striker to provide competition for Gyokeres. However, Beya believes that signing a player with greater long-term potential would be a better approach. Arsenal will have to assess their available options before deciding whether to make another move for a striker. title: Real Madrid revive interest in €40m-rated Borussia Dortmund left-back ahead of possible 2027 move – report
summary: Real Madrid have renewed their interest in Borussia Dortmund left-back Daniel Svensson, with the Swedish international still on the club’s scouting radar ahead of the 2027 transfer windows.According...
content: Real Madrid revive interest in €40m-rated Borussia Dortmund left-back ahead of possible 2027 move – report Real Madrid have renewed their interest in Borussia Dortmund left-back Daniel Svensson, with the Swedish international still on the club’s scouting radar ahead of the 2027 transfer windows. According to Bernabeu Digital , the Santiago Bernabeu outfit has continued monitoring Svensson after tracking him for several months last year. In fact, scouts previously travelled to watch the defender during a Champions League match against Atalanta, which helps explain that the interest is not a recent development. Svensson remains on Real Madrid’s shortlist Real Madrid’s interest in Svensson reportedly dates back to last season, when his potential arrival was linked to the possibility of Fran Garcia leaving the club. Daniel Svensson is on Real Madrid’s radar. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images) Garcia eventually departed for Real Betis last summer, while Marc Cucurella arrived from Chelsea, and yet Svensson has now re-emerged as a possible option to strengthen the left side of José Mourinho’s defence. Dortmund could demand up to €40 million For what it is worth, the outlet mentions that a potential deal would not be easy to pull off as Svensson is under contract with Borussia Dortmund until 2029, giving the German club a strong negotiating position. As far as his valuation is concerned, some reports have placed Dortmund’s asking price at €35 million to €40 million, while others have suggested a starting figure closer to €30 million. At the same time, the transfer fee alone will not be the only problem for Real Madrid, as Arsenal, Inter Milan and Leeds United have also been linked with the Swedish defender, potentially increasing competition if Madrid decide to pursue him. A possible summer 2027 target Daniel Svensson will not come cheap. (Photo by Pau Barrena/Getty Images) For now, Svensson appears to be in long-term consideration, with a possible move in summer 2027 dependent on Real Madrid’s squad needs and the development of their left-back situation. Speaking of left-backs, Jose Mourinho currently has three options available for that position, namely Cucurella, Alvaro Carreras and Ferland Mendy. This means Real Madrid cannot simply look for a new player for the same role without making necessary space, with Mendy being the most likely candidate to leave next summer. Even so, having options like Cucurella and Carreras will not lower Real Madrid’s negotiation power with the Dortmund defender.

title: Real Madrid summer signing wins over the dressing room with humility and hard work – report

content: Real Madrid summer signing wins over the dressing room with humility and hard work – report Bernardo Silva has become one of the most respected figures in the Real Madrid dressing room, with his humility, professionalism and support for teammates earning him admiration beyond his performances on the pitch. According to AS (h/t Madrid Xtra ), the Portuguese midfielder is highly regarded by his colleagues and the club’s sporting staff for the confidence he gives to players, including those who are not regular starters. His approach has reportedly helped him establish himself as an influential presence since joining Real Madrid from Manchester City this past summer. Bernardo Silva sets an example when not starting One of the clearest examples of Silva’s mentality came when he was not being selected in the starting line-up. Rather than complain about his role, he accepted the situation and focused on improving. He told those around him: “I need to be better. Clearly, the ones playing are better right now.” Bernardo Silva has won over the Real Madrid dressing room. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) Instead of allowing disappointment over selection to affect the dressing room, he directed his attention towards training and earning another opportunity. That willingness to accept competition is particularly valuable in a squad that has several high-profile players, where maintaining unity can be as important as managing individual expectations. Bernardo Silva praised Madrid’s squad connection Silva has also spoken publicly about the atmosphere at Valdebebas. Following his presentation, he described the group as having a “very good connection” and shared ambition. For what it is worth, his thoughts perfectly align with the view that is being shared regarding the Portuguese. As such, the dressing room really values Silva’s experience at Manchester City, where he played under Pep Guardiola for nine seasons, which has also given him an understanding of the demands involved in competing for titles. Bernardo Silva’s growing role at Real Madrid Bernardo Silva’s resurgence under Mourinho has strengthened his Real Madrid influence. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) Silva’s composure and ability to control possession provide Mourinho with an experienced option in central areas. His tactical intelligence can help Jose Mourinho manage pressure and maintain structure, while allowing more attacking teammates like Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler to focus on creating and finishing chances. Statistically, Bernardo Silva has made 15 appearances this season, clocking 868 minutes, while scoring one goal and one assist across all competitions. Understandably, those numbers do not tell the full story of his influence, as his role is more about giving his team a reliable connection between phases, helping the team retain composure and making the midfield function with greater control.

title: Schalke 04’s Loris Karius plays coy on Bayern Munich transfer links
summary: Bayern are yet to contact Karius and his agent.
content: Photo by Rene Nijhuis/MB Media/Getty Images | Getty Images Loris Karius’s career hit a downward spiral following his 2017/18 Champions League Final mishap with Liverpool. After losing confidence, he had a two-year loan spell at Beşiktaş, followed by stints at Union Berlin, Newcastle United, and a return to Liverpool. Eventually, Karius landed at 2. Bundesliga side Schalke 04, where he rebuilt his confidence. Last season, he helped Die Königsblauen capture the 2. Bundesliga title and earn promotion back to Germany’s top flight for the first time since the 2022/23 season. Now, the German shot-stopper is putting together a strong campaign with Schalke—and has caught Bayern Munich’s attention. The rumors linking Karius to Bavaria caught many off guard, including the goalkeeper himself. “I heard about it just like you did,” Karius said (as reported by @iMiaSanMia ). “It’s not my place to comment on rumors, and this isn’t the right occasion for that either. I haven’t spoken to anyone. My day-to-day work here is demanding enough as it is. I feel very comfortable at Schalke and really enjoy playing here. We have a lot to look forward to in the coming weeks, so my full focus is on that.” Karius m ay not know much about Bayern’s interest right now, though he’ll have plenty to think about if Die Rekordmeister decides he’s the right veteran option to back up Jonas Urbig next season. title: SCU Torreense vs Celtic – Jota and Duran can be difference makers
summary: Celtic play in Portugal tonight knowing that anything other than victory could seriously damage their hopes of reaching the Europa League knockout stages…Volnei Feltes of SCU Torreense in action dur...
content: SCU Torreense vs Celtic – Jota and Duran can be difference makers Celtic play in Portugal tonight knowing that anything other than victory could seriously damage their hopes of reaching the Europa League knockout stages… Volnei Feltes of SCU Torreense in action during the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Sunderland AFC at Estadio Municipal de Leiria on October 15, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) Standing in their way is an unusual opponent: SCU Torreense, a second-division Portuguese side who have surprised many with their performances in European football’s secondary competition this season. Torreense come into the game in 19th place in the table after two victories and two defeats at the half way stage, compared to Celtic being 32nd in the table with one win and three defeats. Dany Jean of SCU Torreense in action during the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Sunderland AFC at Estadio Municipal de Leiria on October 15, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) The Portuguese minnows are the first team since Wigan in 2013/2014 to be in the second division in their country and be playing in Europa League football. This difference in league positions highlights how important a win is this evening for Martin O’Neill’s side. With Celtic already playing in Portugal this season losing 4-1 to Benfica and looking for their first win in Portugal since 2003. Celtic manager Martin O’Neill arrives prior to the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Kilmarnock at Celtic Park on November 08, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) The Celtic manager Martin O’Neill has also admitted it’s now something of an uphill task for the club to qualify for the knockout stages, and insists his side need to take at least four points from the next two games. Following Mika Baur’s long term ankle injury , Portuguese winger Jota has replaced him in Celtic’s Europa league squad. Jota will relish the unexpected chance to particulate in the group stages of the Europa League, especially on his home soil and he might well be the difference maker for the Hoops this evening Celtic’s European form Celtic’s European performances this season have been really poor. Last time out in the Europa League it was one of Celtic’s better performances this season with a 3-2 win over Besiktas. as substitutes Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran’s double helped Celtic gain all three points, possibly against the odds. Celtic have had two out of their other Europa League performances at Celtic Park with a 3-1 defeat to Hungarian side Ferencvaros a night where Celtic dominated the ball with 63% possession. Also having an xG of 1.30, with 16 shots and 38 touches in the opposition box. Camilo Duran of Celtic scores his team’s third goal under pressure from Ridvan Yilmaz and Emirhan Topcu during the UEFA Europa League match between Celtic FC and Besiktas JK at Celtic Park on November 05, 2026. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images) Compared to the Besiktas game where Celtic had 39% possession and an xG of 1.19 with 10 shots and 13 touches in the opposition box. This shows the difference in Celtic’s finishing and how much more clinical they were against Besiktas than Ferencvaros. Celtic’s speed of play from midfield to attack and when around the box against Besiktas was much better than it was against Ferencvaros, with Besiktas more open and having the willingness to come and play, compared to Ferencvaros. Who were tight and compact and hit Celtic effectively on the counter. October 15, 2026, Lisbon, Portugal: Colby Donovan L of Celtic FC and Gianluca Prestianni R of SL Benfica seen in action during the UEFA Europa League Matchday 2 between SL Benfica and Celtic FC at Estadio da Luz Stadium. Final score SL Benfica 4 :1 Celtic FC Lisbon Portugal – Photo Hugo Amaral IMAGO Celtic’s two other defeats in the Europa League were against Celta Vigo at home (1-2) and Benfica away (4-1). In the Celta Vigo game, Celta had more clear attacking involvements and were lucky to have only scored twice on the night. With Celta Vigo having 56% possession, an xG of 1.30, 22 shots and four shots on target. Highlighting how many chances teams seem to be creating against Celtic. Especially, with the quality on the European stage it only takes one chance to change the game. Camilo Duran of Celtic FC looks on during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between SL Benfica vs Celtic FC at Estádio do Lisboa e Benfica on October 15th,2026 Photo by Joao Bravo/Sports IMAGO Then against Benfica away, Celtic were completely outclassed, with Benfica having 53% possession, 3.18 xG, 26 shots, seven on target and 46 touches in the opposition box. With familiar foe Jhon Duran scoring two goals and causing Celtic problems all game. SCU Torreense’s threat Torreense currently sit 14th in the second division of Portuguese football with two wins, four draws and four defeats. They currently sit four points from bottom and two points from the relegation spots. However, in the Europa League it’s a different story currently sitting in 19th place with two victories and two defeats, only one point from the top eight. Manuel Pozo of SCU Torreense in action during the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Sunderland AFC at Estadio Municipal de Leiria on October 15, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) All seven of Torreense goals in the Europa league have come from open play, with an xG of 4.5 across four games. Highlighting they are over performing in XG. Their first win came away to Norwegian side Lillestrøm with a 2-1 victory. With European top scorer and danger man Manuel Pozo doubling their lead in the 49th minute after midfielder Alejandro Alfaro had opened the scoring in the 23rd minute. Then in the 79th minute the home team pulled a goal back through Thomas Lehne Olsen. In the 86th minute Nuha Jatta was showing a second yellow card. The home side dominated the game throughout with 67% possession and 25 shots with 6 on target, an xG of 2.58 also showed how wasteful the home team were, with 31 touches in the opposition box. Compared to Torreense 11 shots with 3 on target, with an xG of 1.52, with 11 touches in the opposition box, showing how clinical the visitors were, further highlighting their over performance in xG. In their second victory against Armenian side Ararat Armenia they ran out 3-2 victories. Inside 13 minutes the hosts took the lead through striker Jorge Aguirre. Aguirre then went from hero to zero within nine minutes for getting a straight red card. Lucas Paes of SCU Torreense in action during the UEFA Europa League match between SCU Torreense and Sunderland AFC at Estadio Municipal de Leiria on October 15, 2026 in Leiria, Portugal. (Photo by Carlos Rodrigues/Getty Images) Then 19 minutes later the visitors were level through midfielder Karen Muradyan. Not long after the re-start the visitors took the lead through defender Bruno Wilson with a close range finish. Then in the 76th minute, goalkeeper João Bravim was shown a red card. Then, in the final two minutes Torreense scored twice to turn the game on its head with a goal in the 93rd and 95th minute to secure all three points. Key players and prediction Camilo Duran of Celtic celebrates with Jota after scoring. Celtic v St Mirren, Scottish Premiership, Celtic Park, 21 November 2026. Photo Mark Runnacles Shutterstock IMAGO The return of Jota into Celtic’s European squad will be massive for the visitors with his skills, flair and ball carrying skills something Celtic will need coming up against a tight compact European team. With his ability to take defenders and also get past his defenders can cause panic and while also make teams double up on him opening up spaces elsewhere on the pitch. Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain of Celtic celebrates scoring the opening goal of the game Celtic v St Mirren, Scottish Premiership, Celtic Park on 21 November 2026. Photo Mark Runnacles Shutterstock IMAGO It will also be a big game for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain who has been fantastic when playing for Celtic this season, however most of his games have been at home on the domestic front. So it will be pivotal for him to have a good game to ensure Celtic get all three points. The danger men for home side will top scorer Manuel Pozo and former Hearts striker Musa Drammeh who has scored in his last two appearances and will be looking to get one back for his former team as well after last season’s final day defeat. Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran of Celtic celebrate after the UEFA Europa League match between Celtic FC and Besiktas JK at Celtic Park on November 05, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) My prediction is a 2-1 win for Celtic, with Jota and top scorer Duran getting on the score sheet. I think Celtic’s attacking quality and speed up front with the return of Yang on the other side will be too much for the hosts to deal with especially with the creativity of Chamberlain and McGregor in the midfield. Something that will be key against the low block and compact home team. content: Spain beat Morocco to advance as U17 World Cup group winners Spain have beaten Morocco 2-0 in their final group-stage match at the U-17 World Cup, advancing to the round of 32 with a perfect record, 22 goals scored and none conceded. Morocco, meanwhile, finished second and also secured their place in the next round. As for the match itself, Spain controlled possession and dictated play from the start. The opening goal was not long in coming: in the 18th minute, Sergi Manyas set up Tunkara who fired home a powerful shot to make it 1-0. Tunkara is simply on another level. David García Cubillo's side went into the break in control of both the scoreline and the game. In the 60th minute, Guillermo Trujillano found himself one-on-one with the goalkeeper and scored Spain's second to extend their lead. La Roja remained in control until the final whistle and secured victory without much trouble. Spain end the group stage with a masterclass in football and continue to dream of lifting the World Cup, the only trophy missing from the Spanish national team's collection. title: Stats: Barcelona superstar Frenkie de Jong achieves remarkable passing milestone against Sabah
summary: Frenkie de Jong produced a remarkable passing performance in Barcelona’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Sabah, completing all 69 of his attempted passes during a 64-minute appearance. Hansi Flic...
content: Stats: Barcelona superstar Frenkie de Jong achieves remarkable passing milestone against Sabah Frenkie de Jong produced a remarkable passing performance in Barcelona’s 4-1 Champions League victory over Sabah, completing all 69 of his attempted passes during a 64-minute appearance. Hansi Flick once again deployed the Dutch midfielder at centre-back, using his composure and distribution to help Barcelona control proceedings in Azerbaijan. With defensive absences forcing Flick to explore alternative solutions, De Jong’s performance showed the tactical value of having a midfielder capable of organising possession from deep. Crucially, his display against Sabah followed a similar assignment in Barcelona’s 3-2 league victory over Villarreal . De Jong provides defensive security and exceptional accuracy De Jong had relatively little defensive work against Sabah, whose attacking approach lacked the directness to consistently trouble Barcelona’s back line. He recorded three defensive actions, made a clearance and produced an important interception during a counterattack down the left. Alongside Gerard Martin, the Dutchman remained alert whenever Barcelona needed to defend, but his greatest influence came through his distribution. Statistically, on that note, De Jong has completed 232 of his 236 passes across his last three appearances while playing in defence against Atletico Madrid, Villarreal and Sabah, recording a remarkable 98.3% success rate. Against Sabah, he was perfect, completing 51 of 51 passes in his own half and 18 of 18 in the opposition half. Barcelona midfielder achieves Champions League passing milestone Notably, the 69 successful passes he achieved is now the fifth-highest total by a Barcelona player in a single Champions League match without a misplaced pass since at least the 2003-04 season. For what it is worth, De Jong’s performance was particularly impressive given the responsibility of playing in defence and not in his usual midfield position. His ability to receive possession under pressure and distribute accurately allowed Barcelona to maintain their rhythm and prevent Sabah from gaining sustained momentum. Frenkie de Jong had 100% passing accuracy vs Sabah. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Ultimately, De Jong was substituted in the 64th minute, allowing Barça Atlètic defender Alex Campos to make his first-team debut. Flick gains a valuable tactical option from deep Barcelona dominated possession with 72% of the ball and completed 689 passes against Sabah, reinforcing their position among the Champions League’s leading passing teams. On that note, De Jong’s role was crucial as it offered Flick a solution that is certainly not limited to covering a defensive vacancy. Rather, his positioning allows Barcelona to build attacks through a player who understands midfield spaces, while his passing range helps dictate the tempo from the back. Simply put, the Dutchman is effectively operating as a deep-lying organiser, combining the responsibilities of a centre-back with the distribution qualities of a midfielder.

title: Trouble at Bayern! CEO responds after Joshua Kimmich blasts club bosses over Jamal Musiala treatment
summary: Bayern Munich CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen has attempted to cool tensions at the Allianz Arena following an explosive outburst from Joshua Kimmich. The midfielder publicly condemned the club hierarchy for their treatment of Jamal Musiala after a disappointing European night.
content: FC Bayern München v RB Leipzig - Telekom Cup - Getty Images Sport Bayern Munich CEO Jan-Christian Dreesen has attempted to cool tensions at the Allianz Arena following an explosive outburst from Joshua Kimmich. The midfielder publicly condemned the club hierarchy for their treatment of Jamal Musiala after a disappointing European night. Internal friction at the Allianz Arena The atmosphere at Bayern Munich has turned sour following a series of public disagreements involving the club's senior leadership and its most influential players. Dreesen has now stepped in to address the growing unrest after Kimmich launched a scathing attack on how the board has handled the situation surrounding Musiala . The tension comes at a difficult time for the Bavarian giants, who are looking to maintain stability despite mounting external pressure. Speaking to the Abendzeitung newspaper, Dreesen made it clear that he wants to move the conversation away from the public eye. The CEO is eager to ensure that the club's internal business remains private, especially given the sensitivity of the topics involved. 'I want to leave it at what I've said elsewhere. We need to focus on taking care of things, not just talking. We want to resolve this internally,' Dreesen informed the news outlet, signalling a desire for silence. Kimmich defends his teammate Comments made recently by Bayern Munich figures Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have sparked controversy, with both casting doubt on Musiala's ability to return to his previous level following his neurological condition and questioning the German international's salary. The 23-year-old has since received support from several quarters, including teammate Kimmich, who delivered an emotional message in his defence following Bayern's 2-1 Champions League defeat to LOSC Lille on Wednesday. 'Generally speaking, you have to look at the situation from different perspectives. I have absolute understanding for the fact that this is not an easy situation for a club either,' Kimmich said in the mixed zone. A breakdown in communication The core of Kimmich's frustration lies in the perceived lack of protection for the individual player. Musiala has endured a difficult 2026-27 campaign, with the 23-year-old midfielder collapsing twice during pre-season matches in August before revealing that he had been diagnosed with a treatable neurological condition that causes brief 'absence seizures'. Although doctors confirmed that the condition poses no long-term risk to his career, Kimmich argued that while Bayern Munich is historically larger than any individual, this should not justify exposing a player to public scrutiny during such a vulnerable period. 'What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated publicly. It must never happen that a player is made to bear the brunt of it. Of course, the club always comes first and is bigger than us as players, but it's not bigger than the person. And that's an absolute no-go. It's also not the Bayern way. Especially at this particular time, when I've often emphasised how special this club is,' Kimmich added during his passionate address to the media. Demanding a return to unity Kimmich further reflected on his own experiences at the club to highlight why the recent developments felt so foreign to him, with Bayern Munich currently sitting second in the Bundesliga, just two points behind leaders Borussia Dortmund. They are also 15th in the Champions League standings, two points adrift of eighth place, which represents the final automatic qualification spot for the round of 16. 'Even in my own situation, the club was incredibly special . You could really feel that this sense of togetherness was being lived out. What happened now is something that simply must never happen in this way. I find it completely incomprehensible,' Kimmich concluded.

title: Nike vs Adidas: What the Champions League Ball Deal Means for Football’s Biggest Sportswear Brands
summary: Nike vs Adidas is once again a major talking point in football following confirmation that the American sportswear giant will replace its German rival as the official match-ball supplier for UEFA’s men’s club competitions from the 2027/28 season. The agreement, announced on November 16, 2026, will run until 2031 and brings an end to Adidas’s long-standing association with the UEFA Champions League. However, the deal covers considerably more than Europe’s biggest club competition, with Nike also
content: Nike vs Adidas is once again a major talking point in football following confirmation that the American sportswear giant will replace its German rival as the official match-ball supplier for UEFA’s men’s club competitions from the 2027/28 season. The agreement, announced on November 16, 2026, will run until 2031 and brings an end to Adidas’s long-standing association with the UEFA Champions League. However, the deal covers considerably more than Europe’s biggest club competition, with Nike also taking responsibility for the official match balls used in the UEFA Europa League and Conference League. It is another significant development in the battle between two of football’s biggest sportswear brands, but what does it mean for their respective positions in the game? Nike vs Adidas: The End of a 26-Year Champions League Partnership Adidas has supplied the official Champions League match ball since 2001, becoming closely associated with the competition through its iconic star-patterned designs. Over the years, the German manufacturer has introduced several different versions of the ball, with its designs becoming a familiar part of European football. The partnership has also helped Adidas maintain a strong presence across the competition, with its branding visible throughout matches involving some of the biggest clubs in the world. However, that relationship will come to an end after the 2026/27 season, with Nike securing the agreement following a competitive tender process launched by UC3 and its agency, Relevent Football Partners, in March 2026. For Nike vs Adidas, this represents a notable shift in the commercial landscape of European football. Nike is no stranger to the Champions League, having previously supplied the competition’s match ball before Adidas took over in 2001. Its return after more than two decades therefore represents something of a full-circle moment. The agreement will also see Nike become the first manufacturer to supply the official match balls for all three UEFA men’s club competitions simultaneously. What Does the Deal Mean for Nike and Adidas? The new agreement covers the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League, alongside the UEFA Super Cup, UEFA Youth League and UEFA Futsal Champions League. This gives Nike a much wider presence across European club football than simply supplying the ball for Champions League fixtures. For Nike vs Adidas, the importance of the agreement goes beyond the product itself. Unlike an individual club sponsorship, where a manufacturer receives exposure through a particular team’s matches, supplying the official competition ball creates visibility across fixtures involving clubs with different kit manufacturers. Whether a team wears Nike, Adidas, PUMA or another brand, the official match ball will carry Nike’s identity from the 2027/28 season. That is a particularly valuable position for the American company, which has been looking to strengthen its presence in football. The agreement also provides an opportunity to showcase its football technology and product development to a global audience, with the match ball featuring in some of the sport’s biggest fixtures. Nike has already described the deal as a long-term commitment to football, with its Vice President and General Manager of Football, Camilo Andrade, highlighting the importance of innovation while respecting the traditions of UEFA’s competitions. For Adidas, meanwhile, losing the Champions League is a significant change, particularly given how closely the brand has been associated with the competition for more than two decades. However, this does not mean Adidas is losing its wider position in football. The company remains involved in some of the sport’s biggest competitions and continues to supply official match balls for major international tournaments, including the FIFA World Cup and UEFA European Championship. The Nike vs Adidas rivalry will therefore continue, even if the two companies are taking different positions across European club and international football. SPI_040_DK_Madrid_Juve SPI-4001-0040 Will Nike Change the Iconic Champions League Ball? One of the more interesting aspects of the announcement is what Nike’s match balls will actually look like. Adidas’s Champions League designs have become almost as recognisable as the competition itself, particularly because of the distinctive star pattern that has featured on its balls since the beginning of the partnership. For many supporters, the design has become part of the Champions League’s identity, making the change of manufacturer an interesting prospect. Nike has yet to reveal its designs for the 2027/28 season, with further details expected in due course. It will be interesting to see whether the company retains elements of the familiar Champions League aesthetic or introduces something completely different. What Happens Next in the Nike vs Adidas Rivalry? The agreement is another reminder of how competitive the football equipment market has become. Nike continues to invest in its football presence through club partnerships, player sponsorships and product development, while Adidas remains one of the most influential brands in the sport. For Nike vs Adidas, the Champions League agreement represents an important commercial victory for the American company, particularly given the visibility that comes with supplying the official match ball. However, it would be premature to suggest that this deal changes the balance of power between the two brands entirely. Adidas still has a significant presence across international football, while Nike will need to demonstrate that it can make the most of its new UEFA partnerships once they come into effect. Extra Time Notes Ultimately, the success of the agreement will not simply be measured by how often supporters see the Nike logo during Champions League matches. The quality of the products, the reception of the new designs and the company’s ability to turn that visibility into stronger connections with football supporters will all matter. For now, Nike has secured a major position in European club football, bringing an end to one of Adidas’s longest-running associations with the game. The next chapter in the Nike vs Adidas rivalry could look very different, and it will be interesting to see what both companies do from here. title: Sixers Co-Owner Wants Philly’s New Arena to Be Worth a Night Out
summary: Adelman told FOS he wants it to be more than a sports venue.
content: Sixers co-owner David Adelman wants Philadelphia’s next arena to be more than just a sports venue. “You want to create an experience for people,” Adelman, a limited partner in Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment, told Front Office Sports editor-in-chief Dan Roberts on an upcoming episode of Portfolio Players . “It’s a night out, right? So, if you’re getting a babysitter, and mom and dad are going out—like give them something pre-game, pre-concert. Give them a great event inside the concert, but give them something to do afterwards, too.” Adelman, who got his start in residential real estate, pointed toward the success of The Battery, the Braves’ mixed-use development , as a model, not just for how to plan new stadiums and arenas , but also for how these venues support the surrounding community. “They built that to service—there’s something like 11 million square feet of office that doesn’t have a place to go for lunch in that surrounding area,” Adelman said. “So they’re filling a need. And so you can have the people walking around before a game, but it serves other people as well.” While other cities might be trying to perfect the mixed-use model, it was pioneered in New England at Patriot Place. “They really built a kind of a city,” Adelman said, pointing out how the area directly surrounding Gillette Stadium supports retail, restaurants, hotels, and a hospital. In Philadelphia, the Sixers and Flyers announced a 50-50 joint venture to build a new arena to replace the Xfinity Mobile Arena, which originally opened in 1996. Currently, the Sixers are tenants in that venue, wholly owned by Flyers parent company Comcast Spectacor. The new arena, which is estimated to cost $1.5 billion , will also be home to Philadelphia’s forthcoming WNBA team, making it what Adelman calls “the first purpose-built building for three teams.” The WNBA team and the arena will both make their debut in 2030. The South Philly arena announcement came in January 2025 after a dramatic, three-year push by HSBE to build the Sixers a $1.3 billion arena called 76 Place at Market East along a long-beleaguered commercial corridor in Center City Philadelphia. Critics of that proposal had expressed concern that the arena’s location on Market Street, near the city’s historic Chinatown section, would lead to residents and business owners being priced out of the area. Along with the new arena development, planned on the former site of Philadelphia’s legendary Spectrum , HSBE and Comcast jointly spent $56 million to buy two land parcels along Market Street where the Sixers had been proposing their Center City arena. “When we announced coming together with Comcast and the Flyers and pivoting to the Sports Complex, [we] made a commitment to the city that we would still do some development there,” Adelman tells FOS . After plans for the arena collapsed, the city formed an advisory group to determine how to develop the area . Mayor Cherelle Parker recently said she wants to see 2,000 residential units in the area . HSBE and Comcast have not yet revealed their long-term plans for the properties they now own, but during the World Cup, street-level storefronts were converted to a string of pop-up shops that will run through the end of the year. title: Alex Eala shares how it feels to be a part of a golden generation of sport in the Philippines, ‘we’re all excelling’
summary: Alexandra Eala’s season may be officially over, but she is far from enjoying the relaxation she has earned. After all, her schedule is perhaps the...
content: Alexandra Eala’s season may be officially over, but she is far from enjoying the relaxation she has earned. After all, her schedule is perhaps the most relentless on the WTA Tour, given what a national treasure she has become in such a short space of time in the Philippines. Having shot from seemingly relative obscurity to instant superstardom during the 2024 Miami Open, since then, this youngster has only continued to build on that stunning foundation. Now, she sits at a career-high ranking, having just enjoyed her best-ever run at two Grand Slam events, beaten countless top ten players, and won her first WTA Tour-level trophy too. However, with each new milestone comes added pressure, particularly given how important Alexandra Eala has already proven herself to sport in the Philippines. Speaking at her recent homecoming, she reiterated this point about pressure, whilst also heralding the new wave of talent propping up sport in her home country. Alexandra Eala explains what is difficult about achieving a career-high ranking this year Speaking to reporters during a press conference at the Pasig Central Elementary School earlier this week, Eala began with a word on her ranking. After all, the 21-year-old actually managed to sneak into 15th before the WTA season had officially concluded, a new career-high ranking. Discussing this new peak, Eala admitted there is a difficulty that comes with reaching such heights. She claimed: “Of course, it’s very difficult. The higher you go on the mountain, the steeper it gets. “So I’m definitely not expecting anything easy. Nothing fulfilling ever really comes easily. So I’ll do my best to stay there, and hopefully get even better.” Then, discussing sports in the Philippines in general, Eala added: “Of course, sports in general [is in a very good time], but I think women’s sports is having a moment right now. “So, to be part of a generation of such great athletes where we’re all excelling on the world stage, that’s an amazing thing, I believe, for the youth. “And it’s a testament to, it doesn’t matter where you come from or it doesn’t matter how you get there, it’s just that you’re able to get there.” Eala also had a message for her fans ahead of her exhibition match in the Philippines , which will take place just next month. She is also up for a WTA award that has previously been won by Serena Williams and Maria Sharapova .

title: Australian Open chief officially confirms Jannik Sinner will miss 2027 event after speaking to his team
summary: Jannik Sinner has officially been confirmed to miss the 2027 Australian Open. Tennis fans were already expecting the Italian to miss out on the opening...
content: Jannik Sinner has officially been confirmed to miss the 2027 Australian Open. Tennis fans were already expecting the Italian to miss out on the opening Grand Slam of the season, with Sinner having undergone knee surgery earlier this week. But his impending absence has now been made official by Tennis Australia chief Andrew Abdo. Jannik Sinner confirmed to miss 2027 Australian Open AFP have received a statement from the Tennis Australia chief, which reads: “We’ve been in regular touch with Jannik’s team and they’ve confirmed he won’t be joining us for the AO in January following his recent surgery. “Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028. We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon.” It’s a big blow for the Australian Open to take place without one of the biggest stars of the game, with everyone from fans to his fellow players impacted. Many fans will be gutted not to see the five-time Grand Slam champion in Melbourne, particularly given that two of his titles have arrived there. However, perhaps many of his ATP rivals will be breathing a sigh of relief given that historical success. Alexander Zverev stepped up in his absence and the absence of Carlos Alcaraz throughout the 2026 Grand Slam season, and there is now an opportunity to do the same without Sinner at the Australian Open. What is Jannik Sinner’s Australian Open record? The Italian has made seven appearances at the hard-court major, from which he boasts two titles and a 27-5 win-loss record. He first lifted the prestigious trophy in 2024 after a final victory over Daniil Medvedev, and went on to defend his title in 2025 by beating Zverev. This season the former world number one reached the semifinals, where he was beaten by Novak Djokovic in a five-set thriller. His ATP rival Carlos Alcaraz then defeated the Serbian to claim the title and indeed complete the career Grand Slam. Sinner can follow in the footsteps of the Spaniard by winning the French Open, but it remains to be seen if he will be fit enough to take on the clay-court Grand Slam in Paris next year. For now, his rehabilitation following surgery will be well underway, with Alcaraz among the players wishing Sinner well after the procedure.

title: GB win decider to reach Davis Cup semi-finals
summary: Great Britain advance to the semi-finals of the Davis Cup for the first time since 2019 as Henry Patten and Neal Skupski win a decisive doubles tie against Germany in Bologna.
content: Great Britain advanced to the semi-finals of the Davis Cup for the first time since 2019 as Henry Patten and Neal Skupski won a decisive doubles tie against third seeds Germany in Bologna. Patten and Skupski, playing together for the first time since announcing their partnership for the 2027 season, proved too clinical for Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz. They converted two break points and saved five in the first set, before overturning a mini-break in the tie-break to win 6-2 7-6 (8-6). World number one Alexander Zverev had earlier sent the tie to a decider by defeating British number one Arthur Fery in straight sets to cancel out Cameron Norrie's three-set victory over Jan-Lennard Struff. A nerveless Norrie saved four break points in the fifth game of the third set and carried that momentum throughout the remainder of the match to win 6-3 3-6 6-2. Leon Smith's team will discover their semi-final opponent later on Thursday when Spain meet Austria, with their semi-final scheduled for Saturday. title: Great Britain’s Davis Cup captain responds after reporter suggests Cameron Norrie might ‘easily lose’ to Rafael Jodar
summary: Cameron Norrie and Rafael Jodar could meet in the Davis Cup semi-finals. Getting his side off to the perfect start, Norrie beat Jan-Lennard Struff in...
content: Cameron Norrie and Rafael Jodar could meet in the Davis Cup semi-finals. Getting his side off to the perfect start, Norrie beat Jan-Lennard Struff in the Davis Cup quarter-finals. Great Britain eventually beat Germany 2-1, booking their place in the semis, where they will meet Spain or Austria. Spain are, of course, the favourites to advance, with star players Carlos Alcaraz and Rafael Jodar in the team. If Spain play Great Britain in the semi-finals , Norrie will likely face Jodar. During Team GB’s latest press conference, a reporter mentioned Norrie had lost to Jodar ‘quite easily this year’ and asked captain Leon Smith what he expected and whether he agreed with that analysis. Leon Smith doesn’t think Rafael Jodar will ‘easily’ beat Cameron Norrie at the Davis Cup “If your analysis is that [Rafael] Jodar is going to win easily, no. I think Cam [Norrie], in an individual match, is more than capable,” said Smith in response to the journalist’s question. Smith has faith in Norrie should he play Jodar in the Davis Cup semi-finals, despite the 31-year-old’s head-to-head record against the man 11 years his junior. Norrie has never beaten, nor taken a set off Jodar in two attempts. Rafael Jodar and Cameron Norrie’s head-to-head record (2-0) 2026 Barcelona Open QF – Rafael Jodar defeated Cameron Norrie, 6-3, 6-2 2026 Mexican Open 1R – Rafael Jodar defeated Cameron Norrie, 6-3, 6-2 Smith continued to back his player, referencing Soonwoo Kwon’s shock win over Flavio Cobolli in Italy’s quarter-final against South Korea earlier in the week. “It’s very, very difficult. Look, Spain, when Carlos [Alcaraz] comes back and plays singles with Jodar, or [Daniel] Merida, if he plays as well. These are really good players. It’s a really, really strong team,” he said. “In a one-off match in Davis Cup, look what happened last night with [Soonwoo] Kwon against a top-tenner. It’s possible. With all due respect, I wouldn’t put Cam (ATP #52) in the same category as Kwon (ATP #139). It’s definitely possible. “It’s a big challenge. It’s something that Cam, Arthur [Fery], these two – this is why they’re here. This is it. Things happen when you play for your country. I’ve done this long enough to have seen favorites win matches, and I’ve seen our players, when they’re huge underdogs, win matches. “Look, we’ve done our job today. We’ll watch what happens tonight, and we’ll think more of that through the course of tomorrow. Yeah, we got a chance for sure; that’s what I think.” Leon Smith gives his verdict on how Cameron Norrie and Arthur Fery played in quarter-final win vs Germany Smith will need his singles players to deliver the goods when they return for their semi-final match, but how did they play in the quarters? Norrie won his match in a decider, but Arthur Fery lost to the world number one, Alexander Zverev, in straight sets. “Yeah, I’m genuinely really pleased for Cam. He’s talked quite, I think, pretty openly to us, hasn’t he, about how much this week has meant to him. I think he was due a good performance, then hopefully a win. He got that. He got both today. At 2-2, 0-40 was obviously a key moment in the match, and he got through it,” said Smith. Davis Cup QF – Great Britain (2-1) Germany Match Winner Loser Score Tie Score 1 Cameron Norrie (Great Britain) Jan-Lennard Struff (Germany) 6-3, 3-6, 6-2 Great Britain (1-0) Germany 2 Alexander Zverev (Germany) Arthur Fery (Great Britain) 6-3, 6-2 Great Britain (1-1) Germany 3 Henry Patten/Neal Skupski (Great Britain) Kevin Krawietz/Tim Putz (Germany) 6-2, 7-6 Great Britain (2-1) Germany Davis Cup QF result – Great Britain vs Germany “It was going to be a tough match anyway because [Jan-Lennard] Struff has been playing really well. He has got his ranking back up. Indoor swing, he’s done particularly well. So I’m just delighted for Cam. I think, yeah, he deserves that one today.” “And I think for Arthur, it was always going to be a big challenge. Like I said to him the last couple of days, you’ve earned that right to go out. If I said to him 12 months ago, By the way, you’re going to get three matches against [Alexander] Zverev this year, the world number one…. What, I’m 200 in the world 12 months ago. “Now he’s getting to play the number one player a few times in a year. Those reference points are going to be really important for him. He got two games against him in Vienna. Got more today. He’ll get more next time. He’ll just keep learning from it. He’s very studious about his game. He thinks a lot about it. He’ll figure out how to improve. “It’s not easy for him playing against someone 6’6″ when you feel so much pressure on your service games, and it’s tough to break. These are very important matches for him. As I’ve said, he’s earned those opportunities to do that.” Fery played Zverev for the first time in the Wimbledon semi-finals earlier this year, and has since lost another two matches against the German. He’ll need to put his latest defeat behind him as he sets his sights on the semi-finals, where he could take on Carlos Alcaraz.

title: How Great Britain performed the last time they reached the Davis Cup semi-finals
summary: Great Britain have advanced to the Davis Cup semi-finals for the first time since 2019 after defeating Germany on Thursday. Cameron Norrie gave the Brits...
content: Great Britain have advanced to the Davis Cup semi-finals for the first time since 2019 after defeating Germany on Thursday. Cameron Norrie gave the Brits an early lead in Bologna, Italy, beating Wimbledon quarter-finalist Jan-Lennard Struff 6-3, 3-6, 6-2. World number one Alexander Zverev then levelled the tie, defeating Arthur Fery 6-3, 6-2. Henry Patten and Neil Skupski – who are set to form a new doubles team from 2027 – secured victory for the British team, defeating Kevin Krawietz and Tim Puetz 6-2, 7-6. The 2026 British squad will play either Spain or Austria in the Davis Cup semi-finals. Spain defeated Great Britain in the 2019 Davis Cup semi-finals Great Britain advanced to the 2019 Davis Cup Finals after defeating Kazakhstan and the Netherlands in the group stage. The Brits triumphed 2-1 in both ties. Ironically, Britain were subsequently drawn against Germany in the quarter-finals – and once again, the island nation emerged victorious. Kyle Edmund – a former Australian Open semi-finalist who retired from his playing career in 2025 – defeated Philipp Kohlschreiber 6-3, 7-5 in the opening singles rubber. Dan Evans – who retired in controversial circumstances earlier this year – sealed victory for the Brits with a 7-6, 3-6, 7-6 victory against Jan-Lennard Struff. Britain advanced to the semi-finals, where they would face Spain. 2026 Davis Cup quarter-finals Czechia defeated Canada 2-0 Italy defeated South Korea 2-1 Great Britain defeated Germany 2-1 Spain vs Austria Edmund again gave Britain the early lead, beating Feliciano Lopez 6-3, 7-6. Rafael Nadal then levelled the tie after defeating Dan Evans 6-4, 6-0. Britain ultimately suffered defeat in heartbreaking circumstances – Lopez and Nadal combined to defeat Jamie Murray and Neal Skupski 7-6, 7-6. Which nation won the 2019 Davis Cup? With victory over Great Britain, Spain set up a clash with Canada in the final. Canada – a nation that had never won the Davis Cup, fielded the likes of Felix Auger-Aliassime, Denis Shapovalov and Vasek Pospisil. Roberto Bautista Agut secured an early advantage for his nation by defeating Auger-Aliassime 7-6, 6-3. Nadal then secured Spain’s sixth title in 20 years after beating Shapovalov 6-3, 7-6. Nadal was named the Most Valuable Player [MVP] of the 2019 Finals. Photo by Burak Akbulut/Anadolu Agency via Getty Images “I could not be happier,” Nadal said in the aftermath. “It has been an unforgettable moment in this amazing stadium, we can’t thank the crowd enough. Our team spirit prevails.”

title: What happened the last time Jannik Sinner did not play the Australian Open as he’s confirmed to miss 2027 tournament
summary: Jannik Sinner is confirmed not to be playing the Australian Open next year. Sinner has been out of action with a right knee injury since...
content: Jannik Sinner is confirmed not to be playing the Australian Open next year. Sinner has been out of action with a right knee injury since winning Wimbledon in July, which subsequently forced him to announce that he was ending his season early. After the injury continued to persist, Sinner underwent surgery on his knee in Turku, Finland, which is reported to have been successful. Despite this, it has now been confirmed by Tennis Australia’s Chief Executive, Andrew Abdo, that Sinner will not be at the Australian Open next year, with it being his first time missing the tournament since 2019. Jannik Sinner last missed playing the Australian Open in 2019 The Australian Open has been a special tournament for Sinner in his career, as the first major where he ever won a main draw match and also his first Grand Slam title, which he won in 2024, before defending his title in 2025. Sinner was unable to capture a third successive Australian Open title this year, having lost to Novak Djokovic in a thrilling four-hour plus semi-final. Despite this, Sinner has still been part of every Australian Open this decade, with the 2027 event the first he will be missing. Year Jannik Sinner’s result at the Australian Open 2020 Second Round 2021 First Round 2022 Quarter-final 2023 Fourth Round 2024 Won the title 2025 Won the title 2026 Semi-final The last time Sinner was not at the Australian Open was in 2019, which was when he was just 17 years old and had not even played his first ATP Tour match. Sinner was ranked outside the world’s top 500 at the time, and was not even able to get into qualifying, something he did for the first time later that year at Wimbledon, before making his Grand Slam main draw debut at the US Open . With Sinner yet to establish himself in men’s tennis at the time of the 2019 Australian Open, it was another familiar face who would triumph in Melbourne that year. Djokovic had already won six titles at the Australian Open before that year, with the Serbian dropping just two sets en route to another final at his most successful major tournament, where he would go on to beat his great rival Rafael Nadal 6-3, 6-2, 6-3. This was a hugely significant win for Djokovic, as it meant that he had become the first man to win seven Australian Open singles titles, moving ahead of both Roger Federer and Roy Emerson. Djokovic would go on to win three consecutive Australian Open titles, before winning a record 10th at the Melbourne major in 2023. How will Jannik Sinner missing the Australian Open impact his ranking? Although Sinner did not win the Australian Open last year, his confirmed absence from the 2027 tournament will still have a notable impact on his ranking. Sinner has not played a single match since July, but he still remains the world number two after his dominant start to the 2026 season, which saw him win five consecutive Masters 1000 titles, as well as defending his Wimbledon crown. There is still a chance that Sinner will remain in this position after the Australian Open, with only Carlos Alcaraz and Ben Shelton able to overtake him. Alcaraz won the Australian Open last year and would need to defend his title if he is to leapfrog Sinner, with no other planned tournaments on the Spaniard’s schedule ahead of the Melbourne major. Shelton is confirmed to be playing in the United Cup as well as the Australian Open, but the American would need to win both if he is to become the world number two. ATP Rankings Current ranking points Confirmed ranking points after the Australian Open 1. Alexander Zverev 10,350 9,510 2. Jannik Sinner 7,950 7,150 3. Carlos Alcaraz 7,600 5,600 4. Ben Shelton 5,570 5,120 5. Daniil Medvedev 4,220 3,770 Although Sinner will still be a top-three player after the Australian Open, he may still be out of competition for more weeks and even months at the start of 2027. This is when Sinner picked up most of his points earlier this year, and could see him fall down the rankings before he does play another match again.

title: Henry Patten and Neal Skupski discuss potentially playing Carlos Alcaraz in Davis Cup doubles, ‘It will be fantastic’
summary: Great Britain could meet Spain in the Davis Cup semi-finals. The world expected Spain to play Germany in the last four, but Leon Smith’s side...
content: Great Britain could meet Spain in the Davis Cup semi-finals. The world expected Spain to play Germany in the last four, but Leon Smith’s side had other plans. A 2-1 win over Germany sent Great Britain through to the Davis Cup semi-finals for the first time since 2019. They will play Spain, provided Carlos Alcaraz’s side advances past Austria in their quarter-final. Alcaraz isn’t playing singles against Austria, but will step in for doubles if necessary. With Alcaraz set for doubles action in Bologna, how do Great Britain’s doubles stars, Henry Patten and Neal Skupski, feel about potentially taking on the seven-time Grand Slam champion? Henry Patten would ‘relish the chance’ to play Carlos Alcaraz in doubles “Obviously, yeah, it will be fantastic. I would really relish the chance to play against Carlos [Alcaraz]. I think he’s quite a good tennis player!” said Patten during his quarter-final post-match press conference. “He doesn’t play doubles too often, so that will be interesting to see. Obviously, we would try to use our doubles skills to try to combat his athleticism and shot-making. Yeah, that would be something really to look forward to. I think Neal [Skupski] has played before.” Carlos Alcaraz’s last 10 doubles/mixed doubles matches (6-4) 2026 Laver Cup (w/Jakub Mensik) [WIN] vs Alexander Bublik/Taylor Fritz, 6-4, 6-4 2026 US Open QF (w/Serena Williams) [LOSS] vs Flavio Cobolli/Belinda Bencic, 4-5, 1-4 2026 US Open 1R (w/Serena Williams) [WIN] vs Lloyd Glasspool/Erin Routliffe, 5-3, 4-1 2025 Laver Cup (w/Casper Ruud) [WIN] vs Alex Michelsen/Reilly Opelka, 7-6, 6-1 2025 Laver Cup (w/Jakub Mensik) [WIN] vs Taylor Fritz/Alex Michelsen, 7-6, 6-4 2025 US Open 1R (w/Emma Raducanu) [LOSS] vs Jack Draper/Jessica Pegula, 2-4, 2-4 2024 Davis Cup QF (w/Marcel Granollers) [LOSS] vs Wesley Koolhof/Botic van de Zandschulp, 6-7, 6-7 2024 Laver Cup (w/Casper Ruud) [WIN] vs Ben Shelton/Frances Tiafoe, 6-2, 7-6 2024 Laver Cup (w/Alexander Zverev) [LOSS] vs Taylor Fritz/Ben Shelton, 6-7, 4-6 2024 Davis Cup (w/Marcel Granollers) [WIN] vs Jakub Mensik/Adam Pavlasek, 6-7, 6-3, 7-6 Before Skupski could give his thoughts on Alcaraz, whom he played at the 2022 Madrid Open (Skupski and Wesley Koolhof defeated Alcaraz and Marcel Granollers, 6-3, 3-6, 10-7), Smith interjected, making it clear that he and his players weren’t disrespecting Austria, Spain’s quarter-final opponents. “Before he answers, I really do want to stress the point: this is not us talking about Spain. I don’t particularly like it. I think there are a couple of points that can go either way. Italy got through (2-1 vs South Korea) last night. Everyone was saying that wasn’t possible. So, however this is quoted, talked about, this is not us talking about playing Spain. Like I said, last night it was a flip of a coin. Could have gone either way. Just on that one. Sorry. Over to you talk about doubles. I think Neal has played Carlos before,” said Smith. “I played Carlos before, many years ago in Madrid. I’ve played Marcel [Granollers]. Henry has played Marcel. Amazing player. Amazing doubles players. Singles career also. They won’t be easy to beat if we do eventually play them. Obviously they’ve got to play Austria tonight. They are no easy feat. They’ve got a great doubles team as well in [Lucas] Miedler and [Neil] Oberleitner, who won Shanghai. They would be very difficult to beat if they get on the court tonight,” said Skupski. “We have to be prepared for whoever we play against. We’ll watch the match tonight and study some stuff tomorrow, ready for the match on Saturday. But yeah, we’ll be ready. Very much looking forward to whoever we face on Saturday.” Henry Patten and Neal Skupski remain unbeaten after new partnership announcement Not long after he finished the year world number one with Harri Heliovaara, Patten confirmed Skupski as his partner for 2027 . The move shocked many, but the early signs are positive for Patten and Skupski. Patten and Skupski first partnered up at the 2024 Davis Cup, when they beat Canada’s Gabriel Diallo and Alexis Galarneau 7-6, 6-4 in Manchester, Great Britain. They played together again in September this year, when Great Britain defeated Ecuador to qualify for the Davis Cup Finals. The British duo beat Gonzalo Escobar and Diego Hidalgo, 6-3, 6-4. Now 3-0 together, Patten and Skupski will not only fancy their chances of winning the Davis Cup later this week but also on the doubles tour next year. Both players won Grand Slams with their partners in 2026 and will be keen to add to their respective tallies in 2027.

title: Jannik Sinner ruled out of Australian Open after knee surgery
summary: The World No 2 has not played since defending his Wimbledon title
content: Jannik Sinner will miss the Australian Open after undergoing knee surgery . The World No 2 has not played since defending his Wimbledon title in July and will now miss the first grand slam tournament of 2027. Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo said in a statement: “We’ve been in regular touch with Jannik’s team and they’ve confirmed he won’t be joining us for the Australian Open in January following his recent surgery. “Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for the Australian Open in 2028.” The Italian confirmed on Tuesday he had undergone minor surgery after experiencing ongoing pain in his right knee. Sinner said in a statement earlier this week: “Over the past few months, together with my team, we’ve tried everything to treat my injury without surgery. “After some very encouraging progress early on, my knee unfortunately didn’t respond as we had all hoped, that’s why today I underwent a minor surgery to improve the condition of my iliotibial band. “I really miss being on court and will now begin my recovery process together with my team.” The iliotibial band is a thick band of fibrous connective tissue running down the outside of the thigh, and injuries associated with it are typically caused by overuse. Prior to his injury, the 25-year-old had a stellar start to 2026 which saw him win the first five Masters 1000 tournaments of the year, becoming the second man after Novak Djokovic to achieve the Golden Masters. His absence has allowed Alexander Zverev to overtake him in the world rankings, with Carlos Alcaraz in third place. Both men shared their well-wishes after Sinner’s surgery. “The decision of making the surgery, I think his team made a good decision. He’s young, has a lot of years ahead of him. I’m sure he’s going to come back even stronger, even better,” Alcaraz said on Wednesday. Zverev added: “”We know that he’s mentally strong. I hope that he takes every step serious and that, in three, four months’ time, he can be back to 100 per cent and be back playing.”

title: Patrick Mouratoglou says if he thinks Alexander Zverev really is the best player in the world after ATP Finals loss
summary: Alexander Zverev will start the 2027 season as the world number one after recording an outstanding campaign this year. Zverev clinched his first Grand Slam...
content: Alexander Zverev will start the 2027 season as the world number one after recording an outstanding campaign this year. Zverev clinched his first Grand Slam title at Roland Garros in early June, taking advantage of a wide-open draw in Paris and seizing one of the biggest opportunities of his life. The German then reached his first Wimbledon final before adding a second major title to his tally by winning the US Open, six years after his near miss at the same tournament against Dominic Thiem. Despite his achievements this season, Zverev has faced criticism, with many claiming he does not deserve to be the world number one due to being winless against Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner in 2026, as well as his poor record versus top ten players. Photo by Dimitar DILKOFF / AFP via Getty Images Patrick Mouratoglou reacts to Carlos Alcaraz’s comments The criticism raged on after Zverev lost to Alcaraz in the final of the ATP Finals, falling in straight sets. After the match, Alcaraz was asked if he felt like the best player in the world, to which he responded: “No, not at all. The number one is Sascha. He really deserves it. Nobody’s going to take that position and the No. 1 away from him.” In a post on LinkedIn , Serena Williams’ former coach, Patrick Mouratoglou, said: “I love the answer. And he’s right. They all do. That’s why they’re so good. Nobody is diminishing anyone here. When you play those guys, you have to feel it inside you, this conviction that you are the best. If you don’t, you cannot win. “We saw it in Turin when Ben Shelton played Alexander Zverev. I don’t think Ben Shelton entered the court thinking, ‘I’m better than this guy’. He couldn’t play his game, and he lost badly. And yet, generally speaking, Ben Shelton is someone who is super, super confident about his ability to beat everybody. The same is true for Carlos Alcaraz, Jannik Sinner and Alexander Zverev. “If Carlos Alcaraz had wanted to give the politically correct answer, he would have said: ‘Zverev is number one, he deserves it.’ And Alexander Zverev does deserve it, Carlos Alcaraz knows that. Still, deep inside, he thinks “I’m better than him”. He should think it, since believing it is exactly what allows him to achieve what he’s achieving. “The same goes for Alexander Zverev. When he walked on court against Carlos Alcaraz, I’m sure he was convinced he was going to win. Two-time Grand Slam champion, number one in the world, ready to show he was the better player. Personally, I think Carlos Alcaraz and Jannik Sinner are on a different level from anybody. Alexander Zverev believes otherwise, and that belief is a big part of why he is number one in the world. “What I love most about this moment is the honesty. Carlos Alcaraz says what he thinks. He has everything: the game, the attitude, the way to communicate. That’s why he’s such a global superstar. And he chose the truth over the politically correct.” Alcaraz is currently the world number three, but will soon overtake number two Sinner after it was revealed that the Italian will be out for an extended period of time following his knee surgery.

title: Dwight Howard reveals he was scammed while trying to buy the Atlanta Dream
summary: Dwight Howard saw the WNBA boom coming before almost anyone else, but things didn’t pan out. The WNBA has grown massively over the past couple of years, breaking TV and attendance records while kicking off a $3 billion media deal.
content: Photo by John Nacion/Getty Images for Fanatics Dwight Howard saw the WNBA boom coming before almost anyone else, but things didn’t pan out. The WNBA has grown massively over the past couple of years, breaking TV and attendance records while kicking off a $3 billion media deal. As for Dwight Howard, the newly inducted Hall of Famer has kept plenty busy since his NBA days wrapped up. After playing overseas in Taiwan, suiting up in the BIG3, and making a quick comeback in Georgia, the 40-year-old officially stepped away from the game for good in October. These days, he’s focused on his kids, community work, and telling wild stories from his career. Dwight Howard tried to buy the Atlanta Dream One of those stories came up recently, and it’s a tough one. Looking back on how close he came to owning a WNBA franchise, Dwight Howard opened up about the whole ordeal, from pitching big ideas to the Atlanta Dream to the exact moment everything fell apart. Speaking on the Mighty YouTube channel: “I was going to buy the Atlanta Dream… I just kept having visions of the WNBA popping off. Like women’s sports going crazy. I text my agent, ‘Hey, I see something big with the WNBA and I want to do something about it.’ So met with the Dream, we start having private conversations, met with the owner, everybody. I’m getting excited. “I came up with this whole plan to get women, the players involved as far as with their contracts to where they’ll receive all their money, how they’ll be involved with the arena, they get money from arenas, like everything. And then also we was involved with getting the networks to be able to show the lives of the women and how hard it is to play, travel, and be a mom. That’s super difficult. We had all these ideas. “The day that I sent my money in to the group that was supposed to be kind of like the face, they stopped talking. Didn’t hear from them no more. Went missing. They took all the money and went and bought houses, cars, jewelry, paintings, all type of stuff. Just like that.” Today, the Dream are owned by Larry Gottesdiener, Suzanne Abair, and former Atlanta guard Renee Montgomery, who bought the franchise for around $10 million back in 2021. That bet has paid off big time. With Angel Reese now serving as the face of the team, Atlanta’s valuation has skyrocketed to roughly $300 million.
