title: WNBA’s 2027 Cap Math Leaves Little Room For Error For Dream
summary: New WNBA salary rules force Atlanta Dream to spend nearly every dollar on minimum contracts, leaving just $886,000 for free agents.
content: Brett Davis-Imagn Images The WNBA salary cap rules for 2027 create a harsh reality for teams trying to build a winner. The Atlanta Dream faces a math problem that leaves almost no room for maneuvering. According to Sports Illustrated , the league cap can rise by no more than 13% to $7.91 million. This small jump does not help teams that already have limited space. The Dream must sign three new players just to fill their roster. Each of these new signings costs at least $280,800. That adds up fast and eats into the money available for star talent. The Minimum Salary Trap Every team must keep 12 players on the roster during the season. This rule forces franchises to spend money they might prefer to save. Per Sports Illustrated, the lowest full-season minimum salary for a player with no experience is $280,800 in 2027. The Dream already has nine players under contract totaling about $6.18 million. To reach the required 12 players, the team needs to spend an extra $842,400 on new signings. This mandatory spending pushes their total obligations to $7.02 million. The math leaves the team with very little flexibility to sign big free agents. Where the Money Goes The gap between the total cap and what a team can actually spend is now wider than ever. The Atlanta Dream will have to spend $7.02 million just to meet basic roster requirements. This leaves them with about $886,000 to spend freely on top-tier talent. That amount is tiny compared to the cost of a supermax deal. A supermax salary is 20% of the cap for a given year, which would be roughly $1.58 million. Only the current club or, in the event of free agency, the former club can sign an eligible player to a supermax. This restriction makes it hard for other teams to poach stars from the Dream without paying a premium. Spending Limits and Roster Rules A team’s payroll cannot surpass the salary cap at any moment unless it applies a hardship, emergency hardship, pregnancy/childbirth, or season-ending injury exception. For any specific year, the standard maximum salary equals 17% of the salary cap. These tight limits mean teams cannot simply throw money at every problem. They must plan carefully or risk breaking the rules. The Dream’s situation shows how the new rules squeeze out spending power. With only $886,000 left for free spending, the team has very few options to improve the roster beyond the minimums. The Dream, in its present form, must spend $7.02 million, which leaves approximately $886,000 available for unrestricted spending above minimum salaries.

title: WNBA star Jackie Young launches foundation to support students in her hometown
summary: The Las Vegas Aces guard’s foundation will help Indiana students cover school fees, meals and winter necessities. WNBA All-Star Jackie
content: LOS ANGELES, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Jackie Young #0 of the Las Vegas Aces reacts to her three pointer during the first half in the game between the Las Vegas Aces and the Los Angeles Sparks at Crypto.com Arena on September 11, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) The Las Vegas Aces guard’s foundation will help Indiana students cover school fees, meals and winter necessities. WNBA All-Star Jackie Young has launched the Jackie Young Foundation to help students facing financial hardship in her hometown of Princeton, Indiana. Young returned to Princeton on Tuesday, Nov. 24, to announce the foundation, 14 News reported. North Gibson School Corporation Superintendent Eric Goggins estimated its first donation to the district at $20,000. He said school officials had learned of Young’s plans about a week earlier. The money will go toward outstanding school fees and upcoming lunch expenses for students eligible for free or reduced-price meals. The foundation will also donate more than $10,000 in gift cards and winter necessities. “I always try to give back to my community,” Young told the station. Young led Princeton Community High School to the Indiana Class 3A state championship in 2015. She scored 36 points in the championship game and ended her high school career with 3,268 points. In 2016, she was named Indiana Miss Basketball, and the school district named the entrance to her high school Jackie Young Way. Young spent three seasons at Notre Dame, where she won an NCAA championship in 2018. Las Vegas selected her first overall in the 2019 WNBA draft. She won Olympic gold in 3×3 basketball in Tokyo and in five-on-five basketball in Paris. In July 2025, Young returned to Princeton to host a youth basketball camp. In January 2026, Skechers and AdoptAClassroom.org donated $15,000 to her former high school in her honor. The donation provided $5,000 for athletics and $10,000 for academic programs. The Las Vegas Aces guard became the WNBA’s first million-dollar player in April, months after helping the team win its third WNBA championship. Goggins said Young has supported local students for years and welcomed the district’s continued partnership with her. The Aces also celebrated the launch of the Jackie Young Foundation in a Nov. 25 social media post, calling their guard “The Pride of Princeton, Indiana.” More must-reads: Rihanna’s documentary director Peter Berg predicts her return to music: ‘It’s going to be a banger’ LeBron James’ family granted restraining orders against two alleged trespassers Mamdani wins legal fight as judge dismisses landlords’ challenge to NYC rent freeze

title: Ary Borges on Arthur Elias: “He works with us and understands players”
summary: Alongside her strong form at Angel City and her string of call-ups to the Brazilian national team, motherhood has brought a new chapter to Ary Borges’ journey. At a press conference on Thursday (26)...
content: Ary Borges on Arthur Elias: “He works with us and understands players” Alongside her strong form at Angel City and her string of call-ups to the Brazilian national team, motherhood has brought a new chapter to Ary Borges’ journey. At a press conference on Thursday (26), the midfielder highlighted the support she received from head coach Arthur Elias and spoke about the importance of his understanding when he left her out of October’s international window so she could spend the first days of her newborn daughter Melanie’s life alongside her wife, Gabriela. “This is a very special time for me. Arthur is a very caring person who really values relationships, both individually and as a group. In this situation, he showed once again how much he stands by us and understands the players. Arthur watched me grow at Centro Olímpico, and now he has watched me become a mother,” she said. “Before the last squad announcement, he called me, asked about my family and was very honest with me. He said that my saying no at that moment (to joining the squad) was actually saying yes. As athletes, we give up so much, and he gave me peace of mind to enjoy a special moment with my family. He also reassured other players who want to become mothers but worry it could affect their careers,” she added. Ary Borges during a Brazilian women’s national team training session in Hiroshima, Japan Credit: Luciana Vermell/CBF Ary has known Arthur Elias since her days at Centro Olímpico, where she played between 2015 and 2016. As a youngster, she would talk with her teammates about the possibility of being a ball girl at matches involving the team he coached. Years later, he would become her coach with the Brazilian national team and her nemesis in matches between Corinthians and Palmeiras, as she played for Palmeiras from 2020 to 2022, during a period of Corinthians dominance. Among the players called up for this international window, Ary logged the most playing time for her club, Angel City in the United States. She made 28 appearances and played 2,688 minutes, figures that underline her consistent involvement throughout the season. Speaking about the challenges facing Brazil in Japan, the midfielder highlighted the importance of the friendlies against the hosts as part of their World Cup preparations. “We’re very happy to be here in Japan and experience a different culture. Our profession gives us that privilege. In football terms, Japan are opponents who present us with plenty of challenges. This is another opportunity for us to study, improve and work toward our main goal, which is getting closer and closer (the World Cup). These have all the makings of two very interesting games, and I hope that, just like last time, we come away with two wins,” she said. title: Bayern Munich to invest €80 million in women's football facilities
summary: Bayern Munich is to invest €80 million ($87. 8 million) in a stadium and sports complex near Munich, giving the club's women's football department a major boost, according to plans presented at a press conference on Thursday.
content: FILE PHOTO - Jan-Christian Dreesen, chief executive of FC Bayern Munich AG, attends a press conference in Unterhaching. (is associated with: «Bayern Munich to invest €80 million in women's football facilities») Jens Niering/dpa Bayern Munich is to invest €80 million ($87.8 million) in a stadium and sports complex near Munich, giving the club's women's football department a major boost, according to plans presented at a press conference on Thursday. Rather than simply renovating the Sportpark Unterhaching stadium, which Bayern bought a year ago, the club now plans to more or less build a new one. According to the plans, about €60 million has been budgeted for the stadium, while €20 million will be invested in a new training centre next to it - significantly more than previously planned. "With this exceptional infrastructure project, we're investing in the continued development of women's football and are confident it will help us to establish ourselves among the European elite," chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen said. Women's football director Bianca Rech said: "The Sportpark will be more than a new home for our players. It's a space to grow. Here the future of FC Bayern Women will take shape in a way that sets benchmarks across Europe." The entire women's and girls' football operation is scheduled to move in 2029, which coincides with the Women's European Championship set to be held in Germany. The club wants to be "at the top" not only in men's football but also in women's football, Dreesen said.

title: Frankfurt captain Laura Freigang will miss Women's World Cup after 16-month suspension for anti-doping rule violation
summary: Laura Freigang is set to miss the 2027 Women's World Cup after a 16-month suspension for committing three reporting and/or testing failures of anti-doping protocols. The Eintracht Frankfurt captain wi...
content: Frankfurt captain Laura Freigang will miss Women's World Cup after 16-month suspension for anti-doping rule violation Laura Freigang is set to miss the 2027 Women's World Cup after a 16-month suspension for committing three reporting and/or testing failures of anti-doping protocols. The Eintracht Frankfurt captain will only be able to return to the pitch from October 8th, 2027, which will be more than two months after the end of the biggest competition in women's football. Freigang, WADA, NADA and the DFB agreed on this settlement on Thursday as a more severe punishment of two years was also a possibility. The failures to comply with the responsible organizations committed between March 11, 2025 and February 23, 2026. The ban applies retroactively from June 8 as all of her results since February 23 will now be nullified. The attacker will be allowed to train with a team again starting from August 8, 2027. The Kiel-native scored 17 goals in 45 appearances for Germany, including playing in the previous World Cup, Euros and the Olympics. She was initially named in Christian Wück's squad for the South America tour. Frankfurt are currently third in the Frauen-Bundesliga as they head into the last international break of the year with three successive wins in all competitions. They will face Real Sociedad in the quarter-final tie of the UEFA Europa Cup on February 2027.

title: Kim Mulkey reacts to MiLaysia Fulwiley's return vs. Belmont
summary: LSU women's basketball welcomed MiLaysia Fulwiley back to the court earlier this week. Here's what Kim Mulkey said.
content: MiLaysia Fulwiley returned to the court for LSU women's basketball against Belmont. She helped the Tigers come away with a 103-45 victory and head coach Kim Mulkey spoke about how the senior guard showed up for her team. "I know she got winded a little bit," Mulkey said. "Our basketball team is so excited to see her back in the locker room. I mean, she just picked up tonight kind of where she left off, except for a few moments there where she got a little bit winded." Fulwiley missed games against Troy and Farleigh Dickinson last week. She was arrested and booked on five counts, including felonies for aggravated assault and aggravated battery, on November 14. Both felony charges were dropped. Following the contest, Mulkey said she noticed the PMAC crowd give Fulwiley a special welcome to the game when she checked in for the first time. The senior guard also surpassed the 1,500 career points mark against Belmont. "I also noticed they gave MiLaysia a standing ovation," Mulkey said. "She scored 1,500 points or something. That's why they asked me to call the timeout when I did so that she could be acknowledged. I did notice." Through five games, Fulwiley is averaging 17 points and three rebounds per game on 53.1% shooting from the field. Against Belmont, she came off the bench to score 14 points on six of 13 from the field while also contributing five steals, three blocks and three assists. "I want her to get to the rim," Mulkey said. "She can shoot it out there. She's worked on her mid-range jumper. But one thing that never goes away, God blessed her with speed and quickness. And she's got it." This article originally appeared on LSU Wire: Kim Mulkey reacts to MiLaysia Fulwiley's return vs. Belmont

title: Oregon women dominate UMES in Cancun Challenge opener
summary: The Oregon women's basketball team opened the Cancun Challenge in Mexico with a dominant 74-50 win over Maryland Eastern Shore.
content: The Oregon women's basketball rolled to a win in its first game at the Cancun Challenge on Thanksgiving Day in Mexico, defeating Maryland Eastern Shore 74-50. The Ducks (7-1) handled the lowly Hawks (1-6) from nearly start to finish, leading for over 34 minutes of game time and dominating almost every stat across the board. Still, coach Kelly Graves and his team feel like they left points on the board with bigger games ahead of them. "You look at some of those numbers and you’d think we’re gonna beat them by 40 and we just didn’t," Graves told KUGN postgame. "We’re going to have to be sharper the rest of this tournament." The Ducks drew UMES for their first game in Cancun, a tune-up against metrically one of the worst teams in NCAA Division I, but take on Colorado Nov. 27 and Georgia Nov. 28, a pair of Power Four teams with similar early season resumes to Oregon. The Ducks outscored the Hawks by 18 in the paint, led fastbreak points 30-1 and held UMES to 32% shooting from the field by won by just 24 points, a figure Graves wasn't happy with. Ehis Etute had another double-double with 12 points and 15 rebounds, Katie Fiso scored 14 points and dished out nine assists and Mallory Heyer (12 points), Ari Long (11 points) and Avary Cain (13 points) all scored in double figures, as well. "Well, I think we’ve got to clean up defensively, some things," Graves said. "I just think we weren’t connected like we typically are. I think that connection showed offensively, too. We made some calls and we weren’t executing. Everybody’s kind of our on their own island. The game today, they kind of make it ugly, Colorado’s not going to make the game ugly. They’re going to defend you, they’re really solid." Graves and Colorado coach JR Payne go way back, with Payne playing under Graves back in the late 1990s at Saint Mary's under Graves, then serving as an assistant under the longtime Oregon coach at Gonzaga. Payne is in her 11th season in Boulder and has made the NCAA tournament four times in the last five years, including last season. title: Replacing Trinity Rodman, leaning on Lindsey Heaps: Five keys as USWNT face El Salvador with a World Cup berth at stake
summary: Emma Hayes must reshape her attack and turn standout NWSL form into international success as the USWNT face El Salvador for a place at Brazil 2027.
content: USWNT GFX - GOAL Emma Hayes must reshape her attack and turn standout NWSL form into international success as the USWNT face El Salvador for a place at Brazil 2027. For the U.S. women’s national team, the equation is simple: beat El Salvador and book a place at next summer’s World Cup. Emma Hayes’ side open their CONCACAF W Championship campaign with Friday’s quarterfinal in Mansfield, Texas, where victory would secure qualification for Brazil 2027. All four quarterfinal winners will advance directly to the World Cup, giving the Americans a chance to settle their biggest priority in their opening match. Friendlies against Spain, Brazil and Japan have provided valuable tests, helping Hayes assess her players and refine her approach. Now comes the challenge of turning those lessons into a performance with qualification on the line. Hayes’ 23-player squad blends established internationals with newcomers to this stage, including uncapped defender Evelyn Shores. She is just the second player named to a U.S. World Cup qualifying roster before making her senior international debut. El Salvador, meanwhile, arrive for their tournament debut and first meeting with the USWNT after a perfect qualifying campaign. La Selecta topped Group F with three wins over Honduras, Barbados and Trinidad and Tobago, scoring 18 goals without conceding. So, what must the Americans get right to secure their place in Brazil? GOAL breaks down five keys... Heaps needs to step up Lindsey Heaps is the most-capped player on the USWNT roster, with 180 appearances. Hayes has made clear she will lean on experience during this qualifying window, and few players offer more than Lindsey Heaps. The midfielder is the most-capped player on the roster, with extensive experience of World Cups and knockout football, including 10 World Cup qualifying appearances and a goal to her name. “Qualifying for a major tournament, first and foremost, I will be leaning on our experienced players,” Hayes said after the roster announcement. “They know how to do this, and they’ve been with us the longest to be able to deliver that.” Heaps recently returned stateside to join NWSL expansion side Denver Summit FC. For the U.S., she often wears the captain’s armband and provides a crucial link between defense and attack, helping win possession and set the tempo. Her speed of play has occasionally drawn criticism against elite opposition, and keeping the ball moving quickly will be central to her effectiveness against El Salvador. Heaps will need to bring urgency alongside her experience, establishing control in midfield and setting the tone as the Americans look to secure their World Cup berth at the first opportunity. Find the right blend without Rodman Sophia Wilson will help lead the USWNT attack as they pursue World Cup qualification without Trinity Rodman. The wait for another ‘Triple Espresso’ start goes on. Hayes initially included Trinity Rodman, Sophia Wilson and Mallory Swanson in her squad, raising hopes of their first start together since the 2024 Olympic gold medal game. The trio shared the pitch against Spain on Oct. 10 for the first time since that final, but have yet to reunite in the starting lineup. Those hopes were dashed Tuesday, when Rodman was ruled out with a shoulder injury sustained in Washington Spirit’s 2-1 NWSL Championship defeat to Kansas City Current. Jaedyn Shaw replaced her on the roster. It is a frustrating setback for Rodman after one of her strongest NWSL seasons, in which she recorded 15 goals and 10 assists across the regular season and playoffs. Her absence also leaves Hayes with an attacking decision to make just days before the tournament opener. Wilson and Swanson will now have to supply the double shot of espresso, with Shaw, Alyssa Thompson and Michelle Cooper among the options to join them. Whoever gets the nod will need to build an understanding with the pair quickly, helping the U.S. find the attacking rhythm to turn their chances into a World Cup berth. It's still a competition for the No. 1 keeper spot Claudia Dickey, Mandy McGlynn and Phallon Tullis-Joyce have 26 USWNT caps between them. Mandy McGlynn strengthened her case for more USWNT minutes with an impressive season for Utah Royals. Alongside a string of standout saves, she helped the club reach the playoffs for the first time, underlining her credentials as Hayes weighs her goalkeeping options. McGlynn remains in contention alongside Claudia Dickey and Phallon Tullis-Joyce, with all three still building their international experience. They have just 26 caps between them: Dickey leads with 12, followed by Tullis-Joyce with eight and McGlynn with six. Whoever starts against El Salvador should be targeting a clean sheet, while continuing to develop an understanding with the defenders in front of her. With Naomi Girma and Emily Sonnett sidelined, Hayes must draw on other center-back options, including Kennedy Wesley, Tierna Davidson and McGlynn’s Utah teammate Kate Del Fava. Those changes make communication and coordination especially important. The goalkeeper and back line need to establish when to play out, when to clear their lines and how to respond when possession is lost. Building that trust against El Salvador would give the U.S. a stronger foundation for the challenges ahead. Take command at center back Tierna Davidson and Kennedy Wesley are the likely pairing at center back for the USWNT, especially with Naomi Girma and Emily Sonnett still out. With Naomi Girma and Emily Sonnett sidelined, the USWNT are getting an opportunity to build depth at center back. Kennedy Wesley has been a beneficiary, earning starts and substantial minutes as Hayes assesses her defensive options. Wesley’s partnership with Tierna Davidson offers promise. Both are composed and comfortable on the ball, giving the U.S. a platform to build from the back. The next step is ensuring they bring the same authority to organizing the defensive line. Sonnett’s vocal presence is difficult to replace. Wesley and Davidson have quieter styles, but clear communication will be essential to keeping the back line coordinated, particularly when deciding whether to step up, drop deeper or cover a teammate. Against El Salvador, they will need to stay engaged even during long spells of U.S. possession. With Kate Del Fava and Tara Rudd also available, Hayes has options. This window gives those defenders a chance to show they can deliver the consistency and leadership required in knockout football. Bring NWSL form to the international stage Ashley Sanchez returns for a second consecutive USWNT camp after winning NWSL Golden Boot and MVP honors with a 20-goal season. Hayes’ squad is packed with NWSL standouts, including league MVP Ashley Sanchez and Midfielder of the Year Croix Bethune. Both have moved in and out of the national team picture, but their club performances have strengthened their cases for meaningful roles in qualifying. Bethune recorded a league-record 11 regular-season assists for Kansas City Current. Her ability to find the final pass from the No. 10 position could be particularly valuable against El Salvador, giving the U.S. another way to turn possession into clear chances. Sanchez, meanwhile, thrived after moving from attacking midfield to the left wing for North Carolina Courage, scoring 20 goals and matching the league’s single-season record. Hayes must decide where to use her, but her ability to attack crosses at the far post and create around the edge of the box offers flexibility. The challenge extends beyond the award winners. Shaw has another opportunity to bring her Gotham form to the senior team, while Kate Del Fava and Mandy McGlynn can draw on the understanding they developed at Utah. The U.S. need those club performances to translate quickly, with World Cup qualification at stake in the opening match.

title: What will returning Magill bring to Northern Ireland?
summary: As she gears up for her international return, what will Simone Magill bring to Northern Ireland against Greece in Friday's friendly?
content: Simone Magill made her return to football as a late substitute for Birmingham City against Manchester United on Sunday [Getty Images] After 13 months away, Simone Magill made her return to football as a late substitute in Birmingham City's WSL defeat by Manchester United on Sunday. It was a moment that had been a long time coming for the 31-year-old, who gave birth to her daughter, Skye, in May and has been building towards stepping back on the pitch. Now, she will hope to make her international return with Northern Ireland in a friendly against Greece on Friday. "It's been some time since I've been here in a playing capacity, so it's really nice just to be back in the mix again," NI captain Magill told BBC Sport NI. "I officially made my comeback at the weekend and it was really nice to have done that. I'm really looking forward to doing that here at home in front of the fans and my family as well." 'You can be a mum and a footballer - they can co-exist' Greece friendlies an opportunity to build - Andrews In an interview with BBC Sport in October, Magill spoke about how being both a mum and a footballer can "co-exist". While she was not ready to play any role in the matches, Magill, Skye and her husband Mark were all in camp for the World Cup play-off with Portugal last month, all with an eye of integrating into international duty as a family. Having played just a handful of minutes, Northern Ireland manager Michael McArdle said that while he was "delighted" to have Magill back, how much she plays across the double-header would be in collaboration with Birmingham and his captain. "With the circumstances around this one, I'm very mindful that I need to build accordingly and I really need to listen to myself as well," Magill added. "To even be back in this capacity this soon after giving birth, for me, is just unbelievable. "I have no major expectations. I'm just really happy to be here and be a part of it, and if I do come on, that'll be even better." I want to bring leadership Friday's match against Greece will be Northern Ireland's first friendly in three years. The sides will then play again on Tuesday at 16:00 GMT, and both matches can be streamed live on BBC iPlayer and the BBC Sport app and website. The matches will act as preparation for the Nations League campaign in February, when Northern Ireland face tricky tests in the form of Poland, Finland and Belarus. McArdle is developing a young squad and Magill says she hopes to bring "leadership and experience to really help us all move forward". "We've obviously had a transition in the last year whilst I've been out, it's been nice to come back in and just feel where we're at, get on the grass with the girls and see, 'how can I help, what can I bring?'," she added. "I'm very much looking forward to just getting back in the mix and helping try to bring the young players forward, use that experience and let's hold on to the ball, let's get into the final third, let's have a go, be brave - all of the attributes that we're known for. "We're an underdog nation, so it's getting that across to the younger members in the squad to say, 'let's have a go with these teams and not be afraid'." In her absence over the past year, Northern Ireland have used a number of different options in the centre forward role. Winger Lauren Wade has shown her versatility by playing centrally, while Kess Elmore and Cora Chambers have also played up top. Along with Magill, Portsmouth striker Kerry Beattie is also back in the squad to bolster McArdle's striking options. "We've loads of young ones snapping at my heels. It's great, that's what we want. "I feel we're more competitive now than ever. You never know who's going to be coming into the squad. Certainly, in more recent years, you kind of knew the squad every single time, whereas that's not the case now. "We've got some exciting youth coming through, so it's their time now to shine." Magill added that Northern Ireland are "heading in a new direction" ahead of the Nations League campaign next year, and the friendlies with Greece give an opportunity for the team to grow in a pressure-free environment. "We're coming into a brand new campaign and it's really nice that we have a friendly window just now. "We haven't had one in a very, very long time, so this is a brilliant opportunity to get us all back together, get the new faces in, get some more experience, learn things, try things. "I'm really excited about where we're going." Can returning Beattie and Haughey make an impact? Three years on NI Women finally have friendlies again

title: Bizarre Legal Situation Develops Over Bill Watts’ Mid-South Wrestling (WWE News)
summary: WWE looking to bring back Mid-South Wrestling?
content: WWE Earlier this week, WWE filed a trademark for "Mid-South Wrestling." Mid-South Wrestling was the promotion run by ' Cowboy' Bill Watts from 1979 to 1986, becoming one of the hottest territories in the business and housing so many of the major stars of the day and of the future, from the Junkyard Dog to Ted DiBiase, to Magnum T.A., to Jim Duggan, to 'Dr. Death' Steve Williams, to Jake Roberts, to a young Shawn Michaels, to the Midnight Express, to the Rock 'n' Roll Express, and many, many more. The promotion rebranded as the Universal Wrestling Federation - not to be confused with Herb Abrams' company of the same name - in '86, then closed its doors for good the following year. Per POST Wrestling , Tuesday saw WWE file a trademark for the "Mid-South Wrestling" name for purposes of "Entertainment services, namely, a show about professional wrestling," suggesting the market leader could be looking to relaunch Mid-South in some form or fashion. What makes this trademark application all the more interesting is that it comes mere days after PRODUCE and Razor Pro Wrestling announced plans to revive the Mid-South Wrestling brand, starting with an event in Fayetteville, Arkansas, on February 21st of next year. Orange Crush, the art project behind PRODUCE, has since taken to X to post a screenshot of what appears to be their separate "Mid-South Wrestling" trademark application from Monday, one day before WWE's filing. pic.twitter.com/yWjIgB0KpA — ORANGE CRUSH (@orangecrushart) November 25, 2026 It remains to be seen how all of this plays out, though it is worth noting that WWE acquired the Mid-South library in 2012, purchasing that from Bill Watts' ex-wife, Ene, who herself acquired the library as part of her divorce from Cowboy. title: CM Punk Admits He Doesn’t Like Wrestling **** ****** (WWE News)
summary: Fill in the blanks! CM Punk just did. You won't believe who he doesn't like wrestling in WWE.
content: WWE.com CM Punk is no stranger to serving up tasty details during interviews or even on the live mic during promos , but this news might surprise a good few folks. According to the man himself, Punk doesn't actually like wrestling against Cody Rhodes. The former WWE Champ told Wingmen that he's always wary of hurting Cody, so he can't properly concentrate on having a good match. Accidentally injuring his good buddy would be the last thing he'd want to do, but it plays on his mind. Punk and Rhodes shared the ring as rivals at SummerSlam in August. This entire 'Team USA' angle heading into Survivor Series: WarGames could be a ploy to eventually book a rematch - Cody revealing Seth Rollins as the final member of the traditional elimination team might play into that too . This statement collides with something Punker previously said. You guessed it: He once said he regarded Rhodes as a dream WWE opponent . Make up your mind, Phil! Seriously though, Punk does like sharing screen time with the 'American Nightmare'. He'd just rather that was as partners rather than rivals. Perhaps both guys forming a proper tag-team could save the doubles division then . Just a thought. " There’s so much history, but deep down, you guys love each other. Logan Paul is finally coming back from his injury. Almost seven months ago, during an edition of WWE Saturday Night’s Main Event, Paul suffered a triceps injury during his attempt to catch Angelo Dawkins. Paul has been sidelined and ruled out of action since then. Now, after months of absence, WWE recently announced a comeback date for Paul from his injury. It was recently announced on Wednesday, Nov. 25, 2026, that Paul will be in action in WWE’s Dec. 26 live event at Madison Square Garden in New York City. Paul was sidelined back in May. 2026, after tearing his triceps during the above-mentioned Saturday Night’s Main Event. Despite his time away from the ring, Paul has maintained his constant presence on television as an active member of The Vision. However, it is still possible that Paul could make his in-ring return before the Boxing Day WWE event.
